author: javiergrecco
body:
## Objetivo

Completar el límite de lectura del comparador M7. La consulta de aplicación ya recibe el análisis financiero por contrato, pero todavía construye `PersonaRepo`, `PrestamoRepo` y `ParticipacionRepo`. Las lecturas de alternativas y condiciones del préstamo deben concentrarse en infraestructura.

## Alcance

- Definir un puerto pequeño y DTO tipados para persona, préstamos, participaciones y tasa activa que necesita el comparador.
- Mover el acceso a repositorios concretos al adaptador `infraestructura/consultas/`.
- Hacer que `ComparadorDecisionesFinancierasQuery` reciba datos y análisis por constructor, sin SQLite ni repositorios.
- Actualizar el punto de composición y mantener UI/tests consumiendo la fábrica.
- Agregar guardas arquitectónicas y una prueba sin base de datos.

## Invariantes

- Solo lectura, sin cambios de esquema ni registros financieros.
- Preservar alternativas disponibles, etiquetas, roles, orden, capital de referencia, tasa, modalidad, calendario y estado.
- No cambiar XIRR, flujos históricos/futuros, supuestos de inflación, valoración real ni reglas de homogeneidad.
- Mantener las restricciones: entre 2 y 6 alternativas y horizonte de 1 a 60 meses.

## Validación

- Pruebas actuales de listado, comparación, homogeneidad y E2E de UI M7.
- Prueba unitaria con datos falsos, sin SQLite.
- Guarda arquitectónica contra infraestructura/repositorios desde aplicación.
- CI en Python 3.11–3.14, CodeQL, auditoría de dependencias y diff check.

## Seguimiento

Continúa [#267 — Arquitectura modular](https://github.com/JavierGrecco/prestamos_privados/issues/267) y no modifica fórmulas ni la autoridad financiera de Legacy/V3.

author: arthurandrealmeida
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2615.

Require explicit REA server identity before a completed MCP call receives REA routing credit. Cover missing identity, foreign servers, both identity fields, and case-insensitive REA names.

## Problem and expected behavior

A completed call naming `inspect_managed_artifact` but omitting both `server` and `server_name` currently counts as REA use, the correct first tool, and a successful required tool sequence. The tool name alone does not identify its server.

For that transcript, the corrected metrics are `naturalUse: false`, `firstTool: null`, `correctFirstTool: false`, and `requiredToolSubsequenceMet: false`. Explicit `rea` identity continues to receive credit through either field, case-insensitively.

## Change and scope

The existing transcript parser still owns alias resolution, completion validation, arguments, and Evidence authentication. Its parsed server identity now controls the routing filter consistently with the Evidence path. Replace the old test that credited unidentified legacy calls with negative and positive identity cases.

This is an ordinary evaluator bug fix within the existing contribution scope; an advance maintainer scope decision is not applicable. No new provider, target interaction, execution authority, or installation behavior is introduced.

## Contract and boundary impact

- Semantic owner: `evaluateCodexEvents`, when selecting parsed REA calls for transcript metrics.
- CLI/MCP schemas, tool catalog, provider/platform support, target selection, and cleanup: unchanged.
- Evidence authentication, retained artifact identity, provenance, and factual assessment: unchanged. Unknown server identity cannot establish REA routing credit.
- Generated metadata, packaging, and installation: no changes.
- Expected effect: evaluate caller-supplied transcript data in memory; no target interaction or network requests added.

## Evidence and regression coverage

- Executed the updated evaluator suite before the production fix: the missing-identity case failed with the incorrect routing metrics; 27 other tests passed.
- After the fix, all 101 tests in the evaluator, known-answer assessment, and evaluation-report suites passed.
- Regression cases cover absent identity, foreign `server` and `server_name`, and explicit `rea`/`REA` through both fields. Existing conflicting-field, Evidence, error, and workflow tests remain covered.
- A read-only review found no actionable issues.

## Validation performed

Using the pinned Node.js 24.18.0 and npm 11.16.0 on Linux x64:

- `npm run test:local -- tests/evaluation/model-evals/codexAgentEval.test.ts tests/evaluation/model-evals/knownAnswerEvaluation.test.ts tests/evaluation/model-evals/agentEvaluationReport.test.ts` — 3 files, 101 tests passed.
- `npm run check` — passed typecheck, compile, format, lint, Knip, package-metadata checks, module boundaries, and architecture guards. Lint reported 0 errors and 1,211 warnings.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

## Compatibility, safety, and release

Legacy transcripts without server identity no longer establish REA usage; record `server: "rea"` or `server_name: "rea"` to identify those calls. No schema or migration changes. A live model trial, full deterministic suite, and real native providers were not run; the exercised behavior is the production transcript evaluator and its related assessment/report consumers.

## Before merge

- [x] Concrete issue linked; one focused outcome and conventional title.
- [x] Scope and authority questions resolved for this ordinary fix.
- [x] Regression demonstrated on the affected base and passed after the fix.
- [x] Relevant static checks and related evaluator suites passed.
- [x] No documentation, catalog, or package updates required.
- [x] Final diff reviewed for secrets, unrelated changes, and unsupported claims.

author: squid-protocol
body:
Part of #4950 (checklist box 3: container-command names move to IBM's character set).

## What was wrong
Container and channel names on PUT / GET / DELETE CONTAINER, LINK / XCTL CHANNEL and the browse commands were checked only for "not blank, no embedded blank". `^`, `~` or `{` were accepted, which IBM does not allow, and an illegal name had no IBM condition.

## What IBM documents
Only PUT CONTAINER (CHANNEL) gives a set and conditions: "The acceptable characters are A-Z a-z 0-9 $ @ # / % ? ! : | " = , ; > . - and _. Leading and embedded blank characters are not permitted." An illegal CHANNEL name is CHANNELERR RESP2 1, an illegal CONTAINER name is CONTAINERERR RESP2 18. GET and DELETE CONTAINER give no set and no condition. RUN TRANSID's page lists three more characters (`&`, `<`, the not sign) that PUT CONTAINER's page omits.

## Change (both runtimes, the C stub `ggcics.c` and `CicsTask`)
- PUT CONTAINER: a name outside the set gives CHANNELERR 1 / CONTAINERERR 18 and creates nothing.
- Refused by name (ASSUMED / REFUSED, X17): `& < ¬` in a container-command name (IBM's two pages disagree); an illegal name on a command whose page says nothing of one; on PUT, two illegal names, or an illegal one with a negative FLENGTH or no channel in scope (IBM does not rank the conditions); a name over 16 characters.
- RUN / START CHANNEL keep RUN's set, `& < ¬` included. A channel RUN creates with one of them cannot be named by a container command (refused).
- Spec (`containers.py`) states the two PUT outcomes and the new refusals; X17 rewritten.

## Class table
| member | status |
|---|---|
| PUT CONTAINER CHANNEL / CONTAINER name | modelled here (CHANNELERR 1 / CONTAINERERR 18) |
| GET / DELETE CONTAINER, LINK / XCTL CHANNEL, STARTBROWSE, MOVE, QUERY / DELETE CHANNEL names | refused by name outside the set (IBM silent) |
| `& < ¬` in a name | refused by name (pages disagree) |
| RUN / START CHANNEL names | unchanged (#5013) |
| scenario `channel` / container names in the case file (`_CICS_NAME`) | unchanged: any name without a blank; Sibling gap |

## Evidence
- `tests/cics_crucible/test_cics_runtimes.py`: same scripts on the stub and on CicsTask. Every IBM character accepted, 13 illegal names (leading / embedded blank, `^ ~ [ { \ ' ` * ( +`, an accented byte) on both CHANNEL and CONTAINER and through the current channel, the refusals above.
- 947 CICS / det / equivalence / resources tests pass.
- `pr_gates --fast` 6/6, `--ratchets` 7/7.
- `det_port check`: 91 ports changed only in the shared `CicsTask.java` (85 lines, the name check). Re-proved a sample: asynccc-csstats2, asynccc-getname, cbsa-crdtagy1, cbsa-inqcust all PROVED. A full re-sweep was not run.
- Golden masters: no parsing change, none moved.

## Sibling gaps (not in this PR)
- cics-crucible runners do not dispatch RUN children at waits or hand a START CHANNEL copy to the started task (separate corpus; no case uses either).
- R1: a dispatched child's ENQ / DEQ / counter / SQL commands are refused rather than interleaved with the parent (needs a true interleaving scheduler; IBM silent on ordering).
- asynccc ASYNCPNT (waiting FETCH CHILD with CHANNEL): no case; that corpus is not a burned estate.
- The case file's channel / container names (`equivalence_cics._CICS_NAME`) are not checked against IBM's set.

## Summary

Bundle an 85 KB, 0–20 s prefix of the pinned MATLAB WaveStar NMPC controller trace and gate the public Python observer, AR forecast, RTI controller, and actuator in ordinary Python CI. The prefix includes five seconds of active NMPC. The fixture README records the source run, pinned revisions, source hashes, and extracted columns.

Update the parity ledger with measured component errors. The published 225 s autonomous closed-loop trajectory remains open because this gate takes MATLAB stroke and the preceding torque request as inputs. Badge counts do not change.

## Numerical gates

- Observer state: `<1e-10`; observed `6.59e-13`.
- Composed AR forecast: `<25` N m during the unstable 10–11 s fit, `<1e-9` N m after 11 s; observed `18.38` and `5.96e-12` N m.
- Torque command: `<0.01` N m peak and `<0.0003` N m RMS; observed `1.86e-6` and `1.15e-7` N m.
- Actuator axial force: `<1e-7` N; observed `2.30e-12` N.

## Verification

- Focused portable test: 1 passed locally.
- Full local Python suite: 263 passed, 333 skipped in 5m20s; combined line-and-branch coverage rose from 77.61% to 78.25%. `wecsim/control/wavestarNmpc.py` rose from 58% to 88%. The displayed coverage badge remains 78%.

author: marcus-souza-azion
body:
## What & why

**Related issue:** MM-16119

**Pages affected:** 74 files across three commits. Every content change landed in both languages.

A review of the live docs returned 16 findings: 13 on the Azion CLI, one on the Terraform
Provider quickstart, and two general. Most of the CLI findings are factual — the pages described
behavior the CLI does not have. Every finding was checked against CLI 4.23.0, the
`aziontech/azion-cli` source, and the generated command reference before it was applied.

**Azion CLI**

- **The build always runs.** Only `--skip-build` and `--skip-framework-build` stop it. The `.edge`
  folder never decided it, on either the default or the `--local` route.
- **Resources follow what `azion.config` declares.** A project with a function and static files gets
  both, so "a JavaScript project gets a function *instead*" is replaced on `how-it-works` and
  `deploy`. A Next.js project also gets a function, so the language was never the trigger.
- **`--config-dir`** is named where the deploy reads and writes `azion/azion.json`.
- **Storage credentials — two files, two routes.** A default deploy uploads the *source files* for the
  remote build with the credentials in `settings.toml`; `--local` uploads the *built static files*
  with one credential set per bucket in `credentials.toml`. Both pages named only `credentials.toml`,
  for both routes.
- **`azion sync --iac` writes `azion.config.mjs` by default**, and `--extension` takes `mjs`, `cjs`,
  `ts`, or `js`. The extension was stated as fixed on three pages.
- **`azion clone application` reads as a resource command**, matching the CLI's own root description
  ("manage your Azion projects and resources") and the overview page, which already filed it there.
- **`--no-color`** had an empty description row. Filled. The CLI's own help text for this flag repeats
  the `--format` string, so the description does not come from there.
- **`azion create profile`** is named on `how-it-works` and gets an example on `profiles`, alongside
  the new **`--refresh`** flag.
- **`AuthorizeMetricsCollection`** mechanics are out of the reset prose.

**Terraform.** The quickstart pins provider `2.0.0` in its HCL but never stated it as a prerequisite.
It now does, with the reason: the guide uses Azion API v4, which the provider supports from 2.0.

**General.** The root sidebar group becomes **Platform Resources** / **Recursos de Plataforma** — the
nomenclature term in Title Case per `terminology.mdx`, which the sentence-case rule exempts as a
proper noun — along with the two style-guide pages whose prose names that group. The home hero loses a
comma that made a two-item phrase read as an unfinished list.

**WAF** (requested alongside the review). The Exceptions section explained a single exception as "a
hole in the rule set, as large as you make it" but never the aggregate. It now states that exceptions
accumulate, that fewer internal rules score as they do, and that the loss follows the surface they
exempt rather than the row count.

**Navigation Interfaces***: Improved

## Type of change

- [ ] 🆕 New content (`feat`)
- [x] 🩹 Fix (`fix`) — typo, broken link, wrong information
- [x] ♻️ Content update (`docs`) — rewrite, expansion, upkeep <!-- the WAF Exceptions addition and the style-guide rule updates -->
- [ ] 🌐 Translation sync (`i18n`)
- [x] 🏗️ Platform / structure (`refactor` / `chore`) — reviewed by UXE, no content mixed in <!-- the Tabs.vue change; its content pairs are the style-guide rules that document it -->

## Author checklist

- [x] PR title follows `type(scope): summary` (see [GOVERNANCE.md §4](GOVERNANCE.md))
- [ ] Frontmatter complete: `title`, `description`, `meta_tags`, `namespace`, `permalink`, `last_reviewed` 
- [x] No legacy "edge-" product names in the copy 
- [x] How-to/tutorial content includes at least one runnable, copy-paste-tested code block
- [x] Screenshots (if any) have alt text and follow image standards 
- [x] Internal links are relative and resolve locally 
- [x] **If any permalink changed or page moved: redirect added in this PR**
- [x] **i18n:** `pt-br` updated in this PR **or** follow-up `i18n` issue created

author: inactdev
body:
What:
`fabrica up` now also starts `integrations/herdr/`'s watcher, detached the same way it starts the live view, whenever it detects it's running inside a Herdr pane (`HERDR_ENV=1` and a non-empty `HERDR_PANE_ID`) - and does nothing, saying nothing, otherwise. It never starts a second watcher for the same record home.

Why:
Herdr users running `fabrica up` want the task-mirroring watcher (built earlier, issue #125) running automatically in their session instead of having to start it by hand in a second terminal, but Fabrica's own `src/` must never be allowed to name Herdr (CONTRACT rule 8's scan, enforced by `no-herdr-in-core.test.ts`), so the wiring has to be generic from `src/`'s side.

How:
Added a generic, runtime-discovered hook mechanism to `src/cli/up-command.ts` (`loadUpIntegrationHooks`), scanning `integrations/<name>/up-hook.ts` for a `maybeStart({ recordHome, env })` export - the same discovery shape `loadHarnessLauncher` already uses for `skill/<harness>/launch.ts`, just plural (every hook found runs, not just the first). It's called unconditionally after the live-view step; a hook that throws or fails to load is reported to stderr but never blocks the harness from launching. Added a generic `spawnDetachedScript` to `src/cli/spawn-detached.ts` (same detached/stdio/unref mechanism as `spawnDetachedLiveView`, parameterized by entry script and env) for integrations to reuse without `src/` naming any of them. `integrations/herdr/up-hook.ts` is the one shipped hook: it checks `HERDR_ENV`/`HERDR_PANE_ID`, checks `herdr-watcher.ts`'s new `isHerdrWatcherRunning(recordHome)` (a pid file written by the watcher's `main()` on startup, checked for real liveness via a signal-0 `kill`, with a stale file cleaned up), and spawns the watcher via `spawnDetachedScript` only if both pass. Tests: `integrations/herdr/up-hook.test.ts` proves started-once-not-twice and never-outside-Herdr with injected fakes; `herdr-watcher.test.ts` gained tests for the real pid-file liveness check; `src/cli/up-command.test.ts` gained tests proving the generic discovery+invocation wiring (using a neutral, non-Herdr-named fixture hook) and that a failing hook never blocks the harness. `npm test` (789 tests) and `npm run typecheck` both pass, including the `no-herdr-in-core` scan.

Deviations:
The task didn't specify the "already running" detection mechanism - I designed a pid-file + signal-0-liveness check (the standard, portable approach; rejected scanning `ps` output as more fragile/platform-dependent) since the watcher has no network port to probe the way the live view does. Also refrained from refactoring `spawnDetachedLiveView` to share code with the new `spawnDetachedScript` (added it as a separate function instead), to avoid any risk to that already-tested, unrelated code path.

author: natej45
body:
Starter PORTS cards 86 and 95, plus the nested dry-run diff from the gotcha-ports triage.

**Production second factor.** Every script that can write to the `production` Sanity dataset now needs its write flag AND `NCS_PRODUCTION_WRITE=yes`, read from `process.env` directly. Bare runs are dry runs that print the plan.

- New `scripts/lib/production-write.mjs` (not PORTABLE) for scripts outside sanity-lib: `seed-core` (now dry by default), `seed-pages`, `apply-asset-patches`, `import-content`, and the seven sanity-lib scripts that write under their own `--write` flag (sanity-lib only checks `--apply`).
- `modules/*/seed.mjs` and the ten `archive/modules/*/seed.mjs`: dry by default, check inline, variable read before `dotenv` runs.
- `scripts/lib/production-write.test.mjs`: refusals proven in child processes with a fake project and `SANITY_API_HOST=https://example.invalid`. Production is never touched.

body:
Closes STPA finding LS-06 (WP-A-05 OI-9) with the option you chose: gate on the heartbeat's engaged flag.

**Before:** the panda granted `controls_allowed` on the PCM cruise rising edge whatever openpilot's state. Only the 1 Hz engaged-mismatch check removed it, after 2–3 s.

## Changes
- **opendbc `b9f7451`** ([jherrodthomas/opendbc#14](https://github.com/jherrodthomas/opendbc/pull/14)), reference build only:
  - A PCM rising edge opens a 1 s window. Authority is granted once `heartbeat_engaged` is set and the RX checks allow engagement.
  - The grant is made at the edge or in the 100 Hz safety task, never from the host command handler.
  - The window is cancelled by cruise off, brake, an RX fault or a mode change.
- **selfdrived:** `controlsMismatch` ignores `pandaStates` samples in the first 0.3 s after engaging. Without this, the panda waiting for the next 10 Hz heartbeat could cause a spurious immediate disable. The TSR-621 0.5 s bound from the first mismatched frame is unchanged. 3 new unit tests.
- **WP-S-02 v0.20:**
  - TSR-301 gains the heartbeat condition.
  - TSR-621 Impl notes the grace.
  - Trace items are synced.
- **Impact record** `change-2026-10-14-pcm-engage-heartbeat-gate.md`:
  - Engagement timing worst case of about 0.21 s, inside the grace and the window.
  - Behaviour to watch, and open items.

## Verification
- **opendbc:**
  - Safety suite in both variants: 3334 tests.
  - 3 new gate tests in 7 Toyota configurations.
  - MISRA clean in both variants.
  - Reference-variant mutation: 2840 mutants, 3 known upstream `lateral.h` survivors, none in the new code.
- **Host:** supervision tests pass (13).
- **Assurance:** all `assurance.yaml` steps pass locally.
- **Not done:** not verified on the vehicle or a HIL bench (impact OI-1).

## Merge order
`build release` checks that submodule pins are on the fork's `master`, so it fails until opendbc#14 is merged. After that I'll re-pin to the merge commit.

author: bobstrogg
body:
## Why v1.1.26 locked 30 on Albatross The Tesla rate lock read rAF p95 while the load-time scene probe was still in that ring. The probe forces a shadow pass and a synchronous 1×1 `readPixels`. Those gaps pushed p95 over 20 ms, `decimationN` froze at 2, and it never stepped back up. On a 60 Hz panel N=2 is locked 30. After the probe, main-thread rAF was a steady 16.7 ms (the reported overlay: p50/p95/p99 16.70/16.80/16.80, missed/min 0, hist `2x:60`), so 60 was holdable and the "Locked 60: yes" line was only looking at main rAF. Shadows were turned off on the renderer, then `KeyLightRig.applyShadowEnabled` copied `SceneConfig.shadow.enabled` (still true) and turned them back on. The overlay showed PCF plus both `shadowMapSize` 2048 and 1024. The DPR line was `window.devicePixelRatio` (1.96) while the drawing buffer was the CSS size (804×638) from the DPR 1.0 cap. ## What changed - The lock uses the scene-probe median after subtracting an idle readback fence, compared with a 16 ms threshold. Both numbers are in the overlay events. 60 is chosen whenever that scene cost fits. 30 is only the fallback. A lower pixel ratio is kept only if the remeasure lands under 16 ms or cuts the cost by at least 25%. - Tesla shadows stay off unless `?shadow=1`. The context line is `Shadows: off`, and the shadow-map quality lines are removed. - The DPR 1.0 cap is replaced by a load-time budget: ratio 1.25–1.5 and at most 1.6e6 pixels. For the 804×638 @ 1.96 panel that is DPR 1.50 (1206×957). Paper, stems, and clefs use Lambert on Tesla. Noteheads stay standard so the played-note glow still works. No new post-process. - "Locked 60" follows display Hz ÷ decimation N. - `audioSpeed` 1.019 was a ~0.5 s slice. sampleRate 44100 does not take the 48 kHz compensation. A rate is applied only after 2 s, outside ±0.008, and inside 0.9–1.1. - Master volume is a GainNode slider beside play, 44 px tall, stored in `luminoir.masterVolume`. There was no in-app master control before (the hidden unlock element stays at volume 1 for iOS). ## Checks `pnpm lint` (0 errors), `pnpm test` (116), `pnpm build`. Headless SwiftShader at 804×638, devicePixelRatio 1.96, `?platform=tesla&stats=1&renderer=webgl` (this VM, not the car): - `Shadows: off` - `scene-probe: median=82.92 ms fence=0.86 ms scene=82.06 ms threshold=16.00 ms shadows=off dpr=1.50 → locked30 (N=2)` - A trial step to 1.25 saved 10% and was reverted. Framebuffer stayed `DPR 1.50 (native 1.96) 1206×957`. - `Locked 60: no` while `Rate locked30 (N=2)`. After the cadence settled, present hist was `2x:60`. - A 4.02 s AudioContext window at 44100 Hz measured rate 1.0002 (inside the deadband, not corrected). Overlay `audioSpeed` stays blank until that window exists. - Volume slider 120×44 px. Setting 0.40 drove the GainNode; 0.35 persisted across reload. On this software GL the scene really is ~83 ms, so 30 is the correct fallback. A Tesla GPU whose fence-corrected probe is ≤ 16 ms locks 60 and keeps the 1.50 buffer.

author: eciurleo
body:
## Summary

Hardens `.github/workflows/ci.yml` against the findings in #263. All six jobs run on
**self-hosted org runners**, so each hardening item below has a direct blast-radius
reduction. The workflow verifies exactly the same things as before
(`fmt`/`clippy`/`test`/`gui-test`/`gitleaks`/`cargo-deny`) — only *how* it runs changed.

## Per-item resolution

**1. Scoped permissions (least privilege)** — Removed the workflow-wide
`packages: write`. Top level is now `permissions: { contents: read }`. Only the
`build-image` job — the sole GHCR publisher — adds a job-level
`permissions: { contents: read, packages: write }`. Every other job's token is now
read-only.

**2. SHA-pinned actions** — All five actions are pinned to commit SHAs, resolved via
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/ref/tags/<tag>` (all are lightweight tags, so the ref
SHA *is* the commit SHA — no annotated-tag indirection):

| Action | Tag | Pinned SHA |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actions/checkout` | v7 | `3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1` |
| `docker/login-action` | v4 | `dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f` |
| `docker/metadata-action` | v6 | `dc802804100637a589fabce1cb79ff13a1411302` |
| `docker/build-push-action` | v7 | `c3c9e263c25d99ce0380d002d59b67737d91b0dc` |
| `actions/upload-artifact` | v7 | `cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9` |

The human-readable version is kept as a trailing `# vN` comment, mirroring the
project's existing digest-pin discipline for gitleaks and the Dockerfile runtime base.

**3. Timeouts** — `timeout-minutes` added to every job: `lint-test` 45,
`build-image` 45, `actionlint` 15, `gui-test` 45, `secret-scan` 30, `supply-chain` 45.
A stuck/absent runner now yields an actionable red X instead of the 24h3m queue
incident (run 37980161645).

**4. Pinned gate tooling** — `cargo install --locked cargo-deny --version 0.20.2` and
`cargo install --locked cargo-cyclonedx --version 0.5.9`, so the advisory/license gate
and SBOM generator are reproducible run-to-run. The SBOM steps stay
`continue-on-error: true` (best-effort, must not fail the gate) but now log loudly and
carry a comment explaining the trade-off.

**5. Dependabot blind spot for `run:`-string images** — Documented explicitly (the
issue allows "digest-pin **or** add a periodic check"; a documented note is the
chosen, lower-risk route). `.github/dependabot.yml` now states that its docker
ecosystem only sees `image:`/`FROM` references, so `node:22-slim` (gui-test harness)
and `rhysd/actionlint:1.7.12` (workflow lint), pulled inside `run:` strings, get **no**
update PRs and are bumped by hand. A matching comment in `ci.yml` ties every
`rust:1.98.0-slim-trixie` reference (workflow `container:`/`run:` steps and the
Dockerfile builder) to `rust-toolchain.toml` (`channel = "1.98.0"`), which is the single
source of truth for that toolchain.

**6. #246 decision** — **Concurrency adopted; the Gitflow `develop` push trigger was
not added to this copy, with rationale.**

- **Adopted:** workflow-level
  `concurrency: { group: ci-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true }` (the exact
  form #263 item 6 specifies) so a superseded PR/ref run no longer holds a self-hosted
  runner — directly mitigating the queue-incident class.
- **Adopted (safety half):** `build-image` now carries a main-only guard alongside the
  existing fork guard, so a non-main push can never spend a runner on a full release
  cargo build + docker build. PRs still build the image as a check (never pushed), so
  the Dockerfile stays exercised.
- **Not adopted (and why):** the one-line `push: branches: [main, develop]` from #246.
  That change is already merged **on the `develop` branch** (`d9cd165`), and on `main`
  (this integration line, HEAD `114e9d1`) `develop` is *not* an ancestor, so `main`'s
  copy never carried it. For `push` events GitHub evaluates the workflow file **from the
  pushed ref**, so a `develop` push is governed by `develop`'s own `ci.yml` — adding
  `develop` to `main`'s trigger list would be inert for those pushes while implying a
  coupling this branch does not have. This PR's brief also requires leaving `develop`
  untouched. Net: `main` keeps `push: branches: [main]`, and the main-only `build-image`
  guard is the reusable safety that would prevent the doubling #263 item 6 warns about
  were such a trigger ever present.

**7. Stale comment drift** — Repaired the `ci.yml` metadata-tag comment: it claimed PRs
produce a `tucanotime:<sha>` local tag, but `docker/metadata-action` only ever emits
`ghcr.io/<owner>/<repo>:<tag>`. The comment now describes what the config actually does
(tags computed everywhere, pushed on main only).

## Verification

- **actionlint** (`rhysd/actionlint:1.7.12`, the exact version CI uses):
  `docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)":/repo -w /repo rhysd/actionlint:1.7.12 -color` → **no
  output, exit 0**.
- **`cargo fmt --all -- --check`** → clean (no Rust touched; the tree is unchanged).
- YAML parses cleanly; job set unchanged (`lint-test`, `build-image`, `actionlint`,
  `gui-test`, `secret-scan`, `supply-chain`).
- The fork guard on every job is preserved.

## Residual risk

The only non-locally-validated surface is the new `concurrency` block and the
job-level `permissions`/`if` forms — all standard, long-stable Actions schema, and all
accepted by actionlint 1.7.12. This PR is itself validated by the hardened workflow.

Closes #263

body:
## Summary
This implements `docs/admin-auth-plan.md` end to end, in one PR. `/admin` moves from the shared password to **personal Google logins for allowlisted admins**, `/queue` keeps the shared volunteer password, and the database enforces the three access levels: **admin, volunteer, client**.

It also contains the work from the still-open #115 (lint fixes) and #116 (database test harness). If this is merged with a merge commit (not squash), GitHub marks those two as merged too; otherwise close them as superseded.

All development and testing was done against a **local Supabase stack only**. Nothing has been applied to DEV or PROD. See the deployment checklist below.

### 1. Lint and tests (from #115 / #116)
- **Lint:** `npm run lint` goes from 15 errors to **0 errors and 0 warnings**. The legacy prototype is excluded, and refs and state are no longer set during render or directly in effects.
- **Database test harness:** `npm run test:db` (pgTAP in `supabase/tests/`, **103 tests**) and `npm run db:reset`, which rebuilds the **local** database from the root `supabase-*.sql` files in order. The `MIGRATIONS` list in `scripts/db-reset.mjs` is now the source of truth for migration order.

### 2. Portal split and "staff" retired
- `/queue` (Queue and Metrics) and `/admin` (Events, **Allowlist**, **Users**), each with a link to the other. Admin's "View metrics" opens `/queue?tab=metrics&event=<id>`.
- "Staff" is removed from the UI, code, docs and scripts. **The shared login moves to `volunteer@repaircafe.app`** (`VOLUNTEER_ACCOUNT_EMAIL`); see the deployment checklist.

### 3. Database: `supabase-admin-auth-migration.sql` + `supabase-admin-auth-lockdown.sql`
- **New tables:**
  - `admin_allowlist`: pending invites.
  - `app_users`: one row per admin, with a `disabled` flag and last login; only `name` is directly editable.
- **Access checks:** `is_admin()`, `is_volunteer()`, `can_access_queue()`.
- **Before User Created hook:** rejects public sign-ups not on the allowlist, with *"<email> has not been approved for admin access."*
- **Triggers on `auth.users`:** turn an allowlisted user into an admin (and use up the invite), and track last login.
- **`set_user_disabled()` / `delete_app_user()`:** admins only, and never on yourself.
- **RLS:** "signed in" alone no longer grants anything.
  - Personal data needs `can_access_queue()`.
  - Admin tables need `is_admin()`.
  - **Events can be created or updated by admins only** (lockdown).
- **Security fix:** drops the open `"Allow insert"` policy on `waiver_acceptances`, which let anyone forge waiver rows.
- **Seed:** `supabase-seed.sql` adds three default admin emails to the allowlist. The admin tables aren't truncated.

### 4. UI
- **`/admin` sign-in (`AdminLoginGate`):** Continue with Google, always showing Google's account chooser. It has messages for a volunteer session, a disabled admin, a non-admin login, or a rejected sign-in.
- **Allowlist page:** invite by email (validated and lower-cased), and remove pending invites.
- **Users page:**
  - Sortable on every column: a table on wide screens, cards with "Sort by" on phones.
  - Inline rename; disable or re-enable; delete behind a confirmation.
  - Your own row is protected.
  - Disabled users' text is greyed out, but their controls aren't.
  - Created is hidden, though still stored.
- **Shared-device protection:** an admin session can use `/queue`, but that **re-locks `/admin`** until a fresh Continue with Google. The header shows "Name (admin)", and the Logout tooltip reminds people to also sign out of Google.
- **Header and tab bar:**
  - The signed-in identity moves to its own line on phones.
  - The bottom tab bar is now navy, with a white pill for the active tab.
  - **Outline icons** replace the emoji.

## ⚠️ Deployment checklist (per environment, DEV first)
1. **Rename the shared login** `admin@repaircafe.app` to **`volunteer@repaircafe.app`**, keeping the same user and password (Studio → Authentication → Users, or `auth.admin.updateUserById`). Do it when the environment gets this code: the volunteer login fails until then, so pick a time with no event running.
2. **Run** `supabase-admin-auth-migration.sql`, then `supabase-admin-auth-lockdown.sql`, in the SQL Editor. Both are safe to re-run.
3. **Turn on the hook:** Authentication → Hooks → *Before User Created* → `public.hook_before_user_created`. (Not yet verified on the hosted plan; see the plan doc §9 for the trigger fallback.)
4. **Configure Google:**
   - Create an OAuth client (type Web) in the Repair Café Google Cloud project, with redirect URI `https://<project-ref>.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback`.
   - Enter it under Authentication → Providers → Google.
   - Make sure the consent screen's Audience allows the admins (test users, or publish the app).
5. **URL configuration:** add `<site origin>/admin` redirect URLs. For DEV, include the Vercel preview pattern.
6. **Bootstrap admins:**
   - **DEV:** re-running the seed adds the three default emails.
   - **PROD:** `insert into admin_allowlist (email) values (...)`.

   **After step 2, only admins can edit events**, so make sure at least one admin can sign in before an event needs changes.
7. **Hosted check:** confirm deleting a user from the Users page works on DEV (the plan doc §5.2 has the Edge Function fallback).

The **Vercel preview for this PR runs against DEV**, so its logins won't work until steps 1–6 are done on DEV.

## Notes
- **The repo is public:** the three default admin emails in `supabase-seed.sql` will be visible.
- **No conflicts:** a trial merge with #117 (seed refresh) and #119 (CSV export notes) produced no conflicts.

## Test plan
On the local Supabase stack:
- [x] `npm run lint` clean; `npm run build` passes; `npm run test:db`: 103 tests pass; `npm run db:reset` rebuilds cleanly.
- [x] Real Google sign-in: an allowlisted account becomes an admin and its invite is used up. A non-allowlisted account is rejected with its email named. Incognito shows the account chooser.
- [x] Allowlist: add (validation, lower-casing, "already an admin"), and remove.
- [x] Users: sort, rename (empty refused), disable and re-enable, delete, self-protection; table and phone layouts.
- [x] `/queue` then `/admin` re-lock, and re-sign-in; volunteer and disabled-admin sign-in messages.
- [x] Volunteer password login on `/queue`; the volunteer can't edit events; admins can.
- [x] Phone testing over the home network: check-in, queue and fixer pages.

The RC Linux campaign found that an overflowing JSON capacity exponent was accepted as positive infinity. Serializing that otherwise valid PanelConfig produced null, breaking the JSON round trip and finite-capacity invariant. The unbounded temperature coefficient could similarly accept negative infinity.

Reject nonfinite numbers at the PanelConfig validation boundary. Keep the campaign assertions unchanged, retain the observed synthetic input as a regression seed, and test both Python/JSON validation plus valid round trips. Finite configuration behavior is unchanged.

Validation: 42 configuration/model tests pass, including the exact saved input and infinity/NaN cases; Ruff passes and the exact project MyPy check passes all 56 source files. The next RC will rerun the real Linux campaign. The failed RC was not published, and no stable release is requested.

author: jwhite212
body:
The tag-time pages for 1.0.0. With this merged, the commit you tag `v1.0.0` says 1.0.0 is released as a signed and notarised download, and no longer says it's pre-release, untagged and source only.

**It's a draft on purpose.** Merge it only once the notarised DMG exists and you're about to tag, so `main` never claims a download that isn't there yet.

## What changes

- **README:**
  - The status badge reads "release 1.0.0" and links to the latest release.
  - The note says 1.0.0 is out as a signed, notarised download and can still be built from source.
  - Getting started explains installing the DMG before building.
  - In the roadmap, the 1.0 heading reads "released as v1.0.0" and the download item is ticked. No other box changes.
- **CHANGELOG:** `[1.0.0]` is dated **2026-10-14**, with one line saying it's the first release with a signed and notarised download. `[Unreleased]` stays empty.
- **CONTRIBUTING:** a change's changelog line goes under `[Unreleased]` again.
- **SECURITY:**
  - v1.0.0 is the latest release, and v0.1.0 was source only.
  - Fixes reach you by download or build.
  - The download gap now says it's signed, notarised and checksummed, but not reproducible.
- **SUPPORT, privacy and getting-started:** "pre-release" and "no download yet" are gone. Getting-started says how to start from the DMG.
- **releasing:** the status paragraph says v1.0.0 is released with its DMG, and the release steps no longer carry 1.0.0-only sentences.

## Before you merge

1. **Check the go/no-go bar in `docs/dev/releasing.md`:** real shifts, macOS 15.4 and 14, the human checks, and the DMG on a clean account. It's your call whether to release before it's all ticked.
2. **The date:** if you tag on a day other than 2026-10-14, change the CHANGELOG heading in this PR first.

## Then, in order

1. Merge this PR.
2. Tag the merge commit: `git tag -a v1.0.0 -m "SignalLadder 1.0.0" <merge commit> && git push origin v1.0.0`. This is an annotated tag; `v0.1.0` was a plain one, and no signing key is set up, so not `-s`. Tags `v*` are protected and can't be moved or deleted afterwards.
   - Alternatively, skip this step and let GitHub create the tag when you publish: set the draft's target to the merge commit's SHA, not `main`.
3. Run `SIGNALLADDER_IDENTITY=<hash> Scripts/release.sh` on that commit. Check the DMG on a clean account (step 5 of the releasing guide).
4. In the draft release:
   - change the tag from `1.0.0` to **`v1.0.0`**;
   - attach the DMG and its `.sha256`;
   - put the checksum and the Xcode version in the notes.
5. Publish. Immutable releases are on, so nothing can be added afterwards.

## Checked

Every internal link and anchor resolves, and 2,269 tests pass. Pages only.

body:
## Owner and cause

`PrivateEvidenceRead` owns byte acquisition, revision verification and physical-row decoding. Installed Core `012af2ffa`, `src/agent_comms/native_pi.py:691,715-724`, read the complete append into one `bytes`, retained it through `splitlines()` and `verify_snapshot()`, and therefore held the complete 173,654,666-byte session plus row copies while `NativeInputEvidenceRead` decoded it.

Live read-only census artifact: `/home/ts/wt/core-doctrine-segment/.scratch/worker-memory/census-3120903.json`. Top five by shallow reachable bytes:

1. `bytes`: 210,510,567 B
2. `str`: 38,347,162 B
3. `weakref.ReferenceType`: 17,423,040 B
4. `builtin_function_or_method`: 15,314,328 B
5. `set`: 12,520,872 B

The associated stack is `/home/ts/wt/core-doctrine-segment/.scratch/worker-memory/stack-3120903.txt`. The withdrawn live-census method and its incident are recorded in `LIVE-INJECTION-RETIRED.txt`; its scripts were deleted and will not be used again. `retainers.py` kept scanned objects only in function locals, returned, and deleted `capture`; it assigned no lock or context manager to module globals.

## Change

The removed read is the single allocation `self.stream.read(info.st_size - self.size)`, which materialized the entire session append as `appended`; the removed follow-on allocation is `appended.splitlines(keepends=True)`, which materialized references and row copies while preserving that full buffer.

`PrivateEvidenceRead._capture_append` now validates and hashes the fixed revision in 128 KiB chunks. `_decode_captured` then yields one verified physical row at a time, and the same owner performs the unchanged final full-prefix verification. There is no cache, alternate evidence reader or weaker check.

This bounds memory; it intentionally does **not** remove the full sequential verification/decode pass. `NativeInputEvidenceRead.decode_rows` still examines every physical record required to find the header and original input evidence.

## Verification

Toad main alone was also run, but produced no runtime because its frozen lock still omitted the five published dependencies; log: `build.log`. The successful composed build uses the exact dependency-owner PR #619 head without modifying it.

body:
Customers request magical solutions to their problems. A personal garden supplies plants, crushable enchanted stones, plain water and three magical liquids. Creature trials consume real doses and show simultaneous animated responses; players write their own eight-property potion ID from observations instead of receiving an automatic assay.

Adds four-round price negotiations, persisted deliveries and delayed mandatory refunds, including debt for cash shortfalls. Expensive exact-batch expert seals defeat bluff claims but never excuse genuine faults. Garden harvesting uses timing, stamina, water-funded tending, bounded offline regrowth and costly shipment-limited parcels. Warm contacts admit reluctant essences; overheating weakens magic irreversibly, while blended awakening thresholds can concentrate one enchantment independently of phase changes.

The contained workbench fits 320×568 through desktop with horizontal collections, in-flow tutorial/status messages, a wooden spoon and shaded continuous fluids. Touch mapping follows the fitted canvas. Manual IDs tolerate sub-visible settling; seals retain the exact sealed fingerprint. Save version five preserves active brews and migrates the new records. Cached mixture buffers and scalar contact weights reduce allocation overhead.

Browser acceptance passed two complete commissions through visible brewing, creature trials, manual IDs, bargaining, timed harvesting and reload, plus magical liquids and separate sandboxes. author: izworskic
body:
### Reproduction (actual production API, 2026-10-13)
- Clicking **I only have 2 hours / Best same-side viewpoints** was just setting a scoring hint. The API selected **Maid of the Mist alone**, a paid attraction instead of the promised public viewpoints.
- The family and boat quick starts returned essentially identical results, because they did not impose distinct visit-feasibility rules.
- On narrow screens the result panel was offscreen, and button presses appeared unresponsive while network data loaded.

### Fix
- Pass explicitly validated `trip_style` (`boat`, `short`, `family`, `standard`) into the deterministic itinerary engine. Two-hour scenic mode uses public viewpoints only, max two stops; safely scores two different views when both fit. Family mode starts at a public viewpoint, max three stops and one paid admission, plus a conservative walking cap. Boat mode retains the hard published-schedule feasibility gate.
- Clicks display an immediate progress message and scroll to the result panel, then visibly explain the selected visit style. Pressed-button state and accessible status text are updated.
- Do **not** invent the party's child count; preserve user-entered party sizes and ask visitors to check them before relying on fares.
- Do not let an optional map error hide an otherwise valid itinerary.
- Add actual itinerary-behavior tests on both sides of the border, not only HTML regex checks. Ran a separate live DOM simulation and checked request payloads.

Preserve existing video thumbnails, mapped stops, official-source uncertainty, person/canonical identity, URLs, and all other Niagara tools. No paid API, new pages, Redis or cron.

Organisationen får ett **beständigt huvudboksval** (`Organization.ledgerOwner`: `EVENO` standard, `FORTNOX`), skilt från Fortnox-anslutningens och kundaktiveringens status.

**Val (enda vägen):** `POST /integrations/fortnox/customer-activation/ledger-owner` — endast OWNER, i en transaktion med `FOR UPDATE` på organisationen, kräver godkänd `provaAktivering` mot aktuell anslutning och rätt `activationId`, binder databasnummer + orgnr + vem/när. Nekas om valet redan gjorts eller om det finns öppna lokala leverantörsfakturor. Ingen generell PATCH; inget byte tillbaka eller till annat företag.

**Regel vid FORTNOX** (`assertLokalHuvudbokTillaten`, första sats i skrivningens transaktion med `FOR SHARE`): fria verifikat, utgifter, leverantörsbokföring (skapa/betala/makulera/momsjustera/ångra), generell rättelse (`reverseJournalEntry`, även AI:s ångra-väg) och årsbokslut → 409 `EXTERN_HUVUDBOK`. Samma tjänster används av HTTP, AI (`executeTool`) och delegering (oförändrat `EJ_ALLOWLISTAD`).

**Oförändrat:** `createNumberedEntry` för avier, betalningar, depositioner och källbundna rättelser; månadsstängning (operativ periodspärr); kontoplan; läsningar/arkiv; kundstartens grindar.

author: joseph-cursio
body:
## What changed

There are five commits:

1. **`RuleRegistry.backgroundLoadingTask` gets `@ObservationIgnored`.** `@Observable` rewrote the stored property into a computed one, so its `nonisolated(unsafe)` applied to nothing. Both compilers warned about that, and `deinit` lacked the access the annotation was meant to give.
2. **The background-loading Task no longer holds the registry strongly.** The `[weak self]` update callback sat inside the Task, so the Task had to capture `self` strongly to pass it down (the compiler's `ImplicitStrongCapture` warning). A running load therefore kept the registry alive. The callback is now built before the Task.
3. **`ViolationListItem`:** removes an `await` before the synchronous `openInXcode(workspace:)`.
4. **`project.pbxproj`:** Xcode's re-sort of three lines. The entries are unchanged.
5. **`ExplorerApp/InfoPlist.xcstrings`:** Xcode extracted `CFBundleDisplayName` and `NSHumanReadableCopyright` from the Explorer's build settings.

## Why

Commits 1–3 fix compiler warnings, and commit 2 also fixes a real retain. Commits 4 and 5 are edits Xcode made itself, committed so they stop sitting uncommitted.

## What to scrutinise

- **Commit 2 keeps `Self.runBackgroundBatches`.** An earlier draft switched to `RuleRegistry.` on the theory that `Self` in a Task on a non-final class captures `self`. A probe on a non-final `@MainActor @Observable` class shaped like this one showed the instance is freed while the Task runs, under Swift 6.3.3 and Xcode 27's 6.4, with and without optimisation. Spelling the call `RuleRegistry.` would also trip SwiftLint's `prefer_self_in_static_references`.
- **Warnings verified on `main`:** a scratch worktree of `main`, built under both compilers, reproduces exactly the two `RuleRegistry` warnings, and this branch builds without them.

## Testing

All four suites run on this tree (results in a follow-up comment). The Explorer scheme builds, and `swiftlint` reports 0 violations repo-wide.

author: duncan-haywood
body:
Stacked on #6854. This PR adds `src/igmp/qc.py`, `tests/test_qc.py` and a short README section, and changes nothing else. `render.py`, `reels.py`, `models.py`, `editing.py`, `cli.py`, `config.py` and `STYLE_GUIDE.md` are untouched. **Importing `igmp.qc` imports nothing from `render` or `config`.** The refactored renderer imports qc lazily, so qc restates the three output constants, `frames_for` and the ebur128 parser instead of importing them; a test asserts this. The only package import is `MediaError` from `media`.

## Why

The reel critic costs a Claude call every round. Some faults are visible without any judgement. Instagram's ranking guidance says it is less likely to recommend reels that are **"muted or contain borders"**, that are low-resolution, that are mostly text, or (for new audiences) that run over 3 minutes. This module measures those things on the draft. If a draft fails, the critic call is skipped and the findings go back to the story agent as facts.

## Interface (agreed with the renderer session)

```python
problems = qc.check_plan(plan)                                   # -> list[Finding], before rendering
report = qc.check_reel(path, cfg, band=None, *, allow_silent=False, draft=False)   # -> QCReport
report.passed                 # no failed "fail" finding
report.summary_for_llm()      # head line + one bullet per failed/warned rule, with numbers
qc.findings_for_llm(problems) # the same bullets for check_plan's list ("" when clean)
```

- `cfg` can be the package `Config` or `None`. Only `cfg.ffmpeg` and `cfg.ffprobe` are read, and only if they exist. Otherwise ffmpeg is found on PATH or in Homebrew.
- `draft=True` is for the h264_videotoolbox drafts at 1x work scale, possibly at a lower bitrate. It turns `format.pix_fmt`, `format.codec` and `format.bitrate` into info. Resolution and fps still count.
- There are optional keyword-only extras: `check_plan(plan, *, kinds=...)` (asset kinds, which turn the static-photo note into a warning), and `check_reel(..., plan=, kinds=)` (which appends the plan findings to the report).

Actual `summary_for_llm()` output for a 2 s held photo with no audio track:

```
Reel QC FAILED: 5 failed, 0 warned (1080x1920, 2.00 s, 30 fps)
- FAIL audio_present: no audio stream; reels without sound are muted
- FAIL audio_silent: no sound
- FAIL hook_motion: nothing moves enough in the first second (speed 0.00 px/frame, MAD 0.02, changed 0.0%; needs speed >= 0.5 and MAD >= 1, or a cut): open on a moving video shot, a pan or a stronger push, or cut inside the first second
- FAIL frozen: no visible change 0.00-2.00 s (2.00 s): give that shot a move (zoom_from != zoom_to, or a pan) or shorten it
- FAIL duration_band: 2.0 s: under 5 s
```

A clean draft prints a single line: `Reel QC passed: 0 failed, 0 warned (1080x1920, 8.00 s, 30 fps, draft)`.

The CLI is `python -m igmp.qc <file-or-dir> [--band short|medium|long] [--allow-silent] [--draft] [--json]`. It exits 0 when everything passed, 1 when something failed, and 2 when a file could not be read.

## Rules

| rule | severity | what it checks, and why |
|---|---|---|
| `format.video/resolution/fps` | fail | A video stream exists, at 1080x1920 (720x1280 is only a warning), at 29.97-60 fps. Low resolution is down-ranked. |
| `format.pix_fmt/codec` | fail (info in a draft) | yuv420p; h264 or hevc. |
| `format.bitrate` | warn (info in a draft) | Video bitrate outside 6-25 Mb/s. |
| `audio_present`, `audio_silent` | fail | An audio stream exists and is not silent. Silent means volumedetect max_volume <= -60 dB or ebur128 integrated <= -60 LUFS. With `allow_silent=True` both become warnings with the detail "user must add an Instagram sound when posting". This covers "muted". |
| `loudness`, `true_peak` | warn | Integrated loudness within -14 +-2 LUFS; true peak <= -1 dBTP. |
| `borders` | fail | Letterbox or pillarbox bars, with the edges and thickness in px. This covers "contain borders". It is not cropdetect (see below). |
| `hook_motion` | fail | Real motion, or a hard cut, in the first second. |
| `frozen` | fail | No stretch longer than 1.5 s without visible change. |
| `duration_band` | fail | Fails outside 5-180 s, or outside `band=` when one is given. Reports short (7-15 or 20-30 s), medium (30-60 s) or long (60-180 s). |
| `loop` | info | Last frame against the first frame: MAD and a histogram distance. |
| `plan.fit_share`, `plan.fit_start` | fail | Fit-layout shots must be no more than 20% of the runtime, and none may start before 3.0 s. |
| `plan.static_photo` | warn | A fill photo shot with `zoom_from == zoom_to` and no pan. Without `kinds=` this is only info, because the plan alone cannot tell a still from a video. |

**One decode.** ffprobe gives the format facts. A single ffmpeg run then does the rest:
- **Video:** the stream is converted to 30 fps. Every frame of the first second is kept, then every 2nd frame (15 fps), which halves the scaling work. Frames are area-scaled to 270x480 grey and sent through a pipe to numpy, which measures them as they stream in.
- **Audio:** `ebur128=peak=true` and `volumedetect` run in the same command.

Temp files go only to a `tempfile` directory, and the input file is never written.

**Borders.** Each edge is read line by line from the outside in. A line belongs to a bar when all of these hold:
- it is flat along its length: std < 1.5, and no pixel more than 8 levels from the line mean (one star breaks it);
- its mean is within 0.5 of the outermost line's mean, so a gradient drifts out of the band.

The run of flat lines must end in a hard edge within 3 lines: a textured line, or a step of 3 or more levels. A clean, shallow gradient just fades out, so it fails this test. The band's level must also stay within 3 of its median across the reel. The edge counts as a border when the band is at least 2% of the dimension in at least 80% of the 2 fps samples.

**Hook.** For each frame pair in the first second the module computes:
- the MAD (mean absolute difference);
- an approximate speed, `2*MAD/(mean|d/dx|+mean|d/dy|)`. This is the linearised optical-flow magnitude, so it does not depend on content; the same push measures MAD 5.2 on a busy picture and 0.4 on a hazy one;
- the share of pixels that changed by more than 8 levels.

A MAD spike (>= 12 and >= 4x the median pair) is a cut. The first second is a hook when it has a cut, or when the speed is >= 0.5 and the change is visible: MAD >= 1, or >= 0.3% of pixels changed (this second test covers sparse content such as stars).

**Frozen.** Like freezedetect, each frame is compared with the first frame of its stretch. freezedetect's single test, -60 dB (MAD <= 0.26), fails in both directions on the analysis frames:
- x264 re-codes a still at every keyframe, a jump of 0.6-1.9 MAD, which splits frozen shots in two;
- drifting stars carry almost no mean energy, so a Ken Burns over a night sky read as frozen.

So a frame now counts as changed when either:
- its 4x4 block means differ by more than 0.6 on average, or
- inside dark blocks (mean < 48), more than 0.05% of all pixels changed by more than 8 levels.

Restricting the sparse test to dark blocks keeps a low-bitrate encoder's refinement of texture out of it. After the first second frames are read at 15 fps, so a stretch's length is a lower bound (exact at 30 fps). A still held for exactly 1.5 s never reads as longer.

## Calibration numbers

All the thresholds are named constants, and the constants block says they are starting points to tune on real reels.

**Hook speed** (approx. px/frame at 270 wide), measured on real `render_reel` output:

| clip | speed | hook? |
|---|---|---|
| still | 0.00 | no |
| default Ken Burns push 1.00->1.08 over 2 s, on photos | 0.24-0.29 | **no** |
| the same push on a starfield | 0.48 (MAD 0.3) | no |
| pan, focus x 0.3->0.7 over 3 s | 1.31 | yes |
| testsrc2 video clip | 1.75 | yes |

On synthetic clips:

| clip | speed | hook? |
|---|---|---|
| push to 1.15 over 2 s | 0.43 | no |
| pus

author: shinagawa-web
body:
Adds `hpa-reverts-manual-scale/`.

It runs Deployments with a CPU HorizontalPodAutoscaler in a kind cluster with metrics-server and no load, changes `spec.replicas` (or the HPA) in a different way for each Deployment (`kubectl scale` inside and outside the HPA range, client-side and server-side `kubectl apply`, a shorter scale-down stabilization window, a Pod that stays Pending, a raised `minReplicas`, scale-down disabled), and records each HPA sync from the kube-controller-manager log, `spec.replicas` every second, the Deployment's `managedFields` and the Events. `scripts/checks.py` checks each prediction and writes a table to the job summary.

The workflow runs `run-all.sh` on `ubuntu-24.04`, triggered by pushes to this directory. Versions are pinned in `scripts/versions.env`.

author: eyecantell
body:
TD-585 slice 3 of 4 (the ADR 2026-10-12's build 4): the attention board is read in-process through the vendored `ledgerboard.py`. No dev-cadence script runs, so a repo with a board needs no dev-cadence (design §5 *The seams*, §8).

## What changes

- `sessionorc/workorders.read_boards` parses the board with ledgerboard's `parse_board` and `item_record`. Each item's `key` (`board:<8hex>`) comes from ledgerboard's `item_key`, so the keys are unchanged.
- Origin's side is the module's own `_against_origin`. It makes one bounded fetch of the default branch (no prune, ssh in batch mode; on timeout the process group it started gets SIGTERM, then SIGKILL), then the three-way compare against the merge-base: *none*, *matches*, *behind* (origin's copy read, `source` set), *local*, *both*, or *skipped* (with `why`). The sentences use the phrases the Inbox's `ORIGIN_PHRASES` reads, and `fetch_case` and `fetch_why` sit beside `fetch_note`.
- `ref()` and `show()` (for `ao board show`) use ledgerboard's `item_key`, `ITEM_RE`, `CLOSED_ITEM_RE` and `detail_block`. These go: `READER`, `_reader` (the exec of the repo's script), `_item_key`, `_report` and `can_name`.
- This touches grinder-ao-2's files only to drop references to the reader that no longer exists:
  - `shiftlead/ui/inbox.py`: the note "the board of X is not shown: its repo carries no …" goes, and `reader_lacks` takes no script path.
  - `shiftlead/cli.py`: `ao board show`'s "has no board reader" refusal goes (two lines).
- Design §4.5 screen 6 *Boards are read against origin* is reworded to describe the host agent's own read, with a history line under §4.5. TD-585's Status is updated.

## Checks

- On the repo's real board, an independent review compared the old `nudge_user_attention.py --report --json` against `read_boards(fetch=False)`. Every item field is identical except `escalate`, which nothing in `src/` reads, and the keys are identical. The old per-board `note`, `stale`, `settings`, `sweep`, `archive` and `size` keys are gone; no consumer in `src/` reads them.
- New tests:
  - each origin case against a real bare origin;
  - the default branch: origin/HEAD, then `init.defaultBranch`, then main/master;
  - a plain read starts no process and leaves the checkout unchanged;
  - an unreadable board reports `{error}`;
  - the phrase table knows every `Origin` sentence and maps it to its case.

The review findings (a SIGKILL after a SIGTERM grace for the whole group, `init.defaultBranch`, stale wording) are fixed on this branch. `pdm run test` and `pdm run lint` pass.

Left: slice 4, the board writes (`board.py`'s regexes, `message()`, `item_line()`, `decided_line()`, the subjects) and the Inbox's regexes.

## What changes
- **No split words:** the transcript is never hyphenated; still justified, last line left; 62% of the width at 3.1% of the frame, 10 lines.

author: galaxy-ggatheca
body:
Jira: BCE-12881

## Why
- `./ethd version` ran `movan-syncnode movan-syncnode version` inside the container, but there is no `movan-syncnode` binary in the image (the chain binary is `movad`), so the command failed. Hosts worked around it by editing `ethd` by hand, which leaves the checkout with a local change that blocks a clean `git pull`.
- `mova.yml` bind-mounts `./node-data` into the container. It holds the chain data and the node keys, but it was not ignored, so `git status` always listed it and a stray `git add -A` could commit it.

## What changed
- `ethd`: the version command is `movad version`.
- `.gitignore`: ignore `/node-data/`.

## How verified
- `movad version` runs in the container; `git check-ignore` matches files under `node-data/`.
- `pre-commit run --all-files` passes.

## ENV_VERSION
No bump: no variable added or removed.

Migration 0016 created config_apply_run with scope_id,
initiated_by, and status 'pending' — but the apply sweep
(config-apply.ts:287) writes scope_kind, operator,
created_at, and status 'running'. Every canaried apply
therefore failed with 'table config_apply_run has no

config_apply_run stayed empty — so the first production
apply could never be evidenced (R-07).

SQLite cannot rename/drop columns in ALTER TABLE on
older runtimes, so 0023 creates corrected staging tables,
copies any rows (none exist — no successful apply has
landed), drops the old tables, and renames.

author: dot-agi
body:
- Linux: a blocked write in a folder strictly inside `/tmp`, such as `/tmp/build/out.o`, can now get Allow for that folder (`/tmp/build`), the same way a cache folder can. `/tmp` itself stays too broad, so a file directly in `/tmp` gets no Allow. Every existing check still applies: protected names, key files, `.git` and `.claude` folders, system folders, folders on `PATH`, deny rules, and paths taken from error text.
- Before it writes such an Allow, Sandbox Tuner follows links: the folder must really lie inside the real `/tmp`, and outside every system folder in any letter case. Otherwise the press is refused and nothing is written.
- The Allow text for a folder in `/tmp` warns that other apps keep files there.
- On macOS, `/tmp` is a link to `/private/tmp`, so a folder that a report names in `/private/tmp` gets no Allow as a temp folder. The macOS per-user temp and cache folders work as before.

Update: `claude plugin update sandbox-tuner@sandbox-tuner`, then start a new session or run `/reload-plugins`.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Allow recommendations can now include folders strictly inside `/tmp`, such as `/tmp/build`, when they contain the denied file.
  * When no cache or temporary folder applies, the suggested write-folder target falls back to the folder containing the denied file.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Files directly in `/tmp` remain ineligible for Allow recommendations. Temporary-folder checks also reject system locations and paths that overlap with the home folder.
  * Link checks now validate temporary-folder real paths; protected-file and key-file write blocks receive additional cache and temporary-folder protections.
  * Guidance now clarifies that allowing a temporary folder also grants access to folders beneath it.

author: ramereth
body:
Fix the two errors that left the last github-sync run UNSTABLE with 22 failed repos. The sync was protecting branches that had been renamed away, and it was changing merge settings on repos whose branch protection forbids them.

Ten repos (osl-hedgedoc, osl-nextcloud, test-cookbook and others) renamed `master` to `main`. GitHub still answers `GET branches/master` on those repos, returning the `main` branch with a 200. So the check for a leftover `master` always found one, and the protection `PUT` on it failed with `404 Branch not found`.

Twelve other repos (osl-ci-runner, osl-discourse, osl-gpu and others) require linear history on their default branch. While that rule is on, GitHub refuses to turn off squash and rebase merging, so the settings `PATCH` failed with a 422. The rule never restricted anything here. PRs land as merge commits, and the bot merges as an admin, which skips branch protection. The sync now turns linear history off, and it updates protection before the merge settings so the `PATCH` succeeds in the same run. Start with `ensure_branch_protection` and `protection_request` in `lib/github_sync.rb`.

- Count `master` or `main` as existing only when GitHub returns the branch under the name asked for
- Apply the same name check to the chef-repo chain branch lookup in `ChefRepoEnvironments`
- Treat required linear history as drift and set it to false in the protection `PUT`
- Update branch protection before the merge settings
- Carry forward lock, force-push, deletion, fork-sync, block-creation and conversation-resolution rules, because the full-replace `PUT` would otherwise reset them
- List the protection fields the `PUT` still drops, none of which any repo uses today
- Rescue each sync step separately, so one refused write no longer skips the rest of that repo
- Read the webhooks last, so a failed read skips only the two webhook steps
- Correct the documented schedule to every four hours, which osl-jenkins has used since July
- Cover renamed branches, linear history, the update order, the carried rules and step failures in the specs

After merging, unlock the default branch of osl-php-apps in the GitHub UI, because the sync now preserves that lock. Then run github-sync by hand rather than waiting up to four hours.

References:

- https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-branches-in-your-repository/renaming-a-branch
- https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches
- https://docs.github.com/en/rest/branches/branch-protection#update-branch-protection

author: bryclevgp
body:
Serve texts went out without an image after #2090 made it optional. Without an image a text is plain SMS, so anything past one 160-character segment splits into several messages on the constituent's phone. With an image it's an MMS, so the whole composed message (up to `SMS_COMPOSED_MAX_LENGTH`) arrives as one message. That's what we want on every Serve send, the same as Win.

The compose step's Continue is held until an image is attached on both surfaces. `ServeSmsCreateRequestSchema.imageUrl` is now required, so gp-api refuses an imageless send too, not just the UI. The webapp flow is the only caller of that route, and it always uploads the image first now.

The delivery layer's `imageUrl` stays optional. Polls share that layer and don't send images.

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Behavior change for officials who sent imageless Serve texts; enforcement is aligned across UI, schema, and create service with no auth or payment-path changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Re-requires a header image for **Serve SMS** end-to-end so every send is an **MMS** (one message up to `SMS_COMPOSED_MAX_LENGTH`) instead of multi-segment plain SMS after optional images were allowed.
> 
> **API & contracts:** `ServeSmsCreateRequestSchema.imageUrl` is required again; create persists `input.imageUrl` without defaulting to null, and HTTP tests reject creates with no image.
> 
> **Webapp:** Compose **Continue** stays disabled until an image is attached on **both** Win and Serve; Serve copy drops “(optional)”. Serve create always uploads to S3 and sends `imageUrl` (throws if missing). Tests drop the imageless Serve path and assert the new gate.
> 
> **Docs:** Feature TDD and outreach `AGENTS.md` state Serve always includes an image; shared delivery `imageUrl` remains optional for polls.

author: harisxdizdarevic
body:
Two defects found while verifying TENSOR's insight widgets in a browser.

## 1. Crossing labels collide (HAR-1553)

`crossingPoints` labelled every threshold crossing. In TENSOR's change-risk insight, a failure rate that crossed its ceiling four times drew four "Crossed …" labels, and two neighbours ("Crossed Aug 17" / "Crossed Aug 31") overlapped.

Every crossing still gets a ring. Only the **latest** one (the one a headline's "since …" names) has a visible label; earlier crossings show theirs on hover (`emphasis.label`). This is the selective-direct-label rule.

## 2. First glyph clipped in an embedded chart (HAR-1556)

Inside `InsightCard`, the chart is frameless (`padding: 0`), but it kept `.uix-chart`'s `overflow: hidden`. That cut off the ink of a leading "I" in the scatter title ("ncidents within 72 h…"). The card now clips it with `overflow: clip` plus a 4 px `overflow-clip-margin`. The glyph keeps its ink, and a chart still at its old width after a viewport change can't widen the page. A first try with `overflow: visible` let that stale chart scroll the 375 px harness by 512 px, which the a11y spec caught.

## Checks

- `chart-analytic.test.mjs`: 20 pass; the crossing test asserts label visibility `[false, true]` and the hover label.
- `insight-card-dom.test.mjs`: 8 pass. `size-report.test.mjs`: 10 pass. CSS size baseline updated (+1 declaration).
- `npm run test:api`: clean (no public API change). Guide model regenerated.

Patch changeset. It releases together with the pending ToggleRow minor (#124).

body:
Restores the Risk column on `/manage/repositories/risk`. It now shows the score added in #847 (`risk/npm/score.js`, out of 100).

## Changes

- **Server:** each scan risk line now includes `score`, taken from the assessment's `score.score`.
  - Removed versions report malware as 100, the same way `npmRiskRemoved` scores them.
- **Kept lines:** risk lines saved within the last hour (in memory or the database) predate scores. A saved line without a score is assessed again instead of being shown blank.
- **Page:** the Risk column sits between Version and Findings.
  - It shows the number, coloured by `npmRiskLevel` with the viewer's thresholds: red from 75, orange from 50, yellow from 25, otherwise plain.
  - A package flagged as malware by npm's advisories shows 100.
  - Hovering the header explains what the score means.
- **Sorting:** packages are listed highest score first, then still waiting, then failed, then score 0, then not assessed.
- **README:** the scan section now describes the score.

- **Scan:** risk lines carry the score, removed versions with malware score 100, and a kept line without a score is assessed again.
- **Page:**

  - rows are ordered by score;

author: on22s
body:
Fixes #1195.

A delayed `play()` rejection or saved media callback from a stopped sequence could advance a restarted sequence. Each sequence now owns an epoch, and Stop and advancement retire its handlers. Only callbacks from the current epoch can advance or stop playback.

Validation: 50 focused CPU tests passed, including native Node execution with deferred promises and old handler references. An independent review replayed the regression against the original code (six failing cases), passed the five new test methods and seven additional controls, and checked eight review angles. `./ready.sh` passed 7,665 unit tests with zero skips and 72 API checks; the 12 full-mode API checks were skipped by the default quick gate. No acoustic or GPU qualification is claimed.

The release gate tested base `34e04480944fd8bf957f0bc483116ee6245bef89` plus this change. The subsequently fetched upstream changes are disjoint from sequence playback; CI validates the merge integration.

author: bwsalmon
body:
scheduler/preemption: implement Idea 15 speculative early-exit gang quorum and suffix feasibility checker

Implement Idea 15 (Speculative Early-Exit Gang Quorum & Suffix Feasibility
Checker) in the gang preemption framework across Layer 1 headroom checks
and Layer 3 branch-and-bound search:
- CalculateNodePreemptibleHeadroom: Computes theoretical upper bound on
  resources available on candidate nodes considering non-preemptible workloads.
- CheckGangQuorumAndCapacityFeasibility: Evaluates cluster-wide viable node
  quorum (N_viable < minMember) and aggregate scalar capacity knapsack bounds
  (CPU, Memory, Ephemeral Storage, GPUs) immediately post-Layer 1 to fast-fail
  unviable gang preemption requests in O(1) time.
- BranchAndBoundGangSearch: Incorporates candidate quorum pre-check and
  recursive suffix quorum feasibility pruning (EnableSuffixQuorumPruning)
  to prune search branches when remaining candidate nodes/slots are strictly
  fewer than remaining gang pods.
- Unit and benchmark suites validating O(1) early-exit latency reduction
  and throughput under saturated cluster conditions with large gangs (64-512 pods).

author: vputils
body:
## What changed

- Corrects code samples and statements in the website guides that the current C header (`qar_streaming.h`), the C# binding (`qar-streaming-sharp/src`) and `CHANGELOG.md` no longer support. 18 items; each was checked against those sources before it was changed.
  - C# snippets (GUI Panels, App Volumes, Peers, Rendering Streams, API Conventions): constructors instead of object initializers for `Pose`, `GuiPanelSize`, `AppVolumeSize`, `RenderSenderOptions` and `RenderFrameView`; `using Quaternar.Qaros.Mathematics;`; `Peers.Updated` needs a running `SubscribeUpdates()`; `WithHost(host, port)`.
  - C calls: the required cancel token of `qar_peer_subscribe_updates`, `qar_gui_panels_subscribe_updates` and `qar_gui_panels_subscribe_panel_updates`; `QarOnboardHostExt.port`.
  - Statements: a GUI panel shows web content *or* the video stream of a video sender (GUI Panels, Glossary); the C header does state the OpenXR axis convention (Coordinate Systems); render targets are found in the peer list, not through the render request subscription (Rendering Streams, Onboarding and Sessions; this also fixes a dead anchor); a QAROS API app chooses its target applications itself (Source Applications); source alpha is composited only with `mixerSourceAlpha` (The Mixer); the Welcome page lists the C# API reference; a typo in a page description; the site README no longer says that no version is released.
- Adds three pages to the Developer Guide for three C++ libraries that build on the C API (their pull requests: Quaternar/qaros-ogre#2, Quaternar/qaros-qt#1 and Quaternar/qaros-ros-rviz#2): **Ogre, Qt and RViz2 on QAROS** (`ogre-qt-rviz.md`, position 10.5: what the libraries do, when to use which, how they stack, what they need), **Video in GUI panels, and Qt widgets as AR panels** (`qt-ar-panels.md`, position 7.5) and **Limits and behaviours to design around** (`sdk-limits.md`, position 11.5: points where the C header leaves a question open, each with the header lines it rests on). The Welcome page and Language Bindings link to the first. Each new page opens with a notice that the libraries were built and verified against the SDK drop of 2026-09-28 and have not been rebuilt against the later generation of 0.9.0.
- Only `docs/website/docs/**`, `docs/website/README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` change. `versioned_docs/`, `api_versioned_docs/` and everything generated are untouched.

## Changelog

- [x] Documentation changed for readers (new or restructured page, moved URL, corrected
      information): `- **Docs:** ...` entry added under `## [Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` (6 entries under `### Fixed`, 3 under `### Added`)
- [ ] C API, C# or other public surface changed: entry added in the Quaternar superproject's
      changelogs (`CHANGELOG.md` here is generated from them at each release)
- [ ] Neither (typo, wording, build, CI, tests): no entry needed

## Notes for the review

- **How it was checked.** Every changed statement against the header, the C# sources or the changelog, by reading. In addition a small script over all 43 pages (frontmatter, absolute and relative links, anchors, MDX tag balance, every `qar_*`, `QAR_*` and `Qar*` name against the header): no broken link or anchor is left (one dead anchor was fixed) and the only new unknown name is the environment variable `QAR_MIXER_SOURCE_ALPHA` (an environment variable is never in the header). I did **not** run `npm run build` (the local build needs the doxygen and DocFX steps); the `build` job of the "Docs Website" workflow is the build check; it runs when a maintainer approves the run of this fork pull request, best after reading the diff. Outside `docs/website/docs/` the pull request changes only `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/website/README.md` (no workflow, script or package file). The `deploy` job is rejected for pull requests by the protection rule of the `github-pages` environment (only `main` may deploy), so approving the run publishes nothing; the site changes only when the pull request is merged. The C# snippets were compared with the sources, not compiled.
- **Released text.** The edits are in `docs/` (the working copy). The frozen `versioned_docs/version-0.9.0` still has the old text of the pages that were not already identical (37 of the 50 files are identical to `docs/`); I did not touch it. If you want the corrections in the released text, as you did for two pages before, that is your call.
- **Questions for the maintainers** (the pages contradict each other or the changelog; not changed, only you can say which is true):
  1. Certificate renewal and silent rejoin: `operator-guide/security-model.md` (line 48) says renewal is online; `operator-guide/security-deep-dive.md` (lines 183-184, 236) says there is no online renewal and a device onboards again about once a day; `user-guide/getting-started.md` (34) and `working-in-a-session.md` (42) promise an automatic rejoin.
  2. Pairing-code format: 8 digits (`security-model.md:21`, `security-deep-dive.md:45,64`) or 8 characters from an alphabet (`user-guide/getting-started.md:19`, `glossary.md:35`, `launcher-config-reference.md:96`, `api-conventions.mdx:145`).
  3. Transport of the session traffic: "TCP 19120-19200 (Zenoh mTLS)" (`networking-and-federation.md:18`, `security-model.md:40`, `security-deep-dive.md:23,153`) against "TLS sessions (QUIC) are unchanged" in the 0.9.0 changelog.
  4. The log folder at start: "emptied when the Hub starts" (`installation.md:50`, `running-the-hub.md:71`, `launcher-config-reference.md:61`, `maintenance-and-updates.md:38`) against the changelog, which keeps the previous runs under `previous-runs\<UTC time>`.
- **The new pages.** Every statement about the C API on them was compared with the header and the C# sources; the statements about the libraries come from their READMEs and documents; the one C sample compiles (as C++) against the header. They link only the repository roots of the three libraries, and they mention the `docs/SDK_COMPATIBILITY.md` of each, so they fit best after those pull requests are merged (order: qaros-ogre, qaros-qt, qaros-ros-rviz). Observations that were made in live sessions with earlier SDK drops are worded as such.
- **Review.** The new pages went through an independent second pass that checked 55 groups of statements against the header, the C# sources, the changelog and the documents of the libraries (46 true, 8 overstated, 1 unsupported in one detail, none false); the last commit makes the overstated and unsupported statements true (defaults called defaults, the observations of the last section of the limits page no longer tied to one SDK drop). A maintainer of the site should still read them.
- **Status.** Draft. The corrections are complete and the new pages are reviewed as described above. Not written: a page on streaming an Ogre scene and one on operating the RViz2 plugin; both depend on the session set-up of 0.9.0, which the libraries do not use yet.

body:
Move the ingest handler helpers out of otlp_http.rs, otlp_grpc.rs and
remote_write.rs into three modules, with no behaviour change. Function
bodies move byte-identical; only visibility, use lines, call-site paths
and doc lines that named the old file change.

ingest_decode.rs takes the OTLP HTTP Content-Encoding dispatch, gzip
inflate and body caps from otlp_http.rs, and the Remote Write snappy
decode and its charge from remote_write.rs, with their unit tests.

ingest_admission.rs takes the HTTP admission and shed responses from
otlp_http.rs and the gRPC admission, shed and unauthenticated statuses
from otlp_grpc.rs. remote_write.rs's retry_after_seconds was
byte-identical to the moved one and is deduplicated; its
admission_rejection_response and ingest_buffer_budget_shed_response
differ (header constant, Retry-After constant, docs) and stay in place.

ingest_mode.rs takes resolve_write_mode. StrictFlushPolicy stays in
config.rs and INGEST_MODE_HEADER stays in otlp_http.rs, where an external
bench names it.

Three references that named the old location follow the code:
docs/ingest.md for the gzip charge and the snappy charge, and
