[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/stacklok/toolhive/compare/v0.52.0...v0.53.0)

##### 🚀 **Toolhive v0.53.0 is live!**

This release adds group-based upstream selection to the vMCP embedded auth server, and stops the operator from acting on `spec.permissionProfile` as a security fix. It also makes vMCP keep a backend's valid tools when one of its items can't be decoded, and makes MCPRemoteProxy report config failures correctly.

##### 🔄 Deprecations

- **`MCPServer.spec.permissionProfile`** is deprecated and the Kubernetes operator now ignores it. The field still exists in the `v1beta1` CRD so existing manifests keep applying, but it never restricted pods in Kubernetes. Use `podTemplateSpec` security contexts and `NetworkPolicy` resources instead. MCPServers that set the field get a `PermissionProfileUnsupported` Warning event. No removal version has been announced yet. (security fix, commit [d5aa374](https://redirect.github.com/stacklok/toolhive/commit/d5aa37462f06bab0c3a194cbab3b637506c2e6d7))

##### 🆕 New Features

- vMCP operators using the embedded auth server can set an upstream filter in `authserver-config.yaml`. It picks which extra upstream providers each user goes through, based on group claims from the first upstream, so users skip OAuth legs for services they have no account on. The feature is opt-in and fails closed when the group claim is missing. CRD support follows in [#​6740](https://redirect.github.com/stacklok/toolhive/issues/6740). ([#​6739](https://redirect.github.com/stacklok/toolhive/pull/6739))

##### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- The operator no longer passes `spec.permissionProfile` to the runner as a profile name or file path. Before, a crafted value could make the operator read arbitrary local files. The `configmap` profile volume is no longer mounted, and `thv export --format k8s` no longer emits the field. MCPServers that set the field may roll their proxy pods once after upgrading. ([d5aa374](https://redirect.github.com/stacklok/toolhive/commit/d5aa37462f06bab0c3a194cbab3b637506c2e6d7))
- When a referenced config fails to resolve, MCPRemoteProxy now reports `Ready=False` with a message naming the failing handler and an up-to-date `observedGeneration`. Before, it could show `Phase: Failed` while still reporting a stale `Ready=True`. ([#​6776](https://redirect.github.com/stacklok/toolhive/pull/6776))
- vMCP now skips individual `tools/list`, `resources/list`, resource-template and prompt items it cannot decode, and logs a warning naming the backend and the item. Before, one bad item hid all of that backend's capabilities. This applies to the Modern list path only; the Legacy path is tracked in [#​6814](https://redirect.github.com/stacklok/toolhive/issues/6814). ([#​6772](https://redirect.github.com/stacklok/toolhive/pull/6772))
- Tools whose top-level schema `type` is a JSON Schema type array (for example `["object","null"]`) are now kept, with the schema passed through unchanged, because toolhive-core is bumped to v0.0.52. ([#​6815](https://redirect.github.com/stacklok/toolhive/pull/6815))

author: callumbirks
body:
Enemy shields could repeatedly absorb all incoming damage: each cast refilled 35% of target max HP every 6 seconds, lasted 8 seconds, and covered six nearby enemies including bosses. The rules matched legacy; this is a deliberate balance nerf.

All shield parameters now live in `packages/data/json/tuning.json.enemyShields`:
- HP cap: **35% → 30% of recipient max HP**.
- Duration: **8 → 3.5 seconds**; caster cooldown: **6 → 12 seconds**.
- Coverage: **6 → 3 nearest eligible targets**, including self; range stays 160 plus recipient body radius.
- **12-second per-recipient reapplication cooldown**, shared across casters. Live shields cannot stack, refill or have their expiry extended. A broken/expired shield cannot immediately be replaced by another caster.
- Bosses and rift legendaries are excluded. Initial cast delay remains 1–4 seconds, now in data.
- Shield expiry now precedes behaviour early returns, fixing the inherited thief expiry bug. Older solo saves and arena stashes migrate; current saves retain exact deterministic state.

The target is **1.3–1.6× kill time**: shielders remain worth focusing, while regular enemies have an exposed interval. Existing bubbles, shield-hit numbers and support icons remain; a blue remaining-shield bar now appears above HP, including at full HP. Snapshots carry shield HP in a new enemy column. **Breaking protocol v5: deploy server and client together.**

### Before/after headless measurement
Same controlled 30 Hz fixture against base `a14661bf382afb362f3ee2e60d2a69b3f37b4eef` and this implementation. Real spawn scaling and enemy shield AI; median ordinary latest-tier target; representative neutral Tackle builds (level 3 / level 5 / evolved level 5, attack ×1.4 / ×2 / ×3). Damage delivered every 0.5 seconds; shielders stay alive and in range. These are balance fixtures, not playtest telemetry.

| Minute | Target HP | DPS | No shields | Old, one caster | New, one caster | New ratio | Old shield share of EHP | New shield share |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3 | 626 | 62 | 10.03 s | 24.03 s (2.40×) | 16.03 s | 1.60× | 58.3% | 37.5% |
| 8 | 5,599 | 180 | 31.03 s | >180 s | 45.53 s | 1.47× | ≥85.3% | 31.8% |
| 15 | 17,020 | 510 | 33.03 s | >180 s | 47.53 s | 1.44× | ≥84.4% | 30.3% |

Three staggered old casters caused **zero HP damage throughout all three 180-second trials** (shield EHP shares ≥94.7%, ≥85.3%, ≥84.4%). Three new casters give the same kill times as one. EHP = max HP + shield HP actually absorbed; censored old-trial shares are lower bounds. Old censored trials absorbed 100% of incoming damage. Other builds and burst timing can differ.

Reproduce new results with `pnpm --filter @pokesurvivor/sim shields`. Full audit, roster, scaling, methodology and results are in `docs/enemy-shields.md`.

### Validation
- `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm build`.
- 12 shield regression cases cover max-HP caps, expiry (including thieves), overlapping casters, no refill/extension, broken-shield reapplication, caster cooldown, range/coverage/boss exclusions, old-save/arena-stash migration and the 1.3–1.6× TTK goal.
- Binary and JSON full/delta snapshot round trips include shield damage and breakage; bandwidth remains below the existing 30 KB/s budget.
- Chromium renderer smoke: full and partial shields, full and partial HP, and the shielder icon; screenshot inspected, no page errors.
- The 20-minute invulnerable bot fixture now deliberately engages bosses, retaining all boss defeat/event assertions rather than depending on incidental kiting paths. Snapshot speed expectation now includes buffs/traps/weather, as its new seeded build chooses Agility.

author: dibbypeo
body:
This draft targets the rendering issues reported during Classic testing.

- Use the normal back-face culling mode for translucent placement previews. This prevents hidden cube faces from blending through the front and removes the coplanar interface face from the rendered result; crossed bush quads retain both windings.
- Append zombie and particle vertices into separate ranges of their shared VBOs across the lit and shadow passes. Reserve the total capacity before drawing starts. Previously the second pass overwrote memory referenced by the first pass's queued draw command.
- Keep chunk AABBs that touch or nearly touch a frustum plane, reducing precision-related edge popping.
- Remove the preview's custom face sorting, including the GCC 16 array-bounds warning it triggered.

The horizon-floor adjustment and global precision changes are intentionally not included: the floor change is only relevant if fighting is reproduced from below y=0, while near-plane and chunk-relative vertex changes have broader visual and performance effects that should be measured separately.

Hardware validation is still required on the original 3DS target.

author: baphomello
body:
ADR-0048 in code, and the first thing in this project that talks to a model.

`num_predict` is always set — there is no unlimited setting, because a local model without
one generates until the context fills. The budget covers reasoning as well as output, since a
budget sized for the expected code starves a thinking model before it writes anything. A turn
that ran out comes back as `Stop::BudgetSpent`, a variant the caller has to match, rather than
as a short answer the loop has to guess about.

> Stacked on #16 → #15 → #14. Base it down as those merge.

## Two tool-call shapes, both measured here

Ollama parses a tool call into `message.tool_calls` only when the model's template supports
it. On this hardware:

| Model | What came back |
|---|---|
| `ornith1.5:9b` | `tool_calls`, with arguments already parsed, plus a separate `thinking` field |
| `qwen2.5-coder:7b` | no `tool_calls` — the JSON call as plain `content` |

Both are read. A model that emits its call as text is not broken, and refusing to understand
it would rule out half the models that fit 8 GB of VRAM — which is the hardware this project
is being built on.

The text fallback only accepts a whole message that is one JSON object with `name` and
`arguments`, optionally fenced. Hunting for JSON inside prose would turn a model talking
*about* a call into a call, and `prose_about_a_call_is_not_a_call` holds that line.

## No HTTP dependency, and why

The crate carries 180 lines of HTTP/1.1. A local runtime is reached over plain HTTP on
loopback (ADR-0008), so none of what an HTTP library exists for applies: no TLS, no redirects,
no cookies, no proxy, no pooling. The alternative was `ureq`, which is a good crate and brings
a transitive tree to a project whose entire dependency set is three crates for this adapter
and a `cargo-deny` gate over all of it.

Both framings are handled rather than one: Ollama answers a non-streaming request with
`Content-Length` (measured), and llama.cpp's server does not always.

**When ADR-0009's direct provider APIs land in MVP 2 they need TLS and this stops being
enough.** That is the moment to take a real client, with the evidence of having needed it.
Flagging it here so the decision is deliberate rather than inherited.

## An unplanned finding about ADR-0060

The tool schema steers the model away from the shell:

```
command: { type: "string" }                 ->  "pwd && ls -la"
argv:    { type: "array", items: string }   ->  ["ls", "-la"]
```

Same model, same prompt, one schema change. ADR-0060's argv-only rule looked like it would
fight the models; declared properly, it does not.

## Validation

`cargo test --workspace` — **117 passing, 0 failing suites**; 13 new. `cargo fmt --all
--check` clean, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features` no warnings, `cargo
deny check` all four gates ok.

The parse fixtures are replies captured from a running Ollama, not written from the API docs.
The transport tests run against a `TcpListener` the test starts on loopback, so they are
portable across the matrix and need no Ollama.

Driven against the live server, both models, through the public interface:

```
qwen2.5-coder:7b     stop=Done  prompt=174  output=31  calls=1
    -> run({"argv":["library","test","suite","--filter","slice2_seg"]})
ornith1.5:9b         stop=Done  prompt=309  output=62  calls=1
    -> run({"argv":["ls","-la"]})
budget probe         stop=BudgetSpent { num_predict: 4 }
```

Neither produced `cargo test`, because neither was told what project it was in — that is the
contract's job (ADR-0047) and the contract is not wired yet. What is verified here is the
transport, both call shapes, the thinking split, the token counts and the budget signal.

##### Breaking changes

- **Backup history uses a new storage format.** If you plan to go back to an earlier qui after you upgrade, export the backup runs that you need first, because restore fails for every run after a downgrade. Exported archives import on any version.
- **Automation rule JSON is decoded strictly.** A create, update, import, or dry run now returns 400 for an unknown key, a key with the wrong case, or a value of the wrong type. An import with `intervalSeconds` below 60 also fails, so remove these keys from your scripts and saved JSON files.

- **Group IDs are checked on save.** When you edit a rule, the save fails if `grouping.defaultGroupId`, an action `groupId`, or a score rule names a group that does not exist, or a built-in ID with different capitals. Change the ID to an existing group in Edit as JSON.

##### Highlights

- **Automation rules that say what is wrong.** qui lists each mistake in a rule with its JSON path, so a typo no longer saves a rule that never matches.
- **Byte and speed units in your language.** Units, decimal separators, and bit rates follow the interface language, for example `1,5 Gio` in French.
- **Lighter backups.** Each backup stores only the torrents that changed, so backups write about 53x less WAL on Postgres.
- **Update guidance for every setup.** **Install update** shows on every setup, and the dialog explains why automatic installation is unavailable and gives manual steps.
- **Hardlink and cross-seed fixes.** Delete rules on `HARDLINK_SCOPE_CROSS` now delete the matching torrents, and season-less batches cross-seed against tracker names with a year.

author: martijn00
body:
Wave 4 of the blocks roadmap: a drive block (`better-supabase/blocks/drive`) built on the attachments module, with inherited grants, storage policies, revisions, a bin and CentraKit `file_node` adoption.

## What it adds

- Two SQL modules. `drive` holds the folder and file tree, grants that children inherit, shares, stars and recent items. `drive-files` turns attachments into file nodes with revisions. `drive` renders before `comments` through a new `before` field on `SqlModule`, so later migration files keep their numbers.
- Storage policies that check drive access, so a signed URL works only for a node the caller can read.
- Revisions reuse the versions module, and the bin reuses trash: a folder and its contents move to the bin and come back as one batch.
- Hook points for relations and search without importing them: `driveSubject()` returns the subject and the search title for a node.
- `driveTree()` turns the rows into the shape headless-tree and ReUI's tree expect.
- CentraKit adopts `file_node` and `file_node_grant`, with team grants checked end to end in `tests/validation-centrakit/src/drive.test.ts`.
- ADR 0025, the docs page, table rows, bundle baseline, exports snapshot and a minor changeset.

## Follow-ups

- Wire relations (#151) and search (#152) once they land on the base: `driveSubject` already carries `search.title`.
- CentraKit `file_versions`, drive-level grants and the `restricted` flag.
- Guests from outside the tenant.
- Deleting purged files from storage through a `drive.node_purged` consumer.

## Notes

- I didn't run `supabase:sync`, so there's no fixture migration. The integration test writes inside a transaction that rolls back.

author: bmackenna-g66
body:
PR-A de los ajustes que pidió Onboarding B2B el 13-10-2026. Son los cuatro que dejan **datos incorrectos**. El PR-B (contrato y mejoras) va aparte.

Solo es código de `aws/lens-api`. No toca infra, `constants.ts`, la SPA ni las rutas `/v1/analisis` y `/v1/analyses`. Se despliega con `scripts/desplegar_codigo.sh`.

## AJ-05 · No se mezclan documentos de empresas distintas
- **Antes:** un certificado con el RUT de *otra* empresa se leía entero. El representante de la otra entraba a la lista, y si el certificado no traía NIT, se tomaba el de la otra.
- **Ahora:** antes de analizar se lee el texto de cada complementario. Se toma su identidad: en el RUT de la DIAN, el NIT de la casilla 5 y la razón social de la casilla 35. Esa identidad se compara con la del principal.
- **Identidad del principal:** la devuelve la pasada de identidad, que suma `legalName` y `taxId`. El prompt es propio de la API.
- **Regla de comparación:** manda el NIT, comparado sin dígito verificador. Si falta el NIT, se compara la razón social sin tildes, signos ni sigla.
- **Si no coincide:** el complementario queda fuera de todo, sale con `ok: false` y se emite `DOCUMENT_ENTITY_MISMATCH` con su `objectKey`.
- **Si no se puede saber:** el complementario se usa como siempre.
- **Sin doble lectura:** el texto leído se reusa en `analizar`, así que no se pasa dos veces por el OCR.

## AJ-04 · Si Gemini no responde, FAILED por el servicio
- **Reintentos:** espera exponencial con jitter ante red, tiempo agotado, 429 y 5xx. Ningún intento ni espera se pasa del presupuesto de la corrida.
- **Log:** el status HTTP de Gemini queda registrado. La API key se limpia de los mensajes.
- **Corte:** si igual falla la identidad, los 18 campos, las personas o la administración, la corrida termina `FAILED` con `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (`000503`, la entrada del Anexo B). Pasa lo mismo si no queda presupuesto para esas llamadas.
- **Rutas viejas:** sin cambios. La caída se propaga solo en la corrida de Onboarding.
- **Porcentaje de EP-6:** sale con una sola forma por valor: `51`, nunca a veces `51.0`.

> **Hallazgo:** en las dos corridas de México, `legalName` sale del mismo campo («Razón Social») y el cargo de la misma pasada de personas. **No hay un camino de respaldo.** Lo que cambió fue la respuesta del modelo en la corrida en que Gemini estaba degradado (identidad cortada a los 25 s, personas en 92 s). Con este PR esa corrida termina `FAILED` y no `INCOMPLETE`. El cargo no se normaliza: el contrato lo da como texto, y Onboarding ya verificó que sale tal como figura.

## AJ-06 · La cédula sin el código DIAN pegado
- **Cuándo se corrige:** si el número del representante es un código DIAN seguido del número real, se quita el código. Por ejemplo `13` + la cédula.
- **Confirmación:** solo si el texto del RUT lo confirma: el número sin código aparece suelto y el pegado no aparece.
- **Alcance:** solo en Colombia.
- **Tipo de documento:** se completa con el código solo si el modelo no lo dio.

## S3-ERR · El error de S3 dice qué respondió
| Respuesta de S3 | Mensaje |
|---|---|
| 404 | «no existe en S3 (404)» |
| 403 | «sin permiso de lectura (403): revisar la bucket policy de … para el rol de LENS» |
| KMS | «sin permiso para descifrar (KMS)» |

El mensaje llega al `error.message` de EP-2, a los avisos y a un `log.warning`.

## Decisiones para revisar
1. **`SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` como fallo de corrida.** Ahora está en el canal 1 y en el 2. El test que exigía canales disjuntos se acotó: la regla de fondo es no confundir «el análisis sirve» con «no sirve», y en los dos canales no sirve. La entrada del canal 2 lleva el mismo código y HTTP del Anexo B.
2. **La identidad ahora se reintenta.** Antes tenía un solo intento de 25 s.
3. **Administración sin presupuesto.** Antes devolvía `null` en silencio. Ahora la corrida termina `FAILED` por el servicio.
4. **Contrato de Onboarding.** El v2 vive fuera del repo y hay que actualizarlo: §8.2 debe sumar `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` y §8.3 `DOCUMENT_ENTITY_MISMATCH`.

## Lo que no se pudo verificar acá
- **El parser del RUT no se probó contra un PDF real.** Se validó con texto sintético armado con las etiquetas reales del formulario. Los documentos de dev están en `g66-company`, y solo el rol de la Lambda puede leerlos.
- **La aceptación de las pruebas A, B y C** se verifica con una corrida en dev después del deploy.
- **Margen del diseño:** si el parser no reconoce el texto, el complementario se usa como hoy.

## Tests
714 pasan, 90 de ellos nuevos. Las empresas, NIT y cédulas de los fixtures son inventados.

Before: 世界時計の頁は無い。

After: `/globe/clock` で地球儀に乗せると、その時間帯の現在時刻（夏時間を反映・曜日・UTC との差・あなたとの時差）が出る。Shift を押している間は国ごとの時間帯の一覧（米国なら 8 つの時計を西から東へ）。モバイルは案内板の「時間帯 — 国」のスイッチとタップ。時刻は 1 分ごとに進み、地図の共通の時計（`#…/t=<UTC>`・時計の操作盤）に従う。www のデモ一覧にカードを 1 枚（The round Earth）。

時刻は「点 →（admin0 の国・NE の時間帯の面）→ IANA の名前 → ブラウザの `Intl`」で決める。夏時間の規則の表は同梱しない。NE の面は 2012 年の姿なので、時間帯が 1 つの国は国の名前が勝ち（トルコ・ベネズエラ・カザフスタンが直る）、複数の国は小さな手直しの表（ロシア 2014 の組み替え・メキシコ −7・仏の海外県など）→ NE の `tz_name1st` → 標準時の差で選ぶ。

How:
- 頁＝`apps/ortho-globe/clock.html`（器）＋`clock.js`（部品・`mountClock(map, geopbf)` → `destroy`）。`createGlobe` で起動・共有エンジン・地域の申告なし。core・globe には手を入れていない。
- 芯＝`clock-zones.js`（純な関数）＋`clock-zones.json`（IANA `zone.tab`・9.8 KB・`npm run clock:zones -w ortho-globe`）。
- データ＝NE `ne_10m_time_zones` は S3 をブラウザが直読み（R2 には何も置かない）・admin0 は地球儀と同じ名前の GeoPBF（無ければ NE の zip）。
- 段 0＝`tests/t-clock.mjs`（2026 年の冬と夏の固定時刻で 20 地点・`npm test -w ortho-globe`・root の関門に追加）と `scripts/clock-audit.mjs` → `scripts/clock-audit.md`（国 × NE の面 279 組・NE と今が食い違う組 39・手直しの表が直す組 14）。
- 26 言語（`i18n/pages/clock.json`・www の `ui.json`）・`verify-prod` に頁を追加・www のデモの門は 27 枚。

決めること（issue の 6 点）は次の既定で組んだ：URL＝`/globe/clock`・光らせる単位＝案 B（NE の面 1 枚）・国の表示＝国の輪郭と時間帯の一覧（国の中の境は描かない）・精度＝国の中で夏時間が分かれる所（アリゾナ・サスカチュワン・クイーンズランドなど）は後の段・tip＝時刻・曜日と日付・UTC との差・名前・夏時間の印・あなたとの時差・時刻の源＝最初から共通の時計。

残り：
- 共有画像 `og/clock.jpg` とサムネイル `thumbs/clock.webp` は器（SwiftShader・基図タイル無し）で撮った仮。deploy の後に手元で撮り直す（`npm run thumbs -w www -- --only=clock`）。
- 海の上（admin0 50m の海岸線の外）は issue のとおり NE の差のまま＝岸の都市（イスタンブールの海峡など）に乗せると夏時間なしの UTC±n が出る。
- `verify-prod` はこの器から本番へ出られず未実行（dev で頁・Shift・モバイルのタップを Chrome で確認）。

body:
## 배경

삭제 경로가 `resetData`(전체 초기화) 하나뿐이라, 특정 날짜 분만 잘못 올라왔을 때도 평가·피드백·업로드 이력을 통째로 비우는 수밖에 없었다. 사실상 운영 DB 에 직접 SQL 을 넣어달라고 요청해야 하는 상태였다.

## 변경

| 추가 | 위치 |
|---|---|
| `previewDeleteRange` — 삭제 전 건수(평가 + cascade 될 피드백) | `app/(app)/records/actions.ts` |
| `deleteRecordsInRange` — KST 날짜 구간 삭제 + 캐시 무효화 | `app/(app)/records/actions.ts` |
| `deleteDummyByDateRange` — 더미 모드 동일 동작 | `lib/data/dummy-store.ts` |
| `기간 삭제` 버튼(업로드 버튼 오른쪽) + 확인 모달 | `components/records/records-client.tsx` |

- 기준은 **`created_at`(평가 시각)**, 업로드 시각이 아니다. 시작일·종료일 모두 포함.
- 기존 `DateRangePicker` 재사용 — 하루만 클릭하면 그 하루.
- 건수를 삭제 **전에** 보여주고, 0건이면 삭제 버튼을 비활성화한다.
- 삭제 후 `satisfaction`·`feedback` 캐시를 무효화해 대시보드·불만족 관리까지 즉시 반영.

## 설계 판단

- **모달의 기간은 비워서 시작한다.** 목록 필터를 기본값으로 끌어오는 것도 고려했지만, 넓은 구간이 이미 선택된 채 열리면 확인 없이 누른 클릭 한 번이 대량 삭제가 된다. 되돌릴 수 없는 작업이므로 매번 직접 고르게 했다.
- **`feedback` 은 FK `on delete cascade` 로 함께 사라진다.** 팀이 입력한 사유·원인·조치·메모는 파일 재업로드로도 복구되지 않으므로, 확인 창에서 그 건수를 따로 빨간 글씨로 보여준다.
- **`upload_batches`·`upload_batch_rows` 는 남긴다.** "어떤 파일을 언제 올렸는지"는 삭제와 무관한 기록이고, 행 로그의 `satisfaction_id` 는 `on delete set null` 로 끊어진다.
- **감사 로그는 넣지 않았다.** `reset_logs` 에는 기간을 표현할 컬럼이 없고 운영 스키마는 동결 상태라 컬럼을 늘릴 수 없다. 기존 테이블에 끼워 넣으면 "데이터 초기화 이력" 화면에 전체 초기화로 잘못 표시된다. 이력이 필요하면 별도 마이그레이션으로 설계해야 한다.

## 마이그레이션

**없음.** 기존 테이블만 사용하므로 운영 스키마 변경 없이 배포할 수 있다.

## 검증

- **KST 경계 전수 검증** — 미리보기(`kstDatePart` 문자열 비교)와 실제 DELETE(timestamptz `gte`/`lt`)가 같은 행 집합을 고르는지 48,960개 시각으로 비교 → 불일치 0건. 월말·연말·윤년 구간 포함. KST `2026-10-13` 이 정확히 `[2026-10-12T15:00Z, 2026-10-13T15:00Z)` 로 매핑되는 것 확인.
- **`+09:00` 인코딩** — supabase-js 가 `+` 를 `%2B` 로 인코딩하는지 빌더 URL 로 확인. 인코딩되지 않으면 `+` 가 공백으로 디코딩돼 날짜가 9시간 밀릴 수 있는 지점이라 따로 봤다.
- `tsc --noEmit` 통과, `next build` 성공.
- 더미 모드에서 `/records` 렌더 및 버튼 배치(업로드 바로 오른쪽) 확인.

## 미검증 / 머지 전 확인 필요

- **실제 DB 의 DELETE 경로를 돌려보지 못했다.** `.env.test.local` 의 dev Supabase 가 DNS 에서 `Non-existent domain` 으로 응답한다(프로젝트 소멸 추정). dev Supabase 를 다시 만든 뒤 `npm run dev:db` 로 한 번 확인하는 것이 좋다 — 같은 이유로 dev-prod 파리티 워크플로우도 현재 끊긴 상태다.
- 브라우저 클릭 플로우(모달 조작)는 직접 눌러보지 못했다. 서버 렌더 HTML 과 빌드까지만 확인.

author: dmatov
body:
This PR builds on positronic#915 (`Step.exit`, `EpisodeEnd` and the verdict in `eval.outcome`). Review and merge
it after #915. Its diff against the #915 branch holds only this change.

## What changes

The harness gets channel groups with a visibility rule, a group start stage, an `abort` call and an episode phase
signal. These are the harness parts that a human teleoperator needs as a policy. The teleoperator device and the
policy that reads it come in a later PR. This PR has no user of the `TELEOP` group yet, and the tests use fakes.

### Channel groups

- A `ChannelGroup` (`positronic/eval`) is a set of channels beside the embodiment's own: inputs (`Observation`),
  outputs (`Command`) and an optional start call.
- The caller gives the groups to the `Harness` constructor. `wire_embodiment` connects the channels and the start
  call of each group that the harness holds.
- The harness records the inputs of every group whenever it records, also when the policy does not declare the
  group.
- A policy sees the inputs of a group, and sends on its outputs, only when it declares the group. A policy that sends
  on a group it does not declare fails its episode.
- The harness skips a `pimm.SignalError` on the inputs of a group that the policy does not declare.
- The harness constructor checks that each signal name occurs once across the embodiment and the groups. This check
  replaces the two separate name checks in the harness and in `wire_embodiment`.

### One declaration

- `Processor.channel_groups()` returns the groups that the processor needs, as a frozenset of `DeclarableGroup`. It
  is empty by default. `Sequential` combines the declarations of its parts.
- `DeclarableGroup` has one member, `TELEOP`. It has no member for the privileged signals, so no policy can declare
  them.
- The name of each channel of a declarable group starts with the group name and a dot, for example `teleop.`. The
  `ChannelGroup` constructor checks it.
- The harness refuses a rollout whose policy declares a group that the harness does not have.
- `RemotePolicy` declares nothing. It refuses a server-declared stack that declares a group. It drops the keys of
  every declarable group before the declared stack reads the observations.
- `Processor.sends_off_rig()` is true for a part that sends observations to another machine: `RemotePolicy`,
  `RoboarenaPolicy`, `LLMPolicy`, and a `Sequential` that holds one. `Sequential` flattens nested sequences, and it
  refuses a declaration beside such a part when it is built. A part before the remote policy could put the keys of a declared group under an ordinary key,
  and the key drop at the wire would not see them. The key drop stays as a second guard.

### The privileged signals are a channel group

- `Eval.privileged` holds a `ChannelGroup` with no declaration. Each channel is an `Observation` with no serializer,
  so the recording keeps the raw value.
- `Harness.privileged` and its own recording code are removed. The harness records the privileged group as it
  records any group.
- `wire_embodiment` loses its `privileged` parameter. `run_world` takes `channel_groups` in its place, and `main`
  passes `[ev.privileged]`.
- `run_world` connects the privileged group also when it does not record. The harness does not read the inputs of a
  group that the policy does not declare while it does not record.
- The `Observation` docstring says that an embodiment observation goes to the policy, and the input of a group
  only to a policy that declares the group.

### Start stages and abort

Before the policy and the time limit start, the harness runs the start stages:
1. the device ready calls;
2. the group start stage: the start call of each declared group that has one;
3. the prepare calls that the task names.

A policy that declares no group makes no start call. The harness knows no group by name.

- An `abort` call in a start stage ends the episode before the policy starts. The harness answers the call, answers
  `perform_task` with `EpisodeAborted`, and records nothing.
- At other times the harness answers `abort` with an error.
- A pimm call cannot be cancelled, so a call that has no answer when its stage ends stays:
  - A kept start call that answers before the next episode starts came too early. The harness logs the answer, at
    INFO or at ERROR for an error, and drops the call. The next group start stage then makes a new call. So a start
    press during a model trial does not start the next human trial.
  - A kept start call that answers after the episode starts belongs to that episode. The group start stage takes it
    as its own, and makes a new call only when the answer is an error.
  - The harness logs the error of a kept ready or prepare call.
- An aborted episode does not use up its trial (see Drivers).

### The episode phase

The harness emits the episode phase on `phase`, in place of `deadline_ns`. `EpisodePhase` is a closed union, so a
type checker checks each `match` on it:
- `Starting`: the start stages;
- `Running(deadline_ns)`: the policy runs. `deadline_ns` is `None` for a task with no time limit;
- `Ended`: the episode ended. The `perform_task` answer holds the end keys or the error;
- `Aborted`: an abort ended the episode in a start stage.

`deadline_ns` could not show the start of an episode with no time limit. A reader of `deadline_ns` moves to `phase`.

### Drivers

- **Station console:**
  - The page shows Starting while the harness starts the episode, and offers Abort then. It takes a verdict only
    while the policy runs. It refuses Abort while a verdict is pending.
  - An aborted episode closes as `Unrecorded.ABORTED`, and the next Start sends the same trial again.
  - When the harness refuses an abort, for example because the policy has just started, the episode stays open and
    the page shows the reason.
  - The console reads the harness phase, and it calls `abort` from its control loop.
  - While an episode is open, the configured instruction on the page is the one of that episode's trial.
- **`KeyboardOperator`:** `p` ends a pending episode whose policy runs, and aborts it before that. After an abort,
  the next `s` runs the same task again.
- **`run_world`:** it connects the `abort` caller and the `phase` receiver of a driver that has them.
- **`TaskDriver`:** it has no abort source, and it does not change.

### Breaking changes

- `wire_embodiment(privileged=…)` and `run_world(privileged=…)` are removed. Give the channel groups to the `Harness`
  constructor, or `run_world(channel_groups=…)`.
- `Eval.privileged` is a `ChannelGroup`, not a dict of emitters.
- `Harness.deadline_ns` is removed. Read `Harness.phase`.
- `StationConsole.build_app` takes an `abort` callable.

## How it was tested

- New harness tests:
  - only a policy that declares a group starts it, sees its inputs and sends on its outputs;
  - a group that the policy does not declare is recorded and kept out of the observations;
  - a policy that sends on a group it does not declare fails its episode;
  - a rollout that declares a group the harness does not have is refused;
  - the group start stage comes after the ready calls and before the prepare calls and the time limit;
  - an abort in each start stage ends the episode with `EpisodeAborted` and records nothing, and a late error of a
    kept call is logged;
  - the next group start stage takes a kept start call as its own, and calls again only after an error answer;
  - a kept start call that answers while the next episode readies its devices starts that episode with no new call;
  - a kept start call that answers during a model trial does not start the next human trial;
  - an abort during the move back after an episode is refused;
  - a `pimm.SignalError` on a group that the policy does not declare does not fail the episode;
  - an abort while no episode starts is refused;
  - the name checks of the harness and of `ChannelGroup`.
- Existing harness tests read the episode phase

author: davidecarvalho
body:
Found while running the library in production (entre-textos, a thesis editor on Tiptap + Yjs). All four were hitting a real 900 KB-content / 5 MB-state document.

## Restore left the document empty
`applyRestoredContent` cleared the `default` fragment and re-applied the version's update. When the version comes from the document's own history — the normal case — its items are already known to the live doc, and the ones the restore needs are exactly the ones deleted since. Yjs treats known items as integrated, so the update is a no-op and the restore leaves an **empty** document. The existing tests didn't catch it: they only asserted the "restored from" version, and wrote each state from a fresh `Y.Doc` (a different lineage, where re-applying does work).

Fix: copy the restored fragment as new items (`clone()`). Other root types keep the previous merge; the version's `default` items travel in that update marked deleted, so a version from another lineage can't come back next to the copies.

## `listVersions` pulled every snapshot
`LucidStorage.listVersions` had no `select`, so every listing — and every `createVersion`, which lists to compute the next `seq` — transferred all snapshots (62 MB for 46 versions in our case) and mapped them away. Now it selects only metadata.

## Unchanged documents were rewritten on every close
`beforeUnloadDocument` saves unconditionally, so a server-side reader (a sync job opening the document through a direct connection every ~2 min) rewrote the full multi-MB state each time with nothing new. The driver now keeps a sha1 of what storage holds (set in a new `afterLoadDocument` hook and after every save/restore) and skips identical writes.

## New: compaction
Yjs keeps tombstones forever; a document whose content is replaced wholesale carries every previous copy (our 5.2 MB state compacted to 0.9 MB, decode 7.7 s → 0.5 s). `compactDocument` / `node ace collaboration:compact --doc=<name> [--dry-run]` copies the `default` fragment into a fresh doc, checks it reads back identical (Tiptap JSON), keeps the old state as a `before compaction` version and saves the new one. It refuses a document that is open in the process, has anyone in presence, or has roots outside `default`. It's an optional driver capability (`CompactingDriver` / `supportsCompaction`), like `LiveDocumentDriver`. Docs: production + commands pages, with a warning about stale clients.

## Tests
- `test/yjs_versions_state.spec.ts`: restore in the same lineage (fails on main with `expected '' to be 'draft one'`), restore across lineages without duplication, compaction (content, backup version, dry run, refusal), and skip-unchanged saves.
- Full suite 234/234 (after build), Lucid integration 22/22 (Postgres testcontainer), typecheck and Biome clean.

Changeset: minor for `@adonis-agora/collaboration`.

author: denolfe
body:
X post stories now get only the linked post's text. Replies, login walls, and other users' posts no longer reach the summary.

Resolves #8

## Root Cause

X links went through Puppeteer and Readability (Mozilla's main-content extractor). A logged-out X page holds the linked post, its parent posts, and replies, each in its own `article` element. Readability picked whichever block scored highest. Often that was the reply thread or the login dialog.

On past episode links, nearly half of X stories came back as replies, a login wall, or a different user's post. Login-wall pages are long enough to pass the existing minimum-length check.

## Key Changes

- **New X post fetcher**
  - X status URLs skip the generic page fetch. The fetcher returns small HTML that the existing Readability step parses.
  - It covers both the daily pipeline and `--summarizeLink`.
- **Content sources**
  - fxtwitter is the primary source. It returns full long-form text, X Articles, and quoted posts as separate fields.
  - X's syndication endpoint (the API behind embedded posts) is the second source. Its text is complete only for short posts.
  - Puppeteer is the third source. It reads only the `article` that links to the post's own status ID.
- **Fixtures**
  - Tests use real fxtwitter and syndication responses. The X Article fixture is trimmed.

## Design Decisions

fxtwitter is a community-run, unofficial service. It is the only source tested that returns full long posts and X Articles without a login. The other sources are fallbacks for when it is down.

Syndication runs before Puppeteer. It is fast and never returns another user's post. Syndication flags long posts and articles as cut off, so only those go on to the browser.

The Puppeteer step selects the post by status link. Detecting login walls or thread pages by text would depend on copy that X changes. When every source fails, the story keeps the standard "No content found" placeholder. The episode then summarizes the story from HN comments.

## Overall Flow

```diff
 fetchStoryHtml(url)
-  fetchContentWithBrowser(url)         # x.com is a Puppeteer-first domain
-  Readability                          # often picks replies or the login dialog
+  fetchXPostHtml(url)                  # X status URLs only
+    fetchFromFxTwitter                 # ok: full text, quote, article
+    fetchFromSyndication               # ok if short post; long post or article: continue
+    fetchFromBrowser                   # only the article linking to the status ID
+    cut-off syndication text           # if the browser finds no post
+    "No content found" placeholder     # if every source fails
+  Readability                          # parses the small post HTML
```

## References / Links

- [FxEmbed (fxtwitter)](https://github.com/FxEmbed/FxEmbed): source of the `api.fxtwitter.com` status API

body:
## Public Docker image replacement with retained receiver identity

Closes #251 after final acceptance. Adds a mandatory scenario to the existing Docker-backed `./test.sh` that updates a deployed Hello server from qualified immutable image A to B through authenticated `TopologyClient` registration, planning, approval and apply. It verifies a real new container/image/business response while preserving peer and receiver identity, configuration and original history, then checks reconstructed-client replay, no-op behavior and public desired-empty teardown.

### Decision log

- Chosen shape: compose the existing Operations factory, Docker interpreter, private Secrets provider, signed Gateway/Hello health clients and public history owners. Use the fixed qualified Gateway/A/B/pause image tuple; publish no new images.
- Important boundaries: runtime calls delegate once; committed public events correlate actual effects and worker fences; the real replacement receipt joins old/new container identities. Exact fixture resource identities are recorded before dispatch and validated as a complete set before disposal.
- Why: separate fresh-container artifact qualification cannot prove continuity across an update of an existing deployment.
- Alternatives excluded: direct store/coordinator choreography, copied execution or custody state machines, label-discovered cleanup authority, and claiming production external connectivity from a fixture substitution.
- Handoff: #252 may proceed only after North accepts #251. Grandparent #225 and whole-roadmap acceptance remain separate.

### Validation

Final head `e4bcfdd8f875c2baeac163bd97fa0bcde33dd7eb`; tree `38a603b72fa6e45cbeac03c6b90467bfae34b88a`.

Required final-head [CI 38509324627](https://github.com/OpenJ92/control-plane-kit-servers/actions/runs/38509324627), job `115673946995`, passed 26 support and 594 package tests, the joined image-update/replay/no-op/public-teardown scenario, and the project-label-scoped Docker residue audit. Integrity scan: 594 tests, 133 mock evidence sites, zero approved skips. The success summary and exact disposal report both distinguish five configuration volumes from one secret volume. Whitespace validation passes; the PR is mergeable with its required check green. Final independent review and North's acceptance govern merge.

### Security, data and operational history

- Public authentication, approvals, execution claims and durable history remain with their existing owners. Failure reports contain bounded identifiers/classifications rather than raw payloads, provider messages, credentials or process logs.
- Generated connector-token custody uses the real private Secrets provider. Credentials and private keys remain in protected temporary files; registry credentials stay at host image preload. The dedicated controller has Docker socket authority; ordinary test containers and workloads do not.
- External ingress allocation, native connectivity and public routing are explicitly synthetic. This proves real Docker replacement, signed health and custody, not Cloudflare/native/public-TLS acceptance. The graph still declares named ingress.
- Public desired-empty removes managed containers/network. Separate approved fixture disposal removes exact recorded remaining configuration and secret volumes; this does not claim historical retention semantics. Unknown resources or changed ownership preserve the fixture. No broad prune, blind redispatch or automatic compensation is introduced.
- The successful behavioral run verified five configuration volumes and one secret volume removed, controller absence, and the project-label-scoped residue audit. No daemon-wide absence claim is made.
- Original grandparent tunnel, DNS and retained token remain untouched. No failed run is resumed.

## Summary

Owner-approved option 1 for the szl-forge-lab integrity display after #594. Since #594 (2026-10-06 TH10 correction, merged 2026-10-13 17:59Z), the packaged `spaces/szl-forge-lab/thesis_formula_index.json` hashes `e22ec75b…`. `run_manifest.json` still pins the July 2026 MEASURED receipt value `5dbe4405b50672d150437fdcfa941213c6ed88f07979370f91fd60d3f65a13c2`. As a result, `get_integrity()` reports DRIFT and `index.html` shows a red MISMATCH, and until now nothing on the page explained why. This PR keeps the computed state and adds the explanation.

## What changed

- `spaces/szl-forge-lab/index.html`: adds one static `panel-note` (`id="integrity-correction-note"`) directly under the integrity table. It says that `thesis_formula_index.json` was intentionally corrected on 2026-10-06, so TH10 is no longer marked GREEN; it points to `meta.corrections`, the TH10 `correction` field and #594. It also says the July 2026 run receipt is kept byte-identical as a historical record and is not re-minted, and that the MISMATCH reflects a documented post-receipt correction, not tampering. It ends with "No receipt covers the corrected bytes, and this note does not verify them." The integrity script and the MISMATCH/DRIFT logic are untouched. The note uses the page's existing `panel-note` class and adds no external assets.
- `spaces/szl-forge-lab/README.md`: adds the same explanation to the "Machine-readable evidence" section, with the full pre-correction pin.
- `spaces/szl-forge-lab/tests/test_static_contract.py`:
  - Adds `test_post_receipt_index_correction_is_explained_not_hidden`. It checks that the note sits after the integrity table and inside the same section, that the `MISMATCH` rendering is still present, and that both the note and the README contain the correction wording, including the #594 reference and the "does not verify" sentence.
  - The same test checks that the manifest receipt is still `0c0a23e2…a3c4` and that the manifest pin for the index is still `5dbe4405…`. It also checks that the packaged index (LF-normalised) differs from that pin, so the note cannot go stale silently, and that `meta.corrections` names TH10.

- It does not change DRIFT/MISMATCH. The state is still accurate, because these are not the bytes the July run recorded.

author: victorbsilva
body:
## O que muda

Salvar uma edição sem mudanças agora fecha o formulário sem escrever no Firestore, preservando carimbo e autoria. Quando há mudanças, o update envia somente os campos alterados e seus derivados, comparados com os dados da abertura do formulário. Assim, editar o endereço não sobrescreve um telefone atualizado em outro aparelho; alterações simultâneas no mesmo campo continuam sujeitas a last-write-wins.

O formulário usa a identidade do cliente para remontar ao trocar de rota, evitando enviar dados do cliente anterior para o novo. Se faltar empresa vinculada, a edição fica aberta e mostra um aviso.

Inclui testes de regressão e um teste de regra para a remoção dos opcionais com `deleteField()`, preservando `rotaId` e os campos fixos.

## Por quê

Evita escritas desnecessárias, perda de alterações em campos não editados, gravação no cliente errado e fechamento silencioso sem salvar.

## Alternativa descartada

Continuar enviando o formulário inteiro ao salvar, inclusive os campos que o dono não alterou.

## Validação

- `npm test`: passou, com 299 testes.
- `npm run lint`: passou.
- `npm run build`: passou.
- Regras: 114 testes passaram com o emulador `demo-crediario` iniciado separadamente e `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config vitest.rules.config.ts`. O script `npm run test:rules` falhou porque o processo interno não encontrou o Vitest no PATH.

## Teste manual

- Salvar sem mudanças e conferir carimbo e autoria preservados.
- Alterar campos diferentes em dois aparelhos e conferir que ambos permanecem.
- Trocar de cliente pelo histórico com o formulário aberto e conferir os dados do novo cliente.
- Conferir o aviso quando faltar empresa vinculada.
- Editar nome com acento e buscar sem acento; apagar telefone e conferir a remoção de `telefone` e `telefoneDigits`; editar offline e religar para conferir a sincronização.

  - Total sentences, finished sentences, % completion bar.

  - Filterable queue (`Pending`, `Paid`, `Rejected`, `All`).
  - Detailed view per request: Validator Name & Email, Amount (UGX), Mobile Money Network (`MTN` or `Airtel`), Phone Number, Registered Account Name, Number of Sentences.

  - **Reject**: Prompts for rejection reason (e.g. `Account name mismatch`), unlocks sentences, and returns funds to validator's available balance.
- **Tab 3: User Roles & Access Management**:
  - Live search input to filter users by name, email, or role.
  - In-table role dropdown allowing instant promotion or demotion between `validator`, `reviewer`, and `admin` via `PATCH /admin/users/{user_id}`.
  - Account status toggle allowing administrators to deactivate/reactivate user accounts.
  - Contributor metrics: validated sentence counts, total earnings, pending payouts, and paid-out totals.

---

### 2. Clinical & Linguistic Review Station (`src/pages/Review.tsx`)
- Dedicated QA station for clinical reviewers and administrators to verify medical translations before inclusion in the hospital AI model dataset.
- Real-time queue indicator showing number of sentences awaiting verification.

author: edisonmalasan
body:
Follow-up to #405. That record declined to name M13 line 5 target because the dispatched/undispatched split had not been reproduced. This closes that gap by measurement and names the target.

## The probe - and why the first two could not work

There were **three** faults, not two, and each only became visible after the previous was fixed.

1. **Confident zero** - the envelope builders take required positional arguments, so every call raised `TypeError` and a bare `except: continue` swallowed all 48.
2. **Path** - `importlib.import_module` was handed a path with a Windows separator, so every module failed to load. A path fault, not an argument fault.
3. **The substantive one** - with the path fixed, all 48 calls raised `EnvelopeError`. The builders **validate**, and synthetic arguments are exactly the refused shapes. No amount of argument synthesis can produce a valid batch.

The working probe therefore hooks `compat_legacy.LegacyBoot.execute_commands`, reads the branch out of `envelope["commands"][i][1]` - the actual batch a v0 route is about to dispatch - and drives it with the whole committed compat suite.

## Result at HEAD

| | |
|---|---|
| compat tests run | 3077, **0 errors, 0 failures** |
| distinct branches in a real batch | **39** |
| occurrences | 1074 |
| never dispatched | **24** (quoted in full in the record) |

**39 / 24 reproduced.** The probe also independently confirms *why* the earlier `40 / 23` was wrong: `buy_mana_new` is in the never-dispatched list.

`tools/route-coverage/` is **not** contradicted - it answers a different question (citation grounding, not dispatch).

## Target

**`win_daily_bonus` (primary) and `weekly_reward`, behind one `POST /v1/reward`,** replacing `/v0/reward` authority.

The section-1 withdrawal does not bar this: it was scoped to candidacy for a *client-facing* line, and its own claim limits recorded both as non-authoritative for v1. **Delivered is not authoritative** - `/v0/reward` refuses to grant while leaving the one server-computed quantity, the cursor, to be whatever the client last sent.

The cursor arithmetic and clamp are the server own, but `args[1]` is the client, and `timestampLastBonus` has **no reader anywhere**. The fixture executes the consequence rather than arguing it: an oversized next id moves the recorded cursor backwards, `4 -> 1`.

## The index base is corroborated, not guessed

Across the **10** committed save documents carrying a reward cursor: `bonusNextId` is `0` in 7 and `2` in 3; `weeklyRewardIndex` is `0` in 8, `2` in 1, `3` in 1. The branch can only store `1..5`, so a stored `0` is off the ladder and is a fresh-player seed - consistent with one-based, inconsistent with zero-based, **on corpus evidence** rather than on the guess that had to be corrected for the level curve.

## The divergence is structural

`command.py` credits nothing on either branch. A v1 route applying `DAILY_GOLD_REWARDS` would **diverge** from the oracle. So the line takes the derivable authority improvement - successor from the **stored** cursor - and does not invent the payout.

## Notes

- `docs/legacy-m13-line5-candidates.md` section 5 is **superseded, not edited**.
- Its "two instrument faults" is **corrected to three** here.
- `docs/legacy-m13-unrouted-branches.md` section 2.1 `39 / 24` is **confirmed**, not edited.
- Docs only. CRLF, zero lone LF, matching siblings. No Flash, no browser; loopback only.

author: st0newan9
body:
Two changes for a stable chain from the Bridge to the phone that uses fewer Cloudflare calls.

## Bridge relay liveness
Behind a TUN proxy the Bridge's relay socket can stay `ESTABLISHED` while the path to Cloudflare is gone: pings are never answered and the socket reports nothing, so phones could not reach the Mac until the resident was restarted. (Measured on this Mac: TLS to the relay through the proxy takes ~5.5 s every time, and `workers.dev` is reset without the proxy.)
- Pings now have a ten-second pong deadline and registration must be acknowledged within fifteen seconds; either failure closes the socket and redials.
- A late operation is ended by closing its socket, because a pending WebSocket receive may not observe task cancellation.
- Disconnecting no longer waits to send a directory withdrawal, which could hang on a dead path. The relay withdraws the entry itself when the Bridge socket closes.
- Each connection synchronizes the registry once instead of twice: one less billable message and SQLite write per dial. The listener now subscribes before the first sync, so a revocation during a dial is still delivered.

## Phone round-trips
- The host epoch is fixed per Bridge process, so the signed `/v2/identity` announcement is cached per link instead of fetched before every request. Through the relay that removes a round-trip and a Durable Object wake-up per read. The cache is dropped on reconnect and on relocation, since a relocated endpoint may be a restarted Bridge with a new epoch. The existing relocation test caught that case.

## Verification
- `swift test`: 316 tests pass, including three new `CloudRelayLivenessTests`:
  - a path that stops answering pings is redialed
  - a registration the relay never acknowledges is redialed
  - a connection synchronizes the registry exactly once
- Installed on the Mac with the hook-activity fix; the resident reconnects and the phone reconnects.

author: marthendalnunes
body:
## Summary

Fetch and pull currently download every packmap node on every call, even when all packs are already applied. Record a verified head for each remote branch and destination, stop at that immutable ancestor, and download nothing when both the listed tip and head match. Keep local closure verification and full-chain recovery.

The new cache is disposable local state. No server, wire, object, packmap, public API, or authoritative stored format changes.

## Success criteria

- [x] Persist per remote branch the last packmap head whose chain was fully applied and verified, in existing `.mkit` remote state. `checkpoint.rs` stores a checksummed head, tracking tip, pack count, and node count under `applied-packs/.heads/`; the sync README documents the complete format.
- [x] No-op fast path: if the listed branch tip equals the local remote-tracking tip and the remote packmap ref equals the recorded fully-applied packmap head, skip the chain walk and all downloads. The report shows 0 objects. Expected: 2 round trips (ListRefs + ReadRef). `incremental_pull_counts_and_rebaseline_fallback` and `an_anonymous_client_clones_pulls_and_no_ops_over_http` assert exactly those two source calls.
- [x] Incremental walk: while walking `prev` from the new head, stop as soon as a node equals the recorded fully-applied head. `walk_pack_chain_until` compares the content-addressed key before downloading it; the counting test asserts only the newly published node and pack download.
- [x] If the recorded head is NOT reached, fall back to the full walk exactly as today. The walker naturally continues to the root without restarting requests; the two-node re-baseline case checks six calls, two packs, and the correct tracking tip.
- [x] Never trust the recorded head across a remote URL or repository identity change. Keys bind length-prefixed remote, branch, repository, and origin values; `checkpoint_corruption_absence_and_identity_changes_walk_the_full_chain` checks both origin and repository changes with identical content.
- [x] Update the recorded head only after packs are applied, verified, and the tracking ref is published, under the same worktree lock. Tracking publication is durable before the atomic checkpoint write. `crash_between_tracking_publication_and_checkpoint_rewalks_safely` reconstructs the crash boundary with the old record and verifies recovery.
- [x] Cancellation, stale-listing re-reads, PackmapMissing, RemoteMissingObject retry, and verification behavior are unchanged. Existing cancellation, deleted-listing, concurrent re-baseline, missing-object recovery, source-error, and signature tests remain unchanged and pass; the shared full walker still serves push integrity checks.
- [x] CLI output and exit codes for clone, fetch, and pull are byte-identical, except that report counts reflect fewer downloads. No golden or snapshot changes. Validation below includes existing CLI transcripts and affected fetch/pull suites.
- [x] No-op pull issues exactly ListRefs + ReadRef (count the RPCs with a counting source). Both backend regressions assert the exact call sequence.
- [x] One new push downloads exactly the new node(s) and packs. The TransportSource test checks the new node's exact key, a single pack, and four total calls; the ClientSource test checks four calls against a live server.
- [x] Re-baseline or rewritten chain falls back to the full walk and stays correct. The counting re-baseline test publishes an unrelated two-node chain and checks its tracking tip.
- [x] A corrupt or missing record falls back to the full walk. Integration coverage checks both; `checkpoint_roundtrip_rejects_corruption_and_invalid_counts` also checks the checksum, count bounds, and size cap.
- [x] Crash before the record update leaves it consistent. The crash-boundary test retains the old checkpoint, then checks the missed suffix and not-yet-recorded pack followed by the two-call fast path. Signature failure also leaves checkpoint bytes and tracking tip unchanged.
- [x] A different remote URL or repository with the same branch name does not reuse the record. The identity-change regression holds object and node keys constant to catch accidental cache reuse.
- [x] Concurrent pulls under the lock. `concurrent_pulls_publish_consistent_checkpoints_under_the_lock` rendezvous both new-pack transfers before either can publish, then checks the local tip and subsequent two-call pull.
- [x] Signature verification of new commits still runs. `checkpoint_self_heals_a_missing_prefix_and_verifies_new_signatures` rejects a new unsigned commit after both no-op and incremental missing-prefix recovery, without advancing the checkpoint or tracking ref.
- [x] The RPC count model: clone, pull(1 commit), and no-op pull as a function of chain length N, before and after. See the table below and the sync README.
- [x] Both backends (TransportSource and ClientSource) are covered. The shared counting source wraps the memory-backed TransportSource plus both adapters against the same live HTTP server. The HTTP regression uses each adapter's actual destination identity.

## RPC count model

One branch, one ListRefs page, one pack per node, no retries; `N` is the chain length after the operation:

| Operation | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Clone | `2 + 2N` | `2 + 2N` |
| Pull after one appended commit | `3 + N` | `4` |
| No-op pull | `2 + N` | `2` |

For `k` appended nodes containing `p` missing packs: `2 + k + p`. A rewritten chain costs `2 + N + p`. More branches, listing pages, or recovery reads add their own calls. Local closure traversal still scales with reachable objects.

## Decisions and necessity gate

- Keep the public full walker for push-side integrity checks. Add a private stop condition for fetch rather than changing the public API or packmap format.
- Keep applied-pack records and their lifecycle unchanged; re-baselines and other branches still need pack-level deduplication.
- Bind checkpoints through the existing `repository_address` contract in both adapters. Sources without a destination identity retain full walks; the library still reads no CLI configuration.
- Keep the original `RemoteRefBatch::write` behavior, including history invalidation; flush that batch under the apply lock before publishing a checkpoint.
- Keep closure verification even on no-op pulls. Missing local objects trigger the existing recovery event and a full re-walk/re-download when a prefix was omitted. A missing delta base while unpacking an omitted-prefix suffix triggers one full walk with the current applied-pack skips, restoring the original download order without broadening stale-record recovery.
- Preserve complete-chain pack/node counts in the checkpoint for report parity and existing resource bounds: 100,000 nodes, 1,000,000 pack entries, and 64 GiB staging. No limit or deadline increases.
- Publish each checkpoint after a durable tracking write under the existing apply lock. Sources without identities and verification opt-outs retain batched tracking writes. The immutable prefix stays verified when tracking changes; the locked closure check remains authoritative. A regression reproduces a tracking change under an unchanged head (four calls before the fix, two after), and checks that a changed listed tip is still published.
- Use `.heads` because a legal remote named `heads` already owns `applied-packs/heads`. `checkpoint_directory_does_not_collide_with_a_remote_named_heads` covers both the file and directory and checks that no persist warning occurs.

## Guardrails respected

- Intentional behavior change: fewer metadata downloads. Ref bytes, pack bytes, verification, cancellation, errors, CLI text, exit codes, and report semantics are preserved. Counts still include the immutable prefix as already applied.
- No authorization, membership, denial, final guard, hook, or Outcome boundary moves. ListRefs and ReadRef remain fresh on every call; new downloads retain the same ref hints and backend authorization.

body:
A first protected Remote address can now return an exact `auth_pending` allocation receipt and attach its owner-only Basic/Digest form on the existing ticketed tab socket. The real navigation child retains activity and cleanup ownership until settlement. Replies bind the exact request/origin, Page/document/instance, attachment and hold/visibility epochs; expiry and submissions are bounded and credentials never enter replay, status, bus, logs or config. Protected Sound replacement fails closed into the existing explicit Retry.

Verified: 46 focused backend checks; a later 62-check auth/Sound run; production-host/SOCKS/ticket/socket Basic with a 22.153-second wait and unchanged 60.002-second expiry; nine native Digest/socket/navigation/attempt/stored restore/Private/hidden capture cases; WT production HUD build; 2,092 HUD unit checks plus the remaining 15 syntax asset checks under a finite fixture allowlist. Six baseline guard assertions passed and five scratch mutants failed for their intended assertions.

Measured capability limits: same-origin iframe auth reaches the exact owner form. A popup's first protected request does not install OwnerAuth; explicit owner Reload returns `auth_pending` and delivers its prompt. An established separate OOPIF target's protected request reached the fixture but delivered no owner prompt within the bounded two-second measurement. All capability probes sent zero credentials and cleaned up Chrome/pending state. These measurements do not claim universal popup/OOPIF support.

Focused actual auth HUD passed all 14 checks, including real keyboard buttons, approval/Escape priority, strict Settings detach/fresh-ticket reattachment, secret clearing and narrow layout. Earlier reconnect failures came from Python-only polling that starved Playwright routed-socket callbacks; the test now performs a side-effect-free browser round trip. Production code was unchanged.

Independent source review passed. Combined validation passed 2,179 HUD units and 3,222 HUD checks. The 137-suite backend run initially had 134 passes and three failures: two test fixtures and a Find navigation interaction; those were corrected and all 14 affected suites passed on combined head ac8bdedec0c824971d763f26a2f879f2055cbbfb, including real Chrome navigation and both auth/owner HUD suites. Source manifests stayed unchanged during that run and its memory-limited scope ended inactive with no owned processes. No installation, real-account or physical-device claim.

GitGuardian remains **FAIL** on three historical synthetic test fixtures. Its current report attributes `Basic Auth String` to `tests/v2/browser_auth_state_check.py` and `hud/src/lib/browserauth.test.ts`, both introduced in `ca987a2c50022cbddb9058bc5a3029a63583025e`, and `Username Password` to `tests/face/hud_v2_auth_check.py`, introduced in `ac97b436ddf0283620b197ba364cb68fbcf721e5`. The scanner supplies no line annotations; tracked source inspection located the prior candidates at lines 23, 7 and 70 respectively. Root and the independent auth reviewer confirmed these are contrived negative-URL/UI expectations, not owner or service credentials. Reviewed followup `ad25e561eb44460d14cafb450439bd49d2fc0a15` makes their dummy nature explicit without changing test inputs. The fresh check names only those introducing commits, not the followup. This is recorded as a known historical false positive in an advisory check; no scanner suppression, ignore, admin bypass or history rewrite was used. Actual test/review gates remain in force.

Reviewed fixture-only followups preserve synthetic inputs and bound profile navigation admission/cleanup. Their sequential affected checks passed: 9 auth-state tests, 13 auth parser units, all 14 actual auth HUD checks, and the complete 27-test profile suite. The narrow HUD fixture now waits for actual fitted pane geometry before the unchanged overflow assertion; the original combined 13/14 failure and earlier stalled profile receipt are retained. Auth production code was unchanged.

---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Introduces credential handling and CDP auth interception on the owner browser path; design is tightly bounded but mistakes could leak secrets or weaken navigation/driving gates.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **owner-only HTTP Basic/Digest (B-AUTH)** for adopted Remote Browser tabs: protected navigations can return **`loaded: false` with `auth_pending`** and a **`nav_id`** receipt while the document stays blank/prior until Chrome commits.
> 
> The backend introduces **`OwnerAuth`** (CDP `Fetch` pause/challenge handling, supervised navigation with separate 20s work vs 60s auth budgets, bounded prompts/attempts) and wires **`_goto` / history** through it. Credentials move only on the **existing ticketed tab socket** (`auth` / `auth_closed` frames); they are cleared after use and are **not** exposed via MCP, status, bus, logs, or config. **Agent driving** and remote page input are blocked while auth is active; **Sound replacement** cancels auth and keeps the explicit Retry path.

> The HUD adds a **`BrowserAuth`** form in **`RemoteView`** (no autofocus, masked password, hold/nonce/expiry behavior) and treats **`auth_pending`** on restore, load, and history as success rather than a generic navigation failure. Documentation and a large automated test matrix (synthetic CDP, real Chrome, HUD) cover the contract and measured iframe/popup/OOPIF limits.

body:
## O que falhou
CI da `main` em 0b58648 (run 38488740900): Lint e Unit + integração verdes; no E2E, **1 de 710** testes falhou:
`tests/e2e/test_eprotocolo_copia.py::test_equipe_htmx_preserva_foco_na_copia_durante_resposta`, com `wait_for_load_state("networkidle")` estourando 30 s. Todas as asserções anteriores do teste (status 200, foco na cópia, motorista desmarcado) passaram. O mesmo teste passou nos runs 65, 66 e 74.

## Causa
O teste segura a resposta do POST do motorista com `pg.route(..., times=1)` e muda o foco antes de liberá-la. A resposta liberada dispara `GET …/diarias/` e o recarregamento das folhas dos editores. Às vezes uma dessas requisições nunca termina: o banco e o servidor ficam ociosos, a requisição nunca chega ao Django, e o networkidle não acontece.

Reproduzido localmente com 12 execuções em paralelo (`-n 4`). O travamento coincide com a expiração da rota de uso único: o Playwright atualiza os padrões de interceptação no mesmo instante em que essas requisições saem.

## Correção
Só no teste: a rota fica registrada até o fim (há um único POST nessa URL no teste). Nenhum código do produto foi alterado.

## Evidência local
- Rota original (`times=1`): 2 travamentos em 96 execuções, com CPU normal e 4× mais lenta. Antes disso, outros 2 travamentos de mais de 40 s, em `diarias/` e na folha.
- Rota permanente: **0 travamentos em 192 execuções**, com CPU normal e 4× mais lenta.
- `tests/e2e/test_eprotocolo_copia.py` completo: 5 passed.

## Fora do escopo
Outros testes também usam `route(..., times=1)` (test_baixar_carga, test_cadastro_adiado, test_editor_carga, test_filtros_carga, test_resumo_versoes_documentais). Nenhum falhou no CI, então não foram alterados nesta PR.

author: mstrouss-newco
body:
## Problem (from the first real account)
- 26 "on the way": Amazon emails have no order number in the subject (or it's wrapped in invisible LRM marks), so each email was its own order; review requests and Chewy Autoship reminders counted as orders.
- Tiles said nothing about contents; no brand logos.
- AMC tickets showed as on the way.
- Amazon "Health Care" / "Vitamins" orders were saved.

## Fix
- `describe(subject)` pulls contents from subject lines (Amazon's "Shipped 1 item: Garden Supplies", quoted product names, return/refund names, Autoship). `orderTitle` prefers AI item names, then this, then order number.
- Orders without a number group by store domain + contents within 21 days.
- Strip invisible characters before parsing; `NOT_ORDER` (review requests, surveys, Autoship reminders); "arrives"/"delivery estimate" → shipping.
- `SENSITIVE_SUBJECT` drops health-related contents even from regular stores (6 existing rows blanked).
- `SKIP` adds ticketing and restaurant ordering domains so they're dropped without AI.
- `StoreTile` shows the store's logo (Google favicon service, 128px) with letter fallback; contents shown on Today.
- Rows with `kind = 'other'` (blanked) hidden everywhere.

Note: AI steps return 503 because `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` isn't set in Supabase yet, so the one-time cleanup and item reading haven't run.

author: chrspickens
body:
## Summary

Defines the v0.8 campaign playability/workflow contract for #90 under tracker #89.

- Adds versioned `docs/workspace-0.8-requirements.md` covering GM preparation → Table → player session → return-to-preparation flows, context ownership, role/permission matrix, search/deep-link contracts, offline/privacy/SSE/backup boundaries, UX recovery states, sequencing, and approval points.
- Adds proposed ADR-0018 choosing existing durable Session/context plus authorized stable-ID navigation intents; no second session authority, persisted navigation-token store, or game-specific behavior.
- Links the v0.8 requirements and ADR from the ADR index.

## Design boundaries

This is documentation/contract work only. It reuses the existing single-campaign host, pinned module registry, Workspace bricks, authorized adapters, durable Table session, SSE/cursor reconciliation, and v5 backup. It does not implement Campaign Home, search, or new session behavior; those remain child issues #91–#98.

Important decisions needing review:

1. Campaign Home is a composed view, not a new dashboard authority.
2. Deep links/search return authorized stable-ID navigation intents and generic unavailable states; they never grant access or mutate `session.activeEncounter`.
3. Existing implementation spellings `finished`/`finish` normalize to public `ended`/`endSession` at the adapter boundary.
4. No new persisted workflow/navigation records or archive format are required for v0.8.

## Verification

- `git diff --check` passed.
- `pnpm check` passed: build, 123 tests, debug smoke, campaign/System B/Table/offline/offline-storage/Lore/Maps acceptance, and full browser Maps/System B acceptance.

Closes the documentation deliverable for #90; does not close #89 or merge automatically.

## Summary
- Independently validate each TensorDEM report's protocol, requested peak-load identity, finite positive response metrics, signature presence, and ordered finite history.
- Require strictly increasing load amplitudes so campaign ordering is unambiguous.
- Fail closed and retain an explicit per-run `evidence_gate` plus error reason if report validation fails.
- Extend unit tests and the real-solver CI workflow to assert the evidence gate, requested-load identity, and signature.
- Document the validation boundary.

## Scientific boundary
This is a stronger software/evidence-integrity gate for an exploratory load-amplitude campaign. It deliberately does not infer physical correctness, experimental agreement, material calibration, or numerical convergence.

author: greenbear-labs
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"GreenHouse007"} -->
_Requested by **Alex** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01HcmHnSMQzcicovadVpDbCv?thread=cmsg_01HcmHnSMQzcicovadVpDbCv8usRjrbYaaeKoDomyPayKN)_

Before: an adventure could only be playtested by its author. Nobody else could read it.

After: a **Publish** button on the adventure shares it with a link, or submits it to the library. Readers play it at `/paths/read/{id}` with their own saved place and endings. The library at `/paths/library` (linked from the Shadow Paths home) has category shelves, and its cards show Continue and the endings found. The author can update the published copy or stop sharing it. The adventure banner shows whether the story is shared.

Readers play a copy: the author keeps writing, and readers see the changes only after "Update the published copy". Only the admin can put a story in the library. Submitted stories wait for the review queue (step 7), and their link works in the meantime.

**How**
- `published/{adventureId}` holds the story, and `published/{id}/passages/{passageId}` holds each passage's prose, choices, lines, ending and picture. Notes and map positions are never copied. The pure conversion is in `publishModel.ts` and the Firestore I/O in `src/lib/entries/publish.ts`.
- Writes go in batches, and passages that were deleted since the last publish are removed.
- The playtest player moved into a shared `Player.tsx`. `PlayPage` (playtest) and `ReadPage` (reader) are thin wrappers around it. A reader's playthrough is `plays/pub_{id}`.
- New `firestore.rules` for `published/`:
  - Readable when the story is public or unlisted, or by its owner or the admin.
  - The owner can't set `public`; an update keeps it public once the admin has set it.
  - Only the owner writes the passages.
  - **These rules need publishing in Firebase.**

**Checked**
- typecheck, lint, prettier, vitest (215), build, e2e (5).
- An emulator walk with the rules loaded: publish, read as another user at 390px with no horizontal scroll, reach the ending, the library before and after the story is made public, update, then stop sharing.
- Rules probes: the owner can't self-publish to public, another user can't write the story or its passages, and private passages are unreadable.

author: flyme8899
body: ## 问题与复现 公众号「ETF领航者」当天稿 07:31 已发，网易号列表滞后。采集窗口在 09:00 结束，健康检查记失败并发钉钉，之后不再轮询，稿子出来也补不回来。 搜狗微信搜索从这个服务器 IP 对这个号是空的，不能当可靠备份。WeRSS 需要公众号后台授权，当前没有账号，不走这条路。 另外，把 `https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/xxx` 短链直接交给 `parse_wechat_article` 会报「微信文章缺少 id」：短链路径里没有 `sn`，`__biz` / `mid` / `idx` / `sn` 要先从跳转地址或正文还原。 ## 根因 `etf_wait_seconds` 和 `_deadline` 把 pending 窗口停在 09:00。缺稿、抽取失败都在这个时刻发唯一一次告警并结束。日内每次缺稿都会打搜狗，和回补共用一天 4 次额度，空结果也会把额度在上午用完。 `wechat_article_id` 只认查询串里的 `sn` 或 `mid`。短链停在 `/s/xxx` 时这两项都没有。 ## 解决方案 - 昨天开市时，07:35–09:00 仍每 15 分钟看网易号；09:00 发「暂缺」并继续采，09:00–15:00 每 30 分钟一次。15:00 仍缺才发失败提醒。补进当天稿子后发一条不带数字的「已补采」。 - 周一这类补抓日窗口同样放到 15:00，仍然不发当日缺稿提醒。 - 日内搜狗降为 09:00 前最多 1 次、09:00 后最多 1 次，仍受一天最多 4 次、两次至少隔 20 分钟约束。回补继续共用这个额度。 - `scripts/etf_flow_backfill.py --url` 和 `POST /api/news/etf-flow/ingest` 接受 `mp.weixin.qq.com` 长链或短链。短链先补齐 `__biz`、`mid`、`idx`、`sn`，再走原来的视觉抽取和 `ingest_items`。交易日仍从标题月日得到。 ## 兼容性 入库字段、`source_id`（微信用 `sn`）、交易日口径和视觉抽取不变。告警去重文件改成 `alert-etf_flow-{soft|hard|recovered}-日期.txt`。升级当天如果早上已经用旧文件告过警，下午仍可能再发一次。这个接口不进开放 API Token 清单，只走面板登录会话。 ## 性能 只拉长 ETF领航者这一路的轮询。09:00 之后是 30 分钟一次网易号列表，不进行情热路径。搜狗请求比原来更少。 ## 验证结果 ```bash cd backend uv run pytest tests/test_etf_flow.py tests/test_news.py -q uv run ruff check app/news/etf_flow.py app/news/scheduler.py app/api/news.py tests/test_etf_flow.py git diff --check ``` `tests/test_etf_flow.py` 40 通过，加上 `tests/test_news.py` 共 72 通过。Ruff 无新问题。`git diff --check` 无输出。 ## 界面证据 没有页面改动。 ## 风险与回滚 网易号如果 15:00 之后才同步，当天自动轮询已经结束，需要用 `--url` 或接口补采。搜狗从这台机器仍可能一直是空的，日内只留两次探测。回滚本提交即恢复 09:00 截止。 不要合并，不要部署。

author: bankielewicz
body:
## What

issue-forge 0.2.0: **where a run works.** Two new fields in `.issue-forge.json` decide whether a run branches the checkout you start from or gets a git worktree of its own:

- `workspace`: `"ask"` (the default), `"worktree"` or `"here"`. A checkout is *busy* when it has uncommitted changes or isn't on the base. `here` blocks a busy checkout, `ask` offers a new worktree for one, and `worktree` always adds one from `origin/<base>`. The run reads these fields from `origin/<base>`'s copy (`git show`) before it switches or creates anything.
- `worktreeDir`: defaults to `"scratch/issue-forge"` and must be gitignored.

This repository's profile sets `"workspace": "worktree"`, so a run never switches the main folder the installed plugins load from. It also moves the LCOV file to a relative `coverage/issue-forge.lcov`, which resolves inside each run's own folder, so parallel runs don't share one coverage file.

Why: run #27 blocked at preflight because the main folder was on `issue-3-…` with uncommitted work. The only way forward was to move that shared folder onto a new branch.

## Probe P4 (in the SPEC and `gotchas.md`)

On Claude Code 2.1.296:

- **`cwd` is ignored.** `$.agent.spawn`'s `cwd` was ignored for both an unnamed agent and a named one: each ran `pwd` in the session's folder. So in a worktree run, the existing `tool.call` guard (now the pure `guardAction`) keeps the live agent in the worktree:
  - Bash commands become `cd -- '<worktree>' || exit 1` + newline + the command (the probe confirmed this works for both kinds of agent);
  - Grep and Glob paths resolve against the worktree;
  - Edit, Write and NotebookEdit outside the run's folder are refused, in every mode.
- **#27's cause.** A named agent ran as an in-process teammate, and its hand-back arrived as `session.receive` (origin `{ kind: 'peer', teammate, isVerified }`), not `prompt.submit`. Answering it with `{ consumed }` kept the main model idle, and it wasn't delivered again within 78 s. That's the evidence #27 asked for; the fix itself stays in #27.
- **tmux.** Inside tmux, a named spawn of a plugin-registered agent type is refused unless `teammateMode` is `in-process`. This is documented in the README's Limits.

## Case 1: conflicts with other pending work

This can't be known before red has written a diff. At ready, the run fetches the base and runs `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only` of the gated commit against `origin/<base>`. Any conflicting files are named in the publish question, the pane and the PR body. It never blocks.

## Commits

Red `db2e1ea` → two test fixes in their own commits (`b29cf9e`: the dirty-tree test now pins `here` and expects 0.2.0's wording; `72221eb`: the LCOV fixture follows the folder the coverage command ran in) → green `5713e95` → `35631ae` type fix → refactor `f56d8a2` → docs `3cf8381` → coverage `2306a51` → SPEC notes `db7fdde`. The SPEC change itself is `66a2923` + `141a0c5`.

## QA

- `claude plugin validate .`: passed. `claude plugin validate mods/issue-forge` and `plugins/mod-builder`: passed. Every gating hook has `.catch`.
- `claude plugin test mods/issue-forge`: **153 pass, 0 fail** (90 logic, 63 UI and behaviour), as of round 4 below; the suite passed four runs in a row after the race fix. `claude plugin test plugins/mod-builder`: 89 pass.
- `bash plugins/mod-builder/skills/build/scripts/check-archetypes.sh`: all archetypes pass.
- Typecheck (typescript 5.6): exit 0. Rounds 1–3 used a `tsconfig.check.json` copy in the scratchpad; round 4 used the mod's engine-written `.claude-plugin/types/tsconfig.json`.
- Coverage of `hooks/issue-forge-logic.ts` under the kit: **100.00% lines, 99.44% branches** (`main`: 100.00% / 99.33%). No changed line has an untaken branch.
- Smoke test: `claude -p --plugin-dir mods/issue-forge "/issue-forge status"` and `"/issue-forge demo ready"` both answer.
- Round 4, live: in a temporary repository whose profile sets `"worktreeDir": "D:tmp"`, `claude -p --plugin-dir <this branch's mods/issue-forge> "/issue-forge status"` answered `.issue-forge.json doesn't validate: - worktreeDir must be a relative path inside the repository (no .. segment)`. With `"scratch/runs"` it answered `.issue-forge.json validates`.
- Round 4, live, through the new write chain against the real store (Claude Code 2.1.299, private tmux, this branch's copy as `--plugin-dir`, the installed copy disabled):
  - In `scratch/wt-c7`, the superseded #16 pilot run was resumed, and resume answered `still blocked: issue #16 is closed.` (the blocked write). `/issue-forge stop` returned at once with `stopped #16. Its branch issue-16-…-hardc and commits are kept`. Status and the store both read `stopped`.
  - In the main folder, `/issue-forge status` on the #27 run at ready showed `merges cleanly with origin/main`, which is fix (f). `/issue-forge resume` ran the merge check, saved its result (the store was written 12 s before it was read back: `ready`, `{isClean: true}`), and asked the publish question. Esc dismissed it. Nothing was pushed: there is no `issue-27*` branch on origin and no PR.
