author: itsmunzir
body:
Closes #1031

## What

The cell context menu's "Filter by this value" now offers more than `=` / `<>`:

- numeric and date/time cells: `=`, `<>`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`
- text cells: `=`, `<>`, **contains**
- other types (uuid, boolean, enum, geometry, unknown): `=`, `<>` as before
- NULL and masked cells: `IS NULL` / `IS NOT NULL` as before; BLOB and JSON cells still get no filter entries

The entries are grouped under a single "Filter by this value" submenu so the menu doesn't grow by up to seven lines.

## How

- `src/utils/cellValueFilter.ts`
  - `CellValueFilterOperator` gains `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=` and `contains`.
  - `getCellValueFilterOperators(value, { masked, columnType })` picks the operators from the column type: `isNumericColumnType` or `getDateInputMode` for the ordering operators, `isTextColumn` for contains. Precision is stripped before the date check so `datetime(3)` and `timestamp(6) with time zone` are recognised. Geometric types are excluded because names like `POINT` / `LINESTRING` contain "int" and would otherwise match the numeric check. Contains is not offered for an empty string, since `LIKE '%%'` matches every non-NULL row.
  - `buildCellValueFilterClause` handles `contains` as `col LIKE '%value%' ESCAPE '!'`. Ordering operators go through `formatSqlValueForColumnComparison` like `=` does, so the PostgreSQL `real` cast still applies.
- `src/utils/filterBar.ts`: the LIKE escaping used by the filter panel's contains / starts with / ends with is extracted into an exported `buildLiteralLikeClause`, and both features use it. It escapes `!`, `%` and `_` with `!` (not a backslash, so MySQL's default `sql_mode` is fine), doubles backslashes on MySQL-dialect drivers, and escapes single quotes. The panel's output is unchanged.
- `src/components/ui/DataGrid.tsx`: the operator entries are now one item with a `submenu`. New label keys are in `CELL_VALUE_FILTER_LABEL_KEYS`.
- `src/components/ui/ContextMenu.tsx`: a submenu row now also opens on click (and so on Enter / Space). It also gets `type="button"`, `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`. Before, a submenu could only be opened by hovering. That was fine for "Move to group", but it would have made the filter entries harder to reach than they are today.
- Locales: `dataGrid.filterByValue`, `filterGreaterThan`, `filterGreaterOrEqual`, `filterLessThan`, `filterLessOrEqual` and `filterContains` are added in all 11 locales. They follow the format of the existing `filterEquals` strings, and contains reuses each locale's `opContains` wording.

## Testing

- `tests/utils/cellValueFilter.test.ts`: covers every new operator on PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite. It checks numeric, numeric-string and datetime values, the `real` cast with `>=`, and contains with `%`, `_`, `!`, `'` and backslashes, including the MySQL-only backslash doubling. Operator selection is tested for numeric, date/time (with and without precision), text, empty strings, other or unknown types, geometry, NULL and masked cells.
- `tests/components/ui/DataGrid.test.tsx`: the existing filter-by-value tests now open the submenu first. New tests cover the comparison entries on an integer cell and contains on a varchar cell. The hidden cases (BLOB, JSON, insertion rows, query results) now check that the whole submenu is absent.
- `tests/components/ui/ContextMenu.test.tsx`: a submenu opens on click and exposes `aria-expanded`.
- `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm lint`: clean. `pnpm typecheck` runs `tsc --noEmit` against the root `tsconfig.json`, which has `files: []`, so I also ran `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit`. That was clean too.
- `pnpm vitest run --testTimeout=30000`: 362 files, 5881 tests, all passing. With the default 5 s timeout, a few unrelated UI suites (ThemeManager, NewConnectionModal, PluginsTab, K8sConnectionsModal) timed out on my heavily loaded machine. They failed the same way on an unmodified main and pass with the longer timeout.

I have not clicked through this in the desktop app against a live database. I'd appreciate a quick manual check of the submenu placement and of contains on a MySQL table.

## AI assistance disclosure

I made this change with help from Claude Code: it drafted the code and tests and ran the checks above, and the diff was reviewed before this PR was opened. I haven't clicked through it in the desktop app yet, so a visual check of the submenu is welcome.

author: adamforrester
body:
## Summary

Closes #2457. Adds the flush icon button: an icon-only button made to be nested, such as a counter's minus and plus or a card's close. It comes in three color families and two shapes.

- **Shapes.** `flush` has no padding, no fill and no border (Q283.3 A on #2427). `round` is a circle with a light edge and a hover fill (Q287 A).
- **Families (Q295.2 B).** These follow IconButton's own pattern (#1225), where the family is the component, not an axis. One factory, `makeFlushIconButton`, makes three defs:
  - `flush-icon-button`: FlushIconButton, **primary** (the bare id is primary, as for IconButton);
  - `flush-icon-button-destructive`: FlushIconButton.Destructive;
  - `flush-icon-button-neutral`: FlushIconButton.Neutral, the build this PR started with.
- The three IconButton sets are unchanged.

## The change (current)

- **Axes, per family:** `shape` [flush, round] × `size` [small, medium, large] × `state` [rest, hover, pressed, focus-visible, disabled] = **30 members**, so **90 in all**. `variantAxes` is `[shape, size]`. There is no `appearance` axis.
- **The flush box is the glyph.** `size.{size}.flush` → `icon.size.sm` / `sm` / `md` = 20 / 20 / 24px (Q283.13 A). No padding is bound, and it paints nothing at any state.
- **The round box is the Counter's height:** 36 / 44 / 56 (`size.sm` / `md` / `lg.height`), at `radius.round`. The glyph inside stays 20 / 20 / 24.
- **Paint, per family:** IconButton's ghost roles.
  - **Glyph:** `color.interactive.<family>.icon.{rest,hover,pressed}` on both shapes, and `color.disabled.icon` at disabled.
  - **Round wash:** `color.interactive.<family>.overlay.{hover,pressed}`.
  - **Round edge:** the decorative `color.border.secondary` on all three families, and `color.disabled.border` at disabled. The glyph carries the family color. **Decided, Q305.1 A (2026-10-14)**, and recorded in `notes.evolution`.
  - No new token, so CONTRACT is unchanged.
- **Hit area:** at least 44×44 in code at every size, and not drawn in Figma. It is stated in `codeOnly` and in the shipped `docs.do`. `lint-hit-target` `CODE_SIDE_TARGETS` lists all three families, and measures the round circle against the 44px floor at medium and large.
- **Spacing (Q296 A):** the usage text says center to center: "Space two flush icon buttons at least 44px apart, center to center, so their tap areas don't overlap."
- **Reactions** derive from member names (#2574): 30 members, 12 sources and 18 reactions per family.
- **Page:** `↳ Flush Icon Button` under Subcomponents. All three sets sit on it, as IconButton's three share theirs. Canvas furniture is on, and the three sets clear each other's labels.
- **Executor unchanged:** `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays at main's number.
- **Artifact count:** **197**, in `verify.ts` and `ci.yml` together, on the tree merged with main at `764513fc`. Main emits 194, and this PR adds three docs pages. Regen also adds the three defs to main's `docs/public/reports/*` (#2651).
- **Other counts,** recorded at `ba094cb1` (which includes Segmented control, #2418): 36 furniture sets, 38 defs in `used-by.ts`, and 15 defs in the reaction map. The component-surface, paint-census (51 per family) and axis baselines are accepted.

*Superseded:* the earlier pushes built neutral only, with the bare id as neutral, then 15 members, then 30. The progress fragment keeps that record, marked superseded.

### Nesting

`test-roundtrip.ts` builds a fixture host, never registered, that nests `flush-icon-button-neutral` twice, both `nest-exposed` with `expose: ['state']`. The neutral family is the one the Counter will nest. Both instances are exposed in every member and read back with no divergence. A real host is not measured.

### Gates, with expected values independent of the def (docs/34)

- **`test.ts` `#2457`, per family,** with literal ink and wash paths for each: 30 members, the shape axis, no padding, the glyph and flush-box rungs, flush unpainted, the family's ink walk on both shapes, the round box, the decorative edge, and the family's wash at hover and pressed only.
- **`test.ts` glyph contrast:** each family's glyph ink at rest, hover and pressed clears 3:1 against the page in every example brand × mode, measured by `resolveAllModes`. The glyph identifies the control.
- **`test.ts` factory guard,** repeating #1225's:
  - shared fields are byte-identical, and non-color tokens are identical;
  - each def binds only its own family, 8 bindings;
  - each names its own IconButton;
  - the trigger keywords differ, and the confirmation rule is on destructive only;
  - the Q296 sentence appears literally in all three.

Each mutation ran on a committed tree and was restored with `git reset --hard`.

| Mutation | Fails, by name |
|---|---|
| Destructive drops its round wash at hover | `test.ts` `#2457 flush-icon-button-destructive's round shape fills with the destructive overlay at hover and pressed, and at no other state` and `… carries its full interactive.destructive skin — 8 bindings (got 7)` |
| Destructive's ink swapped to neutral | `test.ts` `#2457 flush-icon-button-destructive's glyph walks the destructive ghost ink …`, `… binds ONLY interactive.destructive (stray: flush.icon)` |
| Flush gains a fill | `test.ts` `#2457 … flush box paints nothing at any state` |
| Padding not zero | `test.ts` `#2457 … binds no padding at any member` |
| Round loses its edge | `test.ts` `#2457 … round shape keeps its decorative edge at every state` |
| The hit-area sentence deleted from `docs.do` / `codeOnly` | `lint-hit-target` `… the shipped docs.do does not tell the implementer to extend the hit area` / `… no codeOnly entry states the code-side hit area` |
| `atFloor.sizes` narrowed to `['large']` | `lint-hit-target` `flush-icon-button atFloor.sizes is [large], but the round circle is held to the 44px floor …` |
| The fixture's `state` unexposed | `test-roundtrip` `#2457 two-nest: both flush icon buttons … marked exposed` |
| The Q305.1 `evolution` line removed, not regenerated | `regen --check` `changed  packages/engine/schema/component-maintainer.json` |

### Owner items

- **Resolved (Q295, 2026-10-14):** the name (A), primary and destructive alongside neutral (B), small's hit area at 44×44 (A), size order (A), `shape: flush | round` (A), round at 36 / 44 / 56 (A), the glyph at 20 / 20 / 24 (A), the roles as built (A), and the wording (A). Q296 A: the spacing is center to center.
- **Resolved (Q305.1 A, 2026-10-14):** the round edge stays decorative on all three families; the glyph carries the family color.

- [x] Progress fragment: `docs/progress/pending/components-2457-flush-icon-button.md`
- [x] Engine bump: `packages/engine/changes/components-2457-flush-icon-button.md` declaring `engine: minor`

## Gates

- [x] `npm run verify` → `79/79 gates reached a verdict in 4270s — 79 PASS · 0 FAIL · 0 SKIP · 0 ADVISORY` at `0f03ff0b`, on the tree merged with `origin/main` at `764513fc`, after a fresh `npm ci`

What it adds over the current `main` (the v1.1 lossless audio merge):

- 3.2: offline downloads (including NTFS USB), Quick Connect, chapters, Wake-on-LAN, Live TV, favourites, Dolby Digital passthrough, 24 Hz output, and proper locks for HTTP/HTTPS and the jitter buffer

Their release package for this commit (`release/JellyFin-PS3.pkg`, sha256 `2838f5ea…`, same as the GitHub release) was installed on our PS3 (4.84 CEX, Cobra 8.1) and runs.

### Not included
The five fixes cherry-picked onto the 3.1 merge (vblank backlog drain, VDEC arena reuse, AVC display-order reorder, search "No results", music receive buffer) stay on `merge/lossless-3.1`. The package built from that branch with our local toolchain (PPU GCC 13.2) froze the console a few seconds into the Home screen. It froze with the RSX card/text paths on and with them off. It isn't yet known whether the toolchain or the fixes cause it, so they should come back in a separate PR once that's bisected.

author: alniser0592314333-commits
body:
## Problem
The UUID delivery fix migration is present in `main` but is not recorded in the production Supabase migration history. The live commit-order migration renamed `execute_canonical_sync_command` to `execute_canonical_sync_command_unlocked`, while the old migration only resolves the pre-rename function signature. If Supabase later attempts to apply the pending migration on this production state, it can fail before it reaches its idempotent expression check.

## Change
- Prefer the unlocked implementation function when it exists.
- Fall back to the original dispatcher on environments that have not applied the wrapper/implementation split.
- Keep the same fail-closed checks: patch only exactly one old expression, accept an already-correct expression as a no-op, and raise if the function or expected expression cannot be safely identified.
- Do not modify the public lock wrapper or business data.

## Safety / validation
- This is a migration-file compatibility fix only; it has not been applied to production.
- Production was read-only during this work. The live unlocked function was separately inspected and already contains the corrected `array_agg(id ORDER BY id)` expression with no `MIN(id)`.
- Please require CI to validate SQL/migration contracts before merge. The independent security issue involving six RLS-disabled tables remains separate and is not changed by this PR.

body:
Ticket FORMA-011 (release A1). **Merge right after getforma-dev/forma#7 ("Release A1: forma-ir 0.2.1 and forma-server 0.2.1"), then re-run this PR's CI.**

## Why

`e2e/ssr/build.sh` (FORMA-001's SSR lane) builds the renderer with `cargo run --locked`, and `e2e/ssr/render/Cargo.lock` records forma-ir and forma-server, path dependencies on the forma checkout, at 0.2.0. CI checks out forma's `main`. When forma's release PR merges, `main` reads 0.2.1 and cargo refuses the lock. Reproduced locally with the link pointed at forma's release branch:

```
$ cargo tree --locked --manifest-path e2e/ssr/render/Cargo.toml --depth 1
error: cannot update the lock file …/e2e/ssr/render/Cargo.lock because --locked was passed to prevent this
```

## What changed

Only the two version lines in `e2e/ssr/render/Cargo.lock` (0.2.0 -> 0.2.1), written by cargo itself (`cargo tree --offline` without `--locked`, the link on forma's release branch). No dependency moved.

## CI expectation

Until forma's release PR merges, this PR's `e2e` job fails the same way in reverse (forma `main` still reads 0.2.0). Every other job is unaffected. After the merge, re-run it: the lane passed locally against forma's release branch (packed-set record on the ticket).

author: pryancito
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Pryancito"} -->
_Requested by **Moebius** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Y199qK4uzzNuVdKMLSWKid?thread=cmsg_01Y199qK4uzzNuVdKMLSWKidUJQ6Ejxuv6SK5P8N7kR46k)_

Before: btrfs (`vendor/btrfs-rs`) was the only on-disk root filesystem the kernel could mount. EclipseFS existed only in eclipse-old as `eclipsefs-lib`: an in-memory image builder that could not be modified in place, capped at 16 extents per file and 4096 blocks under `no_std`.

After: `vendor/eclipsefs-rs` (crate `eclipsefs` 0.4.0) is a read/write, `no_std` + `alloc` block-device filesystem.
- **Same API as `btrfs`:** `BlockDevice`, `FileDevice`, `EclipseFS::mount`, `mkfs::format(&MkfsOptions)`, `Error`, `FileKind`, `InodeStat`, `DirEntry`, `FsStat`, and every method the kernel and `xtask` call.
- **Copy-on-write:** new filesystems are copy-on-write (format v0.4). After a power loss you see the old state or the new one, file contents included.
- **Checksums:** every data block has a checksum, and `scrub()` verifies the whole device.
- **Subvolumes:** it has subvolumes, read-write and read-only snapshots, reflinks and dedupe.
- **Attributes:** extended attributes and POSIX ACLs, chattr flags (immutable, append-only, no-COW) and fallocate.
- **Compression:** zlib, LZ4 and zstd, per mount, per file or per directory.
- **send/receive and quotas:** snapshots can be sent to another filesystem in full or as increments, and each subvolume can have a size limit.
- **Several devices:** DUP and RAID profiles, copies that repair each other, and devices added, removed or replaced while mounted.
- **Encryption:** per-directory encryption compatible with Linux fscrypt v2 policies, so `fscrypt` and `fscryptctl` work on it.
- **Kernel:** the kernel mounts it with `mount -t eclipsefs`, and the root probe falls back to it when a disk is not btrfs. The btrfs ioctls, xattr syscalls, fallocate and reflink copies work on it.
- **Installer:** `make iso ROOTFS_FS=eclipsefs` installs EclipseFS instead of btrfs. **btrfs stays the default.**

## Phase 1: copy-on-write format v0.4
- **Trees:** B+ trees keyed by `(objectid, type, offset)` as in btrfs, with 4 KiB nodes checksummed with CRC32C (`btree.rs`).
- **Reference counts:** lazy, Rodeh style (`space.rs`).
- **Writes:** data and metadata always go to new blocks (`cow.rs`). Commits are atomic: nodes are written, then the superblock and bitmaps go through the journal.
- **Small files:** files up to 1 KiB live inline in the tree.
- **Full disk:** a metadata reserve means a full disk returns ENOSPC without leaving a tree half updated.
- **v0.3 images still mount** with their own driver (`v3.rs`), and the kernel probe accepts both versions.

## Phase 2: data checksums and scrub
- **Checksum tree (7):** holds the CRC32C of every data block. Every read is verified, and a damaged block returns EIO.
- **`scrub()`:** reads every node and data block from disk and reports the damaged ones; on volumes with copies it also repairs them (phase 7).
- **`check()`:** requires a checksum for every data block in use.
- **CRC32C speed:** uses the SSE4.2 `crc32` instruction on x86_64, through inline assembly so the crate also builds for the soft-float kernel target.

## Phase 3: subvolumes, snapshots, reflinks and dedupe
- **Subvolumes:** each subvolume is its own tree with its own inode numbers, shown as a directory.
  - The root tree keeps a `ROOT_BACKREF` with its name.
  - API inode numbers are handles: `id << 40 | ino`, or plain `ino` in subvolume 5, so existing numbers do not change.
- **Snapshots:** `snapshot(src, dir, name, read_only)` shares the source's root node, so it costs a few nodes, and each side copies only what changes.
  - Nested subvolumes are left out, as on btrfs.
  - Writes to a read-only snapshot fail.
- **Managing subvolumes:** `create_subvolume`, `delete_subvolume`, `list_subvolumes`, `set_subvolume_read_only` and `set_default_subvolume`.
  - Deleting a subvolume releases its whole tree.
  - `rmdir` removes a subvolume only when it is empty.
  - Links and renames cannot cross subvolumes, as on btrfs.
- **`clone_range` (FICLONERANGE):** works across subvolumes.
- **`dedupe_range` (FIDEDUPERANGE):** shares blocks only if the bytes match.
- **Bug fixed:** deleting a file in a tree shared with a snapshot now copies the leaf before releasing its extents.
- **fsck:** checks every subvolume, and checks that entries and backrefs agree.

## Phase 4: xattrs, ACLs, inode flags and fallocate
- **Extended attributes:** `get_xattr`, `set_xattr` (with `XATTR_CREATE` / `XATTR_REPLACE`), `list_xattrs` and `remove_xattr`.
  - Namespaces are `user.`, `trusted.`, `security.` and `system.`. POSIX ACLs are `system.posix_acl_access` and `system.posix_acl_default`, as on btrfs.
  - Stored as `XATTR_ITEM`s keyed by name hash. A value must fit in one tree item (about 1.9 KiB); larger ones return `NoSpace` (E2BIG).
- **Inode flags:** `get_flags` and `set_flags` use the Linux `FS_*_FL` values.
  - Immutable inodes refuse every change, including names and xattrs. Append-only files accept only writes at the end.
  - No-COW, compression and no-compression are inherited from the directory.
  - A no-COW file is overwritten in place and has no checksums, except blocks shared with a snapshot or reflink, which are still copied. The flag can only change while the file is empty, and reflinks between no-COW and normal files are refused.
- **fallocate:** preallocation with or without `KEEP_SIZE`, `PUNCH_HOLE` (frees whole blocks and zeros the edges) and `ZERO_RANGE`. Reserved space is held in `PREALLOC` extents that read as zeros until written.
- **fsck:** checks xattr items and that their inode exists.

## Phase 5: transparent compression
- **Algorithms:** zlib (as on btrfs), LZ4 and zstd, through `no_std` crates: `miniz_oxide` (already used by `btrfs-rs`), `lz4_flex` and `ruzstd`.
- **Turning it on:**
  - `set_mount_compression` is the `compress=` mount option. It is not stored on disk.
  - `set_compression` is the per-file property (`btrfs property set ... compression`). On a directory it is inherited by what is created in it.
  - `chattr +c` (`FL_COMPR`) compresses with zlib.
  - No-COW files and `FL_NOCOMP` are never compressed.
- **On disk:** an `EXT_COMPRESSED` extent holds up to 128 KiB of file data. The item records the algorithm, the disk blocks, the file blocks and the piece it maps. An extent is kept compressed only when that saves at least one block.
  - Overwrites, snapshots and reflinks can split an extent into pieces that share it.
  - Checksums cover the compressed blocks, so `scrub()` checks them too.
- **Small writes:** writes of 128 KiB are compressed at once. Smaller writes are stored as they are and compressed together when the transaction commits, so a file written a little at a time still ends up compressed.
- **`compsize`:** reports the bytes on disk and the uncompressed bytes of a file.

## Phase 6: send/receive and quotas
- **Subvolume identity:** root items now carry `uuid`, `parent_uuid` and `received_uuid`, shown by `list_subvolumes`.
- **`send(snap, parent, out)`:** writes a read-only snapshot as an `EFSSEND1` stream, where the header and every command have a CRC32C.
  - With a parent snapshot, only the changes are sent. `Store::diff` skips the subtrees both trees share, and data ranges are narrowed block by block.
  - Reflinks inside the snapshot travel as `CLONE` commands. Xattrs, flags, holes and preallocated extents are carried too.
- **`receive(dir, input)`:** builds a hidden subvolume, runs fsck on it, and only then names it, read-only and with `received_uuid` set.
  - A cut or damaged stream leaves nothing behind. Leftovers of a receive interrupted by a power cut are dropped at the next read-write mount.
  - An incremental stream needs its parent received first, matched by UUID, as on btrfs.
- **Quotas:** `quota_enable`, `quota_disable` and `quota_rescan` (superblock bit `FEAT_QUOTA`).

body:
## Что сделано
Первый шаг экранов V11 «Профили» поверх нынешней модели (пространства со своими cookie и избранным, данные F). `system-v5.md`, раздел 10: «чип профиля по центру (касание — список…)».

До этого чип в обзоре v5 был просто надписью. Теперь касание открывает лист **«Профили»**, как меню профилей в Safari:
- **Строка профиля:**
  - значок профиля белым на круге цвета профиля (`accentFill`, раздел 1.2);
  - имя и число вкладок;
  - галочка у текущего;
  - замок у запертого.
- **Профили с других устройств** — отдельной группой «С других устройств», с именем устройства.
- **Одно касание переключает профиль.** Лист уходит, обзор показывает вкладки нового профиля. Запертый профиль сначала просит вход по биометрии — прежний механизм.
- **Если профили выключены в настройках**, чип остаётся надписью.
- **Чип** показывает значок профиля и имя. Раньше там был текст эмодзи, а Vola эмодзи не рисует: ключ профиля превращается в значок Material Symbols (`WorkspaceIcons`).
- **TalkBack:**
  - у чипа действие «Выбрать профиль»;
  - текущий профиль помечен как выбранный;
  - у листа заголовок и «Закрыть».

**Цвета профиля в v5.** В v5 шесть акцентов, в данных восемь цветов. Два цвета без пары идут к ближайшему: бирюзовый — к зелёному, коралловый — к оранжевому (`V5ProfileRules.accent`). Сами акценты профиля на кнопках v5 пока не включены — это шаг V11c.

Общий компонент `V5ListRow` получил:
- место для своего значка слева;
- галочку справа (`V5RowTrailing.Check`).

Дальше:
- **V11b:** «Новый профиль» и правка (имя, значок, цвет из шести, свои cookie) в стиле v5.
- **V11c:** акцент профиля на кнопках v5 и смена профиля свайпом по обзору.

## Проверка на телефоне (флаг `ui.v5`)
1. Откройте обзор вкладок: на чипе внизу по центру значок и имя профиля. Коснитесь чипа: снизу выезжает лист «Профили».
2. У каждого профиля значок на круге своего цвета и число вкладок, у текущего — галочка.
3. Коснитесь другого профиля: лист закрывается, в обзоре вкладки этого профиля, на чипе его значок и имя.
4. Профиль с биометрической защитой: при выборе просит отпечаток, после входа переключается.
5. Смахните лист вниз или нажмите «Закрыть»: лист уходит, профиль не меняется.
6. Настройки → Вкладки → «Дополнительно» → выключите профили: чип не нажимается.
7. TalkBack: на чипе слышно «Выбрать профиль», в листе текущий профиль отмечен как выбранный.

## Проверки
- `scripts/ci/preflight.sh --fast` зелёный. Gradle в облаке нет — сборку и тесты проверяет CI.
- Тест `V5ProfileRulesTest`:
  - соответствие всех цветов акцентам;
  - число вкладок;
  - порядок (свои, потом с других устройств);
  - замок;
  - имя без названия.
- Compose Preview: лист в светлой и тёмной теме, обзор с новым чипом.

author: mahoskye
body:
**Merge after #338** (stacked: #336 ← #337 ← #338 ← this). It targets `main`.

This PR applies a style-guide research report (formatter and style-guide practice and evidence) to the project, plus a suppression-syntax bug that came out of the review.

## Suppression comments

- **Bug:** the documented form `/* @ssl-disable <rule>; */` is broken SSL. Comments end at `;`, so the trailing `*/` is code and raises `comment_text_after_terminator` and `unexpected_token`. The suppression still worked, but the line gained two errors. D3, CONFIGURATION.md §5.10 and `feature.diagnostics_pipeline` now show `/* @ssl-disable <rule>;`, and the tests use it. No production-corpus file uses suppressions, so nothing in the wild changes.
- **Reasons:** the research recommends that suppressions say why. A reason may follow the rule list after `--`, `—` or `:`, and matching ignores it:
  `/* @ssl-disable-next-line sql_injection -- the table name is a constant;`.
  It's optional, so existing comments keep working. `TestSuppressionComments_ReasonAndList` covers it.

## D18: formatter options policy

New formatter options are for compatibility (indentation style) or accessibility (line length), not taste; new layout ships default-on. A whole new pass may have a server-side off switch for gradual adoption, not surfaced as an editor style choice. Existing options stay. Layout changes ship as announced batches. The author's intent (their line breaks, blank lines and lone `;`) is preserved. This draws on the gofmt/Black/Prettier lesson that options are the main regret.

## Release notes

The CHANGELOG gets a `### Formatting changes` section for this release:

author: lpcox
body:
## Summary

- compose Cloud Hypervisor device ACL restoration from the durable workflow baseline plus only currently live peer VMM ACEs
- persist temporary peer UIDs alongside overlapping ACL baselines and retain the composed target across account deletion
- add deterministic two-identity regressions for both cleanup orders, exact runner ACE preservation, and removal of both VMM ACEs

## Diagnosis

Run `38515513439` proved mount cleanup and workload isolation were healthy, while final KVM ACL restoration lost the workflow-owned runner ACE. The two concurrent VMMs used distinct UIDs 999 and 997. Under the shared device ACL lock, a later runtime could capture an earlier runtime's temporary ACE in its durable baseline. Restoring the entire captured ACL made cleanup order observable: one cleanup could erase a still-live peer, while the other could later resurrect an already-cleaned peer or overwrite the runner baseline.

This change classifies and records temporary AWF VMM ACEs at capture time. Each locked restoration removes only the current runtime's ACE, strips captured temporary peers that are no longer live, preserves validated live peer ACEs, and restores the exact durable runner baseline. The pre-deletion composed target is retained and re-applied after `userdel`/`groupdel`, preserving fail-closed identity validation and durable recovery.

## Validation

- `npm run build`
- `npm run lint -- --quiet`
- `npm test -- --runInBand` — 462 suites passed, 8,246 tests passed
- `npm run test:coverage -- --runInBand` — passed
- Cloud Hypervisor suite — 47 suites passed, 1,190 tests passed

## Campaign follow-up

Do not resume or retry run `38515513439`. After this PR merges, dispatch the unchanged Phase 4 campaign as a fresh run with a new campaign ID.

body:
## Summary

Future purchases appeared as actionable work. Exclude them across queue sources and record-detail strips before counting or pagination.

```text
purchase queue eligibility
  date after the current household day -> defer
  live expense lines all marked future -> defer
  otherwise -> retain existing eligibility
```

Deleted expense lines do not count; mixed planned/incurred purchases and undated purchases without lines remain eligible. Documents the policy in `docs/entities.md`. No files, stored data, or contracts deleted.

## Evidence

- **Before:** the new regression counted six purchase findings when only three were eligible.
  **After:** all five work-queue integration tests pass, covering cross-source exclusion, counts, pagination, mixed lines, deleted lines, and empty record-detail strips.
- Passed `pnpm test:postgres src/server/repo/work-queue.integration.test.ts`, `pnpm --filter @cubby/web typecheck`, and scoped Oxlint.
- Browser verification was unavailable because the local server refused connections. This PR changes server eligibility; it does not change UI field presentation.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Read-only projection change; no migration.

**Blast Radius:** queue

Applies to household and member queue reads and record-detail strips.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes read-time eligibility for all work-queue sources and record strips; incorrect date or `future` line logic could hide real reconciliation work or still show planned purchases.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Future and all-planned purchases are no longer actionable work** in the household work queue, record-detail strips, and every queue source (including findings) because eligibility is filtered **before** counts and pagination.
> 
> The shared `queryWorkQueue` path adds a global SQL predicate on purchase-backed rows: defer when the purchase date is after the **current household calendar day**, or when it has live expense lines and **none** are incurred (`future = false`). Deleted lines are ignored; purchases with both planned and incurred lines stay visible; undated purchases with no lines are treated as unknown, not implicitly planned.
> 
> A new integration test exercises those scenarios across findings paging, the combined queue, and empty record strips. **`docs/entities.md`** documents the same policy for `/work-queue` and MCP `activity.work_queue`.

## Problem
14 October 06:21 BST diagnostic: physical FoxESS battery SOC 100% but its last reported state was 1,515 seconds old; same-device Modbus battery power, grid import/export and house load were freshly reported at ~9 seconds. Alpha9.93's 900-second absolute paid-Agile SOC cutoff blocked the optimizer's requested 1.362 kW export despite a healthy live device cohort.

## Fix
- Extend **paid Agile physical SOC cohort eligibility** from 900 to **3,600 seconds** exclusively within the physical house/export reserve guard.
- Preserve the provider's verified same-device evidence requirement and unmodified normal 180-second dynamic freshness and EV-safe requirements.
- Always debit the **entire SOC reading age** at worst-case **10 kW or higher** discharge and 95%-or-configured efficiency; reserve forecast house energy and the unchanged **15% physical export floor**. Older than 3,600 seconds, missing/inconsistent cohort, stale SOC flag, invalid SOC, stale overall telemetry, insufficient house energy and missing tariff evidence all **fail closed**.
- Retain the proven 6.4 kW grid export limit, cheap overnight Force Charge, No Paid Export untouched, and normal Self Use restoration.
- Reproduce actual 1,515.3-second SOC diagnostic in regression tests, test cutoff, worst-case debit, reserve conservation and cheap/no-export bypass. Align manifest and version checks for Alpha9.94.

## Gate
Do not merge or publish until final CI passes: Black, Ruff, pytest, HACS, Hassfest and ESPHome. Runtime export behaviour still needs a live post-install diagnostic; avoid restarting Home Assistant during active critical control periods.

body:
## 3a: evidence retrieval (EXP-011)

> **Merge #2 (3d) first.** This branch already contains 3d, with the one conflict, in `app/view.py`, resolved. Once #2 is merged, this PR's diff shows 3a alone.

Finishes the work on `wip/3a-retrieval`. Each of the top candidates in the dashboard and the API can now show short passages from PMC Open Access articles, each with its PMCID link and Creative Commons licence.
- Evidence is **shown beside a ranking, never used to make one**.
- Evidence is **about diagnosis only**.

### How it works
**On the laptop (pure NumPy and the standard library; nothing new installed):**
- BM25, plus a dense search over vectors precomputed on Kaggle, fused by reciprocal rank (k = 60).
- The query vector is a mix of precomputed vectors, so no model runs on the laptop.
- The dense scores are computed once at load, which makes a query cost microseconds.

**On Kaggle (`notebooks/kaggle_retrieval_corpus.ipynb`; runbook in `docs/11` §4.6):**
- Searches PMC Open Access, keeps only articles whose XML states a Creative Commons licence, and records each licence.
- Stays at or under 3 requests a second, with no API key.
- Embeds with `pritamdeka/S-PubMedBert-MS-MARCO` at a pinned snapshot.
- Writes a SHA-256-checked bundle. The corpus is never committed.

**Treatment screen (FR-6.5, `src/rag/screening.py`):**
- A sentence with any treatment language is never stored, embedded or shown.
- Passages are only runs of consecutive clean sentences.
- An article whose title names a specific treatment is dropped.
- The laptop screens again at load and at display. `safety_check` drops any evidence that recommends a treatment, as the last check.
- The cost: some diagnostic sentences are lost too (e.g. a D-dimer cut-off written in mg/L). This is disclosed in EXP-011.

**Degrades cleanly:** with no bundle (the default, `retrieval.bundle: null`), or a bundle that fails its checks, there is no evidence and every result reports `rag`. It never raises an exception.

**EXP-011 is pre-registered** in `docs/08`:
- 26 fixed queries.
- Pooled, blind 0–2 relevance judgements by two team members.
- Precision@3, nDCG@3/@10 and pooled Recall@10, comparing BM25 alone, dense alone and the hybrid with a paired bootstrap.
- How well the precomputed-vector mix stands in for the embedded sentence.

### Checked on the laptop, with the real graph and the transformer (3a + 3d together)
- 1047 tests pass and 15 skip (PyTorch and live Neo4j). black and ruff are clean.
- `scripts/check_crosswalk.py`: every golden case holds.
- Timing on synthetic bundles (768 dimensions, float16):
  - about 1.0–1.3 ms per candidate at 20–50k passages;
  - about 4–6 ms for evidence on 3 candidates;
  - 4–10 s at start-up.

  Live re-ranking stays fast enough (EXP-022).
- Bugs fixed in the WIP code:
  - a malformed manifest crashed the app instead of degrading;
  - the dense search recomputed every embedding product on each call.

### Open
- **The notebook has never run against NCBI or the model** (as required). Its smoke cell checks the search filters, `sort=relevance` and the model's maximum length early.
- **The 30–60 min runtime is an estimate.**
- **For the team, a contract change:** add `licence` (and `attribution`) to `Evidence` in `src/contracts.py`. Today `/diagnose` carries the PMCID and link but not the licence; the dashboard looks it up from the retriever.
- **The CLI demo** (`scripts/demo.py`) and `scripts/measure_latency.py` still use the empty retriever.
- **The owner's next steps:**
  1. after merge, run the notebook on Kaggle (GPU T4 x2, internet on, *Save & Run All (Commit)*);
  2. unzip `retrieval_corpus.zip` into `data/raw/retrieval_corpus/`;
  3. set `retrieval.bundle: data/raw/retrieval_corpus` in `configs/config.yaml`.
- **EXP-011's relevance judgements** need two team members.

author: kingyosun
body:
## 概要

配信者が app を起動し直した後に session を終えても、視聴者（とくに参加した後に退出した視聴者）の一覧で終わった session にならないことがある不具合のうち、製品の側（#1816 AC-1）を直す。

- 原因（#1816 の調査-1 (b)）: session の hint・読み直しで session を読む `fetch_verified_live_session`（game room は `fetch_verified_game_room`）は、読み先を順に読み、遠隔の読み先が反映済みと同じ版を返すと、そこで読みを終えていた。手元に保持した他の参加者の版については「同じ版なら、それで打ち切らずに提供者の新しい版を先に探す」と決めてある（#1395、ADR 0054）が、遠隔の読み先には当てはめていなかった。読み先の順は読みごとに回るので、まだ前の版を持つ別の視聴者が先に来ると、配信者の新しい版（終了）を読まずに終わる。読みは成功の扱いなので、#1813 の読み直しも起きない。
- 直し方: 反映済みと同じ版を読んだときに残りの読み先を探すかの判定（`holds_relayed_copy` → `searches_past_projected`）で、反映の経路（`keep`。hint・読み直し・表示の読み）では遠隔の読み先の版も探す側にする。操作（参加・終了など）と映像の認可の読みは、読み先への問い合わせを増やさないよう、前と同じくその版で打ち切る。手元の読みの扱い（保持した他の参加者の版は探す、自分の docs author が書いた state は手元で打ち切る）は変えない。新しい版が見つからなければ、前と同じくその版を使う。
- 画面・保存・wire は変えない。

## 対象と条件

- 対象Issue・種別: Refs #1816・fix（#1816 の AC-2〔試験の起動し直しを利用者の終了と同じ経路にする〕は #1811 で直す）
- リスク区分・Scope revision・基準commit: C・2026-10-14-r2・main `51a85898d`
- 変更path・対象外:
  - `crates/app-api/src/service/live_game_support.rs`（判定 1 か所の名前と中身、2 つの呼出元）
  - 試験（`tests/sync/session_newer_provider.rs`、game room の試験の部品を `pub(super)` に）
  - ADR 0054「保持するもの」の session の行に、遠隔の読み先の版も同じく探す 1 行
  - 対象外: 強制終了の後に配信者へ約 30 秒つながらないこと（iroh の古い経路。#1816 の対象外）、読み先の 4 人に新しい版を持つ相手がいないときの読み直し（#1813 の読み直しは「何も読めない」ときだけ）
- 対応する1つの末端AC: #1816 AC-1 → 下の試験 2 件。
- 統合・置換・削除した処理: 判定を 1 つの関数のまま広げた（live と game の 2 つの呼出元が同じ判定を使う）。暫定処理は無い。
- C: shared helper の全 caller: `fetch_verified_live_session`・`fetch_verified_game_room` の呼出元は、(1) `read_session`（`keep` が真。hint・#1813 の読み直し・scope の読み直し `reread_sessions`・表示要求 `set_session_display`）、(2) `fetch_live_session_state_and_manifest`・`fetch_game_room_state_and_manifest`（`keep` が偽。参加・退出・終了・更新の操作、映像の認可 `grant` と転送する視聴者の 5 秒ごとの再確認 `still_allowed`、Dome の操作）、(3) Dome の作成時刻の読み（`keep` が偽。手元に無いときだけ）。変わるのは (1) だけで、遠隔の読み先が反映済みと同じ版を返したときに残りの読み先も読む（同じ 30 秒の期限の内）。(2)・(3) と、新しい版が先に見つかる場合・自分の session の場合・手元の読みの場合の経路は変わらない。

## 変更前後の証拠

- 修正前（#1816 の調査-1、2026-10-14、Ubuntu 24.04 の container・#1800 の試験の仕組み、配信者 1・視聴者 2）: 利用者の終了で配信者を起動し直す形にした live の試験で、退出した視聴者に終了が届かなかった（7 回中 3 回）。gossip の debug の log では、その視聴者は配信者とつなぎ直し、終了の hint も受け取っていたが、session の読みの失敗の警告は無く、projection は配信中のまま。
- 本 PR の試験（`crates/app-api/src/tests/sync/session_newer_provider.rs`。読み先は、先に前の版を持つ視聴者、次に配信者の順）:
  - `a_hinted_live_session_is_read_past_a_provider_that_returns_the_projected_version`: 配信者が session を終えた後の hint で、一覧が終了になる。修正前は配信中のまま（失敗）、修正後に成功。
  - `a_hinted_game_room_is_read_past_a_provider_that_returns_the_projected_version`: 同じく game room の得点の版 2（終了）が一覧に入る。修正前は待機のまま（失敗）、修正後に成功。
- 本 PR の CI の Linux build（`f80919df4`。hint の読みの挙動は `ffe7ec7fa` と同じ）で、#1811 の試験（起動し直しを利用者の終了と同じ経路にしたもの）の live を手元の container で 5 回: 5 回とも LV-1〜LV-9 が通った（LV-8 の起動し直しの後の LV-7 で、退出した視聴者に終了が届く）。直す前の build（#1819）では、同じ試験で 7 回中 3 回、退出した視聴者に終了が届かなかった。

## 検証とリスク

- 実行command・結果:
  - `cargo fmt --check -p kukuri-app-api`: 成功
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p kukuri-app-api --all-targets -- -D warnings`: 成功
  - `cargo test --locked -p kukuri-app-api --lib`: 599 件成功
- CI（対象commit・結果）: `ffe7ec7fa`: [Kukuri Fast](https://github.com/kukuri-app/kukuri/actions/runs/38520895191)・[Kukuri Linux Package](https://github.com/kukuri-app/kukuri/actions/runs/38520895160) の job がすべて成功（macOS・Android の web-e2e は対象外で skip）。
- 挙動への影響: 反映の経路で遠隔の読み先が反映済みと同じ版を返したとき、残りの読み先（近隣の最大 4 人と locator）も読む（同じ 30 秒の期限の内）。変わっていない session の hint・読み直しの読みは、その分だけ長くなりうる（監査の計測で、近隣 4 人がみな同じ版のとき問い合わせが 10 回から 24 回）。scope の読み直しの間は lease の task が hint を待たせる（件数の上限 `SESSION_REREAD_LIMIT` の内）。件数には比例しない。
- 追加発見の分類: 強制終了の後の約 30 秒（#1816 の対象外として記録）。

## 独立監査

- 監査記録・対象commit・判定:
  - 固定 head `f80919df4`: PASS（blocker なし）。修正前に試験が失敗すること（live は配信中のまま、game は待機のまま）、関連の試験 163 件と real iroh の試験 11 件の成功を確かめた。所見 1: 判定の変更が AC-1 の外の読み（操作・映像の認可。転送する視聴者の 5 秒ごとの再確認では、待つ間に子への送信が止まる作り）にも効き、変わっていない session の問い合わせが 10 回から 24 回に増える。所見 2: scope の読み直しが長くなる（上限の内）。
  - 所見 1 を受けて `ffe7ec7fa` で、遠隔の読み先で残りを探すのを反映の経路（`keep`）だけにした。
- 監査後delta: `f80919df4..ffe7ec7fa`: 再監査 PASS（blocker なし）。近隣 4 人がみな同じ版を持つときの 1 回の読みの問い合わせは、操作の読み（`keep` が偽）が基準と同じ 10 回に戻り、hint の読み（`keep` が真）は 24 回（意図どおり）。試験 2 件・関連 163 件・real iroh の 11 件が成功。残る所見: 反映の経路の表示要求と scope の読み直しは、変わっていない session で問い合わせが増える（件数の上限の内）。

author: rnrn428
body:
## 무엇을 했나

발표 자료와 앞으로의 개발을 위해, 지금까지 만든 API를 문서로 정리했습니다. API의 주소·요청·응답은 바뀌지 않았습니다.

**Swagger (`/swagger-ui.html`, `/v3/api-docs`)**
- 컨트롤러 22개, API 61개에 한국어 요약·설명(`@Operation`)을 붙이고 10개 묶음(`@Tag`, 1. 로그인·가입 ~ 10. 공유·검색엔진)으로 나눴습니다.
- 문서 머리에 주소·버전, 세션 로그인, 소셜 로그인 주소, CSRF, 오류 모양을 설명합니다.
- 로그인이 필요한 API에는 `세션 쿠키`, GET이 아닌 API에는 `CSRF 토큰` 표시를 붙입니다(`SecurityConfig`의 공개 목록과 같은 목록).
- 이름이 같은 요청 record(`PostRequests.Write`, `CommentRequests.Write` 등)가 서로 덮어써서 틀린 칸이 보이던 것을 바깥 클래스 이름을 붙여 고쳤습니다.
- CSRF 토큰 API에 쓰지 않는 물음표 값이 보이던 것을 숨겼습니다.
- `OpenApiDocsTest`: 모든 API에 요약과 묶음이 있는지, 로그인 없이 GET을 부르면 401인 API와 `세션 쿠키` 표시가 정확히 맞는지, 자료 모양 이름이 겹치지 않는지 확인합니다.

**Spring REST Docs**
- `ApiDocumentationTest`가 주요 흐름 22개를 실제 CSRF 흐름으로 부르며 요청·응답 예시를 만듭니다. 응답 칸이 문서와 어긋나면 테스트가 실패합니다.
- `src/docs/asciidoc/index.adoc` + `docinfo.html`: 원고지 모양의 한 장짜리 문서입니다.
- `cd backend && mvn -Pdocs verify` → `backend/target/generated-docs/index.html`. 평소 `mvn verify`에서는 예시(snippets)만 만들고 HTML은 만들지 않습니다.

**릴리스**: CHANGELOG `[0.5.3] - 준비 중`, 서버·화면 버전을 0.5.3으로 올렸습니다.

## 연결된 작업

v0.5.3 API 문서 (사용자 요청: 발표 자료용 Swagger 문서 + Spring REST Docs)

## 확인한 것

- [x] `mvn -Pdocs verify` 통과 (기존 테스트 + `OpenApiDocsTest` 3개 + `ApiDocumentationTest` 22개, REST Docs HTML 생성)
- [x] 화면 `npm run lint`, `npm run build` 통과
- [ ] CI 통과 (서버, 화면, 품질 분석)
- [x] 비밀번호, 키 같은 비밀 값이 들어가지 않았다

author: waleedrizwan
body:
A double-quoted span of up to 60 words (straight `"…"`, curly `“…”`, or the ``` ``…'' ``` style of bills) that closes within the paragraph is kept as one sentence, so a quoted statement with inner full stops is no longer cut in half. A quotation that reopens without closing, as news quotes running over several paragraphs do, ends the previous quoted paragraph. Longer or unclosed quotes split as before, so a speech does not become one unpickable unit.

Recovered from uncommitted work in the main checkout (the "Keep multi-sentence quotations whole" session), rebased onto main.

## Results

Development sets at reference length, distill vs `eval/dev-baseline.json`:

| Set | ROUGE-2 change | 95% CI | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| cnndm-dev (n=500) | −0.04 | [−0.28, +0.19] | no clear change |
| billsum-dev (n=300) | +0.05 | [−0.11, +0.25] | no clear change |
| govreport-dev (n=100) | +0.03 | [+0.00, +0.09] | no clear change |

Neutral on ROUGE, as expected for a change that moves sentence boundaries inside quoted speech; the gain is readability (no half-quotes in summaries). Tests cover straight, curly and bill-style quotes, `(CNN)"…` openings, reopened multi-paragraph quotes, and the unclosed and over-length cases that must still split.

- `cargo test --release`: 62 passed (on the pre-#10 base).
- `eval/determinism.sh`: all 24 goldens unchanged.

author: hansade2005
body:
## What and why
Closes more of the "not yet" rows for everyday sites (embedded players, sign-in popups, Zoom-style apps, DRM streaming).

- **Iframes painted and interactive:** frame content is drawn into the parent at its box (clip, radius, transforms, opacity), scrolls inside it, and receives mouse, wheel, keyboard, text and clipboard. Built on PR #26's child-tab frames with partitioned storage. Agent snapshots include frame content with refs such as `f1e5`.
- **`window.open` and popups:** WindowProxy with `opener`, named targets on links and forms, `noopener`/`rel=opener`, `window.close()` for script-opened windows, popup blocker tied to user activation, COOP opener severing, cross-window `postMessage`/`BroadcastChannel`/`storage` events. An OAuth-style popup round trip is tested against local servers.
- **Cross-origin isolation, `SharedArrayBuffer`, `Atomics`** (gated on COOP+COEP, with COEP enforcement for subresources), **WebAssembly threads** (shared memory, atomics, posting memory/modules to workers).
- **WebCodecs:** decoders for VP8, VP9, H.264, HEVC, AV1, Opus, AAC, MP3, Vorbis, PCM; encoders for VP8 and Opus; `VideoFrame`/`AudioData`/chunks/`ImageDecoder`.
- **EME with Clear Key:** encrypted MSE playback (cenc, cens, cbc1, cbcs).
- **DRM layer** (`internal/media/cdm`): one interface for key systems; a separate `sweef-cdm` helper hosts a user-installed Widevine CDM through Chromium's CDM ABI (the browser binary stays static; Sweef never ships or downloads the CDM). PlayReady and FairPlay are compile-checked only and off by default.
- **Fixes:** one host-call dispatcher per VM (a few dozen VMs exhausted modernc quickjs's process-wide limit of 32767 registered callbacks and left new pages without JavaScript); canvas `getImageData`/`putImageData` move pixels as ArrayBuffers (1280x720 readback 0.44 s → 10 ms); CodeQL findings (selector escaping, download names, link schemes, UI markup, protocol bounds, Atomics conversions).

## How it was tested
- Full `go test -short ./...` on Linux locally and in CI (ubuntu, macOS, Windows), packaging smoke, govulncheck, dependency review and CodeQL all green on the head commit.
- New tests: frames and windows (painting, hit testing, input, popups, OAuth round trip, sandbox, named targets), SharedArrayBuffer and wasm-thread counters across workers, WebCodecs VP8 encode→decode (PSNR 31-34 dB), Clear Key decryption equal to the clear reference, Widevine host end to end against a Go fake CDM.
- NOT tested: real Google/Facebook/Stripe/reCAPTCHA popups, the Zoom web client, a real Widevine library or licence server, PlayReady/FairPlay on real machines.

## Evidence
- Stripped linux/amd64 binary: 39.2 MB (budget 40 MiB).
- Canvas readback: 440 ms → 10 ms (`TestCanvasReadbackSpeed`, same machine).

## Checklist
- [x] Short tests pass locally and in CI
- [x] Tests added
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` updated under `[Unreleased]`
- [x] Docs updated (`docs/frames-popups.md`, `docs/webcodecs.md`, `docs/webassembly.md`, `docs/drm.md`, `docs/web-platform.md`)
- [x] No new cgo; no new dependencies
- [ ] Commits are signed off

## Zusammenfassung
Server-Vorarbeit III aus ADR-003: Belege, die mit der iOS-App erfasst werden, kommen nachweisbar unverändert an, tragen ihren Erfassungsweg und werden bei erneutem Senden nicht doppelt angelegt.

- **Neue Belegfelder** (Migration `20261014_0049`):
  - `capture_source`: `web`, `api`, `einvoice`, `mobile_scan` oder `mobile_share`
  - `captured_at`: Aufnahmezeitpunkt auf dem Gerät
  - `capture_device`: Gerätebezeichnung

  Die Weboberfläche setzt `web` bzw. `einvoice`, API-Uploads standardmäßig `api`. Altbelege bleiben ohne Angabe, nachträglich wird nichts ergänzt.
- **Upload-API** `POST /api/v1/documents` und `POST /api/v1/receipt-ocr/suggestions` (JSON und Multipart, ebenso die MCP-Tools `upload_document` und `create_receipt_ocr_suggestion`) nehmen optional `capture_source`, `captured_at` (ISO 8601 mit Zeitzone, höchstens 10 Minuten in der Zukunft), `capture_device` und `client_sha256` an.
- **Prüfung des Geräte-Hashes:** Weicht `client_sha256` vom Hash der empfangenen Datei ab, antwortet der Server mit `422` und speichert weder Datei noch Beleg.
- **Idempotenz:** Mit `client_sha256` liefert ein erneuter Upload gleichen Inhalts den vorhandenen Beleg (`200`, `"duplicate": true`). Der OCR-Vorschlag antwortet in diesem Fall mit `409` und der `document_id`, ohne zweiten Vorschlag. Ohne `client_sha256` bleibt das bisherige Verhalten.
- **Nachvollziehbarkeit:** Die Belegliste zeigt den Erfassungsweg (Tooltip: Aufnahmezeit und Gerät). Das Audit-Log enthält Erfassungsangaben und `client_hash_verified`. Der Prüferexport hat Feldbeschreibungen für die neuen Spalten. Die Verfahrensdokumentation hat den neuen Abschnitt 4.3 „Mobile Erfassung“, inklusive Hinweis zum ersetzenden Scannen (GoBD Rz. 136 ff.).

## Tests
- `pytest`: 846 bestanden; neu ist `tests/test_mobile_capture.py` mit 9 Tests:
  - Prüfung der Eingaben
  - Metadaten und Audit
  - abweichender Hash (kein Beleg, keine Datei)
  - Idempotenz
  - Multipart-Upload
  - OCR-Vorschlag mit 422 und 409
  - Web-Upload und Anzeige in der Liste
  - Feldbeschreibungen in Prüferexport und MCP
- `ruff check .` sauber, `alembic heads` zeigt genau einen Head
- Live am Dev-Server:
  - mobiler Upload `201`, Wiederholung `200` mit `duplicate=true` auf denselben Beleg
  - falscher Hash `422`
  - Belegliste zeigt „iOS-Scan“ mit Tooltip „Aufgenommen … auf iPhone 17 Pro“

## Hinweis
Wie schon „Hochgeladen“ zeigt die Liste Zeitpunkte in UTC. Eine Umstellung der Anzeige auf Ortszeit wäre ein eigener kleiner PR.

author: adamleithp
body:
## Problem

- The org menu in the Today rail opens on click but never shows. It mounts at opacity 0 in the top-left corner, so the click looks dead.
- The web app runs React 18, which drops a ref passed to a plain function component.
- `TodayOrgMenu` renders `TooltipTrigger` through the `render` prop of `DropdownMenuTrigger`. The menu trigger's ref goes to `TooltipTrigger` and is lost.
- Base UI uses that ref as the popup anchor. With no anchor, the positioner never computes a position and keeps its hidden first-frame style.
- Any quill trigger rendered through another trigger's `render` prop has the same problem.

## Changes

- The Today rail org menu opens under its icon again.
- `TooltipTrigger`, `DropdownMenuTrigger`, `PopoverTrigger`, `DialogTrigger` and `DrawerTrigger` now use `React.forwardRef` and pass the ref to the Base UI trigger.
- `TooltipTrigger` keeps its `Payload` generic through a type cast, because `forwardRef` cannot carry a generic signature.
- The quill guide lists the five triggers under its `forwardRef` rule, and the primitives guide says they nest in either order.
- `AlertDialogTrigger` is out of scope. Its Base UI type has no `ref` prop, so it needs a cast.
- No caller changes. React 19 passes `ref` as a normal prop, so the wrappers act the same there.

Before: the menu is invisible, so there is nothing to capture. After:

![org-menu-after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/3b5045677fc37a9bde733b445615756ab4496733/2026/10/4f15ae4f-f640-4ef6-8a04-b6732e570ded.png)

## How did you test this code?

- Local dev app with the original `TodayOrgMenu` code: the menu positioner now has `position: absolute` at (10, 50) under the trigger, at opacity 1. Before the fix, it stayed at `position: fixed`, (0, 0), opacity 0.
- The "Function components cannot be given refs" console warning no longer fires.
- `tsc --noEmit` passes for quill primitives. The quill build passes.
- Frontend `typescript:check` in a clean worktree, set up the way CI does it: no errors. The first push failed this check because a `RefAttributes` intersection in the `TooltipTrigger` cast left `render` callback parameters untyped. The second commit fixes it.
- Not checked: the desktop app, which pins a published quill version, and the other four triggers in a nested `render` setup.

**Test rationale:** No new test. The bug needs a real React 18 ref chain and Base UI positioning, which the primitives package has no test setup for.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Opus 5.5

- Skills invoked: `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`.
- The root cause came from the Base UI menu store in the running app: `activeTriggerElement` was `null` because the trigger never registered its element.
- Two earlier theories were wrong: a second org-switcher modal on the same open state, and the nesting order alone. The first is not in this PR.
- An app-only alternative swaps the nesting in `TodayOrgMenu`. This PR fixes the wrappers instead, so other callers cannot hit the same bug.

author: chaliy
body:
## What changed
Remove `everruns-pg-embedded` from the workspace. The server directly depends on `postgresql_embedded`; its storage module owns the shared native cluster, private database copies and owner-exit cleanup. PostgreSQL-mode API test servers now have private migrated databases, removing shared seed/feature-flag locks. The same fixture builder supports disposable native PostgreSQL and an explicitly configured durable external cluster.

PR CI runs affected workspace tests (including reverse dependencies and focused authorization/migration contracts), lint/repository guards, and relevant UI/docs/API/packaging checks. Broad offline validation coalesces main pushes without cancelling the running batch. Nightly covers feature-isolation/MSRV/portability and provider health; unchanged nightlies skip repeated offline work. Release publication waits for full validation of its exact revision.

Changelog: not user-facing (internal test/CI changes; no new entry).

## Why
The private utility crate has one owner: server storage. A separate package adds an unnecessary boundary. Broad PR matrices and binary consumers made unrelated Rust changes wait for full integration and packaging work.

## Before / After
- Before: a private PostgreSQL package plus process-local seed/flag coordination over the API tests' shared database. After: direct lifecycle-library dependency, per-server database ownership and one migrated template per process/configuration. Cross-process fixtures receive their server's explicit database URL.
- Before: ordinary Rust PRs triggered PostgreSQL shards, all binary builds, SDK cohorts and Docker. After: affected tests form the required Rust gate; API/packaging consumers follow their relevant inputs. OpenAPI generation builds only its exporter. Chaos functional runs reuse the shared server/worker binaries in batches/full validation or harness-specific PRs; the separate release-profile benchmark is manual. Nine lightweight guards share one runner; the duplicate broad core run is removed and isolated feature combinations move to nightly/full validation.
- Main keeps one running batch and only the newest pending revision. Selection compares last successful ancestor batch → selected revision; failed, cancelled, label and PR runs never advance that baseline. No pushes means no main code-validation runs. Provider health/advisories retain their independent scheduled coverage.
- A trusted completion workflow maintains owned Linear issues by durable check identity, preserving human notes and assignees. Stale events cannot resurrect resolved failures. Same-revision green reruns require human infrastructure triage; later containing green batches resolve regressions.
- A manual archive pilot compiles one libtest executable and runs identical verified bytes on native/durable database runners. The durable leg and nightly/full store shard check committed data across abrupt PostgreSQL termination.

Validation:
- `just pre-push`: all 32 checks passed, including workspace all-target/all-feature Clippy.
- Storage tests: 342 passed; lifecycle cleanup covers ordinary exit, SIGKILL and process-group termination. The ignored owner fixture is explicitly invoked by its parent test.
- API contracts: 65 passed with four test threads, including private PostgreSQL-server isolation.
- Full server integration target: 227 passed. Focused domain auth/org/policy/PAT/migration/OAuth cases: 75 passed, including separate-process grant decryption.
- Two concurrent processes passed the same migration/fixture/isolation test against a library-managed external PostgreSQL with fsync enabled.
- 23 executable CI-policy tests passed: baseline selection, dependency closure, PR/full/nightly routing, exact release revision, stale/resolved issue handling, and bounded recovery orchestration.
- Focused jobs restore the existing main-produced cache keys with matching cache-fingerprinted environments; test runtime settings are scoped to execution. Actual run logs exposed and verified the regression fix for `RUST_TEST_THREADS` splitting producer/consumer keys. They do not create PR-only cold cache keys. The first CI run caught the new tracker missing the standard Doppler installer retry; it now uses the guarded one-retry contract. Workflow secret/vault boundaries, label-event behavior, sandbox/provider routing, timeout and publish/release regression fixtures passed. Knowledge and test enumeration guards passed. Linear queries and metadata persistence passed actual read/write/read preflight on the owned follow-up issue; the temporary marker was removed.
- Actionlint passed with only its outdated `queue` schema diagnostic excluded; `queue: max` is verified against current GitHub syntax and preserves every tracker event.
- Final DEV_MODE TCP API smoke: health 200, migrations/seed and agent create/read/delete passed; PostgreSQL stopped with its owner. No model requests. [Final-head CI](https://github.com/everruns/everruns/actions/runs/38522542693) passed all 42 executed jobs, including focused server tests, all SDK cohorts, packaging, chaos, and UI budget E2E. The obsolete separately required full PostgreSQL check was retired from the Main ruleset; Build Check/UI/docs and all other policy fields were preserved.

Post-merge fixture and archive-context corrections are in [PR #4733](https://github.com/everruns/everruns/pull/4733).

- Post-merge: [covering main batch](https://github.com/everruns/everruns/actions/runs/38530922068) passed all 48 executed jobs on `a624e3d4058e1cc6a84d3fc66e5f46d7c53af631`.
- [Corrected archive pilot 1](https://github.com/everruns/everruns/actions/runs/38530961462) and [pilot 2](https://github.com/everruns/everruns/actions/runs/38530965446) passed on that same revision: 3,693 tests per native/durable runner, matching executable checksums, and committed data surviving abrupt durable PostgreSQL termination. Cache miss/hit compile times were 7m32s/5m12s; setup/execution variance and remaining benchmarks are recorded in EVE-1277.
- The [recovery tracker](https://github.com/everruns/everruns/actions/runs/38535033214) closed EVE-1278 on that green batch and preserved its owner/investigation. EVE-1279 remains open for the separate intermittent virtual-user binding race; this CI/test change does not claim a product fix.

## Risk
Medium/high: this intentionally trades some pre-merge cross-component coverage for post-merge batch detection. Focused PR failures still block merging; broad failures stay visible and owned, and releases require full exact-revision success. Legacy raw-pool/global-state suites retain serialization. Native clusters remain non-root, private and disposable; DEV_MODE never consumes the external test-cluster override.

## Security
- Threat categories reviewed: TM-CI, TM-FS, TM-SQL, TM-AUTH, TM-AUTHZ, TM-DOS.
- PR jobs receive no vault/provider/Linear credentials. The tracker executes trusted main code, reads CI metadata rather than PR artifacts, and scopes Doppler credentials to its single command beside pinned actions.
- Manual release validation accepts a full SHA reachable from main; every consumer checks out that revision. Ordinary/PR/different-revision green runs cannot satisfy publication.
- Database identifiers remain validated; temporary directories and loopback/SCRAM settings are retained. External test support performs database operations only and never owns/stops that server.
- Crash probes require the job's service container ID and durability settings before terminating anything; their step timeout bounds readiness/recovery. Offline fixtures verify refusal before destructive commands.

## Follow-ups
[EVE-1277](https://linear.app/everruns/issue/EVE-1277/measure-warm-ci-tiers-and-benchmark-test-archives-and-runner-sizing): collect warm PR/batch wall time and runner minutes, benchmark the archive pilot, workspace caching and runner sizing. Sub-ten-minute ordinary PR CI is a measurement target, not an unmeasured claim. Runner/cache changes stay off the

author: bbenshab
body:
## Overview Fixes the NIXL KV-transfer crash when a P/D disaggregated deployment uses **heterogeneous TP** (e.g. prefill TP16 + decode TP8) with a **mixed MLA** model — a model that combines a replicated MLA latent cache with head-sharded attention regions (GLM-5.3 `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` with `sparse_mla_force_mqa`, i.e. MLA + DSA sparse-attention indexer). Extends the per-region classification introduced in #44583 to heterogeneous-TP page geometry. ## Claims - Heterogeneous P/D TP works for mixed MLA models: prefill TP16 + decode TP8 and prefill TP8 + decode TP16 both complete full benchmarks with correct output quality. - Pure-MLA (DeepSeek-class), pure-GQA, and symmetric-TP deployments keep their existing behavior — every change is gated on conditions only hybrid + mixed-TP produce. - Measured on GLM-5.3 785B fp8 (8xH200): `1P×TP16 + 2D×TP8` = 0.81 req/s vs 0.48 req/s for the best symmetric split (**+68%**) — prefill is compute-bound (wider TP wins) while decode is latency-bound (smaller TP group wins); heterogeneous TP lets each role sit at its optimum. ## Validation Live on an 8xH200 cluster, GLM-5.3 785B fp8, full request-load benchmarks per config: - D>P (prefill TP8 + decode TP16): EPP registration 3s, full benchmark, quality ok - D

Failure signature (before the fix) ``` ValueError: Replicated region i=99 local_len=8192 remote_len=16384 (NIXL handshake validation, decode engine, first request) ``` followed, after each layer was fixed in sequence, by descriptor-size mismatches and finally a multi-source read assertion in `pull_worker`. Performance evidence and the full 11-iteration investigation: internal benchmarking on ServeIt Studio (GLM-5.3 asymmetric TP analysis).

author: malak67
body:
Three layout fixes in the manager, found together while looking at WEB-1788.

### Profile page picked its layout from orientation

The desktop layout was gated on `(min-width: 1024px) and (orientation: landscape)` in the header, and on `lg:landscape:` across 255 classes in the profile view. A window taller than it is wide got the mobile layout no matter how wide it was, which is what Dom hit on a big screen.

The orientation clause was also covering for a breakpoint the layout does not fit. The actions column (favourite, share, renew) was placed at `left: min(50% + 452.5px, 100% - 164px)`, next to the 905px content column but clamped on screen; below 1169px it sat over the About card. The clamp crosses over at 1233px, so with the column only rendering from 1280 it never binds, and the offset is now a plain `left-[calc(50%+452.5px)]`. Main ships that overlap today in any landscape window between 1024 and 1169.

Tailwind's own `xl:` (**1280px**) replaces both. Tall windows get the desktop layout, an iPad in portrait stays on mobile as before, and the overlap band is gone. The 1233-1279 band moves from desktop to mobile, since 1280 is the token and 1233 is not.

Worth knowing before it ships: this changes what a laptop at 1024-1279 CSS pixels sees, which includes a 1440px display at 125% zoom (1152px). It got the desktop layout with the overlapping actions column before; it gets the mobile layout now. Intended, but it is the one case where the profile page looks different to someone who had not noticed a bug.

### Dashboard column floated left below `md`

The page container is `flex-col` below `md` with `items-start`, which in a column makes children size to content: the column sat at about three quarters of the width with dead space on the right, visible between 600 and 767px. `items-start` now applies only with `md:flex-row`.

### Dashboard cards had no gutter below `md`

The cards are full-bleed sections (`rounded-none`, no column gutter) all the way to 767px, next to a notice banner that has one. From the existing `xs` token (480px) the column keeps a 1rem gutter and the cards their rounded corners. Phones are unchanged; moving that line is one prefix if design wants phones padded too.

The grace, commemorative-mint, upgrade and migration-progress banners each carried their own phone treatment (an extra inset, or rounding only from `md`); those now follow the same `xs` line as the cards. None of the four renders for the matrix's mock wallet, so they are checked by reading, not by screenshot.

### `shadow-none` lost to the custom card shadows

Visible on the profile page at mobile widths as a faint box around a bare "About" heading. `ProfileAbout` sets `shadow-none` over the `Card` base's `shadow-temp-card`, but tailwind-merge did not know the custom token was a shadow, kept both, and stylesheet order let the shadow win. `cn` now registers `shadow-temp-card` and `shadow-domain-card` as shadows. Same fix lands in `ProfileHeaderLoading` and `AddressProfileNamesList`, which use the same mobile pattern.

### Verified

A viewport matrix in headless Chromium against the dev server: the name profile, the address profile and the dashboard (mock wallet), at 22 widths from 320 to 2560, each in landscape and in portrait (taller than wide), 132 loads. Each load asserts the header type against the breakpoint, no horizontal overflow, on desktop that the actions column renders and does not intersect the About card, on mobile that the About section carries no shadow, and on the dashboard that the column fills the container with the gutter the band calls for.

130 of 132 pass, including every boundary pair (479/480, 767/768, 1279/1280) in both orientations and a 2560x3584 portrait window. The two misses are the same pre-existing overflow: the primary-name card at 320px needs 7px more than it has. Main overflows by 24px at that width, so this branch narrows it without touching the card.

Also checked by hand in DevTools responsive mode at 1400x1600, 1280, 1279, 1078 and 601. The served stylesheet has no media query mentioning orientation, and the header's queries are `(min-width: 1280px)` and `(min-width: 768px)`. manager: 3091 tests, `tsc` and Biome clean on touched files.

author: jt-mchorse
body:
`io_utils.loads_json` is the one JSON reader every loader uses. #333 made it re-raise `json.loads`' `RecursionError` as a `JSONDecodeError`, so each site's existing handler applies. On 3.11+ `json.loads` has a third refusal: an integer literal longer than `sys.get_int_max_str_digits()` (4300 on the CI interpreters) raises a plain `ValueError`, which no reader catches. On `main`, `validate` and `validate --calibration` therefore exited 1 (the "findings" code) with a traceback instead of reporting the line, and `run` exited 1 (the "a row regressed" code) in its pre-flight load. A GitHub API body containing such a literal also escaped `_do_request`'s not-JSON arm. `diff-json`, `comment`, `drift` and `calibrate` reached exit 2, but only through a broad `except ValueError`, and printed the bare interpreter message. `loads_json` now re-raises that `ValueError` as a `JSONDecodeError` naming the limit. The collecting validators record a `parse` finding and keep walking, and every other reader exits 2 with its own `invalid ... JSON:` prefix.

Closes #365

**Revert probe** (`io_utils.py` from `main`, `__pycache__` cleared): 9 of 11 new tests red. The 2 green are the precondition (the literal really is refused by `json.loads` with a non-`JSONDecodeError`) and the at-the-limit int still decoding.

**Gates:** `pytest` 2709 passed, 19 skipped; `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy` clean (after rebasing on #356 and #358).

author: rasalas
body:
Rebuilding `browser-connect/pkg` from the locked Rust source did not reproduce the committed WASM. The comparison step added during ticket 54 failed in CI (#266), so it was taken out again. Without a reproducible build, nobody can check that the shipped adapter comes from this source.

Two things made the bytes depend on the build machine:
- `ring` compiles C code with whatever Clang the machine has. Each Clang version emits different WASM.
- Absolute paths of the checkout, Cargo's registry and the Rust sysroot remain in the panic locations, even in stripped WASM.

What changed:
- `scripts/build-browser-connect.mjs` requires Rust 1.98.1, WASI SDK 27.0 (its Clang and `llvm-ar`, checked by version string) and the `wasm-bindgen` CLI matching `Cargo.lock`.
- The build remaps checkout, registry and sysroot paths. License files are read in sorted order.
- `pkg/` is the build of CI's `ubuntu-24.04` runner, taken from this PR's run. The manifest gets the new WASM and license hashes.
- `.github/workflows/browser-connect.yml` rebuilds on Ubuntu 24.04. It fetches the SDK archive with a pinned SHA-256 digest, which matches the digest GitHub publishes for the `wasi-sdk-27` release. After each rebuild, `git diff --exit-code -- browser-connect/pkg` must be clean. When it is not, the job uploads its rebuild as an artifact, so the next `pkg/` comes from CI.
- `browser-connect/README.md` documents the toolchain, the Linux reference build and how to check path independence locally.

Why Linux only: the first run of this PR built on both Ubuntu and macOS. The macOS rebuild matched a local Apple Silicon build byte for byte. The Linux rebuild differed in code layout (string merging, one retained panic message), with identical tools, sources and remapped paths. So the build is reproducible per kind of host but not across them, and the committed package has to name one host.

Ticket 97 (`.scratch/project-review-2026-10-12/issues/97-browser-connect-wasm-reproduzierbar.md`).

Tests:
- Locally on macOS, two clean builds were byte-identical. They used different checkout, Cargo and SDK paths. In CI, the macOS rebuild matched them.
- `vite/browser-connect.test.ts` checks that the WASM holds canonical registry paths and no home or temp paths. It fails on the old package.
- The `src/web/connect` transport tests pass with the new WASM.
- Lint passed.
- The `src/web/connect` tests also pass with the Linux build.
- This PR's workflow run shows that the Linux rebuild equals the committed package.

author: trendvidia
body:
Advances #11. It doesn't close it: what to do about v0.12.0's binaries is still open (below).

**The problem.** v0.12.0's binaries report themselves as `alidade v0.0.0-20261014064831-56503fac9adf`, not `v0.12.0`. The release job checks out only the commit, with no tags. Stock Go stamps a version only from a tag it can see. v0.11.0's binaries were checked out the same way but said `v0.11.0`, because the Go fork that built them didn't need to see the tag.

**The fix.**
- The build job now fetches the release tag and fails unless the tag points at the commit the gate passed.
- After building darwin/arm64, the binary the runner can run, it fails unless `alidade version` reports the tag.

**Evidence.**
- *The cause, with stock Go 1.27.2 from go.dev:* in a checkout that fetched only commit 56503fa, the build reports `v0.0.0-20261014064831-56503fac9adf`. After fetching the `v0.12.0` tag, the same build reports `alidade v0.12.0 (56503fa, go1.27.2 darwin/arm64)`.
- *The new steps, run as written against that checkout:*
  - tag check, right commit: exit 0
  - tag check, wrong commit: exit 1 (`::error::v0.12.0 is at 56503fa…, not ca33cd2…`)
  - version check, binary without the tag: exit 1
  - version check, binary with the tag: exit 0
  - after fetching the tag, the tree has no changes, so the build doesn't get a `+dirty` version.
- actionlint passes.
- *Not run:* the workflow itself. Only a pushed tag or a dispatch builds anything, and a dry run stops at the gate. The first real run is the next release.

**Open, for the owner.** v0.12.0's published binaries keep the wrong version string. They work otherwise: all four downloads, fetched without a token, match the checksums. The options:
1. Leave v0.12.0 as it is, and let v0.12.1 ship with the fix.
2. After this merges, run the release workflow by hand for `v0.12.0`. That replaces its published assets, so their checksums change.

I'd recommend (1). The defect is cosmetic, and v0.12.1 runs these new steps on a real release, which (2) does just as well while changing files people may already have downloaded. What would change my mind: anything that reads the version string to decide something, which nothing in the repository does today.

author: grassgod
body:
## Summary

归档上传让 daemon 把 trace 和会话打包传到服务端，链路复杂，却没有解决 daemon 磁盘被代码工作区占满的问题。本 PR 按 ADR 0018 去掉归档上传：记录（trace 与 provider 原生会话历史）永久留在 daemon，Issue/Chat 结束后代码工作区可回收，回收前把未保存的 git 工作做成本机快照，重新打开时恢复。

- 删除会话归档整条链路：服务端模块、路由、表与脚本，Web 归档界面，CLI `session archive` / `issue archive` / `session config`（改为退役提示），部署里的归档存储与 nginx 直传。
- trace 与原生历史留在 daemon；服务端只记 `daemon | none | lost` 指针，读取经 daemon 回源。
- 新 daemon 布局 `registry/ work/ env/ traces/ shared/ .daemon/`；启动时一次性把旧布局移入 `legacy-<日期>/`，7 天后删除，有未保存工作的进 `retained/` 不删。
- 回收引擎：结束且超过保留期（默认 72h，自动化 24h，最多保留 50 个）的主体先检查树里每个 git 仓库。共享缓存的 worktree 有未保存工作则写快照 ref `refs/remi/snapshots/<主体>/<n>`；独立 clone 有未保存工作则保留主体并在报告里给出原因；wiki 改动另存。重新打开时按目录恢复。provider 自己维护的状态（如 Codex `.tmp/plugins`、`memories`）不检查。
- Issue 与 Chat 统一生命周期；自动化 `run_only` 运行变成带来源的真正 Chat，`remi automation quiet` 让无事可报的运行完成后自动归档；空闲 Chat 默认 14 天自动归档。
- 存储设置 `settings.storage`、每台 daemon 的存储报告、预演/立即回收：API、Web 设置页「存储」、Runtime 详情卡片、CLI `remi workspace storage`、`remi runtime storage|gc`。
- 数据库迁移：归档表改名为 `multiremi_legacy_*` 保留；已归档的 trace 指针标为 `lost`；agent 会话线代数加一并清空 provider 会话；新增存储报告与 GC 请求表、Chat 来源列。

## Why

daemon 磁盘主要被代码工作区占用，trace 与会话很小。上传归档没有释放代码目录，又引入打包、上传、回填、重试与恢复链路。记录留在原地、只回收可重建的工作区，链路更短，恢复只依赖本机 git。

ADR: [0018 本地记录与可回收工作区](https://github.com/Grassgod/Remi/blob/9fb17d34435a00b38e7e7614598db18ea3e8dae8/docs/adr/0018-local-records-and-recyclable-workspaces.md)，取代 ADR 0006 决策 5–9。main 已用 0017 记录 Issue 执行与上交，本 ADR 顺延为 0018。
Spec: [存储与保留](https://github.com/Grassgod/Remi/blob/9fb17d34435a00b38e7e7614598db18ea3e8dae8/docs/dev/storage-retention.md)、[Runtime 工作区](https://github.com/Grassgod/Remi/blob/9fb17d34435a00b38e7e7614598db18ea3e8dae8/docs/dev/runtime-workspaces.md)、[daemon 协议 v2](https://github.com/Grassgod/Remi/blob/9fb17d34435a00b38e7e7614598db18ea3e8dae8/docs/daemon-protocol-v2.md)。

## 部署注意

- CI job `session-archive-platform` 改名为 `runtime-platform`。合并前需要管理员把分支保护里的必需检查换成新名字，否则 PR 会一直等待旧检查。
- 先部署 API（启动时执行迁移），再逐台升级 daemon；先在一台上用存储页「预演一轮」确认回收计划。
- daemon 首次启动会把工作区根目录下不属于新布局的条目移入 `legacy-<日期>/`，部署前确认根目录下非 Remi 目录的归属。
- 移除机器上之前为止血加的禁用 GC 的 systemd drop-in。
- 历史影响（已确认接受）：旧归档不再读取；历史执行过程显示为不可用；历史 Issue/Chat 下次执行开新的 provider 会话。

## 已知限制

- 有未保存工作的独立 clone（不在共享缓存里）会让主体一直保留，存储页显示 `snapshot_failed`，需要人工处理。
- 被仓库或机器全局 gitignore 忽略的文件不进快照，回收时删除。
- 仓库检查深度上限 6 层；`freed_bytes` 是近似值。

## Test plan

Bun 1.3.14，基线为 `36472e93a`。

- [x] `tests/unit/daemon`：1512 pass / 55 skip / 15 fail，15 个失败与基线同名（宿主 hooks、网络、负载相关），无新增。

- [x] `tests/arch/` 279 pass；`bunx tsc --noEmit` 0 错误；`docs:test`、`docs:check`、`snapshot-api-routes --check`、`cli:capabilities:check` 通过。

## Summary

- Require every parameter on hidden model factory compatibility overloads restored by MPG, consistent with TypeSpec #11832.
- Keep the visible-primary replacement path unchanged; strengthen its existing lifted-value-type safeguard to assert that published optionality remains intact.
- Add a DataProtectionBackup-shaped regression that checks both the hidden legacy enum overload and the current settings-model overload. Preserve the original expectations unchanged.

## Blocked on upstream — keep this PR in draft

Prerequisite: https://github.com/microsoft/typespec/issues/12178.
