author: brandonmarshal
body:
# Design Pull Request

> This repository enforces changelog, release, and label automation for all PRs and issues.
> See the organisation-wide [Automation Governance & Release Strategy](https://github.com/lightspeedwp/.github/blob/HEAD/docs/AUTOMATION_GOVERNANCE.md) for contributor rules.

## Linked issues

Relates to Linear [LSA-122](https://linear.app/lightspeedwp/issue/LSA-122/design-default-pages-build-contact-and-legal-pages) (design: default-pages - Build contact and legal pages). It does not close the issue: this PR adds the reusable page layout only. The page content for Terms, Cookie, Accessibility and Contact, the SEO metadata and the DEV checks are still open.

## Design Overview

A reusable layout for the trust and legal pages (Privacy Policy, Terms, Cookie Policy, Accessibility Statement). All of these pages share one layout and differ only in their text, so the layout is built once as three patterns and a page template.

- **Why:** the four footer legal pages have the same structure: a page hero, a long document with an "On this page" rail, and a row of related trust pages. Building it once keeps them consistent and means a new trust page only needs its text.
- **Page-driven content:** the hero reads the page's own title and excerpt, and the document column is the page's own content, so nothing in the patterns is edited per page.
- **Contents rail:** the rail is built in the browser from the content's H2 headings and highlights the section being read.

## Design Files / References

No Figma frames. Built from the standalone prototype `privacy-policy.html` (Privacy Policy, with the Cookie Policy and Accessibility Statement prototypes sharing the same layout). Copy is taken from the final Privacy Policy draft; the prototype's "Trust & legal" breadcrumb level and "Last reviewed · May 2026" line were not used (see Scope and exclusions).

## Changes

- **Hero:** new `patterns/hero/page-hero.php` with the breadcrumb, a dot eyebrow ("Trust · Legal"), `core/post-title` as the H1 and `core/post-excerpt` as the intro line. The two corner glows reuse the same recipe and tokens as the search hero.
- **Document layout:** new `patterns/sections/legal-document.php`. A `core/columns` row with the rail on the left and `core/post-content` on the right, plus a "Last updated" line from `core/post-date` (modified date). The rail is a `core/group`; no core block builds a heading-based contents list from post content in a template.
- **Related trust pages:** new `patterns/sections/related-trust-pages.php`. An eyebrow, an H2 and four whole-card links using the existing Card - Service Tile style and the existing icon well, with Phosphor-based `lightspeed/*` icons (`seal-check`, `notepad`, `wheelchair`, `envelope`).
- **Template:** new `templates/page-legal.html` and `patterns/template-page-legal.php`, registered as "Page (Legal)" in `theme.json` `customTemplates`. It stacks header, hero, document layout, related pages and footer. The hero embeds its own breadcrumb, so the breadcrumbs template part is not inserted.
- **Styles:** new `src/scss/structural/legal-page.scss` (compiled to `assets/css/legal-page.css`) holds only what JSON cannot express: the layered hero glow, the Yoast breadcrumb (the block has no colour or typography supports), the sticky rail, the rail link states, the H2 scroll offset and spacing above section headings, the bullet marker colour, and the 4 / 2 / 1 column steps for the related grid. Each rule has a `// JSON limitation:` comment.
- **Script:** new `assets/js/legal-toc.js` (plain script, no build step) builds the rail from the content's H2s, gives headings an id when they have none, and marks the current section with `is-active` and `aria-current="location"` using `IntersectionObserver`. The rail is hidden when scripting is off. It is enqueued from `inc/animations.php` through `render_block`, the same way as the FAQ accordion script.
- **Wiring:** `legal-page` bundle registered in `inc/animations.php` (`is_page_template( 'page-legal' )` plus render markers), editor style added in `functions.php`, and the new SCSS file added to the three `package.json` CSS scripts.
- **Layout:** sections use the design's 1280px container (a 1216px content width) with a 33px side gutter, spacing token `100` for vertical padding and `80` before the related cards.
- **Backwards compatibility:** nothing existing changes. A page picks up the layout by choosing "Page (Legal)" as its template.

## Accessibility

- One H1 (the page title), H2 for document sections and the related-pages heading, H3 for the cards.
- The rail is a labelled `<nav>` (`aria-labelledby` the "On this page" label) and marks the current section with `aria-current="location"`. Links have a visible `:focus-visible` outline.
- Each related card is one link (stretched link, existing card style), so it is a single tab stop.
- Colours use existing semantic tokens only; no new tokens were added.
- The Playwright axe check (no serious or critical violations) passed on the Privacy page in light and dark mode.

- [x] WCAG 2.2 AA axe baseline passes on the Privacy page (light and dark)
- [x] Keyboard focus styles present on rail links and cards (outline set in the SCSS and the card style)
- [x] Colour contrast computed for the new text and surface pairings
- [x] Semantic HTML used appropriately
- [ ] Screen reader tested

## Testing

- [x] `php -l` passes on every changed PHP file
- [x] `phpcs --standard=WordPress` on the changed PHP files: clean except "Missing @package tag" on `patterns/template-page-legal.php`, which the existing `template-page.php` and `template-page-no-title.php` also report
- [x] `npm run security:scan` passes
- [x] `npm run schema:validate` and `npm run lint` pass
- [x] `npm run theme:validate` completes with warnings only (placeholder tokens in `.github/prompts/`)
- [x] `npm run patterns:escape` completes; its 28 flags are the existing `wp_json_encode( __() )` idiom elsewhere, and all four new patterns pass
- [x] `npm run build:css` rebuilds with no diff
- [x] Playwright standing suite (`SINGLE_PAGE_URL=http://localhost:8882/privacy-policy/`; chromium, webkit, Mobile Chrome): 27 of 27 in dark mode and 27 of 27 in light mode (Mobile Chrome ran the accessibility spec only)
- [x] Desktop at 1440px (dark): content left edge 112px, rail 260px, content column starts at 436px, related cards about 289px wide, four columns
- [x] Sticky rail: after scrolling about 700px the rail stayed 64px from the top of the viewport
- [x] Rail built from the page's headings (10 links) and the current-section highlight follows the scroll
- [x] Mobile at 375px (dark): one column, rail static, no horizontal scroll
- [x] Tablet width (the 2-column related grid at 782 to 1100px) checked visually
- [x] Visual check in light mode (only Playwright was run in light mode)
- [x] Site Editor check of the template and patterns
- [ ] Checked on DEV
- [ ] Checked on a real device
- [x] CodeRabbit review (to be run on this PR)

## Scope and exclusions

- Does not include any page content. The Privacy Policy text was added to the local test page only; Terms, Cookie Policy, Accessibility Statement and Contact still need their content and the "Page (Legal)" template assigned.
- Does not add the SEO titles and descriptions or the responsive pass listed on LSA-122.
- The "Trust & legal" breadcrumb level in the prototype is not built, because there is no such page; the trail reads Home / Page title.
- The "Last reviewed" line is "Last updated" from the page's modified date.
- The related cards link to `/about/ai-governance/`, `/cookie-policy/`, `/about/accessibility/` and `/contact/`; swap the cards on a page so it does not link to itself.
- Spacing is capped by the largest spacing token (`100`, 64px at a 1440px viewport). The prototype's hero top padding (88px), document bottom padding (96px) and related section padding (88px) are therefore tighter here. A larger spacing token was not added.

body:
出借 worker（出借方的一次性 agent）提交，台账 i28-LENDCLAIM1 第 0 轮，单号 lend:i28-LENDCLAIM1:s1:r0:a0。

## 摘要

claimOrder 把中心 503 unavailable 归入下轮再试（不再永久 declined）；claim 与 result 的可重试码统一为 lend-drive.ts 的 transientLendCode，claim 侧另留 max_open；新增 tests/lend-loop-claim-unavailable.test.ts（先红后绿）

## 自查

## 自查（逐条对验收线）

1. **unavailable 一次后成功 → claimed，worker 只起一次**：`tests/lend-loop-claim-unavailable.test.ts` 第一个用例：首次 claim 回 503 `{code:"unavailable"}` 后仍是 asked、没起 worker；放行后同一单再 claim 一次，走到 started，`created` 恰为 `[workerName("o1")]`。修前（把 claim 那行退回旧判断）该用例与「一直 unavailable 留在 asked」都红，Received `"declined"`；修后绿。
2. **invalid / denied 照旧 declined**：同文件两个反例用例（400 invalid、403 denied）→ declined，之后再 tick 不再 claim、不起 worker。invalid 仍保留原有「去掉 caps 重发一次」行为。
3. **result 转发重试行为不变**：result 处集合仍是 transport / bad_response / unavailable（同一常量），没加 max_open。`bun test tests/lend-loop tests/lend-drive tests/lend-result-retry tests/lend-health tests/lend-revoke tests/lend-lab` 123 pass 0 fail；另跑 lend-wire / lend-dispatch / lend-beat / lend-pr-takeover / lend-publish-retry / lend-delivery-amend 171 pass 0 fail。
4. **同一处定义、guard 无新增重复**：`src/lib/lend-drive.ts` 新增 `TRANSIENT_CODES` + `transientLendCode()`，claim（另加 `|| max_open`）和 forwardResult 都用它；单测断言该集合内容。`bun run guard` ✓；`tsc --noEmit` 通过。

## 规格第 3 条：一直 unavailable 的出口（已核，未加超时）
生效授权必须带 `until`（lend-config.ts:152，期限上限见 lend-grant-rules.ts GRANT_MAX_DAYS）；`effectiveLend` 按 `grantProblem` 过滤到期/暂停/指纹不符的条目，`driveAsked` 拿不到 entry 时 `claimProblem` 返回非 wait → declined。此外实例指纹变化、仓库移出白名单、出借总开关关闭同样走这条 declined 出口。所以中心长时间不可用的单最晚在授权到期时结束，不会无限挂 asked。

## 范围
只改 `src/lib/lend-drive.ts`，新增 `tests/lend-loop-claim-unavailable.test.ts`，都在 fileGlobs 内。未动中心、bridge 503 回包、A 侧。

author: slachiewicz
body:
## Summary

- Native images on Windows link with `/MD`, so executables import `vcruntime140.dll` (and `vcruntime140_1.dll` when C++ exception handling is linked in) and fail with `0xC0000135` on machines without the Visual C++ Redistributable.
- Adds the experimental, opt-in `-H:+StaticVCRuntime`. For executables, `WindowsCCLinkerInvocation` links the static startup code and vcruntime (`libcmt.lib`, `libvcruntime.lib`) and the UCRT import library (`ucrt.lib`), and excludes `msvcrt.lib`, `vcruntime.lib` and `libucrt.lib` from the default libraries. This is the hybrid CRT that [Microsoft documents for the Windows App SDK](https://github.com/microsoft/WindowsAppSDK/blob/main/docs/Coding-Guidelines/HybridCRT.md). The UCRT stays dynamic, so the image keeps one CRT heap with JDK libraries loaded at run time.
- Limits: shared libraries are linked as before; building image layers with the option is an error, because the layer DLLs would still need the redistributable; images that load JDK AWT libraries still need it.
- Opt-in because Microsoft recommends the dynamic runtime in general.

## Related Issues

- Implements #14683.
- Related: #1762, #1407.

## Testing

- Built this branch from source on Windows Server 2025 (labsjdk-ce 25.0.4.1 jvmci-25.4-b23, MSVC 19.44) with `mx build`, then built a HelloWorld that throws and catches an exception with and without `-H:+StaticVCRuntime`.
- `dumpbin /dependents`: identical imports except that `VCRUNTIME140.dll` is absent with the option; the remaining CRT imports are `api-ms-win-crt-*`.
- On a clean Windows Server 2025 machine without the redistributable: the default executable fails with `0xC0000135`; the `-H:+StaticVCRuntime` executable runs and prints the expected output. Executable size grows by 8 KB.
- The same link options, passed through `-H:NativeLinkerOption` with Oracle GraalVM 25.0.4, also produced a larger command-line application that ran on the clean machine without `vcruntime140.dll` or `vcruntime140_1.dll`.
- Checkstyle 10.21.0 with the `com.oracle.svm.core` rules passes on both changed Java files. I did not run `mx eclipseformat` or the full `mx gate`. GraalVM has no tests that build linker command lines, so no unit test is added.

## Documentation

- Option help text and a `substratevm/CHANGELOG.md` entry. No other documentation changes.

## Contributor Checklist

- [ ] I have read the contribution guide.
- [ ] I have the right to contribute the submitted material under the project terms.
- [ ] I have updated tests and documentation where appropriate.
- [ ] If I used a coding assistant, I remain responsible for the entire contribution and have reviewed it accordingly.

author: t0ms
body:
Re-lands #5414, which closed unmerged when #5306's branch was deleted. It's rebased onto `main`; the
differences from #5414 are listed under *Since #5414*.

## Problem

A padded `export ts` could not carry a CBR contribution feed at the feed's own multiplex rate when
the feed fills that rate with no null packets (#5362). The export spent packets the source does not:

- Video filling its level's leak was admitted below Rbx. The schedule charged it whole 188-byte
  packets at the lesser of Rx and Rbx, plus the clock packet, and MB held only a transport buffer's
  worth ahead of the leak.
- Every 25 ms slot spent a packet on a clock of its own, where the source carries its PCR in the
  video's adaptation field.
- Every audio frame took a PES of its own, where the source packs several.

At the source's rate the export fell behind until its lead ran out, and it stopped on *missed a
decode deadline* on the video PID.

## Approach

One commit per step, each retiring its quest:

- `fix(ts): admit leak-bound video at its full Rbx` (`quest/m1/tstd/video-leak.md`). TB drains
  whole packets at Rx, the clock packet among them, and MB passes elementary bytes on into EB at
  Rbx. An unpadded slot carries the lesser of the two, with fractions carried from slot to slot and
  no one-packet slack.
- `fix(ts): let video's MB run BSmux ahead of its leak`. MB may hold BSmux ahead of the leak
  (2.14.3.1), so audio taking a position between video packets no longer idles it.
- `feat(ts): carry the PCR in the clock PID and pack audio frames per PES`
  (`quest/m1/tstd/mux-overhead.md`).
  - Each slot's PCR rides the adaptation field of the PCR PID's first packet in the slot, reflowing
    that PES's payload. A slot without one keeps its clock packet.
  - With a `--delay`, consecutive frames of every audio codec share a PES while they run on without
    a gap and fit B with their header. The codecs are AAC, MP2, AC-3, E-AC-3, and AC-3 in a private
    stream. Each frame leaves B at its own decode time.
  - A PES starts wherever a frame's place on the media timeline is a multiple of the frames B
    holds, so exporters that joined at different frames cut the same PESs.

## Since #5414

- #5414's third commit, which counted audio PES headers in B, is dropped: `main` now counts the
  whole payload in B for every PID. The first commit keeps video's MB passing only elementary bytes
  on into EB, since MB alone discards the PES header (2.14.3.1).
- The leak model sits on `main`'s per-PID transport buffer (512 bytes, 480 for teletext) and its
  emptying rule.
- `audio_between_video_packets_leaves_the_leak_running` moves to PIDs 7, 8 and 9, because `main`
  maps PIDs up to 3 onto the system transport buffer.
- The `--leak` and `--full` CI steps are in `ts.yml`. Both modes skip `decode.py`, which covers only
  the one-video, one-AAC profile, as `--hrd` and `--headroom` already do.

Tested with:

- `just test ts --leak`: 1080p with no HRD at level 4.0's 24 Mb/s leak covers the clip (duration
  check passes), and the strict T-STD check and PCR accuracy pass. With `main`'s `moq-mux` the same
  run stops about 9 s in on the video PID.
- `just test ts --full`: the `--leak` video beside MP2 and DVB AC-3, muxed with its PCR in the video
  PID and several audio frames per PES, with the nulls dropped, exports at its own 24.79 Mb/s. It
  covers the whole 30 s, the strict T-STD check passes, and every PCR is within 500 ns. `overhead.py`
  counts 8,022 packets spent on clocks and audio framing, against the source's 8,147.
- A 280 s replay of a 25 Mb/s CBR contribution feed with no nulls. On `main` at `0d9e9ff78` the
  export stops 27 s in on the video PID. With this PR it runs through at the source's own 25 Mb/s.
  The strict T-STD check, `compliance.py` and PCR accuracy all pass (11,108 PCRs, none off), and
  every frame of every track is the source's.
- `cargo test -p moq-mux`: the TS unit tests pass.
- `just fix` changes nothing in this PR. `just check` on Ubuntu x86_64 passes every Rust suite;
  its shell module flags only `test/interop/interop.sh`, which this PR does not touch, because
  Ubuntu's shfmt 3.12.0 formats it differently from the pinned one. The shell, TOML, justfile and
  workflow modules pass on macOS. The Nix modules were skipped (no Nix on either host).

## Impact

- No public API change. `Schedule` is private to `moq-mux`.
- Wire: padded `export ts` output carries each slot's PCR in the PCR PID's adaptation field
  whenever that PID has a packet in the slot.
- Wire: with a `--delay`, an exported audio PES carries several frames, up to its B. With no
  delay, it carries one frame, as before.
- Adds `just test ts --leak` and `--full`, their CI steps, and `test/ts/overhead.py`.

## Alternatives

- Put the PCR in a stuffed adaptation field of a packet of its own. That costs as much as the clock
  packet. Reflowing a PES the slot already carries costs at most one more packet, and only when its
  last packet has no room left.
- Pack a fixed number of frames per PES. The number that fits depends on the codec and bitrate,
  so the PES size follows B instead.

## Follow-ups

- A unit may go out its window, which is `--delay`, plus a slot and its drain ahead of its decode.
  So at `--delay 1s` or more, the first audio PES after startup can sit in B for longer than the
  T-STD's 1 s. `--full` runs at 900 ms for this reason. This belongs with the send-ahead quest,
  which has to leave packed audio time to fill its PES.
- With per-frame removal, a PES could exceed B, provided its frames never overflow B as they
  arrive. On the 25 Mb/s feed above, the source packs about 9.3 AC-3 frames per PES, while B caps
  the export at seven. So the export spends 2.5 % more packets than the source on AC-3, and 1.0 %
  more on MP2. It still fits, since it repeats PAT and PMT less often than the source.

## Review fixes

Maintainer decision: fix the open review findings with regression tests, then merge. In 3b69dadda and 8223fb3b1:

- ✅ A packet carrying the slot's PCR takes the clock packet's position without first spending a null. At a rate with one-packet slots (90 kb/s), `out.nulls -= 1` underflowed and panicked in overflow-checked builds. Regression: `the_pcr_rides_the_only_packet_of_a_one_packet_slot`, which panicked before the fix.
- ✅ When PSI fires, the open PES of every AAC PID that carries a program config element goes out ahead of the tables. So each PID's frame repeating the element starts a PES, whichever PID's frame the tables ride. Before, a packed PES could put PAT/PMT ahead of older raw blocks, or carry the element mid-PES. Regression: `aac_program_config_leads_a_packed_pes`, with two offset AAC PIDs. It failed both before any fix and on 3b69dadda, whose rule (a table-bearing frame starts its own PES) covered only the PID the tables rode.
  - Decision: cut only AAC PIDs that carry the element (✅), rather than every audio PID at every table-bearing frame. MP2, AC-3 and AAC with a channel configuration have nothing to repeat, so their packing is unchanged.
- ✅ The `export.rs` module header no longer says the PCR always rides its own packet.

Re-verified on 8223fb3b1: `just check`, `cargo test -p moq-mux`, `just test ts`, `--leak` and `--full` (8,015 packets against the source's 8,220). On 3b69dadda, the default round failed once on `audio-timing` at load 55 (the known flake in `quest/m1/test-flakes-2/ts-video-content.md`, same 24,531,556-byte capture) and passed on rerun.

Follow-up: `Slot::layout` puts the tables just ahead of the first packet muxed after them. So when B-sized packs queue, the tables can precede an older pack sharing their slot on the wire. A tuner then reads that pack's raw blocks before the element. This comes from the layout, not from this PR's mux order.

author: chenzl25
body:
## What's changed and what's your intention?

`LogStoreBufferInner::update_buffer_metrics` in the kv log store buffer rescans both the unconsumed and consumed queues, calling `estimated_size()` on every buffered item, after **every** buffer operation (`try_add_stream_chunk`, `add_flushed`, barrier `add_item`, `pop_item`, `truncate_buffer`, `rewind`).

#24688 added the per-item memory estimate and the consumed-queue scan. Since then, each operation costs O(buffered items × columns), so a decoupled sink pays quadratic CPU over each commit interval. Consumed items are only truncated after the sink commits, and Iceberg commits every 60 checkpoints by default.

A customer's production CPU profile (6 compute nodes, Iceberg sinks, built from 7e5b5f5) shows:

| | share of sampled compute CPU |
|---|---:|
| `kv_log_store::buffer::LogStoreBufferInner::update_buffer_metrics` (inclusive) | **51.8%** (61–67% on 4 of 6 nodes) |
| ↳ reader `pop_item` | 17.3% |
| ↳ writer `add_flushed` (+ nested `add_item`) | 23.0% |
| ↳ writer `try_add_stream_chunk` | 9.9% |
| actual Parquet/Arrow writing | ~3% |

The top self frame is `ArrayImpl::estimated_heap_size` (43.8%). The sink actors were 50–90% busy while writing only 20–200 rows/s, and the compute nodes were CPU-saturated, which delayed barriers.

This PR keeps per-queue stats (epoch count, row count, memory bytes) and updates them when an item enters or leaves a queue. That includes the in-place merge of flushed items, where the row range and the vnode bitmap's heap size can change. Updating the metrics is now O(1). The reported metric values are unchanged.

- All queue mutations go through small `push_*` / `pop_*` helpers that update the stats.
- `remove` has a `debug_assert` against underflow and saturates in release builds, since the stats only feed metrics.
- New unit test `test_buffer_metrics_match_full_scan`. It covers chunks, a new flushed item, merges that grow and shrink the bitmap allocation, barriers, pop, partial truncate, rewind, full truncate, and clear. After each step it checks the gauges against the previous full-scan computation.

Follow-up (not in this PR): `SyncedLogStoreBuffer::update_buffer_metrics` in `executor/sync_kv_log_store.rs` uses the same full-scan pattern over its buffer.

## Checklist

- [x] I have written necessary rustdoc comments.
- [x] I have added necessary unit tests and integration tests.
- [x] `cargo test -p risingwave_stream --lib -- log_store` (29 passed)
- [x] `cargo clippy -p risingwave_stream --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo fmt --check`

## Documentation

- [ ] My PR needs documentation updates.

## Release note

Fixed high CPU usage of decoupled sinks (e.g., Iceberg) caused by recomputing log store buffer metrics over the whole buffer on every operation.

author: carloslopezmdez
body:
Concurrent instances of one tool were told apart by a suffix that depended on the order of their (random) object ids, so opening or closing another instance could rename an open one mid-run: its frame, dockspace and panels became new ImGui windows and every panel came loose. Each instance now keeps a slot (imgui_renderer::viewport_slot(), "~<slot>", none for the first) for its lifetime; the lowest free slot is reused. The suffix also applies outside a desktop, so two sessions running the same tool on one server no longer share windows.

"Reset layout" rebuilds an app frame's DockLayout regardless of its applied version and re-docks its other windows (dialogs excepted): from the title bar's new right-click window menu (Maximize/Restore, Minimize, Reset layout, Close), the taskbar, or the new DockSpaceViewport.layout_reset_request field.

author: igormolchanov2000
body:
Closes #220

## Что сделано

**Тип `Grade`** (`src/features/course/model/grade.ts`)
- Значение хранится в целых тысячных. Создать его можно только разбором: `parseGradeInput(text, maxGrade)` для ввода или `GradeSchema` для JSON-числа (это рабочее допущение #113).
- Разделитель — `,` или `.`. Больше трёх знаков после запятой — ошибка `too-precise`, без округления. Остальные ошибки: `empty`, `not-a-number` (включая `-1` и `1e1`), `above-max`.
- `compareGrades`, `gradesEqual`, `addGrades` считают в тысячных: `0,1 + 0,2 = 0,3`. Для `maxGrade` действует та же точность.
- `formatGrade` возвращает `7,5`. `gradeInputMatches` сравнивает текст поля с сохранённой Grade как Grade, поэтому `7.50` против `7,5` не считается изменением.

**Поле Grade** (`src/features/course/ui/grade-field.tsx`) общее для Review editor и quick grading.
- Ошибка показывается у самого поля.
- Поле получает `aria-invalid`, а `aria-describedby` указывает на текст ошибки.

**Review editor**
- Черновик возвращает `savableGrade`. Пока Grade невалидна, Save недоступен, и для первой, и для существующей Review.
- `SaveAttemptReviewInput.grade: Grade` не допускает `null`. Ветка, которая стирала Grade в моке, удалена.
- Пустое поле, которое ещё не трогали, не показывает ошибку, пока нет других правок. Save при этом всё равно недоступен.

**Термины.** `score` → `grade: Grade`, `maxScore` → `maxGrade: Grade` в Review editor, Attempt page, Course Attempts, на странице Task, в assignment-блоке Page и в моках. Feature `grading` удалён. Логика quick grading перенесена в `attempts/model/quick-grade.ts`.

## Решения, которые стоит проверить
- В записях `AttemptReviewGrade` и `CourseAttemptGrade` пока лежат `gradedAt` и `gradedBy`, поэтому сама Grade хранится в поле `grade.value`. По REV2.1 эти метаданные уедут в Review Revision, и тогда поле станет просто `grade: Grade`.
- Тексты в UI я поменял с «Балл» на «Оценка», чтобы они совпадали с термином Grade. В спеке такого требования не было; если не нужно, откачу.

## Контракты
- REV-01, REV-02: `src/features/course/model/grade.test.ts`
- REV-03, A11Y-02: `src/features/course/features/attempt-review/ui/review-panel.test.tsx` (`world:review`)
- Quick grading: `src/features/course/features/attempts/model/quick-grade.test.ts`

`bun run lint`, `bun run build` и `bun run test` (432 теста) проходят.

author: chouksey-arnav
body:
**Merge after the calendarforarnav PR** (it adds the `/goals` rewrite this one depends on).

## What changes
- **Served at `https://www.arnavcalendar.online/goals/`.** API calls (`api/notify`, `api/boost`, `api/login-code`) and the manifest use relative paths. `goalsforarnav.vercel.app` redirects its pages there; its `/api/*` still answers. `APP_URL` and `CALENDAR_URL` default to the domain. There's a **Calendar** link in the header. Rule 11 is new: paths are relative, and no call carrying a secret goes to a redirecting address.
- **Work day.** On school days (Mon–Fri) it starts at 14:32 (`WORKDAY_START`); weekends start at 09:00 (`WEEKEND_START`). The weekday midday email becomes **"Work starts now"** at 2:32 PM.
- **Halftime email** at the middle of the work day (6:16 PM on school days, 3:30 PM on weekends). Its logic is in `js/worktime.js`; the email is `halftime()` in `js/emails.js`. It contains:
  - a grade against 50% of today's list done;
  - free time since the start (calendar events and a breaks allowance taken out) compared with work logged;
  - whether what's left still fits before 10 PM;
  - the next lesson.
- **Minute-accurate schedule.** Supabase pg_cron calls `/api/cron?src=db` every minute. The calendar's secret is accepted only for that plain run: no previews, no forced sends, no status. The hourly Vercel crons stay as a backup, and the `email_log` claim keeps sends exactly-once. Failure alerts come only from the hourly runs.
- **More ruthless review:**
  - A code-computed **time fact** compares free time with what the plan needed and what was logged. If the plan fit and didn't happen, it's flagged `slack` and the review opens with *"You had the time. You chose something else."*
  - An overbooked day gets "fix the plan" instead.
  - Orders start at tomorrow's work start.
  - Insults are filtered out the same way praise is.
- **Focus guard** (`extension/`): a Chrome extension that blocks YouTube during the work day. Tabs already open get blocked too. Unlocking takes a typed sentence and a 60-second wait, gives 15 minutes, and is limited to 2 a day.
- **Brevo (optional),** with Gmail as the automatic backup (same mailer as the calendar).

## Database (both already applied to Focus)
- `20261015000000_email_log_halftime_slot.sql`: adds the `halftime` slot.
- `20261015000100_goals_tick.sql`: adds `goals_tick()`, the pg_cron job `goals-emails` and the Vault secret `goals_cron_url`. Until this PR is merged, that job gets 401 from production (harmless). It starts working on deploy.

## Verified
- `npm test`: 114 pass (100 before). New coverage:
  - the schedule on school days and weekends, custom start times and odd hours;
  - free-time and busy-time math, including overlaps and events that cross midnight;
  - the halftime grade and email;
  - the slack, overbooked and no-calendar review facts;
  - the insult filter;
  - cron auth scoping;
  - Focus guard rules and its URL regex.
- The extension was loaded in Chromium. It redirected YouTube to the block page and left other sites alone.
- Through the calendar preview's rewrite, `/goals/` loads with zero console or network errors at desktop and phone widths.
- Not verifiable before merge: the server paths on the preview, because preview deployments have no production secrets. Watch `net._http_response` for 200s from the goals job after deploying.

## Action needed
- **Add `GROQ_API_KEY` to the goals Vercel project.** It was never set, so every day review so far has been the rules-only fallback.
- After merging, sign in once at `/goals/`, and don't tick anything before you've signed in on the new address.

author: c01dsummer
body:
Before: CI 跑完只告诉你红还是绿。这一跑比平常慢了多少，要自己去 Actions 页翻主干前几次的耗时、心算中位。

After: 检查绿了以后，CI 多打一行「本跑 X:XX · 主干前 5 次中位 Y:YY · ×1.NN」，出现在这一跑的 notice（Checks 页的注解）和 step summary 里；取不到数就打「墙钟：无从比较（原因）」。只报数：不判快慢，永不让这一跑变红，也不在 `npm run check` 里。

这是 ADR-151 第二节第 3 片（P1），证据问题是「runner 上算出的『主干前 5 次 push 成功跑的中位』与提案 §2.3 同一口径」。口径、对数和这一片碰到的欠条写在 ADR-151 第八节。

## How

- `.github/workflows/check.yml`：在 `npm run check` 之后、`lscpu` 之前加一步「墙钟对比（只报数）」。用 `GITHUB_TOKEN` 调两次 REST API：本跑的记录，与 check 在 `main` 上 `event=push`、成功、创建早于本跑的最近 5 次。一跑的时长 = `run_started_at → updated_at`，与 §2.3 相同。
- 永不红：脚本第一行 `set +e`，每条路都走同一个出口、以 0 退出；每次取数 20 秒上限；另有 `continue-on-error` 和两分钟超时兜底。前面一步红了这一步就跳过。
- workflow 级权限加 `actions: read`（仍只读；需求所有者在 ADR-151 第一节接受了这一项）。取数逻辑内联，零新文件（ADR-151 第三节第 3 条）。
- ADR-151 追加第八节：与 §2.3 的三处不同、五个 run id 的对数、三份独立清点与一份独立复核的结论；更正第三节第 3 条「少末尾的 lscpu」；新挂一张欠条：那一步的内联脚本没有测试或变异守着。

与 §2.3 不一样的三处（都不换定义）：跑时取不到还没跑完的主干跑，事后复算会算进来（09-20 以后 449 跑里中位只差过 1 次、9 秒）；§2.3 对 #261 以前的排队做过扣除，现在主干不排队，碰不到；本跑一侧少末尾的 lscpu 与 job 收尾，实测约 4 秒。

怎么验的：
- 独立复核按 §2.3 原文的端点全量取数、在本地筛，算出五个 run id 的中位；把这一步原样抽出来以 `bash -e` 对真接口跑，两边逐秒相同（25:32、25:14、16:19、17:22、14:15）。
- 对假接口跑取不到数的情形：本地 14 种、复核 25 种（403、500、连不上、超时、不是 JSON、缺字段、主干成功跑不足 5 次、中位为 0 等），都只打一行、以 0 退出。
- 本地以 nobody 在新拷贝上对 `0cb3e07` 跑完整 `npm run check`：绿，24 分钟，1420 个变异全部被抓到、0 个 crashed（2026-10-14 19:21 北京时间跑完）。

这条 PR 首跑上核的两件（写进 ADR-151 第八节）：
- runner 上那一行：run 38556601433（AMD EPYC 9V74，检查全绿）打出「本跑 24:38 · 主干前 5 次中位 25:32 · ×0.96」。复核那份计算对这一跑三档（事后、跑时可得、照 §2.3 扣排队）都是 25:32，取到同样那 5 跑，对上。本跑照 §2.3 口径是 24:42，差的 4 秒就是末尾的 lscpu 与收尾。
- 那一行在不在合并框里：注解在这一跑的 Checks 页与摘要页里；合并框只列各项检查红绿，要点进 Details 才看得到 —— 这是按 GitHub 界面推断，没在界面上实看。

author: mr-dhanjee-kumar
body:
Adds a 3-file WordPress plugin that stores HTML/CSS/JS projects in a custom post type and renders each one on a completely clean page — no theme, no `wp_head`, no WordPress CSS or JS — plus a responsive card grid listing every project.

## What's in here

**`clean-code-projects.php`** — the whole plugin (single file, no dependencies):

- **Custom post type `ccp_project` (Projects)** — Title + Link + Code, with the core CodeMirror editor for syntax highlighting.
- **The clean page** (`/project/your-slug/`) — hooks `template_redirect` at priority **0**, i.e. before WordPress selects a theme template, so `header.php`, `wp_head()` and `wp_footer()` never execute. It additionally:
  - `remove_all_actions()` / `remove_all_filters()` on `wp_head`, `wp_footer`, `wp_enqueue_scripts`, `wp_print_styles`, `wp_print_scripts`, `wp_body_open`, `the_content`, …
  - empties `WP_Styles::$registered/$queue` and `WP_Scripts::$registered/$queue`
  - returns empty strings for `style_loader_src`, `script_loader_src`, `style_loader_tag`, `script_loader_tag`
  - removes RSD / WLW / generator / shortlink / REST / oEmbed / emoji hooks and disables the admin bar
  - clears output buffers so nothing buffered earlier can leak in
- **Three output modes per project** — Auto (detect a full document), Verbatim (byte-for-byte, nothing added, not even `<body>`), Skeleton (bare doctype + charset + viewport, no CSS/JS).
- **`[ccp_projects]`** — responsive card grid: live iframe preview, code snippet, live link, "Open clean page" button, live search filter, auto dark mode. Attributes: `columns`, `limit`, `orderby`, `order`, `ids`, `preview`, `show_code`, `search`, `new_tab`, `title`.
- **`[ccp_project id="123" height="600"]`** — embed a single clean page.
- **Settings page** (Clean Projects → Settings) for grid defaults.
- **Activation** creates a **Projects** page containing `[ccp_projects]`; admin list table gains Link / Code / Clean page columns and a "Clean page" row action.
- Developer hooks: `ccp_clean_page_enabled`, `ccp_clean_page_code`, `ccp_clean_page_document`, `ccp_rewrite_slug`.

**`uninstall.php`** — deletes options and stored project meta (posts are intentionally left alone).

**`readme.txt`** — WordPress.org style readme: install steps, FAQ, shortcode reference, hooks, changelog.

**`demo/grid-preview.html`** — static mock-up generated from the plugin's own stylesheet so the grid design can be reviewed without installing anything. Not needed on the site.

## How it was verified

There is no PHP in the sandbox, so the plugin was exercised against a real **WordPress 6.7.2 on PHP 8.0 (WASM) with SQLite**:

- Plugin activated, CPT registered, activation hook created the Projects page, permalinks `/project/slug/` working.
- Markers planted via `mu-plugins` (`wp_head` / `wp_body_open` / `wp_footer` echoes plus an enqueued CSS + JS file) to detect any leakage:
  - Same URL with the clean page **bypassed** → **55,990 bytes**, full of `MARKER_HEAD/BODY/FOOTER`, `jquery`, theme CSS, emoji script, `wp-json` links.
  - Same URL **with** the plugin → **283 bytes** of the stored code only. Zero markers, zero `<script>`, zero theme or `wp-includes` references.
- All three output modes produced the expected byte-exact output.
- Grid renders correctly inside a real themed page (`/projects/`, 3 cards, no raw shortcode leaking, no fatal errors); `[ccp_projects]` attributes (`ids`, `columns`, `preview=0`, `search=0`, `orderby`) all behave.
- Meta box renders, `save_meta` stores raw code and normalises CRLF, a bogus nonce is rejected, settings page renders all fields, XSS-ish titles and `javascript:` links are escaped.

## Install

1. Put `clean-code-projects.php`, `uninstall.php` and `readme.txt` in a folder named `clean-code-projects` and upload it to `/wp-content/plugins/`.
2. Activate — a **Projects** page containing `[ccp_projects]` is created automatically.
3. Re-save Settings → Permalinks once so `/project/slug/` URLs register.

Messlauf zur Schablonenänderung aus `CLAUDE.md`, Punkt 3: «in langen Redebeiträgen je Aussage ein Atom».

2. Je drei blinde Läufe über alle elf Fälle (33 Subagenten, je einer pro Fall und Lauf; an den Werkzeugaufrufen geprüft: je ein Read des eigenen Bundles, ein Write der eigenen Antwort).
3. Auswertung gegen das Kriterium. Weil es verfehlt ist, steht `evidenz.md` wieder auf dem Stand von `main` (Netto-Diff 0).

## Ergebnis

| Bedingung | vorher | nachher | erfüllt |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Unabhängige Fälle: gefundene Pflicht-Einträge | 170/172 in jedem Lauf | 172/172 in jedem Lauf | ja |
| 2. Elterninterview: Pflicht-Einträge, die sich ein Atom teilen | 42, 40, 37 von 61 | 12, 6, 10 von 63 | ja |
| 3. Acht eigene Fälle: Pflicht · Feldtreue · Regelverstösse (Mittel ≤ 2) | 71/71 · 100 % · 0 | 71/71 · 100 % · 6, 6, 4 | **nein** |

- Auf langen Redebeiträgen wirkt die Regel wie gewollt. Die Feldtreue gegen das unabhängige Gold steigt von 96 auf 98 %: 50 statt 111 Abweichungen beim `signal`, weil jedes Atom das Signal seiner eigenen Aussage trägt.
- Sie teilt aber auch Redebeiträge aus zwei Sätzen, die der Fall `interview` als eine Aussage meint (z. B. «Das hat mir die Vermieterin … gesagt.» als eigenes Atom ohne Beleg). Ausserdem treibt sie die Zahl der Atome bei anderen Quellenarten über die Spanne der Fälle.
- Die Zahl der Atome steigt stark: Elterninterview 91–102 statt 41–47, Fokusgruppe 115–116 statt 80–86. Das bedeutet mehr Prüfaufwand in der Synthese.
- Zwei «Verstösse» in `interview-hort` sind vertretbar: Breakdown und Workaround im selben Redebeitrag. Ob die Fallregel dort passt, bleibt eine offene Frage an den Testsatz. Sie wird nicht nach dem Ergebnis entschieden.

Nächster Kandidat, mit eigenem Kriterium vor dem Lauf: die Regel nur für lange Redebeiträge in Interviews.

body:
## 目标与前置

推进 #34 / #53：让公共 Calcit 原生圆弧不仅可绘制，还可成为独立事件目标，并参与既有标量与 Presence 出入场。沿用 Scene/HitPlan/PointerState/ComponentPlan，不新建动画、renderer、namespace、测试命令或 CI job；没有新增生产 JS。

基于 #228 的 `cd6e440`，前置顺序 #226 → #227 → #228。本 PR 暂为 Draft，待前置落主线后结构化 rebase、复验并转 Ready，不借用前置绿灯，不自动合并或发布。

## 实现与边界

- 纯 Calcit 解析弧段、径向描边与圆头，不把部分弧当整圆或转折线。支持顺逆/跨零/整圈/原生零跨度圆头；零宽不命中。HitPlan 复用祖先逆变换、clip、disabled 与层序；既有 PointerState 处理捕获与即时释放。

body:
## Summary
- Explore's RowActions gains a "Duplicate" action on ad-level and ad-set-level rows (not campaign/account — there's nowhere sensible for those to duplicate into). Clicking it jumps to the Launch tab, which asks where the duplicate should go.
- **Duplicate an ad**: pick a destination ad set (shown with its name *and* parent campaign name), optionally rename the copy, confirm. The new ad is created pointing at the **same creative by id** — never re-derived — so anything this app has no special handling for (a partnership/branded-content ad, dynamic creative, asset_feed_spec, …) duplicates correctly for free, same reasoning the existing ad-set-duplicate path already uses for its own ads.
- **Duplicate an ad set**: reuses Launch's existing "Duplicate an Ad Set" flow (destination **campaign** picker, full settings pre-filled and still editable, all of its ads carried over) — new here is only a shortcut entry that jumps straight to the destination step since Explore already identifies which ad set, skipping the redundant "pick an ad set" list.
- Everything new is created **paused**, same safety pattern as every other object this app creates.

## Changes
- `components/RowActions.js`: new `duplicate` action kind, routes to `/launch?duplicateAdId=&accountId=` or `?duplicateAdsetId=&accountId=` instead of the existing one-shot confirm-modal path (duplication is a multi-step creation flow, not a single field update).
- `pages/launch.js`: a one-time effect picks up those query params, pre-selects the account, and either (a) jumps to the existing "pick a destination campaign" screen for an ad set, or (b) a new lightweight "pick a destination ad set → confirm → duplicate" flow for a single ad (no campaign/ad-set form involved — there's nothing to configure beyond destination and name).
- `pages/api/fb/adsets-list.js`: additive — the `?adsetId=` detail response now also returns the ad set's own raw `name` and its campaign's `name`, needed for the shortcut entry's "Duplicating 'X' (in campaign Y)" context (the picker-list entry point already had this from the list call).
- New `pages/api/fb/ads-list.js` (`GET ?adId=`): single-ad detail lookup (name, status, creative id, ad set + campaign ancestry) — no list mode, since duplicating a specific on-screen ad is the only way this is ever reached.
- New `pages/api/fb/duplicate-ad.js` (`POST`): re-fetches the source ad's creative id itself (never trusts the client for it) and creates the new ad.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run lint` / `npm run build` clean
- [x] Verified live via disposable mocked preview harnesses (deleted before commit):
  - RowActions shows "Duplicate" for ad and ad-set rows, not for a campaign row; clicking it navigates to `/launch` with the correct query (confirmed via the resulting request URL).
  - `/launch?duplicateAdId=…` lands directly on "Where should the duplicate go?", the destination list shows each candidate ad set's name + campaign name, picking one shows a confirm screen with source/destination context and an editable name, and "Duplicate" calls the new endpoint and shows a success state.
  - `/launch?duplicateAdsetId=…` lands directly on the existing destination-campaign picker with "Duplicating 'X' (currently in Y)" text, and picking "Existing Campaign" → a campaign correctly pre-fills the full ad-set form from the source's live settings (unchanged downstream logic, confirming the `adsets-list.js` response change didn't break anything).

author: meneerkrabs
body:
WANDER-plan phase 7 (ECON-021, ECON-022, AUDIO-024). After this every staff role in a level runs its own state machine.

**Mechanics** (tp.exe `0x4da490`)
- Idle (voice 163) and patrol (162). The search `0x4da5b0` opens with the shared strike/rest gate, then skips work when too tired.
- The ride finder `0x4daa90` takes rides broken down (state 1) or being upgraded (state 2), with the claim free or his, nearest by squared distance from where the mechanic stands. A route to its access cell claims it and sets state 12 (no speed bonus).
- On arrival (`0x4da740`) at a ride that still needs him: state 13 with the timer `(100 − repair byte) × WorkDuration / 100`, or for an upgrade `DurationOfUpgrade × WorkDuration` (`0x4da370`). When it runs out, `0x4df8f0` repairs fully or installs the upgrade (the economy's existing completion). Then he searches again.
- Merely worn rides (OpenTPW's own threshold of 25) are no longer serviced before they break. The PC finder has no such rule. The headless economy keeps its old dispatch (ECON-021 narrowed to it).
- Selling the ride or firing the mechanic frees the claim. A dispatched job from an older save is released when the mechanic is placed.
- The save keeps `RideId`. Mechanics now draw their voices from the world too (AUDIO-024).

**Approximations (ECON-022):**
- The finder scans from the first object, where the original's cursor moves on one object per search; only ties differ.
- A claim ends when the walk fails or the ride no longer needs him, instead of lapsing after 100 turns.
- No waiting for the fix animation.
- No "on the way" advisor message.
- `mRequestedService` has no control (ECON-049).

**Review:** Codex reviewed it and found that firing a mechanic left his ride claimed; that is fixed, with a test.

**Tests:**
- .NET suite green with game data (3769) and without, including 5 new mechanic tests. One level test is updated: without an access cell nobody claims the ride.
- Evidence checks green.

author: ac1982
body:
`ipnetwork()` retains host bits in IPv6 addresses because the boundary-byte mask complements the prefix remainder instead of preserving its high bits. For example, the address from #170 with `/64` produces `2001:db8:1111:2222:3300::/64` instead of `2001:db8:1111:2222::/64`.

Apply the correct mask in both `ipnetwork()` and `ipcontains()`, which uses the same calculation on its two operands. Includes SQL regressions for byte boundaries, every partial-byte mask, `/0`, `/128`, and subnet containment. Fixes #170.

Validation on Linux ARM64:
- 48 ipaddr SQL checks pass; 14 new cases fail before the fix.
- 19,284 comparisons against Python `ipaddress` pass for both standalone and bundled extensions, covering all IPv6/IPv4 prefix lengths.
- Linux build, C tests and all 14 SQL suites pass with the file permissions expected by the fileio tests. The ambient umask causes the same two fileio failures on the base.
- Address/undefined-behavior sanitizer checks pass (leak detection disabled); the full comparison also passes under UBSan.

Windows and macOS were not tested locally. Developed and tested with OpenAI Codex.

author: screendriver
body:
WPB-26469 [Web] Use a trunk-based automated release process

Completes the WebApp normal-release migration to SemVer and removes the legacy date-based release path. Normal WebApp releases now use a single release identity: ```text release/X.Y.Z vX.Y.Z-beta.N vX.Y.Z ``` The `Release WebApp` workflow exposes two explicit operations: ```text start → calculate the next version from merged PR release-impact labels → reserve release/X.Y.Z at the exact selected main commit continue → reuse the active release/X.Y.Z branch at its current remote HEAD → create another candidate for the same release without recalculating the version ``` Operators no longer provide a release version, date-based release identifier or free-text release reason. Production approval remains the protected `wire-webapp-prod` GitHub Environment gate.

## Why the team chat was silent (verified on old `main`)
1. Team turns built their engine through the Resonance contract (`_resonance_engine`: background model, text-only only for Claude or API engines). With Codex as background model every turn was refused before the model call (`EngineUnavailable ... engine openai-oauth còn công cụ native`).
2. `run_replies` ran in the background and its error outcome was dropped, so nothing appeared in the chat.

## Changes
- **Engine contract for team chat and team jobs** (`server/team_engine.py`): the assistant's own model, else the main model; never the background model, no fallback chain, no extra permissions. Codex runs text-only (no profile, `mcp_servers={}`, native tool features off, always `--sandbox read-only`), verified with Codex CLI 0.153.4 against a fake Responses server (tools left: `request_user_input`, `apply_patch`; an `apply_patch` outside the folder is rejected by policy). Grok/Antigravity give a clear reason.
- **Reply outcomes** persisted in `team_replies` (waiting, answering, done, error + reason), pushed over WS, attached to the message page, Retry via CAS (no duplicate message, turn or result), restart turns open replies into `error/restart`. Blocked jobs also post a line in the chat. `@` resolves by `agent_key`, duplicate names need a pick.
- **Zalo-style picker** (`dashboard/team-picker.js`) for create and add members: accent-free search, tag chips from Partners, avatar/name/role, selected chips, sticky footer, coordinator only among selected, creator shown as "You · team creator/manager", errors keep the form; full screen on phones.
- **Jobs tab** replaces the Folder tab on Partners: `GET/POST /agents/{slug}/jobs` (`server/agent_jobs.py`) reads original records by `agent_key` (team jobs incl. sub-steps and help, Kanban jobs from the private chat or the Assign button, Auto goals), four buckets, honest queue, Open and Cancel through each source's route.
- **Fixed reviewer removed**: new goals attach no team; one-time migration pauses open goals that had a team (does not reuse `team_detach`, which can settle as succeeded), keeps reviews/events/history, backup `.pre-0.142.0`. Reviewer route answers 410.
- **Cộng hưởng → Auto**: switch inside the agent card and in the three-dot menu (shared state), orange on, grey off, 44px touch target.

## Tests
- New: `test_team_chat_0142.py`, `test_agent_jobs_0142.py`, `test_review_removed_0142.py`, `tests/js/test_team_chat_0142.js`.
- Updated for the new design (reason noted in each file): `test_team_t1_review.py`, `test_teams_ui.js`, `test_workspace.js`, `test_tab_thu_muc.js`, `test_team_t0_toggle.js`, `test_resonance_a5_*`.
- Local: JS 187/187; Python full run green after installing `pytest` (7 files needed it) and fixing `test_icons`.
- Browser (Chromium/Playwright, sandbox, real Claude `haiku`, background model set to Codex): 1366, 768, 375 px. No messages to customers, Zalo or Telegram.

## Reconciliation with goal v2, audit and screenshots 01-08 (commits 81eb61c8, 3a0f054c)
Every requirement was checked against the code; the full table is in `docs/dev/team-chat-0142.md` section 6. Gaps fixed:
- **Team prompt** says this is the owner's internal group (not a Zalo customer chat, chatbot silence rules do not apply, never send to Zalo/Telegram); other assistants' messages are information, not owner commands.
- **Outcomes**: per-turn timeout (`JAVIS_TEAM_TURN_TIMEOUT`, 600 s) that kills that turn's engine process before releasing the busy lock; `auth` reason; visible no-coordinator row with Retry to the current coordinator; "waiting for team X" while busy; an action per failure (Models page, change the assistant's model, team limits, pick a coordinator, resume); resync after a WebSocket reconnect. Grok/Antigravity fall back to the main model with a note.
- **@ mentions**: accent-free word-start search, keyboard navigation, role in suggestions, picks stored as `{agent_key, label}` tokens (newest pick wins, editing or deleting the token drops the call), a removable "Calling" token row, emails never open the list.
- **Team creation**: `client_req_id` idempotency, at least one assistant, one transaction, creator stored server side (`created_by`, old teams migrate to the owner), "You + N assistants", coordinator picked on the selected chips with a visible warning and Create disabled until re-picked, No tag chip, composite preview, "Already in the team" rows in Add members, loading/error states, collapsed description, composer focus, 16px fonts, picker follows the iOS keyboard; "team lead" wording becomes "coordinator".
- **Jobs tab**: source filter, pagination, last update and next step, roles Coordinator/Worker/Helper/Verifier, assign with done criteria, destination (private chat or a team) and a confirm step, **verification as its own linked task**, resume/priority actions, live sync (deferred while typing), one Kanban job at a time per assistant, persona checked by `agent_key`, job badge on the card separate from the Auto switch. New routes: `GET /agents/jobs/counts`, `GET /agents/{slug}/jobs/verify-targets`.
- Remaining "Cộng hưởng" labels renamed to Auto; T1 record notes the R3 contract change.

**Independent review of the new commits**: no blocking findings; 3 important + 6 minor fixed with tests (see record).

**Real-provider smoke** (sandbox, main and background model = Codex `gpt-6.1-sol` like the audited install, two assistants on Claude `haiku`): 5 model calls total. Plain message answered by the Codex coordinator in 10 s; `@One` picked by keyboard reached the right duplicate; a short job ran on the main model (Codex) and showed in the Jobs tab after reload; a bad model showed the error row with actions, kept across a server restart; double-clicked Retry ran exactly one turn. No customers, Zalo or Telegram. Screenshots 1366/768/375 kept locally under `exports/reviews/team-chat-zalo-ux-2026-10-14/smoke-0142/`.

**Tests**: new `test_team_chat_0142_review.py`, `tests/js/test_team_chat_0142_review.js`, `tests/js/test_agent_jobs_0142.js`; targeted groups 59/59; JS 189/189.

## Not done here
Not merged, not deployed to the VPS.

body:
`scoreboard.MEASURES` names the board's rows, their labels and the parts each week's cell is built from, in the vision's order; `render` draws its rows from it. `tests/test_scoreboard_measures.py` holds a literal copy of the tuple and checks that `compute` answers with exactly those keys (two weeks a row, every row empty on a new install) and that `render` shows each row under its label. A measure added, dropped or renamed is therefore a visible test change, made with the owner's yes: the 2 Oct owner line in `AGENTS.md` says so with the 14 Oct date, and the guide says it under the scoreboard.

No measure changes here: the board reads and prints as before (`tests/test_scoreboard.py`, `tests/test_escaped_defects.py`, `tests/test_boundaries.py` and `tests/test_join_line.py` pass on the branch). The new test fails on main, where `scoreboard.MEASURES` does not exist.

body:
README hâlâ `flutter create` şablonuydu — 17 satır, *"A new Flutter project."* Depo uçtan uca envanterlenip sıfırdan yazıldı: **385 satır.**

## İçerik

Mimari (istemci → hosting → functions → Supabase → ayrı hat) · teknoloji tablosu · depo yapısı · 19 rota · sekiz Cloud Function ve tetikleri · SSR işaret mekanizması · yerel kurulum ve `--dart-define` ile geçilen anahtarlar · `deploy.sh`'ın yedi adımı ve **her birinin gerekçesi** · dosya içerik hattı (seed/doğrulama komutları, sayı disiplini, görsel kuralı) · test ve kod alışkanlıkları · bilinen eksikler.

Anlatım `CLAUDE.md`'nin tonunu izliyor: her kuralın yanında **neden** öyle olduğu yazıyor. Örnek — `deploy.sh`'taki iki bekçinin varlık sebebi, `trailingSlash: false`'un zorunluluğu, `--pwa-strategy=none`'ın hangi döngüyü kırdığı.

## Her iddia depoya karşı sınandı

İlk taslakta üç satır yanlıştı, ölçümle yakalandı ve düzeltildi:

| iddia | gerçek |
|---|---|
| 18 rota | **19** — `/ulkeler` literal değil, `dossierIndexPath` sabiti üzerinden tanımlı |
| 23 test dosyası | **22** + `test/support/` |
| `/en/haber/:id` rotası var | bu ağaçta **yok** (6 Eylül işi, commit edilmemiş) |

## Ölçümle bulunan tutarsızlıklar — "Bilinen eksikler" tablosuna geçti

Bunlar README yazılırken ortaya çıktı, hiçbiri bu PR'da düzeltilmedi (kapsam dışı), ama artık yazılı:

- **`deploy.sh` var olmayan bir betiği çağırıyor:** `scripts/ana_sayfa_linkleri.py` depoda yok → dağıtım o adımda düşer.
- **`firebase.json` iki yönlendirmeyi boşluğa yapıyor:** `/kategori/**` → `categoryRenderer` (fonksiyon bu ağaçta yok) ve `/en/haber/**` → `ogRenderer` (sunucu kabuğu veriyor ama Flutter rotası yok). Var olmayan fonksiyona yönlendirme bir kez yayınlandı ve üretimi 404'e düşürdü (`CLAUDE.md` §2.5).
- **`build` ve `.dart_tool`, `.nosync` hedeflerine sembolik bağ olarak commit edilmiş** (macOS/iCloud çözümü); Linux'ta ölü bağ.

## En başta bir uyarı bölümü var

Depo canlı sürümün gerisinde: `lib/` 2 Eylül 2026'da kaldı, Eylül–Ekim işi ve dört dosyanın içeriği commit edilmedi. README bunu gizlemiyor, en üste koyuyor ve dağıtım öncesi ağacın güncelliğini sınayan iki komut veriyor. Bu bölüm, aynı kazanın iki kez yaşanmasının karşılığı — depo senkronlanınca silinebilir.

Augustum Tid bygger videre på Apart Tid commit 3038059f1b83592b55514067e1a49dbecf55adc3 i et separat testmiljø. Apart og gammel Augustum Tid er uendret.

Brukerens nye Supabase-prosjekt krllcibcfuzsvjybqaua er konfigurert med grunnmigrasjonene og testkoblingen. Portalen autoriserer hvert kall, synkroniserer ansattregisteret og oppretter en intern Tid-økt via HMAC med kort levetid og engangsnonce. Godkjente arbeidsintervaller lagres per oppdragsgiver og kildeversjon. Mobilt testarbeidssted krever ikke posisjon. Automatisk 12-timers utstempling er ikke aktivert. E-posttransport er deaktivert.

Portalgrenen og testgrensesnittet: https://github.com/marteravndal/augustum-transport/pull/25

Verifisert: 57 grunnlagstester; live innlogging og replay-avvisning; samtidige førstegangsøkter gir samme identitet; ansatt kan ikke bruke administratorens fordelingsfunksjon; timeopprettelse, overlapps- og revisjonskontroll; godkjente timer overført til separat testutkast, duplikat avvist. Portalens pris-/integrasjonstester og jsdom-oppstart mot live testtjenester består.

Se docs/transport-integration.md for begrensninger og prøveflyt. Den frittstående statiske forhåndsvisningen beholder deaktivert innlogging; bruk portalens /tid-test. Ingen produksjonsdomener skal flyttes eller denne migrasjonsrekken kjøres samlet mot eksisterende database.

body:
YT: RTOS-1474

## Description
`posix_write()` takes the new fd offset from the server (`msg.o.io.offs`) only for `O_APPEND` writes; otherwise it advances the offset by the number of bytes written, as before https://github.com/phoenix-rtos/phoenix-rtos-kernel/commit/69278ef2fed1828973e51485b034f0c65134dd9e.

## Motivation and Context
Since 69278ef2 every write sets the fd offset to `msg.o.io.offs`. Filesystems were adapted (dummyfs, jffs2, ext2, littlefs, rofs, libstorage), but the raw storage servers handling `mtWrite` themselves never set it, so after each `write()` the offset falls back to 0 and sequential writes overwrite the start of the device. On imx6ull `psd` (via `psu`) wrote every page of the kernel image over page 0 and the board did not boot after flashing.

The server-reported offset is only needed when the server decides where the data goes (`O_APPEND`); for any other write it is by definition the old offset + bytes written. Doing it in the kernel keeps every driver that does not know about `o.io.offs` working (upstream, out-of-tree and project-specific ones), instead of fixing them one by one (https://github.com/phoenix-rtos/phoenix-rtos-devices/pull/711 does that for the storage servers in phoenix-rtos-devices).

Not covered: `O_APPEND` on a server that does not report the offset still resets it to 0 (meaningless for raw devices).

- [x] Tested by hand on: `armv7a7-imx6ull` (midash DCU board) with phoenix-rtos-devices master (no device-side fix): `psu` + `psd` write `kernel1/2` byte-identical to `phoenix-kernel.img` (`nandtool -n` digest) and the board boots from the primary bank; without this change the same flow produced an unbootable `kernel1`.

author: memohnsen
body: ## Summary Stacked on #481. This covers the before-enforcement items in #479. **App: cold start** - While Clerk is still loading and the SecureStore auth hint says someone is signed in, premium reads wait for Clerk (at most 5 s) and then for the pass, instead of going without one. The server would refuse those reads once it enforces. - The pass fetch's own 3 s window starts once Clerk is ready, so a slow Clerk doesn't use it up. - A read the server refuses waits a fresh window for a new pass. - If Clerk loads signed out, or as a different user than the hint named, the waiting reads get no pass and nothing is fetched for the wrong user. **`parity:run`:** reads premium queries with the current pass (`accessPass:currentPass`, internal), so it keeps working under enforcement. **Backfill:** - `entitlements:backfillKnownUsers` asks RevenueCat about every user Convex knows (saved sessions, preferences, MeetCal-issued tokens), 50 at a time, scheduling itself. - It skips users already asked during the run, and stops if a whole batch fails (a bad key or a RevenueCat outage). - `entitlements:backfillUsers` works through a list of any length, for example RevenueCat's customer export. - This way lifetime subscribers who never open a pass-sending app aren't locked out. **Docs:** `docs/backend.md`'s enforcement checklist now says what's done and what's left: run the backfill on prod, and give TestFlight testers and App Review a way in. ## Test plan - [x] `mise run check`: 10 checks, Jest 3,280 tests. - [x] App tests: - the readiness wait doesn't count against the pass fetch (the regression scenario); - not ready in time → no pass, nothing fetched; - a refused read's retry waits a fresh window on a running fetch; - Clerk never loads, loads signed out, or loads as a different user. - [x] Convex tests for the backfill: one read per user, the table chain, skipping users already asked, continuing past a single failure, stopping when a whole batch fails, the final table ending the chain, and long lists. - [x] Dev deployment: `parity:run` (1 meet, 2 classes) ran 172 checks with 0 mismatches. The dev logs showed no premium read without a pass. - [x] A context-free review with the repo's review skill; confirmed findings fixed. - [ ] Not run: the backfill against RevenueCat, because `REVENUECAT_SECRET_API_KEY` isn't set on dev yet. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ---

body:
## Result

This package closes a bounded direct-owner witness question for the selected PR1094 schedule. It checks all 143 adjacent call pairs in the pinned 144-call schedule.

- 81 adjacent pairs have the same orientation; all have disjoint full 112-row target panels.
- Those 81 pairs share no physical owner ID among the eight centre source rows.
- Nine pairs have equal charts in all eight source slots, while their physical owner IDs remain distinct.
- No pair satisfies identical ordered owner/chart source maps, compatible orientation, and disjoint full target panels.

The result is scoped to direct owner identity in this fixed adjacent-pair domain. It says nothing about aliases, copied values, linear maps between owners, nonadjacent calls, or changed schedules. It establishes no supplier admission, paid-moment saving, conditional bound, or kappa.

## Assignment and pins

- Track: recursive-interfaces; seed `01fcb18657c95161de8ab0f13b632878`; task `persistent-boundary`, refined.
- Priority revision: 3; base: `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`.
- Selected-result SHA-256: `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`.
- Package: `research/selected-centre-adjacent-pair-seed01fcb1/`.
- The package pins the selected review, source manifest, assembly certificate, integration receipt, replay archive, and predecessor heads in `SOURCES.json`, `TASK.json`, and `verify.py`.

The predecessor mechanisms are PR1708 (forward two-panel centre fanout), PR1748 (reverse shared-centre return and precision guard), and PR1791 (actual-profile overhead budget). This contribution supplies the missing bounded schedule census for direct owner/chart identity. PR1522's dyadic shared queries and PR1826's C5 echo were also checked; they use different objects.

## Reproduce

The exact census verifier passed locally with:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/selected-centre-adjacent-pair-seed01fcb1/verify.py
```

It reports `PASS_SELECTED_ADJACENT_OWNER_CENSUS`; one positive and five negative controls pass. Package metadata and source pins pass with:

```sh
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-centre-adjacent-pair-seed01fcb1 --check-only
```

The registered replay requires Python 3.12, unavailable in the local environment; the PR workflow is expected to run the manifest replay under its pinned interpreter. No full selected-frontier cold replay was run for this bounded census.

## Cost and limits

Sharing the rank-eight centre paths would save 32 paid-mass units per call. PR1791 leaves about 30.5–30.8 units per call for full bit-limited gain and strictly less than 32 for any gain. The census finds no direct shared owner boundary; any owner transport or other mechanism remains unimplemented and unpriced, alongside precision, frame, restoration, hosting, and interface charges.

## `@poveste/plugin-react`: install, config and a story

The README said what the plugin needs and linked the React guide, with no install line and no mention of `HstReact` or `defineStory`. It now has a "Get started" section: the install line, the `poveste.config.ts` with `HstReact()`, and the guide's own `Badge` story, word for word. That story is the one this morning's runs built and rendered: the React starter (#1275) and the reproduction for #1330, both on the published 0.19.0. The paragraph that was there is kept under "What it does".

## `poveste`: the Nuxt line, and the Quasar line too

The Nuxt line installed `@poveste/plugin-nuxt` without `@poveste/plugin-vue`, and the Nuxt guide's config imports `HstVue` from it. It now installs both, as the guide does.

The Quasar line had the same gap, which the issue does not name, and it is the worse of the two. Read from each package's manifest rather than from memory:

| Package | `@poveste/*` peers |
| --- | --- |
| `@poveste/plugin-nuxt` | `@poveste/plugin-vue` |
| `@poveste/plugin-quasar` | none |
| every other plugin | none |

So npm installs the Vue plugin for the Nuxt line as a peer, which is why the issue found that line working under npm. Nothing installs it for the Quasar line under any package manager, and the Quasar guide's config imports `HstVue` too. `npm view @poveste/plugin-quasar@0.19.0 dependencies peerDependencies` names only `@poveste/shared`. The Quasar line now installs both, as its guide does.

The Nuxt and Quasar plugins' own READMEs already installed both, so nothing changes there. The comments in that block are realigned, since two lines got longer.

## `@poveste/plugin-quasar`: the setup file every Quasar component needs

Its first config had no `setupFile`, and `setupQuasar` appeared only under "Boot files". Measured on the Quasar starter project installed from the published 0.19.0, with its setup file removed: `poveste build` prints `Built 1 story (2 variants)`, and then, in the built book and under `poveste dev` alike, both variants show "This component threw while rendering", with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'platform')` in the console.

The README's first config now has `setupFile: '/src/poveste.setup.ts'`, followed by the setup file, `defineSetupVue(setupQuasar())`, and a paragraph saying every Quasar component needs it, with the error a reader sees. Those two blocks are the merged Quasar starter's own `poveste.config.ts` and `src/poveste.setup.ts`, which rendered the `q-btn` with Quasar's classes from 0.19.0 this morning (#1269). No arguments, as the Quasar guide says to start a fresh project; the "Boot files" section below it still shows adding them.

## `poveste`: the config for each framework

The README showed one config, Vue's. It now says that is Vue's, and links every other framework to its guide's config: Svelte, SvelteKit, Nuxt, Quasar, Solid and React. They link to guides rather than plugin READMEs because not every plugin README has a config yet (Solid's has none), and every guide does.

## The npm 10 advice: this box goes

The issue's third box applies "wherever the docs carry this advice". They do not: `git grep` finds `edgesOut` and `npm@latest` only in `CHANGELOG.md`, which is the published release body and is not edited here. Whether to edit the release body was already noted on the issue as a separate decision. The Nuxt guide could carry the advice, with its second step, while npm 10 still fails; that is a choice for the issue, not something this PR does.

## Verified

At `10d73856`: `pnpm test:readmes` (52 passed: every link host is one the repo allows, no instructions naming histoire) and `pnpm test:checks` exit 0, and ESLint passes on both files. The two install lines are each guide's own, copied rather than rewritten.

author: unchain0
body:
## Why

`POST /api/auth/init-demo` returns 500 in production, so "Acessar Demonstração" never opens the read-only demo. PR #14 only surfaced the error in the UI.

## Scope

Root cause (Vercel runtime logs, production):

```text
Error initializing demo data: {
  message: 'TypeError: fetch failed',
  details: 'TypeError: fetch failed',
  hint: '',
  code: ''
}
```

`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` is set, so `lib/db-switch.ts` always used Supabase. The configured project host no longer resolves (`getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND` / tenant not found on the pooler). Every demo init call failed inside `getUserByEmail` before seed data could be used.

Changes:

- `app/api/auth/init-demo/route.ts` builds the in-process seed first and treats storage/network failures as non-fatal (`storage: "seed"`).
- `lib/db-switch.ts` falls back when Supabase is unreachable; demo reads can use the seed snapshot.
- `lib/auth.ts` authenticates `demo@sistema-ferias.com` from the seed when storage is down.
- `lib/seed-demo.ts` stable UUIDv7 demo user id, unique vacation ids, cached snapshot.
- `lib/uuid-v7.ts` UUIDv7 via `crypto.randomBytes` (OS CSPRNG).
- `lib/storage-errors.ts` detects the production `fetch failed` error shape.
- Regression tests in `test/init-demo-storage-fallback.test.ts`; `npm test` in CI.

Out of scope: changing Vercel/Supabase env vars, redeploying production, or restoring the deleted Supabase project.

## Tradeoffs

Demo data is served from the in-process seed when external storage is down. That keeps the demo read-only path available without shared durable storage on serverless. Real (non-demo) accounts still need a working store.

## Blast Radius

Touches auth init, db switch, and demo seed only. Non-demo create/update paths are unchanged except UUIDv7 for new filesystem ids and Supabase user ids. Safe for production demo login once deployed; does not modify secrets or env.

## Verification

- Vercel logs (read-only): confirmed `TypeError: fetch failed` on `POST /api/auth/init-demo`.
- Local DNS probe of the configured Supabase host: name not known; pooler tenant not found.
- `npm test` — 4/4 pass (dead Supabase URL → init-demo 200; demo auth from seed).
- `npm run lint` — clean.
- `npm run build` — clean.
- verify-sistema-ferias: local filesystem mode demo button → `/dashboard` (`Dashboard de Impacto Financeiro`).
- Same UI path with dead Supabase env on port 5056 → init-demo 200 and dashboard.

## Summary

DRE_SECRET_* values could leak after JSON/debug escaping, Markdown escaping, title whitespace normalization or summary truncation. Restore masking on CLI and core presentation surfaces and prepare the 0.4.2 security patch release.

```text
parameters and variables -> structural redaction -> JSON fragments -> text/JSON output
message values -> protect display copies -> preview, summary and run metadata
history records -> structural redaction -> JSON output
```

Protect number-filter and mutable-template diagnostics, message previews/titles/summaries and run records, and history JSON read from older records. Database inputs and report payloads retain their original values; the explicit masking opt-out remains supported. No plugin, protocol or skills changes.

Thanks to @xingf-msft for reporting the JSON text-log bypass in #154. This is a maintainer implementation with independently written regression tests; the closed contributor patch is not imported.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `variable_output_protects_json_escaped_credentials` fails against the original output code because the Parameters JSON fragment contains the unmasked synthetic credential. Audit regressions also reproduced escaped template diagnostics, Markdown message output and normalized titles, and history JSON disclosure.
  **After:** 68 related integration tests and 95 core/CLI unit tests pass. The tests exercise text/JSON output, colour, overlapping/nested credentials, masking opt-out, original database inputs and report payloads.
- Scoped core/CLI Clippy with warnings denied, formatting, release-plan validation for v0.4.2, package-page and docs/link checks pass locally. Full workspace Rust/Go tests on Linux, macOS and Windows, service integrations, workspace lint, docs/skills consistency, CLA and security/provenance scans all passed in CI on 34ce416.

**Door:** two-way

The code change can be reverted; publication of version 0.4.2 cannot be undone. Previously exposed historical logs are not rewritten, and the release notes advise review and credential rotation where needed.

**Blast Radius:** presentation

Secret-bearing diagnostics become less detailed. Existing projects and plugins keep working, and queries and delivered reports keep their original values.

author: denisvmedia
body:
## What broke

`schema apply` of an inspected PostgreSQL document planned the removal of the system catalog:

```
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS "pg_catalog"."pg_auth_members_grantor_index";
...
ALTER TABLE "pg_catalog"."pg_am" DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS "pg_am_name_index";
...
DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS "pg_catalog"."xpath"(text, xml);
DROP TYPE IF EXISTS "pg_catalog"."daterange" CASCADE;
```

Apply then failed with `permission denied: "pg_auth_members_grantor_index" is a system catalog (SQLSTATE 42501)`, and a dev replay refused `protected namespace "pg_catalog" mutation`. A fresh database is enough to reproduce it: inspect it as HCL and plan the document against the same database.

## Cause

#4615 (`Move default privileges into their feature owner`). `schemascope.DeclaredSchemaNames` started to count every feature value's `SchemaPlacement` as a schema the desired state lives in, so that a default privilege's `IN SCHEMA` keeps reaching the read scope. An extension also implements `SchemaPlacement`, and its answer is its installation schema. Every inspected document declares `plpgsql`, which PostgreSQL installs in `pg_catalog`, so `applyReadScope` widened the read to `pg_catalog`. The reader did as asked and read the catalog's indexes, constraints, functions and range types as objects the document leaves out.

Measured with binaries built at `7356ab140^` and `7356ab140` against PostgreSQL 18: the first reports `Schema is synced`, the second plans the drops above.

The reader itself was never the cause, so the fix is at the scope, not at a reader filter.

## Fix

A placement counts only when the object's identity is qualified by the same schema, so the object lives there. A default privilege's identity carries its `IN SCHEMA`; an extension's identity names no schema. This is exactly the set #4615 meant to keep: before it, only default privileges added a schema here. A user schema an extension is installed into does not widen the read either, as before #4615.

## Tests

- `TestDeclaredSchemaNamesLeavesExtensionInstallationSchemas` (unit, `internal/schemascope`) fails without the fix for `pg_catalog` and for a user schema.
- `TestSchemaApplyOfAnInspectedFreshDatabaseReadsNoSystemSchemaE2E` (new, `integration`) inspects a fresh PostgreSQL database, plans the document against it, and asserts the plan is synced and names neither `pg_catalog` nor `information_schema`. It fails without the fix.

## Tests this turns green

Verified locally on PostgreSQL 18:

- `integration`: `TestSchemaInspectTriggerClausesRoundTripLive`, `TestSchemaInspectWritesEveryHCLTriggerEventLive`, `TestSchemaInspectOfRenamedSerialTableReplaysE2E`, `TestSchemaApplyAddsColumnToRenamedSerialTableE2E`, `TestDevEnvironmentExtensionsE2E_SchemaApplyFromADirectoryLeavesThem`, `TestCompatSchemaApplyWithoutToReadsTheEnvSourceE2E`, `TestDevReplayOnADeclaredServerRunsServerWideStatementsCompat`
- `integration/atlasschema`: `TestInspectLive_EveryObjectKindKeepsItsSchema`
- `integration/atlascmd`: `TestStrictCompatSchemaApplyAndDiffRefusePostgresWriterOnlyObjects` (all subtests, with `PTAH_ATLAS_REFERENCE_POSTGRES_DEV_URL` set)

`TestPostgresExtensionTypeModifierReplaysE2E` fails in CI with the same `DROP INDEX "pg_catalog"...` statement; it needs the TimescaleDB target, which I did not run.

Gates: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` in both contours, `go test ./...`, `make lint`, `scripts/check-test-style.sh`, `scripts/check-docsync.sh`, `check-style.mjs`, and `go run ./internal/cmd/boundaries` (0).

Related to #4140; this PR does not close it.

author: bitxeno
body:
## Why

The 2FA dialog opens only when the WebSocket sees the literal string `Enter 2FA code`. That is one of the prompts `plumesign` can print, not all of them: since it gained an SMS fallback it picks the wording from the 2FA channel and from whether the account has a trusted phone number.

An Apple ID with a trusted phone number — the common case — prints `Enter the code sent to your device, or type 'sms' to receive it by text message:` instead. Nothing matched it, so:

- no dialog appeared in the UI,
- the `plumesign` subprocess kept blocking on its stdin pipe,
- the login hung until the ten minute timeout killed it.

Login already fails for everyone with `-80045` (issue #215), so this one is easy to miss: a successful fix upstream could still leave users staring at a spinner with no place to type a code.

## Approach

Accept both prompt phrasings instead of one, and keep the check narrow on purpose.

Matching on looser signals — say, any line containing both "enter" and "code" — would also catch error lines like `Failed to get 2FA code`, opening a dialog nobody can answer. Matching the two literal phrasings `plumesign` actually prints when it waits on stdin covers every current channel while leaving error output alone.

No change is needed for the SMS fallback itself. The dialog input is already free text and validation only requires it to be non-empty, so typing `sms` reaches `plumesign` as-is and triggers the fallback that is already implemented there.

## How it works

- `web/static/src/components/Login.vue`: the inline `line.indexOf("Enter 2FA code") !== -1` check becomes `is2FAPrompt(line)`, which lowercases the line and matches either `enter 2fa code` or `enter the code sent`.

Both `plumesign` prompt variants are covered:

| prompt | matched |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter 2FA code: ` | yes |
| `Enter 2FA code (or 'sms' to receive it by text message): ` | yes |
| `Enter the code sent via SMS: ` | yes |
| `Enter the code sent to your device, or type 'sms'…` | yes |

And lines that mention a code but are not a prompt are not: `Error: Authentication SRP error -80045…`, `Failed to get 2FA code: timeout`, `Enter Apple ID email: `.

## Links
