## Summary
PLAN M4-09 and M4-10. Flutter expenses against the frozen contract 0.6.1, using the generated client and the Prism mock. It reuses the incomes list and form pieces from #85, which this PR moves into `core/`.

### Refactor (first commit): shared with incomes
- `core/records/record_list.dart`: a generic `RecordListNotifier<T>` / `RecordListState<T>` (pages, totals, `hide`, optional header `legend`). `IncomeListNotifier` now extends it.
- `core/records/record_save.dart`: generic save outcomes. `income_save.dart` now uses them.
- `core/forms/form_leave_guard.dart` (with `confirmDiscardRecord`), `core/forms/money_suggestions.dart`, `core/fiscal/iva_math.dart`, `core/fiscal/iva_labels.dart`, `core/fiscal/regimes_held.dart`.
- PR #85 follow-ups:
  - `StackedUndo.notify` queues a plain toast behind a pending Undo instead of closing it. Incomes uses it now too.
  - `restoreEach` restores every item of a stacked Undo instead of stopping at the first refusal.
- Renamed ARB keys: `incomeDiscard{Body,Keep,Confirm}` → `recordDiscard*`. Added `recordErrorInvalid`. The incomes copy is unchanged.

### M4-09: list
- Shows one month of the active taxpayer's expenses, by `paid_on`, with the month switcher and regime filter.
- The header shows the mandatory legend from `ExpensePage.legend`, never a client copy. It shows on an empty month too.
- Totals card; rows show the category name when there is no description, plus a "No deducible" badge.
- Delete opens a persistent Undo toast for every account. Restore never answers 402 (0.6.1).
- A stacked Undo restores every expense it can and reports "Se restauró N de M gastos" plus the reason.
- Gated by `module_expenses` through `FlagGate` (`useFlag`) on home and the router's `FeatureModule`.

### M4-10: form page (more than 6 fields, so its own page)
- **Category**
  - Searchable picker over `GET /v1/taxpayers/{id}/expense-categories?regime=&on=`, most used first.
  - Below it: a plain-language hint (deductible, partial, not deductible, no ISR; RESICO PF adds a line about IVA; 606 blind 35 %), then the note and basis, then the server's legend.
- **Amount**: amount before IVA with a live "Total con IVA", all in integer centavos (no doubles). The IVA amount follows the rate until the user types the CFDI's.
- **Context fields**: IVA rate (the allowed ones), payment date, payment method (last used, debit card the first time), "¿Tienes factura?", regime only when there is more than one.
- **Cash warnings**: cash over the catalog's `cash_payment_limit_cents` (never hard-coded), or fuel paid in cash, shows inline warnings as soon as the amount and method imply it. They cover deductibility and `iva_not_creditable_cash_payment`, and they never block the save. "Sin factura" warns too.
- **Más detalles** (collapsed): IVA paid; the "¿Es deducible?" switch, which shows the suggested value until overridden, with "Usar el valor sugerido" to go back to it; folio fiscal (hidden without a CFDI); description.
- **Retenciones a tu proveedor**: personas morales only. Opens by itself for fees, rent and freight.
- **Saving**
  - Idempotent client id; a retry resends the same id.
  - "Guardar y crear otro" keeps date, payment method, CFDI, rate and regime. It clears the rest, starts a new id and moves focus to the category.
  - Edit opens prefilled and sends a diff-only merge-patch. A cleared field goes as `null`, and `deductible: null` clears the override. An edit with no changes sends nothing.
  - 402 opens a paywall that names the expenses cap ("Llegaste al límite de gastos de prueba"); a read-only account gets the read-only paywall.
  - Server verdicts land on their fields. Warnings, including `provisional_parameters`, go in a toast that stays until closed.

## Test plan
- [x] Widget tests written first (60 in `test/features/expenses/`: list, form, edit, domain rules, plus `test/core/records/stacked_undo_test.dart`). They failed before the slice existed.
- [x] Guideline tests (tap target, labels, contrast) pass in light and dark on the list and the form.
- [x] `make mobile-check`: format, analyze (0 issues), 959 tests.
- [x] `make mobile-cover`: 95.73 % (gate 80 %).
- [x] `make mobile-client-check`: no drift.
- [x] `test/integration/expenses_mock_test.dart` against Prism (`MOCK_API_URL`): 5/5.

## Notes
- The page's state class is about 200 lines, the same shape as `IncomeFormPage`.
- Income follow-up 2 (`IncomeFormModel.basis` fixed from the first regime) does not apply to expenses: `paid_on` is the only date.

body:
Extends the sendspin-server-cpp server adapter to the server- and client-initiated metadata, artwork and controller scenarios.

## What changed

- **Metadata:** `set_metadata()` with the `--metadata-*` track at `now_us()`. `metadata.expected` is the last `server/state` metadata object written, in the snapshot shape the runner compares. `metadata.first_state_sent` takes `bound_us` from the stamp of the first `trace_writes` completion after that state, so the reading is taken once the frame is on the wire.
- **Artwork:** encodes a `--artwork-width` × `--artwork-height` JPEG with the stb_image_write the library vendors (its `sendspin_server_cpp_stb` target) and hands it to `set_artwork()`. `encoded_sha256` hashes the image reassembled from the traced announce and part messages (ID 8 + channel), once written. Channel, source, format and size come from the traced artwork `stream/start`.
- **Controller:** offers `--controller-command` with the repeat and shuffle state through `set_controller_caps()`, and refuses a command it cannot offer. `received_command` is the controller object of the inbound `client/command` in the trace. `supported_commands`, `volume`, `muted`, `repeat` and `shuffle` come from the last controller `server/state` written. The library adds `switch` itself.
- An outbound state or image counts only once a later write completion covers it, as the existing `server/time` and `stream/start` evidence already does.
- The server `RoleSpec` gains `metadata`, `controller` and `artwork`. The README and adapter-contract coverage lines are updated.

## Results

`conformance run --from sendspin-server-cpp --to aiosendspin,sendspin-cpp,sendspin-dotnet,SendspinKit,sendspin-js` with `repos/` at default-branch heads:

| Scenario | aiosendspin | sendspin-cpp | sendspin-dotnet | SendspinKit | sendspin-js |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| server-initiated-metadata | ✅ snapshot + timestamp | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ ¹ |
| client-initiated-metadata | ✅ snapshot + timestamp | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ ¹ |
| server-initiated-artwork | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ ² | ❌ ³ |
| client-initiated-artwork | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ ² | ❌ ³ |
| server-initiated-controller | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ ¹ |
| client-initiated-controller | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ ⁴ | ✅ | ❌ ¹ |

1. "the client sent client/hello but never took the connection with a client/state after server/activate; handshake failed". sendspin-js fails every scenario against this server, the PCM ones included, as it does in the published baseline.
2. "no artwork transfer of the image was written in full (only an empty image, clearing the channel, was)". When the artwork stream starts, the library first sends an empty image to clear the channel (aiosendspin's client sees it too: `received_count` 2). The SendspinKit client adapter's `consumeArtwork()` finishes on the first artwork event, so it says goodbye before the image arrives.
3. "sendspin-js client adapter does not support role family/families artwork".
4. "Client controller state reports no supported_commands list". The client sent `next`, so it had seen the list. The published baseline fails the same cell with the aiosendspin server.

The PCM, 24-bit, protocol-baseline, state-format and chunk-framing cells are unchanged. `scripts/detect_regressions.py` reports no regressions against the published baseline.

`python -m compileall src scripts` and `python -m unittest discover -s tests` pass.

body:
Les angles morts de l’audit du 14 octobre : ce qui se passe chez les visiteurs, et les sauvegardes.

## Les erreurs et la vitesse dans les navigateurs

Jusqu’ici, `tracer` n’écrivait que dans la console : une page qui plante sur un iPhone, personne ne le savait.

- **La sentinelle** (`src/lib/sentinelle.tsx`, dans la mise en page) envoie :
  - les erreurs de l’appli : non rattrapées, promesses rejetées sans suite, pages d’erreur sans empreinte du serveur (le serveur a déjà les siennes). Cinq par page au plus ; les scripts d’autres sites et le bruit connu (ResizeObserver, « Script error ») sont ignorés ;
  - la vitesse de la page (les Web Vitals de Next : LCP, INP, CLS, FCP, TTFB), une fois quand elle passe à l’arrière-plan.
- **Le serveur** (`src/server/navigateur.ts`, `POST /api/navigateur/erreur` et `/mesures`, sans compte, limités par adresse) masque et borne : le message coupé, sans emails, longs nombres ni identifiants ; la source réduite à un fichier de l’appli ; l’écran au lieu de l’adresse ; la famille du navigateur (iPhone, dans une appli…) au lieu de l’User-Agent. Une erreur est une ligne par signature et par jour (`erreurs_navigateur`) ; la première du jour prévient l’équipe, dix alertes par jour au plus.
- **/admin, bloc « Navigateurs »** : la vitesse de chaque écran au 75e centile (téléphone et ordinateur, en vert, orange ou rouge selon les seuils de Google) et les dix erreurs les plus fréquentes. L’aperçu `/apercu/admin` le montre avec des chiffres d’exemple.
- Gardé 30 jours (la purge). La page de confidentialité le dit, en une ligne : `TODO(produit)` à valider.

## Les sauvegardes

- **BACKEND.md, « Les sauvegardes »** : la fenêtre de restauration de Neon (à vérifier dans sa console), `BLUSH_CLE` sans laquelle une sauvegarde est illisible, restaurer d’abord sur une branche sans toucher la production, et s’exercer une fois.
- **Le registre des effacements** (`effacements`) : « Tout effacer » et « Supprimer l’histoire » y laissent leurs identifiants (jamais l’email), 90 jours. Une base restaurée ramène ce qui a été effacé depuis : le registre, lu avant la restauration, dit quoi ré-effacer (RGPD).

## Base

Une migration : `0019_navigateurs_et_effacements` (trois tables, aucune colonne touchée ailleurs).

body:
Phase 2 of the Marketing redesign. It fixes the error handling behind the two errors in the owner's screenshots and explains the actual cause.

## What the errors mean
- **"Something went wrong talking to the Marketing server: internal"**
  - I checked the Firebase callable SDK source (`@firebase/functions`, `postJSON` / `codeForHTTPStatus`). It produces `internal` / `"internal"` when the request gets no usable response (status 0, so the browser blocked or failed it) or a 500 with no error body.
  - Our server never sends a bare "internal": its guard returns "Unexpected server error.".
  - A function that isn't deployed returns a 404 without CORS headers, so the browser blocks it. That gives exactly this error.
- **"Your Firestore rules don't allow this yet"**
  - This is a `permission-denied` read of `users/{uid}/marketing*`.
  - The rules exist in `firestore.rules` but only apply once they're published to the Firebase project.
- **Likely cause:** neither the functions nor the rules have been deployed. This can only be confirmed in the Firebase console, which the sandbox can't reach.

## Changes
- **Server Health card** (Overview) replaces the old status line:
  - Checks sign-in, Firestore access, the server, the InsightSocial key and the Claude key separately.
  - Each row shows OK / Problem / Warning, what's wrong, and the fix.
  - The setup guide opens automatically when something is wrong.
  - Shows when this device last reached the server and last loaded data.
- **Clearer messages:**
  - A bare `internal` error now explains the likely cause.
  - Unexpected server errors include a short reference (`details.ref`) that matches the Cloud Functions log entry.
- **Tabs:**
  - Data errors show **Try again** and **Server Health** buttons.
  - The budget and research cards no longer repeat the server error.
- **Timeouts:** 20s timeouts on the status call and on data loads.
- **Server:**
  - New `functions/lib/guard.js` logs the function name, reference, message and stack. It never logs request data or keys.
  - All callables use it.
- **README:**
  - (A) Publish rules from the Firebase console, no command line needed.
  - (B) Deploy functions from Google Cloud Shell in a browser.
  - (C) How to check it worked.
- Cache bumped to v36.

- `cd functions && npm test`: **35/35 pass** (3 new guard tests).
- `functions/index.js` loads and exports all 5 functions.
- Playwright Marketing test, mocked server: **101/101 pass**. It includes the screenshot case (bare `internal` plus rules blocked), an error with a log reference, Try again, the Server Health button, the guide opening automatically, timeouts, and no overflow at 390px.

author: diofeher
body:
`code-security.yml` called reusable workflows that repos in the `gdsfactory` org can't reach, so every run failed at startup.

## Template sync
Workflow wrappers are synced from [`pdk-ci-workflow-public`](https://github.com/doplaydo/pdk-ci-workflow-public) by the `check-template-drift` pre-commit hook. These files are the hook's output, not hand edits:
- `.github/workflows/code-security.yml`: now calls `doplaydo/pdk-ci-workflow-public/.github/workflows/code-security.yml@main` (Semgrep + Trivy, public tooling, read-only access).
- `.github/workflows/sample-project-upload.yml`: catches up with upstream template changes.

The new workflow fails on findings (Semgrep `--error`; Trivy on fixable HIGH/CRITICAL). The changes below are specific to this repo and can't come from a template; they clear this repo's existing findings.

## Code Security fixes
- **Trivy (dependencies):** `uv.lock` upgrades for packages with fixable HIGH/CRITICAL CVEs: `jupyterlab`, `notebook`, `tornado`, `urllib3`, `virtualenv`.
- **Semgrep (repo-local workflows):** `.github/workflows/release.yml`: actions pinned to commit SHAs (same versions as the old tags). Where `${{ github.ref_name }}` was interpolated into `run:` scripts, it's now passed through `env: TAG` and used quoted.
- **Trivy (DS-0002/DS-0029):** `scripts/magic/Dockerfile` now runs as a non-root user and installs with `--no-install-recommends`, adding `ca-certificates` explicitly so `git clone` over https still works. The image build hasn't been tested end to end (it compiles Magic and open_pdks from source); the same change was test-built for gf180mcu, where the Magic step completes.
- **Accepted finding:** `.trivyignore` lists CVE-2026-0994 (protobuf DoS). It can't be fixed from this repo: `vlsir` 7.0.0, the latest release, requires `protobuf<5`, and the fix is only in 5.29.6+. It comes in through `gdsfactoryplus` → `vlsirtools` → `vlsir`. Remove the entry once vlsir allows a fixed protobuf.

Verified locally with the same Semgrep (1.180.0) and Trivy settings as the reusable workflow, plus a full `pre-commit run --all-files`.

## Summary by Sourcery

Update repository automation to use accessible security checks and harden related CI, release, sample-upload, and reference-generation workflows.

Bug Fixes:
- Restore Code Security checks by switching to a publicly reachable reusable workflow.

Enhancements:
- Improve release workflow safety and reproducibility by pinning GitHub Actions and quoting the release tag.
- Run Magic reference generation as a non-root container user and reduce Docker image package recommendations.
- Support optional synchronization of mapped sample projects during sample uploads.

Build:
- Refresh locked Python dependency versions.

CI:
- Adopt the public Semgrep and Trivy Code Security workflow with read-only repository access.

Chores:
- Add repository-local Trivy suppressions for accepted findings.

## Implemented and tested — actionable prevention, not another promise

**Research invariant:** intrinsic normative classification of authentic contractual provisions **with cumulative, source-grounded provision-skeleton learning** to reduce later classification errors, supported by machine-only challenges. Eventual executability is downstream. Jev/number of reviewers are engineering hypotheses, not locked architecture.

**Actual code on this PR**
- `PROJECT_STATE.json.research_contract` records a concise stable research target and required updating-library vs frozen/cold comparison.
- Existing `.claude/hooks/context_guard.py` injects that target at every Claude Code session/prompt, rejects malformed/changed research contracts, requires `EXPERIMENT_ALIGNMENT.json` for **new** experimental directories, checks DIRECT_GOAL_TEST declares intrinsic normative **classification error** and a growing-vs-frozen/cold library comparison; separate/component studies are explicitly limited.

- Tests include an explicit **V4-shaped regex/Brier false-continuity rejection**; honest distinct hypotheses and planned single-delta work are permitted.

Existing historical experiment directories are exempt. This guard does not run on `main` until merged. `main` is presently unprotected, so a user with write access could bypass checks. Production enforcement needs an owner-reviewed merge and required status checks plus PR review configured for `main`.

author: tuckett45
body:
## Problem

Users had to hard-refresh the browser for a status change to show up in the onboarding candidate list:

> "I am having to hard refresh each time i change a status for it to record in the onboarding candidates"

## Root cause

The candidate list caches its loaded candidates in `CandidateListStateService` (a `providedIn: 'root'` service) so that filters, sort, and page position survive navigation to the detail/edit views and back. The cache is only meant to be reloaded when `invalidateData()` is called — **but `invalidateData()` was never called anywhere in the codebase.**

As a result:
1. User opens the list → candidates are cached.
2. User opens a candidate's **detail view** and changes status via `advanceToStatus()` (or edits/saves in the form). The backend updates, but the cached list array is now stale.
3. User clicks **Back to Candidates** → `ngOnInit` restores the cached (stale) candidates and skips the API call.
4. The change is invisible until a **hard refresh** wipes the in-memory `root` service.

(The inline status dropdown in the list itself worked because it mutates the same cached object reference.)

## Fix

Call the existing `invalidateData()` after any out-of-list candidate mutation:
- `candidate-detail.component.ts` → after a successful `advanceToStatus()`
- `candidate-form.component.ts` → after a successful create and update

`invalidateData()` empties the cached candidates array while keeping the filter/sort/page state, so the list's existing `ngOnInit` branch reloads fresh data (preserving the user's position). The change now appears immediately on return — no hard refresh needed.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json` → **0 errors** across the project.
- Changes are limited to injecting an already-provided service and calling an existing public method.

Webhooks may reach **internal hosts** a site admin lists, the activity notification **recovery list drains**, and the **FreeBSD** bundle runs as a service. This release adds the following new features: **Bots** - external runners a board hands cards to.
Board Settings / Bots: hand cards to an AI agent, CI job or script, as kanbots does. Thanks to xet7. Board Settings → **Bots**, below Workflow view, is the Rules page's view for bots, laid out like kanbots in the board's theme. The rail lists the bots, the live runs and their activity. The board's lists are the columns, each card showing its run's state, its current step and the answers to the bot's question. The drawer shows the card's thread, **Hand to bot**, **Stop** and a reply box. A bot has no rights of its own. WeKan only sends to it: a dispatch goes through the outgoing-webhook queue, behind the SSRF guard and signed, and a bot receives no board activity. The runner works on the board through WeKan's REST API with its own user's role, and reports at one route that needs write access. Board admins only: in the view, or with the new Rule action **Hand the card to bot**. See [Bots](docs/Features/Automation/Bots.md). Tests: `tests/botRuns.test.cjs` and `server/lib/tests/bots.tests.js`.
**Search** - finding a card on the board.
Board search shows each card found on the board, and Enter steps to the next. Thanks to rlach and xet7. A result opened from the board search is also scrolled into the middle of the board and highlighted for a moment. Enter again in the search box steps to the next card found, wrapping round, with "2 of 7" under the box, as finding on a page works. Shift+Enter or the arrows beside the count step back ([previous](https://redirect.github.com/wekan/wekan/commit/7dd484f8c2)). A list found is revealed the same way. Tests: `tests/revealOnBoard.test.cjs` (jsdom), and a Playwright spec in `tests/playwright/specs/04-search.e2e.js`.
**Labels and avatars** - order and recognition at a glance.
Sort a list by the board's label order. Thanks to mnantel and xet7. Board admins move a label up or down when editing it, and Sort cards has **Label order**: a card comes where its first label comes, and cards without labels come last. It is a display order only, like Sort by votes: it never changes the dragged order. `tests/labelOrder.test.cjs`.
Minicard avatars in the order people were added, each with its own colour. Thanks to HolgerGH and xet7. The minicard floated each avatar to the end of its row, which drew them reversed: the first person added, whom a team treats as responsible, came last. They are a wrapping row in added order now, still right-aligned, as issue [#​5081](https://redirect.github.com/wekan/wekan/issues/5081) asked. Each person's initials avatar has a lasting colour of their own, readable at WCAG AA, and the tooltip names them. `tests/avatarColor.test.cjs`.
**Webhooks** - where they may go.
Outgoing webhooks may reach the internal hosts a site admin lists. Thanks to xet7. Admin Panel → Settings → Global Webhooks → **Internal destinations** lists hosts on WeKan's own network that outgoing webhooks may reach: a Node-RED, a chat server, a Matrix hookshot. Each entry is a name or an address, with a port to allow only that port. It is empty by default. Only site administrators read and change it, through methods, and it is never published, so a board member still cannot point a webhook inward. A listed host is called without following redirects; everything else stays behind the SSRF guard. `tests/internalWebhookHosts.test.cjs`.
**Documentation** - how-tos the decided issues asked for. - [Bitbucket login through the generic OAuth2 settings](https://redirect.github.com/wekan/wekan/commit/f715e95b40), checked against the OIDC code. Thanks to thuanpq and xet7. - [Matrix notifications through an outgoing webhook and matrix-hookshot, no bot](https://redirect.github.com/wekan/wekan/commit/dff0856585). Thanks to killua-eu and xet7. - [RFID tags moving cards through the REST API](https://redirect.github.com/wekan/wekan/commit/c47fe98ab0). Thanks to xet7. - [WeKan on current Rancher with the Helm chart](https://redirect.github.com/wekan/wekan/commit/28477b5a85). Thanks to Dreampie and xet7. **Member Settings** - how a new card's title is typed.
Keep #label and @​member in a new card's title, as a Member Settings switch. Thanks to biji and xet7. Picking a label with `#` or a member with `@` while typing a new card's title gave the card that label or member and removed the text from the title. Member Settings → **Keep #label and [@​member](https://redirect.github.com/member) in new card titles** keeps the text as well, for those who read the title as a sentence. It is off by default, so nothing changes unless a user turns it on. `models/lib/titleTags.js` decides what stays; `tests/titleTags.test.cjs` checks both settings, a label known only by its colour, and that nothing like `@undefined` is ever left. The two strings are in every locale ([translations](https://redirect.github.com/wekan/wekan/commit/8fd04f9984)).
**Platforms** - where WeKan runs.
The FreeBSD bundle runs as a service, with an rc.d script. Thanks to xet7. `bundle/rc.d/wekan` in the FreeBSD bundle runs the bundle's own `start-wekan.sh` - the bundled Node.js and FerretDB on SQLite - under `daemon(8)` as an unprivileged user, set up in `rc.conf`: `wekan_enable`, `wekan_port`, `wekan_root_url`, `wekan_data`, `wekan_env`. `service wekan stop` stops FerretDB with WeKan. The FreeBSD bundle job fails without it. [FreeBSD](docs/Platforms/FOSS/OS/FreeBSD.md) has the install steps and an outline of a ports Makefile to propose to FreeBSD. `tests/freebsdRcScript.test.cjs`.

author: peterdsharpe
body:
Closes #2689.

A tensordict shape op used as a context manager (`with td.squeeze(0) as tdt:`) should undo itself on exit and keep what the block wrote. For some ordinary argument forms it raises on exit instead, and for one it returns but leaves a size-1 dim on every leaf. This PR makes the undo step handle those forms on TensorDict, tensorclasses and lazy stacks.

## What was wrong

```python
td = TensorDict(a=torch.zeros(2, 3), batch_size=[2, 3])
with td.squeeze(0): ...           # RuntimeError: update() got a source with batch size [1, 2, 3] ...
with td.squeeze(-1): ...          # returns, but td["a"].shape is now (2, 3, 1)
with td.flatten(0, None): ...     # TypeError: '<' not supported between 'NoneType' and 'int'
with td.transpose(dim0=0, dim1=1): ...  # ValueError: not enough values to unpack
```

The same goes for `flatten(None)`, `flatten(start_dim=None)`, `flatten(end_dim=None)`, `transpose(0, dim1=1)`, `swapaxes(axis0=0, axis1=1)` and `swapdims(0, axis1=1)`. All of these work outside a `with` block. A plain `td.squeeze(0)` outside a `with` block also left its undo step on `td`, so a later bare `with td:` raised the same `RuntimeError` on exit.

## The fix

All three causes are in the undo functions in `tensordict/_contextlib.py`:

- `_reverse_squeeze`: `squeeze(dim)` of a dim whose size is not 1 returns its input, so the block already wrote into `td`, but the undo step still unsqueezed `td` into itself. It now returns early when the batch dims did not change. I compare `batch_dims` rather than `self is out` because on a tensorclass `self` is the tensorclass and `out` its `_tensordict`, so an identity check misses it.
- `_reverse_flatten`: `None` for `start_dim` or `end_dim` reached the `< 0` comparisons. It now becomes 0 or -1 first, as `flatten` itself does.
- `_reverse_transpose`: it unpacked only the positional arguments. It now takes `(*args, *kwargs.values())`. Transpose is symmetric, so the keyword order does not matter, and this covers `dim0`/`dim1` and `axis0`/`axis1`.

The other undo functions (`unsqueeze`, `permute`, `movedim`, `unflatten`, `view`, `flip*`, `roll`, `rot90`) work for every argument form I tried. This is exit-only code, so the ops themselves cost the same. TorchRL uses `with data.flatten(1, -1)` and `with td.flatten()`, which do not change.

Not changed here: `with td.squeeze():` without a dim still raises, as its docstring says. An op called with `inplace=True` inside a `with` block (`with td.flatten(0, 1, inplace=True):`) still does not restore `td` on exit; whether it should is a design question for a separate issue. The `atleast_*` cases are in #2641, which edits the start of `_reverse_flatten` next to this change.

## Behaviour changes

`with td.squeeze(d):` with a negative `d` of a dim whose size is not 1 used to return with a size-1 dim added to every leaf. It now leaves the shapes as they were. Every other changed form raised before.

## The test

In `test/tensordict/test_methods.py::TestTensorDicts`, which runs over every tensordict type (lazy stacks, sub-tensordicts, memmap, h5, TensorDictParams, TypedTensorDict and others), next to the existing `*_decorator` tests:

- `test_squeeze_decorator_noop_dim` (`dim` 0 and -2 on a `[4, 3, 2, 1]` batch): writes in the block, then checks the batch size, every leaf shape and the values, and that a plain `td.squeeze(dim)` followed by `with td:` exits cleanly.
- `test_flatten_decorator_none_dims`: the four `None` forms, with values written back.
- `test_transpose_decorator_keywords`: `transpose(dim0=, dim1=)`, `transpose(0, dim1=)`, `swapaxes(axis0=, axis1=)`, `swapdims(0, axis1=)`.

In `test/tensorclass/test_tensorclass.py::TestTensorClass`, `test_shape_op_context_manager` covers the same forms on a tensorclass.

On main, 182 of the 206 new cases fail. The 24 that pass are the transpose cases on lazy views, where entering the block already raises the expected `to_tensordict` error. All 206 pass here.

## What I ran

Local testing was CPU-only: Python 3.12, torch 2.14.1+cpu, with `TD_GET_DEFAULTS_TO_NONE=1 LIST_TO_STACK=1 TD_CHECK_INVARIANTS=1 TORCHDYNAMO_INLINE_INBUILT_NN_MODULES=1`.

- `test/tensordict/test_methods.py test/tensorclass/test_tensorclass.py`: 9437 passed, 424 skipped (CUDA, mypy, streaming).
- The same files with torch 2.13: 8936 passed, 403 skipped.
- `pre-commit run --files` on the three changed files: passed.

author: tap
body:
## What this changes

This is the roadmap's A8 (row P10; Q6 decided a hard gate, two-sided at ±3 %). Each engine gets host workloads (`bench/icount/host_main.cpp`, binaries `tap_sr_<engine>_hostcount_*`):

- The float converter streams 128-frame blocks at 2 and 12 channels.
- `scripts/icount.py --target host` counts them under valgrind's callgrind and gates them against a new `host` key in each `bench/baselines.json`, with the same mechanics as the QEMU legs.
- A new CI job, `Instruction-count ratchet (host)`, runs the gate.

## Why

The channel-parallel host path sat outside every ratchet. `TAP_DSP_CHANNEL_PARALLEL` is off under Helium, the M33's DSP extension and Hexagon, so no QEMU leg compiles it, and a host regression there could land unseen. async's 12-channel rows run that path.

## Verification

**What pins the count** to the code, the compiler and the C library:
- **One function counted.** Only `tap_sr_host_counted()`, the streaming loop, is counted (`--toggle-collect`). Construction, the fixture's `sin()` calls, process start-up and the environment stay outside.
- **Eager binding.** `LD_BIND_NOW=1`, so no PLT resolution lands inside the counted window.
- **glibc pinned.** `GLIBC_TUNABLES` holds glibc's CPU-dispatched routines to their x86-64 baseline variants and pins the copy thresholds glibc derives from cache sizes. Before the pin, this machine's `memcpy` resolved to the AVX variant, 1 % of the 12-channel async count.
- **No `-march`.** The compiled code is the x86-64 baseline whatever the runner.

**Recorded** with g++ 13.3.0 (`13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1`), glibc 2.39 (`2.39-0ubuntu8.9`) and valgrind 3.22; the job prints the runner's versions. All of these count identically:
- two runs of one binary;
- a second build with another generator;
- a replay of the CI job's own build and gate steps.

**On CI:** the runner reproduced all ten counts exactly, +0 against every baseline with the same checksums (job 115919836408, run 38583667902), and all 32 checks are green.

| Engine | Workload | 2 ch | 12 ch |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| async | `pipeline_float` | 109,526,808 | 362,078,536 |
| bridge | `up_float` | 79,352,295 | 470,621,528 |
| bridge | `down_float` | 99,664,796 | 593,181,679 |
| rational | `up2_float` | 57,296,876 | 288,223,796 |
| rational | `down2_float` | 29,983,981 | 161,054,642 |

async at 12 channels runs about 30 M instructions per channel over the stream, against 55 M at 2: that is what the channel-parallel path buys. bridge has no frame-major path and costs the same per channel at both counts.

**Also checked:**
- clang 18 `-Werror` build, clang-tidy and clang-format are clean on the three new files.
- `check_retired_words.py` passes.
- The M33 cross configure defines no host workloads, and the README tables are regenerated.

## Notes for the reviewer

- The QEMU tables in the READMEs are byte-identical. The host figures are a second table from the same generator, between the same markers.
- The book's icount chapter gains "The host, under callgrind"; the root CLAUDE.md and the roadmap (A8 landed, P10 green) describe it.

body:
Follow-up to #183 (refs #181). On the live paper stack, `mmr breaker reset` was refused `BREAKER_RESET_REFUSED: reconciliation is incomplete`, although `reconcile unknown` listed no command.

Cause (my bug in #183): `CircuitBreaker.reset` checked `reconciliation_safe()`, which means "no unresolved ledger row on the account". The reset runs inside the coordinator, so its own row is unresolved at that moment, and the check could never pass. My #183 unit tests faked the check, so they missed it.

Fix:
- `CircuitBreaker` now passes the reset's command id to `reconciliation_complete(command_id)`.
- The command stack wires the existing `reconciliation_complete`, which leaves out that one row. The arming ports already use it the same way (`command_stack.py:1135`).
- Any other unresolved command still refuses the reset.

Tests:
- Two new tests run the reset through a real `TradingCommandCoordinator` and `CommandLedger`: it passes with only its own row in flight, and it is refused with another `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` row.
- Updated the four test constructions of `CircuitBreaker`. Related files: 149 passed. I did not run the full suite; CI runs it.

author: henryzhangpku
body:
## Why

In the first model-proposed portfolio campaign (20 trials, external evaluator, 20 US large caps), roughly 15 trials were variations of one idea — sector-neutral short-term reversal. The family quota counted them as different families because the family was the outermost operator plus inputs, so `rank(…)`, `xscore(…)`, `neg(…)` around the same core all passed.

## What

- `research/external/recipes.py`: when the frozen vocabulary publishes operator `semantics` (`sign`, `child_signs`, `horizon_params`), the family is the sorted set of input paths, each `input:sign:lookback-bucket` (≤1w, ≤1m, 3–6m, 1y+). Normalisers contribute nothing, so wrappers of the same idea collapse: `neg(ewm21(ret))` and `rank(neg(ewm21(ret)))` are both `ret:-:1m`; a long-minus-short spread is `ret:+:1m+ret:-:1y+`. Without semantics the previous structural rule applies.
- `research/external/campaign.py`: takes the vocabulary and fails closed if its hash differs from the contract's.
- `research/external/proposer.py`: the prompt states the family rule.

## Effect

Re-scoring that campaign's 20 recipes: the two largest families (1-month reversal, and 1-month + 3–6-month reversal blends) each held 4 trials; a quota of 2 would have refused 4 trials and pushed the proposer to other ideas.

## Verification

`uv run pytest`: 476 passed (2 new: semantic grouping incl. normalisers, spreads and the fallback; quota enforcement and vocabulary-hash mismatch in a campaign).

## Follow-up in this PR

A second model-proposed campaign under the new rule spread across 19 families (largest: 2 trials, previously 4) and exposed two gaps, both fixed here:
- Integrated inputs: when the vocabulary publishes `observation_semantics` (e.g. `logprice` integrates `ret`), paths are named by the base input, so `diff(logprice, 126)` and `rolling_sum(ret, 126)` share `ret:+:3-6m`; an undifferenced level counts as a 1y+ lookback.
- Operator descriptions: the prompt now shows each operator's published description. The model had read `tscore(ret, 126)` as six-month risk-adjusted momentum; it is a one-day signal (388x turnover).

author: joyja
body:
## Cause
`handleWriteTag`'s whole-tag scalar path called `Tags.Set`, which creates a store entry for any name. A typo, or a CONSTANT's name (constants are not tags), answered 204 and made a top-level tag no program reads (and a Sparkplug edge would publish). Unknown members were already refused; unknown whole names were not.

## Fix
Before the scalar write, the name must be declared: in the store, typed by the manifest, bound by a program (VAR_EXTERNAL / tag table), or a driver input/output not yet delivered. Otherwise 400 `undefined tag X: not a declared tag, so there is nothing to write (a CONSTANT is not a tag and cannot be written)`. This also covers a string value to an unknown name (was 422). The tag-model page and README no longer list an operator write as creating an undeclared tag. A TagWriter (Logix) still takes over as before.

## Test
`TestWriteTag` (undeclared string and number writes, nothing created), `TestWriteStringOnlyToStringTag`, and `TestProjectConstantIsNotATag` (POST to a constant's name is a 400 naming it, no stray tag, program still reads 90). With server.go reverted they fail with 204/422. FN-055 is no longer partial; TAG-002 text updated. Extension CHANGELOG entry added.

HMI kit (`hmi/src/lib/realtime.svelte.ts` writeTag) already documents refusing unknown tags and surfaces the reason; the dashboard and the it-cluster/node-3d example HMIs only write declared tags. Nothing found relying on create-on-write.

Several fallback messages still sent users to upstream. Uninstall suggested `npm uninstall -g t3`, browser setup suggested `sudo npx t3 browser setup`, service repair printed upstream commands, and the mobile beta card linked to upstream downloads. Following any of them could modify or install the wrong product.

- Uninstall, browser-setup and service-repair instructions are generated from how this install actually runs: proven npm ownership, package runner, marked fork desktop shim, standalone binary, or source entry. They keep the selected home and use the channel's own command name. Preview and PR runner recovery pins the installed version.
- npm uninstall advice names only `shuv2code` and its proven prefix. Tests confirm upstream launchers and services are never touched.
- Browser-stream errors keep the server-generated command. Malformed responses fall back to the fork command, not upstream.
- Mobile downloads are marked unavailable until fork store listings exist (#271). Desktop download links go to the fork's GitHub releases page, and the obsolete upstream mobile-beta toast is removed.
- Adjacent pairing, update, authorization, activation and triage instructions, plus the affected user guides, were audited. Compatibility protocol and internal package names are unchanged.
- The npm update-availability check is deliberately unchanged here. It is handled per destination environment in #272.

Verification: 292 focused tests across server CLI/cloud, shared, client-runtime, desktop and web; five affected typechecks; scoped lint. Not yet verified: copy-pasting recovery instructions on disposable npm, script and source installs, and a real-client UI check.

author: suyatdev
body:
## What this does

Measures the worktree-location guard well enough to decide whether to arm it, and fixes one real
defect found along the way. **It does not arm the guard.** `WORKTREE_GUARD_MODE` is still `log`.

Card: `docs/features/worktree-location-guard.md` (task 10, the flip; task 18, the leak fix).

## The recommendation this branch arrives at: do not flip yet

Arming today would break three ordinary things, none of which is a misplaced worktree:

1. **Opaque or unlexable Bash.** Roughly 70 of the first 76 layer-1 refusals in the post-fix
   window are `SEG_UNPARSED` / `SEG_OPAQUE` false denials — heredocs, `python3 -`, and pipelines
   all trip it. This is a separate open blocker, not a tuning detail.
2. **Your own `git pull` in a primary checkout.** All 19 real-repository layer-2 refusals before
   the measurement window cut, reflog-confirmed as yours. Correct refusals by policy; ordinary
   work in practice.
3. **Every judge subagent's scratch clone** — which reaches `gh pr create` through
   `judge-guard.sh`. Demonstrated live twice while preparing this PR.

Plus arming would turn `hooks/git-guard.test.sh` red — the regression suite for a *different*
guard.

Whether that cost is acceptable is a call for a human, not something this card can settle. The
card says so explicitly and says not to flip without asking.

## The code change (task 18)

Two lines, one per suite:

```bash
export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null
```

**Root cause.** `core.hooksPath` is set in this machine's **global** git config and points at the
layer-2 `reference-transaction` hook. Every fixture repository `hooks/git-guard.test.sh` and
`hooks/verify-hook-wiring.test.sh` built therefore armed layer 2 and wrote log lines — into the
very log the criterion-3 review has to read. 1062 of 1066 fixture would-deny lines trace to those
two suites.

Safe because neither file reads global config: each sets identity per-repository with
`git -C "$dir" config user.email` / `user.name`.

It also removes a **false comment** in `verify-hook-wiring.test.sh` which claimed the suite's fake
`$HOME` meant there was no global config to inherit. It does not — `$HOME` there is only ever a
path, and the fixture-building commands run in the script's own environment with the real `HOME`.
Believing that comment is what let the suite leak.

**Falsified by the live log, not by a green suite** — a passing suite cannot tell you a side
effect stopped:

| suite | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `git-guard.test.sh` | 176 passed / 0 failed, **+54 log lines** | 176 passed / 0 failed, **0** |
| `verify-hook-wiring.test.sh` | 37/37, **+40 log lines** | 37/37, **0** |
| `worktree-guard.test.sh` (untouched) | 243/0/1 skip, 0 | unchanged |
| `reference-transaction.test.sh` (untouched) | 182/0/1 skip, 0 | unchanged |

Pass counts are byte-identical across the change, which is what shows neither suite depended on
the configuration it lost.

## Committed evidence

`docs/features/evidence/worktree-location-guard/` holds the raw extracts, four review reports and
two re-runnable scripts. That is deliberate: an earlier review of this card lost all its per-row
verdicts to a session scratchpad, leaving only unauditable prose. `README.md` records provenance
and the source logs' sha256.

The 971 previously-unexplained layer-2 lines were attributed by **two independent methods**, then
both were checked against the log itself rather than against each other — two readings that agree
can still be one error repeated. `verify-fixture-fingerprint.py` returns 5/5 PASS.

## Corrections made in this branch

Five of my own wrong claims are marked as corrections in place, with the old value kept visible:

- `D` and `B2` are **live** arm labels — four layer-1 labels, not two.
- The layer-2 population is **not** mostly test fixtures; that was inferred from `/tmp` path shape.
- The variant group is 184 dirs / 506 lines, not the ~23 read off truncated output.
- The attribution total for `git-guard.test.sh` is **967, not 941** — 941 is `435+506`, the total
  of one fixture *shape*, reused as the total for a whole *suite*, dropping 26 bare-root lines.
- Task 18's "the log will afterwards be nearly empty" was **false**, and whole-line count was the
  wrong leak signal: **81% of the log is `ALLOW` lines criterion 3 never reads**, and 13 of 25
  fixture-building suites still have no config isolation. The right signal is `WOULD-DENY`
  restricted to `var/folders`.

The last two were found by the observability judge and confirmed by independent re-measurement
before being accepted.

## Known and deliberately unresolved

- **Criterion 3 is not complete.** The first pass read 76 layer-1 lines; the window has since
  grown past a thousand. Its findings hold; its coverage does not.
- **Task 18 is inert until this merges**, because the suites run from whichever checkout a session
  is in and the primary still holds the leaking copy. The clean window starts at *this merge*.
- The layer-1 `SEG_UNPARSED` / `SEG_OPAQUE` false-denial rate is a separate open blocker.
- 4 layer-2 lines remain unattributed, and are recorded as unattributed rather than guessed at.

## Why the remaining work is smaller than it looks

Of the 173 would-deny lines outside `var/folders`, across 63 distinct roots, only **4 roots are
genuine repositories** (21 lines); the other 59 are agent scratch clones. Split at the window cut:
**19 before** — exactly the population already reviewed and judged 19/19 correct — and **2 after**,
both `vibe-scape`.

**So the layer-2 criterion-3 re-run reads 2 new lines, not the 571 the raw delta suggests.**

## After merging

Confirm the primary checkout's `hooks/git-guard.test.sh` is the merged blob before starting the
clean window — a merge does not make a hook live, since hooks run from `$HOME/.claude/hooks/`.

---

**Review status.** Observability judge run twice: round 1 at `87dd0f4` and round 2 at `386cb00`,
both `risk=low` / `confidence=high` with no failing dimension. Round 1's two findings were
confirmed by independent re-measurement and fixed in `386cb00`. Round 2 verified those fixes and
raised three smaller factual slips, which land as a follow-up commit on this branch.

body:
## Summary

Unify restrained interaction motion across TouchAI's desktop UI without adding an animation dependency. This PR changes 71 files (60 modified and 11 added): 63 source/style files and 8 test files.

- Introduce shared duration, easing, distance, scale, and loading-cycle tokens so CSS and the existing motion-v integration use a consistent rhythm, with support for the system's reduced-motion preference.
- Add or standardize transitions for buttons, inputs, switches, search dropdowns, dialogs, context menus, collapsible details, and settings tab indicators.
- Refine settings sidebar sizing and label visibility. Disable easing during width dragging to keep resizing responsive. Normalize existing conversation loading feedback, return-to-bottom controls, and AskUser animations.
- Separate immediate business results from visual exit cleanup for confirmation dialogs and context menus. Scope cleanup to each instance so an exiting instance cannot dispose of a newly opened one.
- Normalize motion tokens and reduced-motion rules in the Widget host's base styles without changing tool execution or content-generation protocols.

### Review map

Paths below are relative to `apps/desktop/`.

1. `src/styles/motion.css` and `src/composables/useMotion.ts`: shared motion tokens and accessibility policy.
2. `src/components/MotionCollapse.vue`: interruptible height transitions, lazy first mount, and inert collapsed content.
3. `src/composables/useConfirm.ts`, `useContextMenu.ts`, and dialog/menu components: separation of results from visual exits, instance isolation, and teardown cleanup. `DialogShell.vue` makes closing content immediately inert to prevent keyboard activation during exit.
4. `src/views/SettingsView/components/SectionTabs.vue` and `NavigationSidebar.vue`: sliding indicators, geometry observation, and responsive dragging.
5. Remaining UI integrations: adopt shared components, replace scattered hard-coded timings, and restrain existing spring effects. Streaming text does not receive per-token entrance animations.

## Related issue or RFC

Related to #518 — unify motion design across desktop interactions.

Based on remote main at `d0c9ecd2`. A fresh fetch before PR creation confirmed that the base matched `origin/main` at that time.

## AI assistance disclosure

- Tool(s) used: Codex.
- Scope of assistance: Motion-system implementation, component and caller updates, tests, code review, and local runtime diagnostics.
- Human review or rewrite performed: The user confirmed that the main window opens normally in the local test instance. Full visual and interaction acceptance remains pending review of this PR.
- Architecture or boundary impact: Shared frontend motion infrastructure and UI lifecycle behavior only. No changes to the Rust backend, database schema, AgentService, MCP protocols, or tool-execution logic.
- No online search tools were used. No images were read, and no screenshots were captured or inspected.

## Testing evidence

- Full desktop unit suite: **174 test files / 1,178 tests passed**, exit code 0. Command: `pnpm --filter @touchai/desktop exec vitest run --configLoader runner --passWithNoTests --maxWorkers=4 --no-cache`, with TEMP/TMP pointing to an isolated directory on drive G. The initial `pnpm test:unit` attempt failed during loading because of ENOSPC; the retry passed after moving temporary files. The log still includes a non-blocking bundle HTTP 504 message.
- After the full-suite run, pre-commit review identified and fixed keyboard activation during DialogShell's exit: closing content becomes inert immediately and becomes interactive again on reopen. The new regression test failed before the fix and passed afterward. Final motion-focused verification: **7 test files / 15 tests passed**.
- `pnpm type:check` and `pnpm test:typecheck` passed, including a fresh run after the inert-on-close fix.
- ESLint on changed files: **0 errors / 18 warnings**, concerning optional prop defaults and multiple components in test mocks. The final DialogShell change and new regression test were linted separately: **0 errors / 0 warnings**.
- Prettier checks on changed files and `git diff --check` passed.
- The local Tauri development build is running, and the user confirmed that the main window opens normally. The cache-read error did not recur after restarting the test instance. This does not establish a root cause or a permanent cache fix; this PR contains no backend fix for that issue.
- The complete `pnpm test:pr`, Rust coverage, and E2E checks were **not run**. Drives C and D have insufficient free space; the test instance uses isolated dependencies, data, and build directories, with builds on drive G. No additional full native build or E2E instance was started, to avoid disrupting the user's active manual test session. Full quality gates must be checked in CI before merge.
- Seven motion test files with 15 cases were added. These checks do not establish that the entire implementation followed a strict test-first process or that all visual behavior has been verified.

### Code review follow-up

- Commit `50cd1b7f` prevents keyboard selection from a closed SearchableSelect while its leave transition retains the DOM. Leaving content becomes inert, and reopening restores interaction.
- Added two regression cases (failed before the fix, passed afterward) and strengthened context-menu tests to preserve intentional replacement behavior without a spurious close notification.
- Fresh verification after the fix: motion suite **8 files / 17 tests passed**; `pnpm type:check`, `pnpm test:typecheck`, Prettier, and `git diff --check` passed. Targeted ESLint: **0 errors / 5 existing warnings**.
- Commitlint passes for the entire PR commit range after wrapping the follow-up commit body to meet the 100-character line limit; the source tree is unchanged by this metadata-only correction.
- The full unit-suite result above applies to the original implementation commit. The full suite and CI must rerun against this follow-up commit; local verification for this follow-up was targeted.

### Manual acceptance checklist

- [ ] Switch settings pages and top tabs. Selection responds immediately; the indicator has the correct position and width and does not slide in from the left on first render.
- [ ] Collapse and expand the settings sidebar, reverse direction mid-transition, and drag its width. State remains correct, and resizing tracks the pointer without lag.
- [ ] Exercise buttons, input focus, and switches. Feedback is restrained, list click targets do not shift, and disabled controls remain disabled.
- [ ] Open and close add/edit dialogs, then reopen quickly. Entrance and exit transitions work without leaving a stale overlay. Rapidly press Enter on a valid add-model form; closing content must not trigger another submission during exit.
- [ ] Delete a disposable test item through confirmation. Confirm executes once, cancel does not delete, and the business action does not wait for the exit animation.
- [ ] Use search dropdowns and context menus with the mouse and Esc/arrow keys/Enter. Selection takes effect immediately; rapidly reopening on different items never applies an old instance's action to the new item.
- [ ] Expand and collapse model groups and tool details, reversing direction mid-transition. Hidden content cannot receive keyboard focus.
- [ ] Stream a long answer. Existing text does not repeatedly animate in; scrolling, text selection, copy, and return-to-bottom remain functional.
- [ ] Exercise tool-call status updates and AskUser selection/submission. Animations do not trigger duplicate actions.
- [ ] Export data and check progress/completion states. After the progress dialog closes, the underlying UI is interactive.
- [ ] Enable the system's reduced-motion preference. Dialogs and menus still close completely, and looping motion no longer continues indefinitely.

author: nathanohare
body:
Before: Chem Illustrator gave no configuration for axially chiral molecules. The chemistry engine (RDKit) labels stereocentres and double bonds, but not atropisomers or allenes.

After: a biaryl or other hindered bond, an allene, or an alkylidenecycloalkane drawn with a wedge or hash on one end shows (Ra) or (Sa). The label appears in the preview, in Show Stereo Labels and in the analysis summary, just like R/S and E/Z, and can be moved or typed over by hand. Edit > Preferences can write these labels as P/M instead (Ra = M, Sa = P).

How: `src/chem/axial.ts` reads the molfile the drawing already makes for stereo labels. The end whose groups have wedges is taken to stand across the page. The groups on each end are ranked by CIP rules 1a and 2, using a hierarchical digraph with duplicate atoms. Alternating six-membered rings are read as aromatic, so the result doesn't depend on which Kekulé structure was drawn. The descriptor is IUPAC P-93.5.1: near 1, near 2, far 1 going clockwise along the axis is Ra. When those rules can't rank an end, no label is given. The labels are added to the engine's tags in `readTags`, so undefined groups (R, Ar) are handled the same way as for R/S.

Tests: `tests/axial.test.ts` checks an allene. It also checks that the label is the same after turning, renumbering or moving the wedge to the other end, and opposite for mirror images. For a biaryl it checks both Kekulé structures, a wedge on the ring bond versus on the substituent, and that a symmetric ring gives no label. Full suite: 1117 passed.

author: guangyu-reflexio
body:
## Summary
Compression admission must check the actual provider request before saving a new job. Add `plan_with_client(...)` so callers can prepare exact source sections, validate their native messages/schema/output reservation, and freeze a witness before any model, lease callback or checkpoint I/O.

## Changes
- Reuse the core prepared geometry through `CompressionPlan.check_requests(...)`; native checking does not repack sources.
- Bind actual generation policy, pinned transport ladder, capacity declarations and augmented initial messages in a separate native witness. Check drift before cached selections; check every dynamic reduction/repair at dispatch.
- Keep v6 node keys, exact original excerpts, bounded whole-group recovery, output caps and once-only parent usage forwarding. Native elapsed time includes preparation and execution, excluding the caller's wait between them.
- Share the existing descriptor normalization between the public client probe and internal actual-request guard. No new public client method or worker activation.
- Document that durable authorization/quota and witness comparison remain caller-owned. Native preparation now requires valid capacity for non-passthrough work, including cache-only replay.

## Test Plan
- 119 focused core, adapter and public-request-contract cases passed. Coverage includes actual MiniMax/OpenAI native preparation, zero-dispatch overflow, initial-message/policy drift, real native repair overflow before a second transport, cached replay and parent accounting.
- Ruff lint/format and Pyright on all five changed Python files passed; import-path assertions prove the feature sources were tested.
- One saved-input compatibility replay used a parent guard forbidding every provider dispatch: 31 old cache hits, zero provider attempts, identical 19-section packet and all non-timing fields. This does not establish semantic retention; the earlier diagnostic omissions remain.
- Independent full-branch local Codex review at `cabf348c70587841dd6f6cb26f5d33e948a352f7` against fixed base `90388e95f9f1f78629a5fbbac2de02cbecf95b55` exited 0 with no actionable findings and unchanged clean Git state. Current-head CI is required before merge.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Compression plans now validate complete model requests—including input limits, schema instructions, and output reservations—before execution. Oversized requests are rejected before provider dispatch.
  * Plans are rechecked before execution, preventing requests with changed models, policies, or messages from proceeding. Preparation does not access caches or contact providers.
* **Documentation**
  * Updated service documentation to explain request validation, plan execution, and usage accounting.

## Summary

Keep color-review conclusions consistent with their evidence, including the final summary.

```text
contrast conclusion
  calculated pair -> supplied colors and explicit compositing assumptions
  rendered check  -> inspected UI, states and appearances
  pending         -> missing input or observation
```

Only the better-colors verification paragraph changes in the installed skill bundle. Sync its human docs, provenance digest and patch Changeset, with sanitized native trial evidence.

## Evidence

- **Before:** One 0.4.2 Codex response contradicted its own rendering limits. The original contradiction did not recur in three unchanged repeats. A separate baseline Claude answer overclaimed exemptions from token names and remains failed.
  **After:** The candidate passed Codex 6/6 and Claude 6/6 in fresh isolated sessions, including implicit entry, explicit color invocation, fully specified compositing and staged routing. This is preventive clarification, not proof that stochastic errors are eliminated.
- 38 repository tests, 5 review-integrity controls, strict plugin validation and 24-session evidence verification passed. Report: `evals/design-color-evidence-2026-10-14/REPORT.md`.
- User authorized the patch release and both global installation updates. Private native logs, authentication and host context are excluded.

Only color-evidence wording changes. Post-release checks will verify the immutable tag, both actual global installations and fresh native sessions before reporting activation.

body:
Последний из четырёх слоёв, скрытых цепочкой `&&` в `typecheck:all`. Предыдущие — PR #1987 и #2004. ## Причина ``` src/notify/__tests__/review-renderers.test.ts(188,42): TS18046: 'mixed.error' is of type 'unknown'. ``` `SchemaLike.safeParse` (`packages/core/src/commands/registry.ts:27`) объявляет `error: unknown` **намеренно** — так `@rox/core` остаётся свободным от zod: ```ts export interface SchemaLike

{ safeParse(value: unknown): { success: true; data: P } | { success: false; error: unknown } } ``` Тест же обращался к `mixed.error.message` напрямую, что для `unknown` недопустимо. ## Исправление Сужением, а не приведением: проверяем `instanceof Error` и берём `message` только тогда, когда это действительно ошибка. Заглушек (`as any`, `@ts-ignore`) не добавлено, тип `unknown` в контракте сохранён. ## Четвёртый слой одной маскировки `typecheck:all` (`package.json:33`) — цепочка через `&&`, останавливается на первой упавшей рабочей области. За каждой починенной ошибкой открывалась следующая: | # | Рабочая область | Файл | PR | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | `packages/shared` | `session-tokens.test.ts` | #1987 | | 2 | `packages/ui` | `lazy-motion.tsx` | #2004 | | 3 | `packages/core` | `review-renderers.test.ts` | **этот** | После этой правки `bun run typecheck:all` **впервые проходит целиком: 0 ошибок**. ## Проверено | Проверка | Результат | |---|---| | `tsc --noEmit` по `packages/core` | **0 ошибок** | | `bun run typecheck:all` | **0 ошибок** | | `review-renderers.test.ts` | **12/12**, 66 expect() | ## Просьба отдельной задачей Четыре независимых дефекта жили незамеченными именно из-за `&&`. Стоит либо гонять области параллельно, либо накапливать ошибки и падать в конце. Иначе «зелёный `typecheck:all`» продолжит означать «проверено до первой поломки», а не «проверено всё». --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

author: zenrows-dev-pool[bot]
body:
## Summary

`outputFormat` takes `markdown`, so a crawl can return each kept page converted
to Markdown. A crawl also reports `discovery`, the strategies it found URLs
with, and a create can ask for them. `content()` takes `{ download: true }`,
and `CrawlErrorCode` gains `api_key_cap_reached`.

## What the task asked for

The client had drifted from the API it wraps. It accepted `"html"` alone as an
output format. It dropped the `discovery` parameter and the field echoing it.
It offered no way to ask for a page as a file. It knew one run error code fewer
than the API can answer with.

## How the check confirmed it

`pnpm run check` passes on 41 files and `pnpm exec vitest run` passes, 369
tests with no type errors. This change adds two checks to the Crawl acceptance
suite: 22 for `discovery` and 23 for `content(..., { download: true })`.

A running Crawl service answered the same way. It took `discovery: ["links"]`
and came back with `["links"]`, and a create that left it out came back with
the same. It took `output_format: "markdown"` and came back with `markdown`.

`Encoded by`: acceptance checks 22 and 23.

## How to try it

```ts
const crawl = await client.crawl.create({ url: "https://example.com/", outputFormat: "markdown" });
console.log(crawl.discovery);                       // ["links"]
const page = await client.crawl.content(crawl.crawl_id, result, { download: true });
```

## Provenance

`discovery` is optional on the response type, not required. The API documents
`["links"]` as the default. An optional field also parses an answer from a
server that does not send it yet. A required one would reject the whole
response instead.

The discovery type lists `links` only. A crawl can report a strategy this
version does not list, and the open string type carries it through.

The lock records the API description this surface follows. It lists
`GET /healthz` and `POST /internal/v1/crawls/{crawl_id}/stop` as pending. Both
are in the description and callers cannot reach either. Listing them keeps a
change to either from reading as drift here.

## Review

| Severity | File and line | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Low | — | No finding survived the pass. |

One pass, by the author. Human must verify: that the default of `["links"]` is
the right reading for a crawl created before `discovery` existed.

## Deviations

None.

## Record owed

None.

author: michaelfeil
body:
UltraBERT classification checkpoints now load their saved `classifier.weight`/`classifier.bias` head and nested `ultrabert.*` encoder. Sequence classification scores CLS; token classification scores each logical token. Both reuse the embedding encoder, Mistral layers, rotary caches, and attention dispatch.

Supports the trained 150M/380M UltraBERT MSMARCO rerankers through `/rerank` and `/predict`, multi-class sequence heads through `/predict`, and token heads through `/predict_tokens`. Default HF label mappings are restored when metadata omits them. Missing trained heads and inconsistent label counts are rejected; masked-LM base weights are not silently treated as trained classifiers.

Five files, 227 additions / 9 deletions. No new model implementation, kernel, dependency, or checkpoint artifact.

Validation:
- Independent HF float32 SDPA references for both trained rerankers (150M revision b8d94a0187a6b14a3ba6707602a346fdb4c4d7d6; 380M revision 8eb108396bb418225e546122eff0837a8fe4c524), plus deterministic two-label sequence and three-label token fixtures. Fixtures test layout and bias, not classification quality.
- All fourteen ragged/single cases pass on CPU FP32/FP16 and H100 FP16/BF16; token logits are compared across sequence boundaries. The existing nine embedding reference cases still pass.
- HTTP raw reranker scores and ordering, multi-class/default labels, softmax, and token scores match their references. Sequence classification accepts 32768 tokens and rejects 32769.
- Missing-head/label-consistency and default-label unit checks, formatting, and GitHub CI pass.
- Built and verified local image `infinity-v3:ultrabert-classification-hopper`, sha256:281f3b4f0a2d8654aca095ebd6b5d5a3f749c06ecfa32dc26ca535a9caa5298a. The rebuilt container repeats the reranker, multi-class, token, and 32768/32769-token HTTP checks with `ATTN_BACKEND=fa4`, exercising FA2 fallback where needed. The image is local and has not been pushed to a registry.
- Rune container text/image answers, confidence, and probabilities exactly match the prior verified image. Rune source and its existing snapshots are unchanged. Its previously documented compact-layout snapshot issue predates this PR.

author: shezinkhais
body:
The rest of General CS to the end of the project, after #142:

- **Phase 6, #59:** room-level status events and private refocus prompts, the two parts of the issue #142 leaves out.
- **Phase 7, #65:** the scheduled purge runner.
- **Phase 8, #71:** load, reconnect and failure-recovery testing, the Teams mock adapter under load, the demo deployment, and the report.

**Based on main**, with #142, #141, #136 and #143 merged in (see below). The contract is unchanged: `room.confirm`, `room.status`, `prompt.attention` and `alert.raised` are already in `events.schema.json`, and no route is added.

## Phase 6: breakout rooms and refocus prompts

- **Rooms.**
  - A student says which room they are in with `room.confirm`. The room's status comes from its members' own voice-activity flags, so no audio is involved.
  - Staff are sent `room.status` when a room changes, and every room as it stands when a panel joins or refreshes. Students are never sent either.
  - A room nobody has been heard from is `unknown`, never `quiet`.
  - A room silent past `ROOM_NEEDS_ATTENTION_AFTER_SECONDS` raises one `breakout_inactive` alert per silence. It is stored through the `AlertRecorder`, with its confidence set to the share of members whose devices report voice.
- **Aggregation.** Scoring reads a rolling, time-weighted window of the student's signals instead of only the last one, so one glance away is a small part of two minutes.
- **Refocus prompts.** A watch looks at signals and rooms every `SIGNAL_WATCH_SECONDS`. A student gets a private prompt only when all of these hold:
  - the window covers enough time;
  - the signals alone are low (the mean of gaze and face presence is below 0.6);
  - Cyber 1's rule agrees on two kinds of evidence, one of them participation, so the camera alone never prompts anyone and a student with an accommodation is never prompted automatically;
  - the cooldown has passed.

  Every existing prompt limit still applies, and staff are not told.
- **Fits #142.**
  - The window reads each signal as `attention_windows.py` kept it, and a signal dropped as too soon counts towards neither the score nor a room.
  - Withdrawing monitoring or the microphone clears what the room heard from that student.
  - `signal.attention` and `room.confirm` are throttled per socket before they take the session lock.

## Phase 7: the purge runner

- `retention-purge` runs `PurgeRunner` daily from the app's scheduler.
- Each task deletes a bounded batch at a time, oldest first, and the runner stops between batches while any class is running.
- A run is held to `RETENTION_PURGE_TIMEOUT_MINUTES`; one cut short carries on next time.
- A zero retention period is refused.
- Each run logs one `retention_purge` line saying what it deleted.
- General CS registers the upload-file purge.

## Phase 8: load and failure recovery

`python -m scripts.loadtest` runs the backend as its own process, in production mode, against a throwaway database, with one real WebSocket per client. The full results are in `docs/load-and-recovery.md` and `docs/load-test-results.json`. All **68 of 68 checks passed**, including the database outage. Measured on one Windows machine:

- **40 students:** connected in 1.2 s. A question reached all of them with a median of 18 ms after the lecturer's click, of which the server's send was 1 to 2 ms. The median answer receipt was 15 ms.
- **Reconnects:** half the class dropping mid-question and the whole class at once were both resumed from their cursors, with nothing missed or repeated. A cursor from a stream before a restart is refused.
- **Signals and rooms:** 150 frames a second. Every silent room raised one alert, every student looking away got one prompt, and no student was sent room data.
- **Reports and the purge:** a report was built during a class without slowing questions. Every purge run during the class gave way to it.
- **Crash, restart and database outage:** after a crash and after a planned restart the class carried on. With the database down, no socket dropped, and only requests that need it failed.
- **Model down:** the tutor fails plainly and the class is unaffected.
- **Scheduler:** ten sessions on the automatic cycle, worst lateness 0.05 s.

The demo stack in `docker-compose.demo.yml` passed `scripts/smoke_test.py`, 12 of 12, through the nginx proxy.

## Merged with main

Main gained Cyber 1's Phase 6 work (#143), AI 2's local indicators (#136) and Cyber 2's panel (#141) after this was opened. The conflicts were in `ws.py`, `attention.py` and `classroom.py`, and both sides are kept:

- **Personal baselines** learn from the signal window's summary, once per question close and once per new signal. The watch rescores without teaching the baseline.
- **Accommodations:** the watch passes the accommodation flag to scoring, as a question close does.
- **Consent:** withdrawing the camera purges the visual baseline. Withdrawing monitoring or the microphone still clears what the room heard.
- **ws.py** keeps both the frame size limit and the room and signal throttles.
- **The signals-low check:** scoring no longer scores camera evidence alone, so this check is worked out from gaze and face presence directly. Through `compute_engagement` it would always be None, and the watch would never prompt.
- **Tests:** the refocus tests now give the student participation evidence first, so each no-prompt case fails for its own reason. The stress tests turn off the 2 s signal spacing, which made their room alerts depend on machine speed (8 of 8 runs pass).

**CI:** the backend check fails on the same four tests that fail on main, the three baseline tests in `test_engagement_fairness_live.py` and `test_no_table_stores_a_raw_attention_reading`. #149 fixes them; with its two test files applied, they pass on this branch too.

## Testing

- **Suite:** 2005 passed after the merge; the 4 failures are main's, fixed by #149. ruff, the format check and `export_contract.py --check` are clean.
- **Stress run:** signals, rooms, answers, reconnects and consent withdrawal in random order over 12 seeds.
- **Mutation pass over the new guards:** of the survivors, two are guarded twice, which is noted in the code, and one is now killed by a new test.

## For the other workstreams

- **BBIS:** register a table purge with `get_purge_runner().register(task)`; see `docs/reports.md`. Until then only upload files are purged, which is all the README now claims.
- **Cyber 2 (#141):** room status arrives as `room.status` over the socket, with every room sent when the panel joins. There is no REST rooms route. A room sent with `members: 0` has emptied and should be removed from the panel.
- **AI 2 (#136):** sending every 5 s with `window_seconds` counted from sensor start fits what the server keeps.
- **Cyber 1:** the refocus prompt uses `should_send_dynamic_prompt` unchanged, plus a check that the signals on their own fall below `ENGAGED_THRESHOLD`. Your baseline is fed the window's summary rather than a single reading.
- **Not done here:** no frontend for rooms or reports. That is Cyber 2's.

author: nosmile99
body:
Fixes #867.

`links discover` and `links batch-suggest` (plus the MCP tools and REST routes) accepted any `--mode` value and silently answered as keyword with exit 0. `LinkDiscoveryService.discover_neighbors` now validates the mode up front and raises `ValidationError` naming the three valid modes (`keyword`, `semantic`, `hybrid`); `batch_suggest` is covered through its delegation. The refusal surfaces unchanged on every transport: CLI exits 1 with `VALIDATION_FAILED`, MCP returns the refusal envelope, REST answers 422.

Regression test: `tests/test_link_mode_validation.py` — 9 tests driving all six surfaces; 8 fail on pre-fix code, all 9 pass post-fix (the 9th guards that valid modes still run). Related suites green: link suites 54/54, MCP read scoping 53 passed + 2 skipped.

**Review follow-up (eb722c87):** `batch_suggest` now validates the mode at its own top as well — previously an empty source KB returned `[]` for a bad mode without ever reaching `discover_neighbors`' validation. Added `test_service_batch_suggest_refuses_before_empty_source_loop` (10/10 pass) and `changelog.d/867-link-discovery-mode-validation.fixed.md`.

**Notes from the review:** the check is exact membership in `("keyword", "semantic", "hybrid")`, so a differently cased mode like `Keyword` is refused too (verified: raises `ValidationError` naming the three valid modes).

`pyrite search --mode` has the same gap and is deliberately out of scope here: `SearchService.search()` maps any unknown mode to `SearchMode.KEYWORD` via `try/except ValueError`, and the trace then reports `requested_mode: keyword`, rewriting the caller's input so the mistake is undetectable (verified: `svc.search(query="hello", mode="zzz", trace=tr)` runs fine with `requested_mode`/`actual_mode` both `keyword`). Filed separately as #917 with repro, root cause, and the same up-front-validation fix shape.

author: guim31
body:
## What

A Gladys external integration for **ecobee** thermostats and their SmartSensors, through the ecobee cloud. It needs Gladys ≥ 5.2.0 (the `thermostat/preset` feature type and the widget button forms).

- **Sign-in**: ecobee closed its developer program to new API keys in 2024, so the main path is the ecobee web-portal login. It goes through Auth0 on `auth.ecobee.com` with authorization code + PKCE, handles two-step verification by authenticator app or SMS through an action, and is the same flow `python-ecobee-api` 0.4.4 and Home Assistant use. A developer API key that someone still has also works, through its PIN. Tokens are kept in `/data/ecobee-session.json`; the password is never written there.
- **Devices**:
  - One device per thermostat: temperature, humidity, heat and cool setpoints, mode, auxiliary heat only, operating state, fan always on, fan running, comfort setting (Gladys preset: schedule/Home/Away/Sleep), the comfort setting in effect, the hold in effect, and occupancy.
  - One device per remote sensor: temperature and occupancy.
- **Commands**: changes made from Gladys are holds that last until the next program change by default, like in the ecobee app.
- **Scene actions**: `resume_program`, `set_comfort`, `start_vacation`, `cancel_vacation`.
- **Scene triggers**: `home_occupied` and `home_vacant` (aggregated over the thermostat and all its sensors, which a single feature cannot express), and `alert`.
- **Widget** `thermostat`: live tiles, setpoint lower and raise, and mode and comfort forms.
- **Refresh**: the integration runs its own timer, every 3 minutes by default (the minimum ecobee asks for). The core's `onPoll` is only a fallback because of Gladys#3198. Only changed values are published, plus a heartbeat every 6 h.
- **Languages**: en, fr, de and es everywhere, including the four docs.
- `scripts/probe.mjs` tests the real client read-only. The session proxy refuses ecobee, so it has to be run elsewhere.

## Checks

- `npm test`: 158 tests pass. That includes `gladys-rules.test.js` (48 scenarios: 4 fixtures × 4 languages × 3 unit choices) and `i18n.test.js`.
- `format:check` and `lint` pass.
- The store validator passes with `--skip-image-check`.

Developed without the hardware or an ecobee account.
