author: sdougbrown
body:
Staging PR for review before submitting upstream (tracks earendil-works/pi#10628).

Copy-on-select in the fullscreen TUI emits a raw OSC 52, which tmux consumes into its own paste buffer without relaying it to the client — confirmed on tmux 3.4 and 3.5a with `set-clipboard on`, `Ms` advertised, and an OSC 52-capable outer terminal. On a headless Linux host over SSH, OSC 52 is the only copy route, so copies silently do nothing while pi flashes "Copied!".

## Changes

- `packages/tui/src/terminal.ts`: new exported `tmuxPassthrough(sequence)` — wraps a sequence in the tmux DCS passthrough (`\ePtmux;\e<seq>\e\\`) when `$TMUX` is set; byte pattern matches the convention used by kitty's clipboard kitten and the nvim osc52 plugins.
- Both OSC 52 emit sites now go through it: `packages/tui/src/tui-alt-screen.ts` (TUI fallback) and `packages/coding-agent/src/utils/clipboard.ts` (`emitOsc52`).
- `packages/coding-agent`: new `clipboard.copyCommand` setting — a shell command that receives copied text on stdin, tried before the built-in backends; a failure falls through to the built-ins and OSC 52, so it is strictly an override. Remote sessions still dual-write OSC 52. Precedent: tmux's `copy-command` option and vim's `g:clipboard` providers. Wired through `SettingsManager.getClipboardCopyCommand()` into both fullscreen copy paths and the `/tree` selector copy.
- `docs/settings.md`: documented the new setting.

## Validation

- `packages/tui`: `node --test test/terminal.test.ts test/tui-alt-screen.test.ts` — 88 pass (includes new `tmuxPassthrough` unit tests for both branches with exact-byte assertions, and a mouse-drag integration test for the wrapped write)
- `packages/coding-agent`: `node node_modules/vitest/dist/cli.js --run test/clipboard.test.ts` — 35 pass (includes copyCommand precedence, fallback to built-ins, fallback to OSC 52, and exact unwrapped-bytes assertion)
- `npx biome check packages/coding-agent packages/tui` — clean
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — only the pre-existing `packages/ai/test/together-models.test.ts` error (stale test expectation vs regenerated catalog; present on upstream/main)
- End-to-end: fake-client mouse drag against the patched build relayed the wrapped OSC 52 through the inner tmux to the client

## Limitations

- The passthrough survives one tmux layer; deeper nesting needs the intermediate layer to bridge via the `pane-set-clipboard` hook — no writer-side strategy can be depth-agnostic since `$TMUX` carries no depth.
- With the wrap, the selection no longer lands in the inner tmux paste buffer as a side effect, so `prefix ]` paste of pi copies is lost when the outer terminal lacks OSC 52 support.
- `copyCommand` executes via `sh -c`; on Windows it fails and falls through to the built-in path.

author: leyvanah
body:
Task: leyvanah/talkkeeper-tasks#105 (part 1 of 2: point 3 of the task)

## Problem

Point 3 of the task asked whether starting a recording with live text breaks a summary being written for the previous meeting. It does. Loading any recognition model goes through `audio::common::prepare_for_stt`, which calls `force_shutdown_sidecar()` unconditionally: the built-in summary model is stopped mid-answer and the summary ends with an error. The same happens when the next recording's refining pass loads its model — which is exactly the queue scenario in the task.

The other direction was already safe: a summary starting during a refining pass waits on the engine lock the pass holds (`SttBatchLease`) before it unloads recognition.

## What changes

- A summary holds a `SummaryWriting` guard for its whole background run (`api_process_transcript`). A long meeting is summarised in several requests, so the sidecar's own "request in flight" counter alone would leave gaps between them.
- The sidecar exposes `has_active_requests()`, so single requests (meeting chat, person overview) count too.
- `prepare_for_stt` leaves the summary model running while either says it is busy, and logs it. Both models share memory until the summary is done; the sidecar's idle shutdown frees the LLM afterwards, as it does now.

Points 1–2 of the task (summary for meetings processed in the queue, and the queue surviving a restart) come in a separate PR stacked on #47, which changes the same post-call code.

## Checks

- `cargo test --tests --no-fail-fast` — library 693 passed + 1 failed, integration tests 23 passed. The failure is the timing test `loudness_normalizer_tests::the_microphone_chain_keeps_far_ahead_of_the_device` (median per-second cost under a parallel suite); untouched here, passed 3/3 rerun alone on the same build. New test: `a_summary_keeps_the_model_busy_until_its_guard_is_dropped`.
- Not run in the app — manual check below.

## Manual check (dev, built-in summary model)

1. Record ~1 minute, Stop, let the summary start. While it is being written, start a new recording with live text → the summary finishes; the log has "builtin LLM kept: it is still answering".
2. Without a summary running, starting a recording still frees the summary model as before ("shutting down builtin LLM if running").

author: rafaelngp
body:
Free, rule-based triage of issues (option 1 of the discussion): no AI, no secrets.

## How it works
- `.github/workflows/issue-triage.yml`: on issues **opened / edited / reopened**, and by hand (*Actions > Issue triage > Run workflow*, with an issue number) for issues already there. Token permission: `issues: write` only.
- `.github/triage/triage.py` (stdlib Python) reads the bug form's fields and matches `.github/triage/rules.json`:
  - known problems → `area: …` label + a short explanation (certificates -15872 *fixed in 0.9.6*, certificate verification -9984 → console date/time, region refusal, Xbox not waking, entitlement, free-to-play, controller, crash);
  - release older than the fix or than the latest → asks to update (`outdated-version`);
  - missing release or log on a bug form → asks for it (`needs-info`), pointing to *Report a problem*;
  - firmware → `fw: X.YY` label (an app version typed there is ignored).
- Adds labels only (never removes yours), creates them the first time; **one** comment per issue, updated in place on edits.
- Safety: the issue text is untrusted — it's only matched with regexes, never put on a command line; the script and rules come from the default branch.

Adding a known problem later = one entry in `rules.json` (+ a test).

## Tested
- 9 unit tests on made-up issues (run in CI, new `triage-rules` job).
- Dry run on the 5 real issues: #45 → certificates/clock + asks for the release; #38/#20 → fixed in 0.9.6; #39 → controller + outdated + asks for the log; #10 → free-to-play. (Caught and fixed a false "crash" from "in**stalled**".)
- Read-only GitHub API check (latest release, issue, comments).

After merging, existing open issues (#45, #39) can be triaged with *Run workflow*.

author: totallynotkasai
body:
Phase 24 of round two: **Block Drop**, a classic falling-blocks game in Solo Games ("tetris" is a search keyword). It has the next-piece preview, a ghost piece, hard drop, levels that speed up and a saved best, and no hold.

## Rules (`games/blockdrop/BlockDropGame.kt`)
- A 10 × 20 well, with the seven pieces dealt from a shuffled bag of seven.
- Clockwise turns. A turn tries the piece in place, then a column either way, then a row up (for the floor). The I also tries two columns and two rows. The O doesn't turn.
- A half-second lock delay. A move or turn on the ground restarts it up to 15 times, and reaching a new lowest row gives the 15 back. After that the piece locks as soon as it's on the ground.
- 100 / 300 / 500 / 800 × level for 1–4 rows, and a point a row for soft and hard drops.
- The level goes up every 10 lines. Gravity follows the usual curve: 1 s a row at level 1, about 0.06 s at level 10, with no further speed-up after level 15.
- Full rows flash for 0.3 s before they go.
- The game ends when the next piece has no room, or when a piece locks above the top.

## Screen
- The well beside a panel of Next, Score, Best, Level and Lines, in the classic piece colours on a dark well (both themes).
- Play on the empty well to start. **Pause** in the top bar (as in Snake), and leaving the app pauses too. Paused and Game over show a `GameOverCard` over the dimmed well. New game asks first once you've scored.
- **Controls, anywhere on the screen:** drag sideways to move a column per cell, drag down to soft drop a row per cell, and flick down (over 1,500 dp/s) to hard drop. A tap turns the piece. Each drag sticks to the direction it starts in.
- **Feel:** ticks for moves and soft drops, a soft tone for turns, and a knock for locks (louder for a hard drop). Lines play a C major chord, four lines a bigger six-note chord, and a level-up two rising notes. Light, firm and heavy taps go through `Vibes`.
- **TalkBack:** the well reads e.g. "Well, T piece in columns 4 to 6. Score 120". Its actions menu has Move left, Move right, Rotate, Soft drop and Hard drop, and clearing rows is announced.
- **Saved state:** a recreation or process death brings the game back paused, rows mid-clear included.
- **Icon:** a new `ToolIcons.BlockDrop` glyph, a T piece a row above the notch it fits, on a red tile.

## Website
The site is served live from `main`, so the tile waits for 1.3.0, by the owner's choice. `WebsiteTest` now skips tools in an `unreleased` set, and the site still says 40 tools. `docs/icons/blockdrop.svg` is exported but not linked yet. Phase 28 adds the tile and empties the set.

- New `BlockDropTest` (13): the bag, starting positions, wall and floor kicks, a turn with no room, walls, drops and the ghost, line scores by level, gravity, the lock delay, its cap and its reset, both kinds of game over, and saved state.
- `GamesA11yTest` (1): the well's TalkBack state.

- Search finds it under "tetris" and "block", and the icon reads well on the home grid.
- In play: moves, turns, soft and hard drops and the ghost. A line clear was caught mid-flash (37 → 155, 1 line).
- Pause and its card, the New game confirm, and Game over with "New best!". The best survives a force-stop.
- A process death while paused mid-clear came back in a new process with everything in place, and finished the clear on Resume.
- Dark mode and 1.3× text.

## To check by hand on the phone
The phone runs release 1.2.0, so these wait for the 1.3.0 update:
- [ ] Sounds: the move tick, the turn tone, the lock knock, and the chords for one line and for four lines.
- [ ] Vibration on moves, locks and lines. It should stay light, not buzzy.

author: parth-patil-uipath
body:
**TL;DR:** Two short additions to the Automation Hub publish guidance. Both come from what the RPANAV-19150 live evals caught the CI agent doing:
- **Slow create:** wait on a create that takes a while, and never start a second one; doing so duplicated the process.
- **Category:** pick the most specific active category that fits, and "Other" only when nothing does.

## Summary

```diff
 references/publish-process-cli-guide.md  Step 5: Create the process
+  The create can take 20–30 s. Run it as its own command, not chained behind the
+  preflight checks, and wait for its envelope. If your shell hands back before the
+  command finishes, wait on that same command; never start a second create and never
+  read the silence as a failure.

 references/publish-process-cli-guide.md  Category id      (CLI flow)
 references/publish-process.md            Category id      (API flow)
-  pick from the tree (category_is_active: 1 only); several plausible → ask with names
+  pick from the tree (category_is_active: 1 only): the most specific one that fits the
+  material, and "Other" only when nothing fits; several plausible → ask with names
```

## Evidence

From the live smoke runs of the RPANAV-19150 eval stack on alpha DefaultTenant (agent: Codex `gpt-5.6-luna`), 2026-10-14:

- **Before (slow create):** `automations create` took 13–20 s while several runs hit the tenant. The agent's shell handed back at about 10 s: "the create call returned without a visible JSON envelope after about ten seconds". The agent then did one of two things:
  - ran the create again: two successful creates, a duplicate process (2 runs, #3760 and #3850);
  - stopped without attaching the PDD: "the single create command returned no JSON result" (3 runs).
- **Before (category):** for a retail account-onboarding PDD, the agent picked "Other" in 2 runs, although the tenant has "Manage customers and accounts", which other runs picked.
- **After:** the stack's smoke runs pick this up once it merges and #3760 is rebased on it. The skill's own checks here (CLI verb gate, skill descriptions, package build) are this PR's CI.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. Guidance text only.

**Blast Radius:** low. Every agent using the publish flow reads it.
- The create change only adds "wait, don't re-run"; how a success or a failure is handled is unchanged.
- The category change narrows a choice the guide already left to judgment.

author: gaborbernat
body:
I checked each README claim against a real `sphinx-build -b text` run on current main and corrected the ones the output disproves. 📝 Only the README changes; the main sentences:

```diff
-If types appear twice in your docs, you're likely running both this extension and Sphinx's built-in type hint processing.
+With Sphinx's own `autodoc_typehints` set to `"description"` or `"both"`, Sphinx adds the parameters a docstring leaves out with its own plain, unlinked types (`y (*str*)`) next to the ones this extension writes.

-To avoid duplicate return type entries, disable the return type block in both extensions:
+Napoleon and this extension share one return type by default: napoleon's `:rtype:` gives way to the annotation. With `napoleon_use_rtype = False`, napoleon puts the docstring's type in the `Returns` text instead, so set `typehints_use_rtype = False` too, or the type shows twice:

-or `napoleon_use_keyword` set to `False`, napoleon lists all parameters in one field
+or `napoleon_use_keyword` set to `False`, napoleon lists the parameters, or the keyword arguments, in one field each

-the class is documented with `.. autoclass::` and `:members:` or `:undoc-members:`.
+the class is documented with `.. autoclass::` and both `:members:` and `:undoc-members:`, since a field without a docstring is otherwise skipped.

-- **Disabled** (`typehints_document_rtype = False`) -- no return type shown, regardless of other settings.
+- **Disabled** (`typehints_document_rtype = False`) -- no return type is added from the annotation, regardless of other settings; an `:rtype:` written in the docstring stays as written.

-| `typehints_fully_qualified`      | `False` |
+| `typehints_fully_qualified`      | follows `autodoc_typehints_format` |
```

The builds behind them: with napoleon's defaults the return type shows once, only [`napoleon_use_rtype = False`](https://www.sphinx-doc.org/en/master/usage/extensions/napoleon.html#confval-napoleon_use_rtype) alone doubles it, and the old recommended pair swaps the annotation's `list[int]` for the docstring's `list`. A dataclass or `TypedDict` with only one of the two options renders just the class, and with `autodoc_typehints_format = "fully-qualified"` a `Path` renders as `"pathlib.Path"`. The README also gains four notes: `simplify_optional_unions` only matters before Python 3.14, where [`Union` and `|` are the same object](https://docs.python.org/3.14/whatsnew/3.14.html#typing); the generator example's `bool` return type needs napoleon, since without it the whole `Generator[...]` shows; a plain alias such as `Count = int` needs its `.. py:type::` entry read before the function, while a `type` statement alias doesn't; and "How it works" says signatures keep their annotations under `typehints_use_signature` or `typehints_use_signature_return`. The repeated `NewType` explanation is gone from the alias section, since the "Typing constructs" table covers it.

author: wjarka
body: ## Why Squeal's browser tier on `main` failed dozens of specs with `the agent-browser provider is not installed`. Chrome is fine (`browser-doctor.json` passes every check). The real chain of failure: 1. `test-env-up.sh` served the checkout itself (`--repo $REPO_ROOT`). In the main checkout, `.ai/cezar` is the live cockpit's data dir. The cockpit holds `cockpit.lock`, so the e2e server refused to boot: `A cockpit already serves /home/agent/projects/cezar/.ai/cezar at http://0.0.0.0:4321` (`.ai/qa/test-env-app.log`). 2. The descriptor is written only after a healthy boot, so a `status: "running"` descriptor from 2026-09-12 survived. Its pid was dead, and its browser notes said `installed: false`. 3. Every spec read that descriptor and reported a missing browser (or `fetch failed` against the dead `baseUrl`) instead of the boot error. A boot that did get through would have been worse: its test runs, task worktrees and seeded skills would have landed in the user's real data dir. ## What - **The server serves an isolated clone.** On each cold boot, `.ai/scripts/e2e-served-repo.mjs` builds a fresh clone at `.ai/qa/served/`, using the same construction as a local lane (`cloneIsolatedCheckout`, extracted from `createLane`): own objects and refs, `HEAD` plus the current tracked edits and untracked source files. The descriptor records it as `servedRoot`, and reuse requires it, so a pre-change descriptor is never reused. A lane is already such a clone and serves itself. The helper replaces only a clone it created itself (`removeLane`'s ownership checks), and it refuses an unignored target inside the checkout, which would otherwise copy into itself. - **A cold boot deletes the old descriptor first**, so a failed boot leaves "no env" plus a pointer to `test-env-app.log`, not a dead env's browser notes. - **Specs that seed server-read state** (skills, workflows, `.ai/cezar` config/todos, the boot project's registry root) write under `servedRoot()` from `agent-browser.ts`, not under paths derived from `import.meta.dirname`. Evidence and artifacts stay in the checkout's `.ai/qa`. - Docs: `packages/web/e2e/README.md` (new section) and AGENTS.md validation. Squeal inputs now include the two scripts. Cost: about 2 s per cold boot (a local mirror clone of the ~730 MB pack; a CI shallow checkout clones shallow, which I tested). Scope note: this also isolates task worktrees and CI rather than only the main checkout. That keeps one code path, which CI exercises, and stops dry-run task worktrees landing in the shared repository. ## Verification - New and changed launcher tests (`test-env-launcher.test.ts`): serves an isolated clone with the current edits, refuses a legacy descriptor, a lane serves itself, never replaces a directory it did not create, and a failed cold boot leaves no descriptor. All 4 tests **fail against the old `test-env-up.sh` and pass with the change**. - Squeal unit tiers: 0 known failures at the final revision (an unrelated `spawnSync ETIMEDOUT` flake at load average ~130 cleared on rerun). - `npm run typecheck:web` and `npm run typecheck -w @wjarka/cezarion`: clean. - Focused cockpit e2e in a worktree (`env -u CEZ_AUTOMATIONS npm run test:e2e -- `): **11 files, 78 passed, 6 skipped, `TEST_E2E_STATUS=passed`**. The real boot refused the old descriptor, cloned, and was healthy after 8 s. A before/after listing of the checkout's `.ai/cezar` and `.ai/skills` shows no new writes; the server's runs.db and workflows landed in the clone. - Full browser suite and package E2E: left to CI. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

author: janit
body:
## What was wrong

`packageDirsAt` decides which top-level directories are scanned for a nested `node_modules` / `.venv` / `vendor` to link into a worktree (#481). Its marker check was

```ts
DEPENDENCY_MARKERS.some((m) => fileExists(path.join(repoRoot, dir, m)))
```

`fileExists` returns a Promise, and a Promise is always truthy, so the filter passed every directory. A docs folder, or a scratch directory holding a stray `node_modules`, counted as a package directory.

## The change

The checks are awaited, one by one.

## Behaviour change to be aware of

A top-level directory that has a `node_modules` but **no** manifest or lockfile is no longer scanned, so its `node_modules` is no longer linked into worktrees. That is what #481 documented ("a depth-1 dir containing any manifest/lockfile … is scanned"), and no existing provisioning test depended on the old behaviour — all of them pass unchanged.

Port notes: applied to upstream `main` without conflicts.

Closes #1226

Ported from janit/pi-rukas#42 (a4523bf).

## Tests

`test-package-dirs-marker.ts` (new): five directories — `package.json`, `Cargo.toml`, no manifest, only a `node_modules`, and a dot directory. Three assertions fail on the old source, which returned all four non-dot directories.

Gate on this branch: `bun run build`, `tsc --noEmit`, `bun run check` clean; offline smoke loop `P: 550  F: 0`.

author: rasuvaeff
body:
Fixes #40

## Problem

On MariaDB 11.6.2+ (`innodb_snapshot_isolation=ON` by default) under REPEATABLE READ, `claim()`/`claimReady()` (and `releaseStaleClaims()`, same select-then-update shape) fail with `SQLSTATE[HY000]: 1020 Record has changed since last read` when another connection changes a selected row between the id `SELECT` and the guarded `UPDATE`. A plain concurrent `INSERT` does not trigger it; a change to a candidate row does.

## Fix

These transactions never rely on their snapshot — the `status`/staleness guard in the `UPDATE` re-checks every row. On the MySQL driver they now run as `READ COMMITTED`, so the guard skips a changed row instead of the engine failing the statement. SQLite (supports only READ UNCOMMITTED/SERIALIZABLE) and PostgreSQL (already READ COMMITTED by default) are unchanged. No public API change; roave reports no BC breaks against v2.6.0.

Caveats (documented in both READMEs): the level is not applied when the call runs inside a transaction the caller already opened; writes under READ COMMITTED need `binlog_format` ROW or MIXED (the defaults).

## Tests

- `CrossDatabaseMigrationTest::claimSurvivesACandidateChangedAfterItsSelect`: a second connection takes a candidate row between the select and the update (the injected clock is the seam — the claim reads it once, after the select). Fails with 1020 on MariaDB 11.8 without the fix; passes on MariaDB 11.8, MySQL 8.4 and PostgreSQL 17 with it.
- `database-integration` matrix gains a `mariadb` leg (`mariadb:11.8`, digest-pinned).
- Local: `composer build` green, mutation Covered MSI 97% (gate 93), no escaped mutants in the new code.

author: morio
body:
Some BIOSes issue ATA commands unsupported by an ATAPI device like a CD-ROM drive. Added a command handler, `cmd_unsupported()`, that hides the failed command from the log file with debug off. It now reports that ATAPI does not support the ATA command with debug on.

Current ATA commands using the `cmd_unsupported()` handler:
 - Initialize Device Parameter (Set CHS settings)
 - Set Multiple Mode (sets number of block to transfer via R/W multiple)

These commands were issue by the BIOS of an Intel Entry Server Board SE7230NH1-E.

## Problema
Ladina (Algoz, besta), quinta heroína do MVP2.6: kit completo e jogável no servidor autoritativo, escolhível na seleção e jogada pelo bot. refs #162

## Antes / Depois
- Antes: 4 heróis. Depois: 5, com Virote, Rajada em Leque (3 virotes a −12°/0°/+12°), Bomba de Fumaça (nuvem de 3 u por 3 s que vale como moita para qualquer herói; lançar não revela) e Emboscada (avanço de 8 u, golpe único, ×1,3 se oculta).
- A nuvem chega ao cliente por evento do servidor (`ImpactRelay.smoke_shown`), não pelo estado da Ladina, que some de quem está fora dela.
- Bot (todos os heróis): passa a gastar o ponto de habilidade pela curva típica do GDB §3.2; antes o E só chegava no nível 7 e a fumaça nunca saía.
- Capturas no roadmap: `mvp2.6-f58-ladina-fumaca.webp`, `mvp2.6-f58-ladina-emboscada.webp`.

## SPEC / Fonte
SPEC-058, ADR-0013, GDB §4.5 e §7.3, CONVENTION §4.7.

## Validação executada
- GUT: 1005/1005 (dados, Rajada a 1,5 u / 6,5 u, Muralha, nuvem, Emboscada com e sem ×1,3, bot, VFX, relay, equipamento).
- Soak `tools/soak.ps1 -Count 50 -Require rogue`: 50/50 terminadas, 0 falhas, 358–410 s, todas com vencedor.
- Offline `--bot --bot-hero=rogue --autopilot=bot` (seeds 1–3): fase 1 completa, fim por kill_goal, 0 erros.
- Frame time (`--equip --smoke`): GPU 3,68–3,69 ms vs 3,63–3,68 ms da base; CPU 4,44–4,46 vs 4,32–4,96 ms.
- Docker 100 ms: Ladina × Cavaleiro e × Arqueira limpos (0 `past the history limit`, 0 `Node not found`, 0 estado recebido escondido).
- Lint local: `gdlint`, `gdformat --check`, tipagem (`check_scripts.gd`) e `no-magic-numbers` verdes.
- Verificação visual do PI aprovada em 2026-10-14.

## Limitações / o que não entrou
- Medição de rede × Bárbaro e × Bruxo pendente: o Docker Desktop (VM do WSL com 4 GB) caiu durante o build; o PI aceitou o card assim. Roteiro no `DEVELOPMENT.md`.
- Balanceamento: a Ladina perdeu as 40 partidas do soak contra outros heróis (chega aos 5:00 no nível 4). Registrado para o F30/MVP4 por decisão do PI; números do GDB §4.5 mantidos.
- Tamanho: 136 arquivos, ~2/3 são `.glb`/`.png` e seus `.import`/`.uid` (modelo, VFX, 3 raridades de besta, ícones). O código é o que está em `game/scripts/` e `game/test/`.

author: jfrader
body:
## Las dos cosas que Fran marcó

**1. La página `#/components/card-flights-regressions` no debería existir.** El archivo de historias de regresión declaraba su propio título (`Games/CardFlights/Regressions`) y el motor de docs arma **una página por título** — era el único de los 226 archivos de historia del repo con un título de tres niveles. Su `!autodocs` ocultaba historias, no la página.

Arreglo con la convención de la casa (un archivo de historia por componente; las pruebas técnicas dentro, marcadas `!autodocs`, como hace Combobox): **se borran los dos archivos** (`card-flights-regressions.stories.tsx` y `card-flights-regression-fixture.tsx`) y sus historias se fusionan con las del componente — **los 14 bloques `play` quedaron byte por byte** — con nombres por lo que prueban, sin "regressions" en el código.

**2. El provider exigía `div` + `ref`.** Ahora `<CardFlightsProvider>` **posee su scope**: renderiza el wrapper él mismo y acepta `component` (azúcar de `slots.root`), `slots.root`, `slotProps.root`, `className`, `sx` y `ref`; `scopeRef` queda como escape hatch opcional que apunta el scope a un elemento del consumidor y no renderiza wrapper (cubierto por la historia `ExternalScope`).

Así se lee ahora:

```tsx
<CardFlightsProvider>
  <Match />
</CardFlightsProvider>
```

## Verificación

`pnpm generate`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm verify:exports` (113), `pnpm verify:docs` con el guard de uso autorado (112 archivos de historia, uno menos por el archivo borrado), y **18 pruebas** de CardFlights con axe en `error`. `pnpm --filter @jfrader/docs build` y **Chromium aislado**: no queda ninguna entrada `card-flights-regressions`, hay un solo enlace CardFlights y ninguna historia técnica a la vista (captura: `/tmp/opencode/screenshots/games-2409/card-flights.png`).

Incluye el merge de master resuelto a mano: master había pasado los snippets a imports por subpath (GURI-2359) y esta rama reescribía el mismo bloque; quedaron los subpaths **y** la forma nueva del provider.

## Queda para GURI-2410

El `querySelector` que todavía vive en la fixture es el que borra el registro interno de GURI-2410 — CardFlights: un hook y registro interno — el consumidor no consulta el DOM ni arma el estado del reparto.

Refs GURI-2409

author: g1ovell
body:
## 概要

渠道服（vivo、九游、4399、应用宝、MuMu）在会话重置、刷开局前后的登录适配。基于当前 main `098686e`：

| 提交 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `207a89f` | 渠道 SDK 登录界面无障碍推进；渠道 SDK 临时竖屏不再停止屏幕捕获 |
| `fed2f6f` | 渠道登录界面同时覆盖入口流程与会话重置起点；渠道专属行为改为按选中账号的服务器开关 |
| `89f41c7` | 4399 / 应用宝 / MuMu：刷开局登录游戏服前先大退客户端，刷完冷启动 |
| `a369c9d` | 文档：4399 刷开局前大退实机确认通过 |
| `8ae931f` | 删除实机未生效的 4399 无障碍点击规则，以及只为 4399 游戏盒授权页加的「登录时游戏不在前台继续等」 |

除下表列出的服务器外，其他服务器（含国服 B 服、小米、华为、OPPO）的行为与 main 相同。

## 问题与依据

| 渠道 | 现象 | 证据 |
|---|---|---|
| vivo | 返回标题后 vivo SDK 的 `UnionActivity` 转竖屏约 4 秒自动登录，捕获在第一次尺寸变化时就停止，会话重置卡在 `WAITING_LOGIN` | 诊断包 2026-09-25：`updateRotationUnchecked` → `屏幕捕获停止：屏幕尺寸从1920x1080变为1080x1920` → 4 秒后 `sdk onLoginSuccess` |
| 九游 | 返回标题后弹「登录历史」对话框，入口规划器把它当公告前画面，一直点对话框外的 (950,930) | 调试包 2026-10-05：`latest.jpg` 为登录历史对话框，日志为连续 `派发点击 x=950.0 y=930.0` |
| 4399 | 返回标题后登录时 4399 SDK 报 `User not Valid`，重新弹「用户协议及隐私政策」与竖屏「账号授权」 | 诊断包 2026-10-12 / 2026-10-14：`Back_To_Title` → `PlatformManager Login` → `operate User not Valid` → 协议框 |
| 应用宝、MuMu | 6002「返回标题」重新登录后要求重新输入账号密码；直接关闭游戏再打开则不会 | 用户实测描述（无日志包） |

4399、应用宝、MuMu 的共同原因：助手刷开局时用同一账号登录游戏服，客户端被顶号；客户端随后遇到 6002 点「返回标题」时会让渠道 SDK 登出。进程被直接结束不会走这次登出，下次冷启动 SDK 静默登录。只切到后台不够：进程还活着时用启动 Intent 拉起，游戏同样会返回标题（2026-10-14 诊断包）。

## 改动

### 1. 刷开局前大退（4399 / 应用宝 / MuMu）
- `ChannelSdkTraits.closesClientBeforeReroll`：只对这三个服务器为真。
- `GameClientHardCloser`：游戏在前台时先用无障碍按主页键，确认前台已不是游戏（最多 5 秒），再 `ActivityManager.killBackgroundProcesses`。新增普通权限 `KILL_BACKGROUND_PROCESSES`，不需要 root。所有等待有上限，关不掉就不刷并给出原因。
- `LabyrinthController` 新增 `beforeRerollLogin` / `afterStandaloneReroll`，在批量刷取、批量复用开局复核、单独刷取三条路径登录游戏服前调用；单独刷取结束后冷启动。
- `GameSessionResetWorkflow.start(clientHardClosed = true)`：跳过 20 秒在场等待与触发会话失效，直接冷启动后由入口流程从标题页导航；批量记录的同步动作为 `hard-close-cold-start`。

### 2. 渠道 SDK 临时竖屏（vivo / 4399 / 九游）
- `CaptureTransientRotationGate`：显示器尺寸恰好是捕获尺寸的转置时，保留原 VirtualDisplay（不 resize，避免 MuMu 缩角问题）、丢弃旋转期间的画面，转回后 1 秒恢复投递；竖屏超过 120 秒或分辨率真正改变时，仍按原来的方式停止并要求重新授权。
- 只在 `ChannelSdkTraits.toleratesTransientRotation`（vivo / 4399 / 九游）时生效，由 `CaptureRotationPolicy` 注入；其他服务器保持「尺寸一变就停止」。

### 3. 渠道 SDK 登录界面（九游）
- `ChannelLoginPrompts.kt`：按选中账号的服务器取规则，用无障碍按文字推进。同一窗口须同时出现标题文字和目标按钮，目标文字完全相等且唯一（「登录其他手机号」这类按钮不会被点）；连续两次认到才点，同一规则冷却 4 秒、最多 3 次，用完仍在就停止并写明原因。
  - 九游「登录历史」→「最近登录」所在的账号条目。
  - 4399 曾尝试同样按文字点「用户协议及隐私政策」「账号授权」，实机未匹配到协议框，已在 `8ae931f` 删除；4399 改由第 1 节的大退解决。
- 会话重置在 `WAITING_LOGIN` 每 500 ms 轮询；起点看到渠道登录界面时跳过触发会话失效；入口流程在入口阶段同样轮询。认到界面后 1.5 秒内不判阻塞弹窗、不让入口规划器点击（入口流程「返回标题」的点击点 (961,739) 也可能落在对话框上）。
- 屏幕捕获停止时会话重置立即带原因结束，不再等到总超时。

文档：`android/docs/channel-servers.md` 已同步（渠道 SDK 登录界面、刷开局前大退、屏幕临时旋转、已知限制、实机验证）。

## 验证

| 项目 | 档位 | 结果 |
|---|---|---|
| 全量单元测试 `:app:testDebugUnitTest`（`8ae931f`） | 本地 | 1107 项，0 失败，0 错误，45 跳过（跳过项均非本 PR 新增） |
| `:app:assembleDebug` | 本地 | 通过 |
| vivo 返回标题自动登录（临时竖屏） | 实机（测试员，雷电 9，1920×1080） | 通过（`207a89f` 版本） |
| 九游登录历史 | 实机（测试员，雷电 9，1920×1080） | 通过（`207a89f` 版本） |
| vivo / 九游 在后续提交下回归 | — | **未实机回归**；与实测版本的差异：「登录时游戏不在前台继续等」已删除（恢复为 main 的判失败；两者登录页均在游戏进程内，按日志不受影响），九游新增入口流程处理 |
| 4399 刷开局前大退 | 实机（测试员，`89f41c7` 版本） | 通过 |
| 应用宝 / MuMu 刷开局前大退 | 单元测试（`GameClientHardCloserTest`、`ChannelLoginPromptsTest`） | **未实机验证** |

## 已知限制 / 待验证

- `killBackgroundProcesses` 只能结束已在后台、且没有前台服务的进程；若某渠道客户端常驻前台服务，大退可能不生效。实机可用 `adb shell pidof <包名>` 确认。
- 大退后每局多一次冷启动（启动画面、权限申请、资源检查、渠道 SDK 登录），每局会慢几十秒。
- 渠道登录界面的文字规则来自录屏与截图，SDK 改版换文案就会认不到（认不到时不点，入口流程照旧超时停止）。
- 九游「登录历史」点的是上次登录的账号，不核对它是否就是助手里选中的账号。
- 旋转容忍只在雷电 9 上观察过；MuMu 实机未验证转回后的镜像画面。
- 「查询状态」等其他登录游戏服的路径没有加大退，仍会顶号。

## 自查（android/docs/pr-checklist.md）

- 单测可达路径未新增 Android 平台 API 调用；新增等待均有上限；热路径无新增日志（旋转与点击只在状态变化时记录）。
- 渠道专属行为均按服务器开关，开关集中在 `ChannelSdkTraits`。
- 与本主题无关的改动未包含（另一个开局选人问题会单独提 PR）。

author: dmmdea
body:
feat(agent): an optional search-results rung in the compaction ladder, default off

### Added - an optional search-results rung in the compaction ladder, default off

- **What it does.** `compactOpts.SearchResults` (internal option, off by default) adds a rung to the agent loop's compaction ladder
  that thins older search listings: the grouped `search_files` output and bare `path:line:text` lines (as `grep -rn` or ripgrep
  print), alone or inside the `exit=` / `--- stdout ---` / `--- stderr ---` framing of `run_shell` and `run`. Each line is scored
  with BM25 against the objective (the last user message of the protected preamble, taken as its first 48 distinct terms in order
  of appearance; the line's own path counts as part of the line), error-looking lines get a fixed boost, and up to 30 lines, 5 per file and 15 files are kept, chosen round-robin across files
  and written back in listing order under a counted footer (`[... 74 of 100 lines elided, 12 of 30 files elided ...]`). The tool's
  own "more matches" or "truncated" note is kept. Anything that is not, line for line, one of those shapes (the `web_search` list,
  `mode:"files"` output, test output, an error result, binary or non-UTF-8 text) comes back untouched, and so does a result that is
  not strictly shorter.
- **How it sits in the ladder.** One struct field and one call site, after dedupe and GCF and before the generic skeleton, over the
  same older span as the skeleton rung: the protected preamble, the kept-recent tail and pinned bodies are never touched, only a tool
  message's body changes, and pairing is intact. The result opens with the skeleton disclosure line, so the existing idempotence
  check, the re-execute-on-repeat path (ADR 0016), the corpus harvest refusal and the elision marker's original size all treat it as
  the compaction artifact it is, with no change to any of them. There is no CLI flag or loop setter yet, and `compaction-eval` cannot
  replay the rung yet; whether it ever becomes a default is for the measurement gate to decide on a harvested corpus.
- **Why.** A long listing is the commonest bulk tool result on a small window, and the generic skeleton keeps its first and last
  lines whatever the task asks. Ranking by the task keeps the lines the task is about. The idea is documented by the Headroom
  project (Apache-2.0); this is a clean-room implementation of that documented behaviour, credited in `NOTICE`.
- **Tests.** The default ladder is pinned byte for byte before the rung existed (`internal/agent/testdata/ladder_default_golden.json`:
  the mini corpus plus frozen search-shaped and mixed transcripts, three budgets, five option sets, sha256 of messages, tool calls and
  the fit verdict; recorded from the unmodified ladder and unchanged by this change). The rung's tests were committed red first and
  pin determinism, idempotence, monotonicity, failing closed, the artifact contract, ranking (relevance, path, rare terms, line length,
  error boost), the caps, file diversity, the footer counts, the shell tools' real framing and truncation note, and the rung's place in
  the ladder (older tool bodies only, pins and the recent tail untouched, off by default, inert on the mini corpus). A 1,500-input
  mutated-listing sweep (a fuzz target runs the same properties) found one real defect before commit (a flat listing whose files
  interleave was regrouped by file); 27 source mutations were each caught by a test, and every one was proved applied and restored
  byte-clean (one more, deleting the early return after the rung, changes no output, because every later rung guards on the budget
  itself, so no test can tell it apart).
- **Measured, side note only.** On the frozen fixtures the 20 listing bodies keep about 51% of their tokens under the rung and about 46%
  under the generic skeleton, so the rung is not a size win (`TestSearchRungBodySavingsReport`); its case is what it keeps: with three
  task-relevant lines planted in each of 40 listings, the rung kept 120 of 120 and the generic skeleton 48 of 120
  (`TestSearchRungKeepsPlantedLinesReport`, a synthetic probe and not a corpus verdict). The committed mini corpus holds no listing, so
  the rung changes none of its outputs.

## Gates

body:
Call transforms now record whether they emit a zipped operand at the rendering boundary. Validated manifest templates retain their placeholder usage, and preamble construction consumes that fact instead of searching completed call source. Ordinary caller callbacks retain lexical matching at the callback boundary and can supply an explicit `uses_zipped` boolean.

This avoids unused imports when an omitted zipped datetime's literal text appears inside an ordinary string argument. Manifest-owned goldens cover emitted, omitted, and absent zipped operands through ordinary callbacks in Go and both Python target versions, alongside the Go matching-text regression. There are no new unit tests.

Validation: full suite (9,067 passed; 40,640 subtests), 100% line and branch coverage; generated Go fixtures pass compiler, vet, and runtime checks; Python fixtures run; manifest and orphan-fixture checks, formatting hooks, and Pylint pass. Fresh hosted CI is pending on the updated head.

author: joeyyax
body:
Builds on jy0 were crawling into the 2400s docker timeout. Four `next-build`s from earlier timed-out deploys were still running inside `vardo-buildkit` (12h and 23h old, ~3.4 cores, ~2.1 GB swapped). BuildKit had 6 GiB of swap on top of its 6 GiB limit, so it paged instead of failing, and two new builds landed on top. Killing the leftovers took the docs deploy from 16m11s to 71s.

## Changes

- **Build gate.** Builds queue first come, first served for the builder. Slots = `max(1, min(BuildKit memory ÷ largest recent build peak, cores ÷ 4))`, 3 GiB per build until a peak is recorded, 1 under memory pressure, never 0. `VARDO_MAX_CONCURRENT_BUILDS` overrides it. Peaks are recorded only for builds that ran alone (`build_peak` table). Logs `[queue] Waiting for the builder…` while it waits.
- **Abandoned builds.** A timeout or abort sends SIGTERM to the build client first so buildx cancels the build, then SIGKILLs the group after 15s, and settles only once the client exits. The first build into an empty builder kills any steps still running (`buildkit-runc kill`, then the step's `cgroup.kill`, since runc loses track of steps whose processes keep running).
- **No swap.** `memswap_limit` matches `mem_limit` on the BuildKit service. An over-limit build fails fast and says it hit BuildKit's limit.
- **Timeout clock.** Waiting for the builder doesn't count toward the sweeper's 45-minute budget.
- **SSE.** The app events and gateway streams drop events only for a client that stopped reading, not whenever one chunk is queued.
- Vitest capped at half the cores.

Stays out of every file #1004 touches. The deploy stream route's copy of the SSE bug is fixed in #1004; wait events for the UI follow on top of it.

## Deploy notes

- `memswap_limit` applies only when the BuildKit container is recreated. jy0 already has it live (`docker update`), so nothing to do there.
- Compose builds are gated and swept, but don't record a peak or pause the timeout clock yet (`swap.ts` is a #1004 file).

## Verification

- `pnpm test`: 853 files, 12,089 passed, 1 skipped. `pnpm build` passes.
- Orphan behavior checked on jy0: `buildkit-runc list` showed the dead steps as `stopped`, PID 0, with their cgroups still at `/sys/fs/cgroup/buildkit/<id>`.
- Gate admission tested against a real Redis 7.4.

author: michaelegner
body:
# Plan — v0.7.0 I3.1c: independent expected answers (oracle) and matrix

Planning started at 2026-10-14T17:07:10Z. I3.1a (#539) and I3.1b (#540, `1ff3f64`) are merged: decision record D1–D12 and the frozen `0.7` models/schemas exist. This slice authors the **expected public answers before any projection code** (I3 §12: "Expected outputs SHALL not be generated from AIP execution"). I3.2 (projection) and I3.3 (REST/MCP/evidence resolver) are **not** part of this PR.

## Governing Specification
`docs/specifications/0.7.0/i3-api-aware-current-state-projection-and-public-answer.md` §12 (20 required rows), §13 "I3.1" (the last bullet); decision record D11 (case list A01–A19, E01–E02, C01, V01…), D3–D9, D12. Precedent: v0.6.0 I3.1c (`docs/specifications/0.6.0/i3-vectors/author_expected_answers.py` → `expected-answers.json`, `i3-expected-answer-matrix.md`, `tests/unit/test_v060_i3_expected_answers.py`).

## Scope (docs + one unit test; no `app/` change)
1. **`docs/specifications/0.7.0/i3-vectors/author_expected_answers.py`** — standalone, **stdlib-only** (imports nothing from `app`; same allowed-import set as v0.6: `__future__, copy, hashlib, json, pathlib, typing` + `base64`), writes `expected-answers.json` next to it byte-for-byte reproducibly. It re-implements from the frozen rules alone: I1 consumer/route ids (V01/V03), I2 measurement window/interaction ids (M04/M06 formulas in `i2-vectors/ids.json`), D9 `query_context_digest` and `evidence_ref` (`ld` = 8-byte big-endian length prefix + UTF-8), D8 cursor (unpadded base64url of sorted compact JSON).
2. **`i3-vectors/expected-answers.json`** (generated) — cases of three kinds as in v0.6:
   - `answer`: `inputs` + exact `request` + the complete expected `ApiConsumerUsageAnswer`;
   - `property`: ordered `steps` + machine-readable `assert` items, for what one literal answer cannot state (paging A15/A16, cross-gateway A14);
   - `request`: must be a validation error (`{"validation_error": true}`).
   Case ids: **A01–A19, E01–E02, C01, V01…** per D11 (the matrix fixes the final list and the V rows).
3. **`docs/specifications/0.7.0/i3-expected-answer-matrix.md`** — kinds, matching procedure, worlds/inputs, and the table mapping the 20 I3 §12 rows (S01–S20) to cases (`COVERED`/`PROPERTY`/`DEFERRED` with owner), as in the v0.6 matrix.
4. **`tests/unit/test_v070_i3_expected_answers.py`** — machine check of the oracle (not of an implementation; I3.2/I3.3 execute it).
5. Decision record: one-line status touch only (I3.1c delivered; D11 ids final in the matrix). No decision changes.

## Design (the part to review)
- **Inputs** are synthetic **I2 snapshot fragments in the frozen handoff shape** (`i2-i3-handoff.md` §1): the relevant `api_usage_v1` sections (`windows`, `coverage`, `route_operation`, `target_service`, `interactions`, `qualification_rows`, rule ids/versions) plus the `gateway_configuration_v1`/`api_contracts_v1` facts target resolution needs (Routes, Operations, Services, configuration source). One shared **base world** (gateway `gw-prod-1`, `prod`, window of `i2-vectors`, 3 consumers, 4–5 Routes incl. one in a second gateway, 2 Operations, 2 Services) and per-case overrides, so each case states only what differs. Nothing is produced by AIP execution.
- **Literal values, almost no symbols.** The snapshot id / model revision / producer are *inputs* of the case, so every id, query digest, evidence ref and cursor in the expected answer is a literal computed by the author's stdlib formulas. The only placeholder is `{{*}}` for a limitation `message` (D12.3: free text, I3.2 chooses it). Matching rule for harnesses: exact equality, `{{*}}` matches any non-empty string.
- **Independence.** The author *composes* literals per case from the input rows (it does not re-implement selection, enumeration or qualification). Only id/ref/cursor derivation is mechanical.
- **Evidence cases.** E01 resolves one ref per kind (all five D9 kinds, with the allow-listed sanitized payloads written by hand from the inputs); E02 covers forged, cross-snapshot and cross-context refs ⇒ all `NOT_RESOLVED`, indistinguishable, outcome `NOT_ANSWERED` / `PARTIAL` per D6.
- **Credential canary (C01).** Canary strings (e.g. in a key/plugin-config field of the input world) are asserted absent from the serialized form of every expected answer and evidence payload (test + a `property` assert).
- **Paging (A15/A16/A17).** A15 as `property` with steps: page 1 (`PARTIAL`, `MORE_ROWS_AVAILABLE`, literal `next_cursor`), page 2 from that cursor (no duplicate/lost row; the union equals the one-page result), plus the substituted-`after` case (rows strictly after it, same selection only). A16: same cursor after a different snapshot ⇒ `SNAPSHOT_NOT_AVAILABLE`. A17: stale `snapshot_id` ⇒ same refusal, `snapshot` = current ref.
- **Requests (V rows).** Bad id per target kind, bad patterns (`gateway_instance_id`, `environment`, window format), `limit` 0/201, `cursor` without `snapshot_id`, undecodable cursor, 0/21 refs, unsorted/duplicate refs, unknown mode, extra field; a reversed window is a **valid** request (answer case, `window.valid=false`). ## Summary

Adds an ephemeral `verifier` builtin role to the Duo team and requires an independent verifier review before the planner's final handoff to the user in `code` and `code:enhanced` modes (never `chat`).

The verifier judges, from chatroom logs only, whether the user's last message was achieved. It executes nothing — no tests, builds, or repository inspection — and returns one advisory verdict (`ACHIEVED`, `NOT_ACHIEVED`, or `INCONCLUSIVE`) with evidence and the missing items.

author: derdigitalaffine
body:
## Problem
Nach einem hochgeschobenen Modal/Sheet kann iOS in der installierten PWA einen verkleinerten bzw. verzögert zurückgesetzten `VisualViewport` melden. FamilyOS hat diesen Wert direkt für Bottom-Navigation, App-Höhe und Global Create verwendet. Dadurch bleiben Navigation und/oder App-Shell nach dem Schließen sichtbar nach oben versetzt; der Create-CTA kann in die Navigation ragen.

Das ist ein anderer Fehler als der Layer-/Portal-Fix aus #683 und ein Follow-up zu #685: #685 hat Nav und CTA zwar geometrisch gekoppelt, beide aber weiterhin an den transienten `VisualViewport` gebunden.

## Lösung
- persistente Bottom-Navigation wird am Layout-Viewport (`bottom: 0`) verankert
- Global Create bleibt über denselben Nav-/Safe-Area-Tokens positioniert, konsumiert aber keinen `--app-viewport-bottom` mehr
- `VisualViewport` verkleinert den App-Inhalt nur noch, wenn tatsächlich ein editierbares Feld fokussiert ist und die Verkleinerung einer Software-Tastatur entspricht
- bei `focusout`, `pageshow`, `visibilitychange`, Rotation und Viewport-Events wird der Zustand neu bewertet; ohne Editor-Fokus wird die stabile Layout-Höhe sofort wiederhergestellt
- `--app-viewport-bottom` bleibt nur noch als neutrale Kompatibilitätsvariable (`0px`) bestehen

Damit bleiben Safe Area, Nav-Höhe, Floating-CTA-Abstand und der semantische Layer-Vertrag aus #685 erhalten, ohne dass transiente iOS-Viewport-Zustände die dauerhafte App-Chrome verschieben.

## Regression
- simuliert transienten/stalen `VisualViewport` ohne Editor-Fokus: Nav, App-Höhe und Global Create dürfen sich nicht bewegen oder überlappen
- simuliert echte Software-Tastatur bei fokussiertem To-do-Feld: Content darf schrumpfen, persistente Navigation bleibt am Layout-Rand
- simuliert die iOS-Dismissal-Race: Fokus ist bereits weg, `VisualViewport` aber noch klein; App-Höhe muss sofort zurückspringen
- bestehender Hit-Test für Navigation/Create und Layer-Reihenfolge bleibt erhalten

Best-Practice-Abgleich: MDN unterscheidet Layout- und Visual-Viewport ausdrücklich; Bildschirmtastaturen können den VisualViewport verkleinern, ohne den Layout-Viewport zu verändern. Persistente App-Chrome wird deshalb nicht mehr an eine transient/stale VisualViewport-Unterkante gekoppelt.

Refs #683
Refs #685

author: agent-next-sbx[bot]
body:
## What changed

Makes `pm-trader-mcp` servable as a multi-user **remote** MCP endpoint, opt-in. With
`--auth-issuer`, `--auth-audience` and `--resource-url` the server acts as an OAuth 2.1
*resource server*: it validates bearer JWTs minted by an external OAuth/OIDC issuer, serves
the protected-resource metadata the MCP authorization spec requires, and gives every
verified subject its own paper accounts. Without the flags nothing changes — stdio and the
existing loopback streamable-HTTP behaviour are byte-identical.

Three commits:

| Commit | Contents |
|---|---|
| `69735db` | `docs/remote-mcp.md` — the one-page spec (goal, non-goals, threat model, interface, acceptance oracle), written and committed **before** the code |
| `9632e10` | `pm_trader/remote_auth.py` (new), the CLI/`_run`/`_data_root` wiring in `pm_trader/mcp_server.py`, the `remote` extra, `tests/test_remote_auth.py` |
| `d845aa8` | `docs/integrations.md` pointer + one `## [Unreleased]` CHANGELOG entry |

### Behaviour

- **Token validation** (`pm_trader/remote_auth.py`): only asymmetric `RS*`/`PS*`/`ES*` are
  accepted — `alg: none` and every `HS*` are refused from the header alone, before any key
  lookup (a JWKS key is public, so an HMAC token would be forgeable by anyone). The key is
  fetched through OIDC discovery (`{issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration` →
  `jwks_uri`), cached 5 minutes under an `asyncio.Lock` so concurrent callers share one
  fetch, and the token is then decoded with `issuer`, `audience` and
  `require=["exp","iss","aud","sub"]`. Any failure returns `None`, which the SDK's
  `RequireAuthMiddleware` turns into **401 + `WWW-Authenticate`**; an unreachable issuer
  fails closed and never degrades to "accept without checking".
- **Per-user isolation**: `~/.pm-trader/remote/<sha256(issuer \x1f sub)[:32]>/<account>/paper.db`.
  The directory name is a hex digest, so no part of the caller-controlled `sub` claim
  reaches the filesystem; `account` stays a sub-account *inside* the caller's own root and
  is still validated by `_validate_account_name()`. `leaderboard_card` now scans
  `_data_root()` instead of `~/.pm-trader/`, so it cannot enumerate another user's
  accounts. A call that reaches remote mode without a verified token raises instead of
  silently falling back to the local tree.
- **Tool surface**: `backtest`/`pk_battle` stay removed on every HTTP transport,
  authenticated or not.
- **The unauthenticated-bind warning** is unchanged and still prints without `--auth-issuer`;
  with an issuer configured it is not printed.

### MCP SDK surface used (verified in the installed package, `mcp` 2.3.0)

- `MCPServer(auth=AuthSettings(...), token_verifier=...)` — `mcp/server/mcpserver/server.py`;
  both fields are read when the streamable-HTTP ASGI app is built (`streamable_http_app`),
  never before, which is why `remote_auth.configure_server()` can set them on the
  already-registered module-level server instead of re-registering every tool.
- `AuthSettings(issuer_url, resource_server_url, validate_token_resource)` —
  `mcp/server/auth/settings.py`. `validate_token_resource=False` is set explicitly because
  the verifier checks `aud` against `--auth-audience` itself (the precise check the SDK
  docstring asks a resource server to make), which also silences the SDK's deprecation
  warning.
- `TokenVerifier.verify_token()` → `AccessToken` — `mcp/server/auth/provider.py`.
- `get_access_token()` / `auth_context_var` — `mcp/server/auth/middleware/auth_context.py`;
  `RequireAuthMiddleware` + `BearerAuthBackend` — `.../middleware/bearer_auth.py` (the 401
  body, the `resource_metadata=` challenge parameter and the `expires_at` re-check).
- RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata + the well-known path insertion are served by the SDK
  from `resource_server_url` (`create_protected_resource_routes`, `build_resource_metadata_url`
  in `mcp/server/auth/routes.py`).

One supporting change in `_tool()`: `loop.run_in_executor` does not copy contextvars, so the
request's verified identity would have been invisible to the sync tool body. The wrapper now
runs the tool under `contextvars.copy_context()`.

### Dependency

`PyJWT[crypto]` as the optional **`remote`** extra (`pip install "polymarket-paper-trader[remote]"`).
`PyJWT` is already a hard dependency of the MCP SDK (`mcp` requires `pyjwt`); only the `crypto`
extra — the `cryptography` RSA/EC backend — is added, and it is pulled lazily so stdio users do
not pay for it. `token_verifier()` fails at startup with an install hint if it is missing. The
`dev` extra also carries it, because the new tests sign real RSA tokens. No core dependency
changed.

## Verification

### `make check` (four packages, 100% coverage gate)

```
$ make check
TOTAL                       2970      0   100%
Required test coverage of 100% reached. Total coverage: 100.00%
1208 passed, 44 deselected in 128.46s (0:02:08)
TOTAL                       2104      0   100%
Required test coverage of 100% reached. Total coverage: 100.00%
589 passed, 1 deselected, 2 warnings in 74.74s (0:01:14)
TOTAL                         125      0   100%
```

author: tljohnsilver
body:
Two patterns that CodeQL reports as exponential (js/redos), and one wording fix.

- **Agent hooks** (`lib/hooks/policy.js`): the admin-command check matched the flags of `zn stats … share on` with `(?:\s+--?\S+)*`, where a flag such as `--a` can be read two ways. A command with many flags (an agent writes these commands) made the check take exponential time and could stall the hook. Each flag now has one reading (`-{1,2}[^\s-]\S*`). `POLICY_RULES_VERSION` bumped, snapshot updated. Test: 40 repeated flags and 5,000 short flags finish in well under 500 ms; `stats --json share on`, `stats -v share on` and `stats share on` still match.
- **Plugin repository generator** (`plugins/tools/build-plugin-repo.js`): `import()` calls with comments between `import` and `(` are now found with a plain scan instead of a pattern with nested repetition. Same results (tests unchanged and passing).
- **Stats sharing** sends pseudonymous counts (with an installation identifier), not anonymous ones: the CLI messages, comments and the CHANGELOG now say "pseudonymous" (Node and Python).

**CodeQL "clear-text logging" on `zn-gate scan --format github` (Python).** The message of each `::error` line is `v['reason']`, and every reason is fixed text: a rule's description (`(id, pattern, description)` tables in `rules.py`), "Exposed credential detected by DLP filter", the truncated-key notice, or "Smuggled Base64 execution: " plus a rule description. No reason contains text from the scanned file. New test `tests/test_scan_github_reason.py` scans a file with an AWS key, a Stripe key, a password in a URL, a Base64-wrapped injection and a private key, and checks that none of those values appears in the output and that every message is one of the known fixed reasons. The alert can be dismissed as a false positive with that reason.

author: chefboyrdave21
body:
## What
The authority (chiap08) caps local workers at 2 (production_admission `max_concurrent_workers`). When lane_launch hit that cap it logged `LANE_LAUNCH_STOPPED|node-occupancy-cap` and broke out, stranding every remaining pick even when builders (chiap01-04) had headroom.

- `builder_dispatch.ineligibility()` returns the first fence that keeps a card off builders (pure, label only). `eligible()` is now `ineligibility() is None`, behaviour identical (tested per fence).
- `builder_dispatch.fallthrough_offers()` + rotator `_fallthrough_to_builders()`: on the occupancy cap, the picks not yet launched (including the card that hit the cap) are offered to builders through the unchanged `offer()` path (same placement, route probe, test-profile preflight, claim custody, managed worker wrapper). Skips cards already offered this cycle, fenced classes, and stops at the cycle deadline. Logs `LANE_LAUNCH_FALLTHROUGH|host|offered|blocked|skipped=fence:n`.

## Why source-only is required (not relaxed here)
`eligible()` (builder_dispatch.py) accepts only `source-only` (or production glm-only + dispatch-approved) cards: a builder reconstructs the card from a credential-free https repo at an exact 40-hex revision (`_source`, `materialize_source`) and holds no host-local state; the label also states the no-external-action constraint, and the test-profile preflight (`production_test_profile.preflight`), custody, retry and exit chains key on the literal label. `seat-*` cards belong to a seat identity and its placement-manifest host. Widening on a bound-but-unlabelled card would skip the test-profile gate and silently break those links.

## Measured (read-only, chiap08 2026-10-14)
Ready cards: 148 folded. 61 have no route and no source binding (cannot run on a builder: nothing to materialize), 9 bound but no route, 3 bound+route but no source-only label (a governed relabel, not a code change), 39 source-only+route (already builder candidates; builders offered 1 per cycle, the rest blocked by `required-test-profile-unqualified` requalification or `source binding conflict`). The lane loop on the authority was running seat-niobe glm cards and seraph reviews, which are correctly not builder-eligible. So the cap fall-through only recovers cards the earlier offer phase did not reach (offer phase time cap, transient idle); the larger lever is test-profile requalification throughput and routing/binding triage of the unrouted majority.

## Tests
tests/test_builder_lane_fallthrough.py (fences, production glm rule, fall-through offers, skips, deadline, cap branch order); existing builder dispatch, reachability, offer order and scheduler_decision suites pass. ruff clean on touched src/tests (rotator keeps inherited baseline), black clean.

author: poyrazk
body:
GitOps revision review currently exposes a definition before approval, but users cannot assess its field changes in CI or subscribe to environment drift and source-access transitions. This adds a read-only candidate plan workflow and durable account notifications, and completes the GitLab dashboard binding forms.

- `POST .../gitops/plan` verifies an immutable commit through the bound provider, observes scoped intent and ownership, and returns redacted changes with a candidate hash, generation, and observation metadata. It creates no revision, adoption, controller run, or workload. Candidate hashes cannot authorize adoption or execution.
- `gregale ... gitops plan --commit SHA` produces JSON or escaped Markdown; `--fail-on-blocked` writes the plan before exiting 2. Go, Node, and Python clients and GitHub Actions/GitLab CI examples cover the workflow.
- Explicit `environment.gitops.changed` account subscriptions receive drift/source transitions and recovery. Baselines and receiver deliveries commit atomically, survive restart, omit values, and suppress unchanged status and stale reports.
- GitLab forms preserve manual approval, report mode, and retained resources. A merge-scope fix replaces main's unsafe queue-error byte truncation with `safetext.Truncate`, clearing the text-encoding policy gate.

GitOps customer review/reporting milestone; architecture: ADR-1155. Production enforcement and native qualification remain gated. This changes no VM lifecycle behavior.

Validation: focused Go planner, HTTP authorization, dashboard, signed dispatcher, CLI, and SDK tests; disposable PostgreSQL candidate scope, redaction, stale observation, notification rollback/restart and migration replay tests; clone schema coverage; Node build/tests and Python tests; SDK/OpenAPI parity and regeneration drift checks; lint on changed packages; ADR, runbook SQL, shell quoting, and text-encoding policy checks.

author: lucasmartins-ai
body:
## Problem

`lookacrawler extract <url>` failed intermittently with `Extraction error: disk I/O error`. The error is `SQLITE_IOERR_VNODE`, thrown by `setCachedPage` after a successful fetch (not by the extraction itself).

## Cause

While a connection is open, something outside lookacrawler adds a second hard link to the `-wal`/`-shm` files of a cache DB under `~/Downloads/lookacrawler`. Polling `stat` during an extract showed nlink 2 in 44 of 60 samples. The SQLite build bun uses on macOS then rejects the next write. I couldn't find what creates the extra link: a search by inode across `/Users`, `/tmp` and `/var/folders` found nothing.

Same code with a fresh DB: 4/6 extracts failed in the repo dir and 0/6 failed in `~/.cache/lookacrawler`.

## Change

- The default cache path is now `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/lookacrawler/crawler_cache.sqlite`, or `~/.cache/lookacrawler/` if that is unset. `LOOKACRAWLER_DB_PATH` still overrides it.
- Every cache call goes through one wrapper. A SQLite error (at open or at query time) is logged once on stderr and treated as a cache miss, so the cache can no longer fail an extraction.
- `index.ts`: the cache-stats resource handles a null `db`.

The old `crawler_cache.sqlite*` in the repo root is no longer used. It is a 24 h cache, so moving it loses nothing that matters.

## Verification

- `bun test`: 370 pass, 2 skip, 0 fail. `tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- New `cache-best-effort.test.ts` covers an unopenable path and a DB that fails mid-run. It fails on the old `cache.ts` and passes on this one.
- 20 consecutive `lookacrawler extract` runs (HN, GitHub, Wikipedia, docs.python.org, example.com, each with a cache-busting query): 0 failures, 0 cache warnings.
- With the cache forced back to the repo dir: 10/10 runs exited 0 with content; 2 of them hit `IOERR_VNODE` and fell back to no-cache.

All of this was measured on one macOS machine. Linux and Docker were not tested.

## Not in this PR

On news.ycombinator.com the output stays as raw HTML tables. `turndown-plugin-gfm` keeps tables without a header row as HTML, and HN's layout is built from such tables. That needs its own rule and is left for a follow-up.

author: jwinarske
body:
With grid pacing, a frame could start twice in one refresh. Each paced hand-out set the earliest next start to the vblank after the frame start, counting vblanks from the last presentation. If the reported period is slightly off, the frame start of a deferred delivery (a vblank counted from an older presentation) can land a few microseconds before the vblank the latest presentation counts. The next allowed start then fell in the same refresh, and a request about 1 ms later passed the start window (#788) and began a second frame. A presentation that arrives after the next vblank, but before the timer, had the same effect: its frame start is a refresh old, so the next allowed start was already in the past.

The two commits went out 1 ms apart. Both presentation feedbacks were bound to the first commit, which the second one replaced, so both were discarded. The frame that reached the screen was never reported shown.

- **Next start after a vblank hand-out**: when a hand-out's frame start is a vblank (a deferred delivery, a presentation, or a start inside the window), the next allowed start is the vblank after that refresh: half a period past the frame start, counted from the latest presentation, and no earlier than the vblank after now. Frame starts stay locked to the latest presentation. Hand-outs at the current time (a discard, an inline kick, an unpark) keep the old rule.
- **Docs**: `shell/vsync/README.md` covers both cases under the start window.

## Results on target hardware

Wayland EGL with a platform view, alternating runs on the same bundle. A is v3.0 pacing and B is this change; both carry the same scratch trace stamps. "Double frames" counts consecutive frames whose starts are under half a period apart.

| run | double frames | discards during gesture steps | gesture p95 (frames) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 / B1 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | 2.17 / 2.49 |
| A2 / B2 | 3 / 0 | 4 / 0 | 2.68 / 2.56 |
| A3 / B3 | 1 / 0 | 2 / 0 | 2.44 / 2.55 |

Counting six earlier runs with v3.0 pacing, v3.0 had 12 double frames in 9 runs, against 0 in 3 with this change. In one of those earlier runs the lost feedback failed a gesture step. p95 stays within the run-to-run spread; this change isn't meant to move latency.

## Tests

- `AVblankJustBeforeARealOneStartsNoSecondFrameInItsRefresh`: a deferred frame starts on a vblank that falls 30 µs before the latest presentation's vblank. A request in the start window then waits for the next vblank, counted from the latest presentation. Fails on v3.0.
- `ALatePresentationStartsNoSecondFrameInARefresh`: a presentation arriving after the next vblank hands out the baton, and the next request in that refresh waits. Fails on v3.0.
- vsync_pace 31, vsync_park 6, wayland_vsync_grid 22 and flip_arm 8 pass. The changed files are clean under check_spelling.sh, format.sh --check, gen_config_reference.py --check and clang-tidy.

author: estebanforge
body:
## Context
Task ID: WWID-2777
Task Link: https://app.asana.com/0/0/1219354385925238
Related PRs: none

## What
On a member portal's Gravity Forms profile form, the State/Province select spun for 5-10s (sometimes forever) after a Country change. This PR also promotes the plugin into the stack: `main` carries the plugin as it shipped on the client site at v1.0.0, and this branch carries the three fix commits (v1.0.1-1.0.3).

## Why
Members could not reliably edit their profile address. The stuck overlay made the form look broken while the fields were actually populated and usable, so members waited or abandoned the edit.

## How
- Lazy states-cache load (the multi-MB transient no longer fetches on every request), error-path force-hide, recurring failsafe, and diagnostic-page hardening (v1.0.1).
- The loading hide survives page listeners that throw during the select swap (v1.0.2).
- Root cause: multi-step persistence re-announced already-stable fields through change handlers, creating an unbounded jQuery event loop measured at 10,767 events/s that starved the main thread and held the overlay. Persistence now converges (skips when value and backup already match), the periodic interval is gone, and an age-stamped failsafe force-clears any container loading longer than 3s (v1.0.3).

Verified live on the ticket's Pantheon multidev, md5-identical to this branch: idle event rate 10,767/s → 0/s, and a country change clears the spinner in 301ms. The same files shipped on the site repo branch for this ticket.

Follow-ups: release-bot onboarding for this repo (header version tracks the site ship at 1.0.3), and composer pickup by sites once a tag exists.

author: varshith-kali
body:
Fixes #384.

A malicious pickle stored under an extensionless name — a zip entry or a bare file — scanned with zero findings (`SCAN_NOT_SUPPORTED` skip) while the byte-identical `.pkl` payload was flagged CRITICAL. Stripping the extension was enough to silence the scanner on a payload it provably detects.

**Root cause:** `FormatViaExtensionMiddleware` derived formats purely from `Path(source).suffix`. With no suffix, `PICKLE` never entered the model's context and `PickleUnsafeOpScan.scan` returned `None` → silent skip.

**Fix:** when the extension yields no format, the middleware now sniffs the stream's magic bytes before giving up — pickle protocols 1–5 start `\x80` + version byte, protocol 0 starts with a known opcode. A candidate is confirmed with a full `pickletools.genops` parse (decode-only, never executes the payload) ending in STOP, so non-pickle content that merely starts with an opcode-like byte is not misclassified. The stream is rewound after the peek, and the rewind itself is fail-closed so the sniff can never break a scan.

Deliberately pickle-only and minimal — numpy sniffing (`\x93NUMPY`) left out to keep the change small.

**Tests** (5, in the existing harness style): extensionless zip entry flagged CRITICAL with an extensionless README in the same zip still skipped; bare extensionless pickle file flagged; protocol-0 extensionless payload flagged; extensionless non-pickle still skipped (no behavior change); `.pkl` regression control. The 3 positive tests fail on unmodified main; the full suite is green apart from the pre-existing `test_scan_numpy` numpy-2.x failure, which fails identically on clean main.

body:
## Summary

Fixes #8. Bumps the golangci-lint pin in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` from `v2.12.2` to `v2.14.0`.

`3610d00` moved CI to Go 1.27.2. Go 1.27 writes compiled-package type data in format version 5, and golangci-lint v2.12.2 only reads up to version 4. So `CI / lint` failed type-checking `dashboard/embed.go` on every PR. Go 1.27 support arrived in v2.13.0 (golangci/golangci-lint#6642).

**Version source:** the latest golangci-lint release as of 2026-10-14, from `gh api repos/golangci/golangci-lint/releases`.

- [ ] `CI / lint` passes on this PR.

No regression test: this is a CI tooling pin, and the `lint` job itself is the check.

Linting on macOS without `GOOS=linux` gives 5 findings that are specific to the OS. They're unrelated to this change and will be filed separately.

author: dr-phil-2004
body:
## Pourquoi

Approche « trust first » (Lauren Tan) : avant de déléguer plus à des agents, on rend les erreurs fréquentes impossibles ou détectées automatiquement, et on donne à l'agent un moyen de prouver que son travail marche (`npm run verify`).

## Bugs corrigés (trouvés en mettant les garde-fous)

- **Webhook Stripe** : `checkout.session.completed` tombait dans `updateSubscription()` ; les achats sur compte connecté ne passaient jamais l'attendee en `CONVERTED` (metadata manquante). La suppression d'abonnement est maintenant synchronisée, et une signature invalide renvoie 400.
- **`createCheckoutLink`** : faute de frappe `webinardId` → crash du parcours « Book a call ».
- **Page Webinars** : `Link` utilisé sans import.
- **Live webinar** : `LiveWebinarView` rendu sans la prop `call` (host et participant) → `call.on(...)` plantait.
- **CountdownTimer** : les secondes bouclaient à 24 au lieu de 60.
- **Stripe.js** : le loader des comptes connectés ne renvoyait rien et recréait une promesse à chaque rendu.
- `asChild` (Radix) utilisé sur des composants Base UI (sans effet) → `render`.
- Modules serveur importés en valeur dans du code client.

## Garde-fous

- ESLint : `no-fallthrough`, interdiction de `asChild`, interdiction des imports serveur côté client, warnings plafonnés (48).
- Vitest + 7 tests de régression du webhook (4 échouent sur l'ancien code).
- `npm run verify` + workflow GitHub Actions.
- `CLAUDE.md` : définition de « fini », conventions, échelle de correction.

## À vérifier à la main

- Paiement test Stripe sur un webinar (compte connecté) → l'attendee passe en `CONVERTED`.
- Le webhook Connect doit être configuré côté Stripe pour recevoir les événements des comptes connectés.

author: jackywxd
body:
## 內容

UltraSignup 匯入列表的三項改進，加上一項跟進：

1. **底色**：紀錄和 UltraSignup 一致是綠色，不一致是黃色，目錄裡沒有這場或這個分項是紅色。因為同一場另一筆已匯入而鎖定的那一行不上色。
2. **手工對應目錄**：紅色那一行可以用系列、賽事、分項選擇器指定目錄裡的賽事，年份固定用 UltraSignup 的。匯入時走和手動登錄一樣的 `POST /api/race-records`，**不**把對應寫回目錄當別名。
3. **申請加入目錄**：新集合 `race-catalogue-requests`（後台「賽事 › 目錄申請」）。
   - 只有申請人和 admin 讀得到。
   - 會員可以新增；狀態、連結賽事和給會員的說明只有 admin 能寫，會員送出時就算帶了 `approved` 也會被拿掉。
   - 同一個會員對同一個 UltraSignup 行，同時只能有一筆未結案的申請。
   - admin 照平常的方式在目錄新增賽事和分項之後，回來批准並連結賽事。批准不會自動寫目錄，也不會替會員匯入。
   - 列表上顯示「等待審核」、「已加入，重新讀取後可匯入」，或「未通過：說明」。
4. **記住手工對應**：匯入的紀錄帶上 UltraSignup 的標題和日期（`race-records.ultrasignupTitle` / `ultrasignupDate`）。下次讀取時，`picksFromRecords` 用它們把手工對應認回來，所以那一行會是綠色。matcher 自己能對上的行不受影響。

## Migration

兩個，都只做新增，可重複執行：

- `20261014_180000_add_race_catalogue_requests`：新增一張表，以及 `payload_locked_documents_rels` 的一個欄位。`down()` 刻意不刪那個欄位，原因寫在檔案開頭。
- `20261014_200000_add_race_record_ultrasignup_source`：`race_records` 加兩個可為空的欄位，不回填。

兩個都已套用到本機 D1，並確認重跑時拋出的錯誤正是 migration 會容忍的那一個。合併後 `deploy.yml` 會套用到 staging；production 要在 deploy 流程裡批准。

## 驗證

- `pnpm typecheck`、改動檔案的 eslint、`assert-test-strategy`、`assert-schema-screen` 都通過。新的申請集合在 schema-screen 裡登記為「由那一行填入」，每個必填欄位都寫了原因。
- `pnpm test:unit`：489 通過。新測試是 U-ULTRA-33～36。
- 本機 dev server（3100 埠）上，M-ULTRA 和 M-ULTRA-API 共 14 個測試通過。新測試是 M-ULTRA-11 和 M-ULTRA-API-3。本機資料庫跑之前沒有重置。
- 每個新測試都故意弄壞程式碼，看到它在名稱描述的那一行失敗：
  - 會員送出的申請回來是 `approved` → M-ULTRA-API-3 失敗；
  - 頁面沒拿到伺服器的申請 → M-ULTRA-11 在重新整理後的狀態斷言失敗；
  - 讀取時不還原手工對應 → M-ULTRA-11 在「重新整理後應為綠色」失敗。
- 失敗的測試跑完後也確認過：測試建立的資料都按 id 刪乾淨了。
- 手動走過一遍，用本機測試會員、讀真的 UltraSignup：把 TDS 手工對應到 UTMB Mont-Blanc / TDS 並匯入，資料庫裡的紀錄正確（39:24:51）；Sinister 7 送出申請後是 pending；後台列表和編輯頁正常顯示，沒有 console 錯誤。

## 已知限制

- 以前匯入的紀錄沒有 UltraSignup 標題，所以不會被認回來。這次刻意不回填，猜測可能把行對到錯的紀錄上。
- 申請沒有通知 admin，靠後台列表的「待審核」狀態。
- 申請批准後，若 UltraSignup 標題和賽事名稱不同，admin 還要把標題加進該賽事的 UltraSignup 別名，否則那一行仍然對不上。後台欄位說明有寫。

author: timblankers
body:
Closes #13

Adds the Renovate preset `default.json`, this repo's own `renovate.json` (extends it), a `renovate-config` CI job (`renovate-config-validator --strict`, Renovate 44.155.2), and a README section. **Shared file: once the Renovate app is installed, every repo extending the preset follows it.**

## What the preset does

- `config:recommended` + `schedule:weekly` (early Monday, UTC) + `group:allNonMajor` (minor/patch in one PR).
- `minimumReleaseAge: "1 day"` (matches `.npmrc`).
- `helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests`: Actions pinned by SHA. `timblankers/.github` reusable-workflow refs are left alone (apps use `app.yml@main` on purpose).
- `pinDigests` for the `dockerfile` manager only: `ARG NODE_IMAGE=node:24.21.0-trixie-slim` → `…@sha256:…` (Renovate expands `ARG` in `FROM`; confirmed in the dry run below).
- **Node.js group**: `.nvmrc` (nvm), the Dockerfile image and `devEngines.runtime` share `groupName: "Node.js"`. All three use Renovate's `node` versioning, whose `isStable` is "has reached LTS", so no Current/odd majors (`config:recommended` includes `workarounds:nodeDockerVersioning` for the image).
- TypeScript: `allowedVersions: "~6.0.0"`.

## Two things that need a person (both in the README)

1. **npm in `devEngines.packageManager`**: Renovate would bump it to the latest *standalone* npm (12.x), not the one bundled with Node, so that's disabled. A Node PR still needs the bundled npm version set by hand, or `npm ci` fails with EBADDEVENGINES; the Node PR body says so (`prBodyNotes`). Today's case: Node 24.22.0 bundles npm 11.19.1.
2. **Image lag**: Node 24.22.0 was released today and `node:24.22.0-trixie-slim` doesn't exist yet (Docker Hub 404). So `.nvmrc`/`devEngines` would move before the Dockerfile can. The `node-version` datasource gets a 3-day release age so the image normally joins the same PR. If it doesn't, the `dockerfile` check from #28 fails CI until it does.

Also: `@types/node` majors are disabled (bump them by hand with a Node major).

## Tested

- `renovate-config-validator --strict default.json renovate.json`: OK. `actionlint`: OK.
- Dry run on app-template (`renovate --platform=local --dry-run=lookup`, preset as config) proposes:
  - Node.js: `.nvmrc` 24.21.0 → 24.22.0, `devEngines.runtime` 24.21.0 → 24.22.0 (the Dockerfile has no 24.22.0 image yet: see above)
  - pin digest: Dockerfile `node:24.21.0-trixie-slim` (all 3 `FROM`s via the ARG)
  - non-major: lucide-react, react, react-dom, @playwright/test, shadcn
  - disabled as intended: `devEngines.packageManager` npm, `timblankers/.github` workflow `@main`

## Enabling it

- **Now**: app-template, .github (this PR's `renovate.json`), rpi-infra. app-template and rpi-infra each need a `renovate.json` extending the preset (or the onboarding PR edited to that).
- **Not yet**: sourdough, daily-leaf, pixel-perfect, until they're aligned (Phase 4).

body:
Refs #1026

Part 1 of 2 for #1026: findings 1 and 3. Finding 2 (equipment entries summed on retrieve) comes in a separate PR that closes the issue. Owner answer D-1026-3: an entry the game cannot read is kept unchanged and logged.

## Finding 1: a second deposit from one stack was refused
**Before:** with Gemstones 7, "store 1" worked and a second "store 1" was refused by the engine (`E_DUPLICATE ... split requires a fresh identity`). A partial store splits into `<stack id>:part:<count>`, and the chest entry keeps that `item:` id, so the next same-count split asks for an id the world already declares.
**Now:** `_fresh_split_id` returns `<base>:part:<count>` when it is free, and otherwise `<base>:part:<count>:2`, `:3` and so on.
- "Free" means not declared anywhere in the world (both characters' items, every sibling container's contents, the containers, the ammunition stocks) and not minted earlier in the same request.
- When there is no clash the id is byte-identical to before.
- It is used for both splits in `core/nql/storage.py`: the ammunition store and the generic store/retrieve.

## Finding 3: a chest entry the game cannot read was deleted
**Before:** the chest was rewritten from the engine's view only, so an entry genesis skipped was deleted at the next store or retrieve at that chest. That covers an entry with no `item_name`, or one whose stored `item:` id another entry also stores.
**Now:**
- Those entries are appended back unchanged, as the sheet already does with `kept_untracked`.

author: spengrah
body:
Every linked worktree now shares the main checkout's Go build cache (`<main checkout>/.gocache`) instead of building its own from scratch. The anchor matches `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`, and the `verify-personal-crm` helpers use the same one.

## Why

Before this change, `GOCACHE` defaulted to each checkout's own `.gocache`, so every worktree in a spec-and-ship arc rebuilt the standard library and every module dependency. `frontend/node_modules` looks equally large in `du`, but bun installs it as APFS clones from its global cache: a fresh install measured 0.8s and 12 MB of real disk. The Go cache was the real weight.

## Measurements (`make test-unit`, Mac)

| Cache state | Time | Cache written |
|---|---|---|
| Cold, per-worktree cache (old behavior) | 88s | 1.7 GB |
| Brand-new worktree, shared cache | 42s | Only the repo's own packages |

A new worktree still compiles the repo's own packages, because Go includes each package's directory in its cache key unless `-trimpath` is set. `-trimpath` would share those as well, but the test harness locates fixtures via `runtime.Caller` (for example `backend/tests/testsupport/testsupport.go`), so this PR does not change it.

## Safety under concurrent worktrees

Go keys cache entries by a hash of each build's inputs, and concurrent `go` processes may share one cache. I ran `make test-unit` at the same time in this worktree and in the main checkout, both against the shared cache, and both exited 0.

## Behavior outside the Mac main-checkout case

- **CI:** no change. The checkout is the main checkout, and the existing GOCACHE pin steps in `ci.yml` and `backend-slow-tests.yml` still override the default.
- **VPS sandbox:** the main checkout sits on the persistent `sandbox-crm-workspace` volume, so the shared cache survives container recreates. Go's own default (`~/.cache/go-build`) would not.
- **Env override:** `GOCACHE=<path> make …` still wins (checked against make's variable dump).

## Codex sandbox (falsified)

Under Codex `workspace-write` (writable roots: workdir, `/tmp`, `$TMPDIR`), a worktree build against the shared cache **succeeds but silently drops new entries**:

1. Injected a unique compiler flag (`go build -gcflags=-D=/probeN ./internal/matching/`) inside `codex exec -c sandbox_mode=workspace-write` from this worktree. The build printed `EXIT=0`, and a control `touch` into the cache dir printed exit 1. Rebuilding the same flag outside the sandbox recompiled 1 package, which shows the sandboxed result was not stored.
2. Repeated with `-c 'sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots=["<main checkout>/.gocache"]'`. The session header listed the path, the build printed `EXIT=0`, and the rebuild outside the sandbox recompiled 0 packages.
