Vérification n° 1 du chantier « formateurs freelance », équipe B : les scénarios de mission, en tests Playwright tagués `@formateurs`, joués par le job « banc-formateurs ». **Aucun code applicatif modifié.**

## Ce que la PR ajoute

- **Scénarios** : `tests/e2e/formateurs/e13…e34-*.spec.ts` et `eb1-seuil-urssaf.spec.ts`, un fichier par scénario.
- **Harnais** : `tests/e2e/fixtures/formateurs/missions-*` (fichiers distincts de ceux de l'équipe A, pour éviter les conflits).
  - Un processus `tsx` persistant par fichier de spec charge le **vrai** code : actions de la console, actions de l'espace formateur, services, passages planifiés.
  - Seuls la requête et l'extérieur sont remplacés, par crochets de résolution :
    - `@/auth` : un administrateur fictif ;
    - `next/headers` : le cookie formateur, signé par la vraie fonction ;
    - `next/cache` et `server-only` : neutralisés ;
    - `@sentry/nextjs` : coupé ;
    - `@/lib/r2-storage` : un dossier local, puisque le banc n'a pas de seau.
  - Le réseau est coupé.
- **Horloge** : jamais truquée. Les passages reçoivent `maintenant` ; les actions lisent l'heure réelle, comme en production.
- **Interrupteurs** : allumés **par les actions de la console** (écran Interrupteurs, puis « Valider ce texte » avec empreinte), donc avec les préalables vérifiés par le serveur.
  - Un compteur de porteurs sous verrou consultatif évite qu'un fichier en éteigne pour un autre. Le dernier porteur restaure l'état d'avant.
  - Écart : la console **refuse** la date de passage au paiement (préalable « canal de changement de compte » non lisible). Le banc constate ce refus puis pose la date en base.
- **E-mails** :
  - Ils entrent dans la vraie file BullMQ, mais sur la base Redis n° 1, que le worker ne consomme pas. Le worker plafonne à 40 envois par heure ; un passage des scénarios en enfile environ 70, et la preuve de livraison de `envois-par-la-file.spec.ts` attendait derrière eux.
  - Le contenu est contrôlé en rendant le job en file avec le moteur du worker.

## Résultat local, job reproduit (Postgres pgvector, Redis, Mailpit, worker ; `CI=1`, 4 workers, `--retries=0`)

33 réussis, 5 sautés (les 4 `test.fixme` ci-dessous et le fixme déjà présent de F-CAL-1), 41 s. Chaque `test.fixme` a été vérifié **en échec** sur `main` avant d'être marqué.

## Défauts et écarts consignés (`test.fixme`)

- **V1-B-2** (haute) : après une lettre rectifiée (F29), plus aucune relance F27. `lireLignesLettre` exige un F26 pour la nouvelle lettre, qui n'en a jamais.
- **V1-B-1** (moyenne) : « À pourvoir » est silencieux (ni journal ni alerte) quand le silence du dernier choix libère la place. Cause : `cause === "passage"` et `sautes === 0`.
- **V1-B-3** (écart, lot L11f non livré) : pas de lettre à l'organisme par lien, ni de paiement sur facture déposée.
- **V1-B-4** (écart) : pas de nouvelle version « favorable » ou « engageante ». L'envoi F45 refuse tant que le résumé de la v4 n'est pas écrit.

Autres écarts au plan, notés dans l'en-tête des specs :
- F27 1re à J+2, sans « mi-chemin » ;
- aucune indemnité pour un désistement (art. 7.4) ;
- lettre émise au-delà du seuil URSSAF pour une mission déjà acceptée (décision du 14/10).

author: thanatos9404
body:
# What does this PR do ?

Raise a failed background checkpoint finalization at the start of the next training step instead of at the next save.

# Issues

Fixes #4707

# Usage

N/A (internal). No config or API changes for users.

## Problem

With background finalization, a checkpoint whose async write or `tmp_step_N` to `step_N` rename fails does not stop the run. Training keeps going until the next save, which is up to `save_period` steps later, and only then raises. By that point the newest visible `step_N` is older than the step the run has reached, and the error is reported from a later step's save than the one that broke.

## Root cause

`CheckpointManager.begin_finalization()` runs `wait_fn` and `_rename_checkpoint()` on a daemon thread. On failure the thread only stores the exception in `self._finalize_error` ([checkpoint.py#L439](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/blob/66c092528bedcc68c79e963544ed9efd2042fdc1/nemo_rl/utils/checkpoint.py#L439)). The only code that raises it is `finalize_pending()` ([#L446-L458](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/blob/66c092528bedcc68c79e963544ed9efd2042fdc1/nemo_rl/utils/checkpoint.py#L446-L458)), and the training loops reach that only:

- at the next save, through the `finalize_pending()` call at the top of `begin_finalization()` ([#L422](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/blob/66c092528bedcc68c79e963544ed9efd2042fdc1/nemo_rl/utils/checkpoint.py#L422)) or the explicit `checkpointer.finalize_pending()` the GRPO loops make before `init_tmp_checkpoint()` ([grpo.py#L4118](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/blob/66c092528bedcc68c79e963544ed9efd2042fdc1/nemo_rl/algorithms/grpo.py#L4118), [#L6010](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/blob/66c092528bedcc68c79e963544ed9efd2042fdc1/nemo_rl/algorithms/grpo.py#L6010)), or
- at exit, through `shutdown()`.

Nothing looks at `_finalize_error` between saves.

## Change

- `CheckpointManager.raise_if_finalization_failed()`: if the background thread has already recorded an error, it calls `finalize_pending()`, which joins the finished thread, clears the state and raises the same `RuntimeError("Background checkpoint finalization failed")` with the original exception as its cause. It never waits for a finalization that is still running.
- Every training loop that uses `begin_finalization()` calls it at the top of each step: GRPO (`grpo_train` and `async_grpo_train`), GRPO over TransferQueue (`grpo_sync.py`), SFT, SFT v2, DPO, RM, PPO (`ppo_train` and `async_ppo_train`), distillation, cross-tokenizer off-policy distillation, and the single controller train pump. In the async loops it sits right after the existing per-step `check_health` call; in the single controller it runs before the `maybe_gpu_profile_step` calls.
- Single controller: the rollout checkpoint pump can be inside `finalize_pending()` on a worker thread (via `asyncio.to_thread`) while it holds `_checkpoint_save_lock`. The train pump skips its poll while that lock is held, so two threads never flush at once; a skipped poll is caught at the next step. The call stays synchronous (no `to_thread`), so the `locked()` check and the poll are atomic on the event loop.
- Docstrings and the comments next to the three `begin_finalization()` call sites now say that a failure that has already happened is raised at the start of the next step.

### Why a non-blocking check

The issue lists a few options. I went with a check that does not block because of what async save is for:

- Joining the finalize thread at every step boundary would make each step wait for the previous checkpoint's disk write, which removes the overlap between the write and training that `async_save` was added for. With `save_period > 1` the write currently has several steps to finish.
- Raising from the finalize thread or a done-callback cannot reach the training thread safely; it would have to interrupt it at an arbitrary point, possibly inside a collective or a Ray call.
- Reading `_finalize_error` once per step costs nothing when saves succeed, keeps the async write overlapping with training, and reuses the existing error path, so the exception type and message do not change. `finalize_pending()` before the next save and `shutdown()` at exit stay the hard barriers they are today.

The trade-off: a write that is still running when the next step starts is not waited for. If it fails during that step, the failure surfaces at the following step boundary (or at the next save or exit, whichever comes first). So the delay is bounded by the step in flight when the write fails, instead of by the save period.

## Tests

New tests:

- `tests/unit/utils/test_checkpoint.py::TestRaiseIfFinalizationFailed`: raises a failure that already happened (original exception kept as `__cause__`, `tmp_step_1` left in place, raised only once); does not block while a finalization is in flight; no-op when nothing failed.
- `test_grpo.py::test_grpo_failed_checkpoint_finalization_stops_before_next_step[grpo_train]` and `[async_grpo_train]`: a real `CheckpointManager`, `save_period=2`, `max_num_steps=6`, and `policy.finalize_async_save` raising `OSError`. Asserts the run raises after exactly 2 training steps and that `tmp_step_2` was never renamed.
- `test_checkpointing.py::TestAsyncSaveFinalization::test_failed_background_finalization_stops_before_next_step`: the same scenario through the single controller train pump (`save_period=2`, `max_num_steps=4`), asserting it stops at `_train_steps == 2`.
- `test_single_controller_actor.py::test_train_pump_polls_finalization_only_while_no_save_holds_the_lock`: no poll while the lock is held, one poll once it is free.
- `test_failed_checkpoint_finalization_stops_before_training` in `test_sft.py`, `test_dpo.py`, `test_rm.py` and `test_distillation.py`: with the mocked checkpointer's `raise_if_finalization_failed` raising, the loop raises and `train` is never called.

The GRPO and single controller loop tests join the finalize thread before the next step starts, so the failure has already happened when training reaches the step boundary, as in the issue's trace. On main, all 11 new tests fail: both GRPO loops and the train pump run steps 3 and 4 and only fail at the step-4 save (`assert 4 == 2`), the four wiring tests fail with `DID NOT RAISE`, the lock test sees no call, and the three `CheckpointManager` tests hit `AttributeError`.

Edits to existing tests:

- `test_failed_background_finalization_raises_at_next_save` is now `..._raises_by_next_save`, with its comment saying the failure surfaces no later than the step-4 save; the assertion is unchanged.
- `_train_pump_controller` in `test_single_controller_actor.py` builds the actor with `object.__new__` and sets each attribute the pump reads. It now also sets `_checkpointer = MagicMock()`, since the pump reads it every step.

<details>
<summary>Commands and results (CPU only, Python 3.13.14, torch 2.13.0+cpu, `HF_HOME` set; not the CI container)</summary>

```bash
# the 11 new tests: all pass here; all fail with nemo_rl/ reverted to main
python -m pytest tests/unit/utils/test_checkpoint.py::TestRaiseIfFinalizationFailed \
  tests/unit/algorithms/test_grpo.py::test_grpo_failed_checkpoint_finalization_stops_before_next_step \
  tests/unit/single_controller/test_checkpointing.py::TestAsyncSaveFinalization::test_failed_background_finalization_stops_before_next_step \
  tests/unit/single_controller/test_single_controller_actor.py::test_train_pump_polls_finalization_only_while_no_save_holds_the_lock \
  tests/unit/algorithms/{test_sft,test_dpo,test_rm,test_distillation}.py::test_failed_checkpoint_finalization_stops_before_training

# related suites
python -m pytest tests/unit/utils/test_checkpoint.py tests/unit/single_controller tests/unit/algorithms/x_token \
  tests/unit/telemetry/test_sft_v2.py tests/unit/data_plane/test_sync_one_hop.py \
  tests/unit/data_plane/test_architecture_invariants.py \
  tests/unit/algorithms/{test_grpo,test_sft,test_sft_v2,test_dpo,test_mpo,test_rm,test_ppo,test_distillation}.p

author: noahatc12
body:
R4 from the generator redesign wave, designed 2026-07-07 and on hold since. It is the plan fix from the 2026-10-14 review. **Waiting on Noah's yes before merge.** Only new plans change; saved plans are untouched.

## What changes

The first-match pick is replaced by a vetted library (`roles.ts`). Each movement pattern has a short list of real catalog lifts, each tagged with its job: **heavy**, **stretch** (loads the muscle long) or **squeeze** (peak contraction).

- **Main slot:** a muscle's first compound slot takes the heavy lift. A second slot that day takes the next job. Bench is followed by incline dumbbell press, never by decline bench.
- **Fresh lifts first.** A compound slot moves to a fresh compound from the next job before repeating, so deadlift is followed by Romanian deadlift. It repeats rather than dropping to an isolation, so flyes never become the main chest lift.
- **Variety:** an isolation slot varies before it repeats.
- **Novices** repeat their main lifts every session, which is simple linear progression.
- **Never the same exercise twice in a session.** Never an exercise on the lifter's avoid list; the saved avoid list is consumed for the first time.
- **Fallback:** generic matching remains for anything off-list, minus odd variants such as Bosu or stability-ball moves.
- **Cues** belong to the exercise, so a hip thrust gets the glute cue. Tempo follows the job: a squeeze holds the top, a stretch pauses at the bottom. Rest stays tied to the pattern.
- **Seed:** an optional seed rotates among equally good lifts. Without one, the same inputs give the same plan.

## Before and after, real catalog

Build muscle, intermediate, 4 days, full gym:

| Day | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Upper A, 2nd chest slot | Decline Barbell Bench Press | Incline Dumbbell Press |
| Lower A | Barbell Full Squat, Hip Thrust, Bosu Ball Cable Crunch With Side Bends | Barbell Squat, Barbell Deadlift, Hanging Leg Raise |
| Lower B | Barbell Squat (the same squat again), Romanian Deadlift | Front Barbell Squat, Romanian Deadlift, Cable Crunch |

Two more profiles:
- **Novice, strength:** the same squat, bench, row and press every day, where it used to rotate odd variants.
- **Dumbbell-only novice:** a stiff-legged dumbbell deadlift every day instead of a band good morning.

## Not changed: say if you want it next

A hypertrophy upper day still has **no direct arm or lateral-raise work**. That isn't selection. Pressing and rowing earn half credit toward arms and shoulders, which meets their minimum, and the model counts all three delt heads as one "shoulders" muscle. Fixing it means changing the volume allocator and the day templates: add a lateral raise plus one arm slot to upper days. That's about 10 more minutes per upper session. A diagnostic is added here: every priority muscle with a home in the split reaches its minimum, and it passes.

## Checks

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| lint, typecheck | clean |
| coverage run | 569 of 569; generator 95.13% branch against a 95% gate (passes, thin) |
| Real catalog | 5 profiles printed before and after |
| In the app | onboarding on this build shows the new plan; live shows the old |
| design:nav / personas | 24/24, 0 failures |

There are 16 new tests on real catalog rows. The fixture holds every vetted id, all 77 confirmed in the pinned catalog, plus generic and odd rows. Control run on the old generator: 10 failed and 6 passed. The 6 cover behavior the old code already had.

## Undo

`git revert -m 1 <merge>` on main. Plans already built keep their exercises.

body:
Implementa en `miot-fleet` el modelo de assets y relaciones entre organizaciones (`~/.miot/plans/gps-tenant-relationship-model.md`), con datos de ejemplo. Sigue a #1913 (mergeado).

## Modelo
- **Evidencias con vigencia** sobre un asset:
  - `REPORTS`: credencial → asset, de la señal.
  - `OWNS`: transportista → asset, de un viaje o una acreditación.
  - `OPERATES`: operador → asset, y el transportista que el viaje nombra.
  - `LINKED`: asset → asset durante un viaje, por ejemplo la jaula o el señuelo.
- **Vencimiento:** una evidencia vence en `validUntil` si la fuente lo trae. Si no, vence un TTL después de `lastSeen`. Los TTL son por fuente (`miot.fleet.network.ttl.*`; señal 30 días, viaje 7, acreditación 30).
- **`NetworkResolver` deriva todo y no guarda nada:**
  - qué assets ve una organización y por qué: la reporta, es dueña, la opera, o viaja con una que opera;
  - sus relaciones con otras organizaciones: operación (operador↔transportista) y servicio GPS (proveedor↔transportista), con fuentes, fechas, vencimiento y estado.

## API (`fleet:network.view`, rol `FLEET_VIEWER`)
- `GET /api/v1/orgs/{org}/fleet/network/assets`
- `GET /api/v1/orgs/{org}/fleet/network/assets/{assetId}`: 404 si la organización no lo ve.
- `GET /api/v1/orgs/{org}/fleet/network/relationships`

La fuente se elige con `miot.fleet.network.source` (`MIOT_FLEET_NETWORK_SOURCE`):
- `demo` arma una red ficticia alrededor de la organización que consulta, que hace de operador. Es el valor por defecto en el perfil `%dev`.
- Sin valor, la API responde 503.

## App
- Página **Ajustes › Red de assets** (`/users/settings/network`), con dos tablas:
  - organizaciones relacionadas;
  - assets visibles, con la razón y la fecha hasta la que se ven, y búsqueda.
- La entrada del menú y Spotlight se muestran solo con `fleet:network.view`.
- Proxy `GET /api/fleet/network/*` al modulith de StreamHub.

## Pendiente (siguientes PRs)
- La fuente real: el catálogo desde las señales, y las evidencias desde viajes y acreditaciones.
- Los ids de asset con `:` (MAC) no pasan por el proxy del front, que solo acepta `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`.

## Verificación
- `miot-fleet`: 16 tests (resolvedor, demo, recurso, permisos). `miot-cli` empaqueta con todos los componentes.
- App: `vitest` en `settings-admin/network`, `api/fleet`, `features/layout` e i18n (73 tests). `tsc` sin errores nuevos; `eslint` sin avisos en los archivos nuevos.

Closes #1915

author: mkuhtze-code
body:
## Audit finding
The shared `useDialogA11y` hook only inspected its ref on the owning component's first mount. For sheets rendered conditionally inside a component that remains mounted, the ref was null at that time, so the hook never installed Escape handling, focus containment, or focus restoration. Several existing modal dialogs did not use the shared hook at all.

## Changes
- Make the shared hook respond to callback-ref attach/detach so it works for both initially mounted and conditionally mounted dialogs.
- Preserve modal focus trap, safe initial focus, Escape dismissal, hidden-control filtering, and focus restoration.
- Keep desktop task-detail pane non-modal by respecting `trapFocus: false`.
- Apply shared focus handling to Open Lists, Travel Vault, Plan a Trip, Trip Tools, Meeting export's missing-media/export-ready dialogs, and the meeting photo lightbox.
- Add a regression test for a dialog that mounts after its owner, including focus containment and return to the trigger.
- Record the source-level findings and remaining manual acceptance in `docs/MOBILE_MODAL_ACCESSIBILITY_AUDIT.md`.

## Scope
Accessibility/reliability only. No new features, data changes, visual redesign, or changes to deterministic business logic.

## Validation
Both Vercel checks and the dialog accessibility test must pass before merge. Physical-device keyboard/screen-reader acceptance and full WCAG 2.2 AA verification remain outstanding.

## 1. "Otel seçilmedi" artık bir kez görünüyor (KK1–KK2)
- `siradakiAdim` yeni bir girdi alıyor: `ekranda`, yani aynı ekranda kendi satırı olan eksikler. Bunlar öneri olarak seçilmiyor; öncelik sırasındaki sonraki adım geliyor.
- Gezi sayfasının plan modunda Plan bölümündeki otel satırı hep görünüyor. Bu yüzden `ekranda: ['otel']`:
  - tek kişiyse adım "Arkadaşını davet et" oluyor;
  - "Dağıt" satırının altındaki "otel de seçilmedi" notu da kalktı;
  - otel satırı olduğu gibi duruyor.
- Testler: kural başına bir test (otel, dağıt notu, davet, plan kur, yemek, yarın, harcama). Sayfa testinde "Otel seçilmedi" artık tek.

## 2. Günlere dağıt: sığmayan mekanlar penceresi (KK3–KK6, kanvas 28)
- **Gün kapasitesi:** günün kendi penceresi; `days.start_time`/`end_time` yoksa seyahatin `day_start`/`day_end` değeri. Eski sabit 9 saatlik (10:00–19:00) kapasite kalktı.
- **Pencere:** sığmayan mekan varsa yazmadan önce açılıyor. Başlık "N mekan günlere sığmıyor", alt satır "M mekan · G gün · günler 09:00–20:00". Altında "NASIL SIĞDIRALIM?" ve yalnız uygulanabilen seçenekler:
  - **Süreleri kısalt:** en az kısaltan oran aranıyor (%1 adımla, en düşük %75).
    - Taban: kendi süresinin %75'i ya da 20 dk, hangisi büyükse.
    - Yemek durakları ve varılmış / tamamlanmış duraklar kısalmıyor.
    - Satırda "ortalama 75 → 60 dk", altında gün gün önizleme (mekan sayısı, başlangıç–bitiş).
    - Çipler: "Hepsi sığar" ya da "N tanesi daha sığar; K mekan Listem'de kalır"; yemek durağı varsa "Yemek durakları aynı".
  - **Günleri uzat:** en küçük ortak uzatma (5 dk adımla), en geç 22:00. Bitiş yalnız gereken günlerde uzuyor: "Pzt, Sal ve Çar bitişi 20:00 → 20:15; süreler aynı kalır." Bitişler farklıysa gün gün yazılıyor.
  - **Listede kalsın:** bugünkü davranış: "24 mekan dağıtılır; Sazova Parkı, Kent Park ve 1 mekan daha Listem'de kalır."
- **Varsayılan (KK4):** hepsini sığdıran ilk seçenek; hiçbiri sığdıramıyorsa en çok mekanı sığdıran. Düğme "N mekanı dağıt", altında "Süreleri sonra Plan'da tek tek değiştirebilirsin."
- **Yazım (KK5):** yeni `gunlere_dagit` RPC'si üç işi tek işlemde yapıyor:
  - yeni durakları ekliyor;
  - kısalan durakların süresini (`stops.minutes`) değiştiriyor; mekanın varsayılan süresi aynı kalıyor;
  - uzayan günlerin bitişini (`days.end_time`) değiştiriyor.
- **Tek kayıt ve Geri al:**
  - Satır tetikleyicileri her değişikliği yine yazıyor; hepsi işlemin `dagit` kaydına `changes.grup` ile bağlanıyor.
  - Son değişiklikler ve sohbetteki sistem satırları yalnız grupsuz satırları okuyor. Dağıtım tek satır görünüyor: "12 mekanı günlere dağıttı · süreleri kısalttı".
  - "Geri al" (`degisikligi_geri_al`) her şeyi tek seferde döndürüyor: eklenen duraklar siliniyor, süreler ve bitişler eski haline geliyor. Geri alma da tek kayıt ("günlere dağıtımı geri aldı").
  - Hesap tamamen sığarsa pencere açılmadan aynı yoldan yazılıyor.
- **Saf hesap (KK6):** `src/features/listem/sigmayanlar.ts`. Testler: taban, yemek istisnası, varılmış durak, kısmi sığma, 22:00 sınırı, varsayılan, uygulanamayan seçeneğin gizlenmesi, yazım biçimi.
- `planKur` gün başına kapasite alabiliyor (`PlanGunu.kapasiteDk`). Sihirbaz ve Planı kur bunu kullanmadığı için onlarda değişiklik yok.

## 3. Keşfet'te listedeki yer (KK7–KK8)
**KK7 bulgusu (gerçek veri, yalnız sayılar):** 4 seyahatte 42 mekan var.
- Gezi durağının place_id'si doluysa, durağın 15 m içindeki liste mekanlarının kimliği **20/20 aynı** (farklı: 0). Hazır geziden doğrudan alınan kimlikler Google'ınkiyle aynı.
- Aynı listede aynı noktada (15 m) farklı kimlikli iki mekan **0**, seyahatler arasında da **0**. Liste içi 15–60 m'deki 8 çift komşu, ayrı mekanlar (Odunpazarı kümesi).
- **Riskli yol:** place_id'si boş duraktan adla çözülen mekanlar (`eskisehir-iki-gun`'ün 11 durağı boş; 6 liste mekanı bunlara 15 m yakın). Keşfet'in Nearby sonuçları sunucuda saklanmadığı için bu kimliklerin Nearby'ninkiyle aynı olup olmadığı veriden doğrulanamıyor. Google'da aynı noktada iki ayrı kayıt da olabiliyor ("Odunpazarı Evleri" / "Tarihi Odunpazarı Evleri" gibi).

**KK8 güvenlik ağı (`src/features/yerler/benzerYer.ts`):**
- Listedeki bir mekana 60 m'den yakın ve adı benzer olan öneri de listede sayılıyor. Ad karşılaştırması: küçük harf, aksansız (Hermes'te `normalize`'a güvenmeden), "tarihi / müzesi / belediyesi…" gibi ekler atılmış; biri öbürünü kapsıyor ya da sözcüklerin yarısından fazlası ortak.
- Bu öneri haritada pin, çekmecede satır ve gizli sayısında görünmüyor.
- Ad eldeki hafif veriden geliyor; ek Google isteği yok. Adı bilinmeyen liste mekanında yalnız kimlik süzgeci çalışıyor. Testlerde adı farklı ya da uzak komşular gizlenmiyor.

## Ayrıca: fotoğrafsız mekan
"Tarihi Odunpazarı Evleri"nin kutusunun boş kalma sebebi şu: Gezi sayfası açılışta Google'a gitmiyor (#181 KK13). Fotoğraf yoksa artık kategori ikonu çıkıyor (kategori renginde, pastel zeminde). Bu, Listem önizlemesinde (`FotoKutusu`) ve Listem satırlarında geçerli.

author: michaelbetfinal
body: `.github/` is on the sensitive list, so this waits for Michael. ## What changed `pull_request` `ready_for_review` re-fires CI even when the head SHA did not change. An `already-passed` gate in `ci.yml` now skips `check` or `e2e` on that event when the newest finished, non-skipped run of that job on the head SHA passed, and that run started after the base branch last moved. A PR run tests the merge with the base, so a pass against an older `main` does not count. The push time comes from the activity API, and the run's start is its check suite's creation time. If another run of the job is still going, the gate does not skip. A lookup error skips nothing. `e2e` still skips drafts. `main` still runs it, since a push has no `pull_request` payload. `check` runs on every PR push, drafts included. A job skipped by `if:` counts as success. Claude review no longer triggers on `ready_for_review`. Every push already gets a pass, drafts included. Add the `claude-review` label for another pass on the same commit. The `shots` CI job is gone. `pnpm shots --grep ` stays an agent step for UI work, run locally. Merge policy no longer lists shots as a merge gate. Branch protection and rulesets are not available on this private repo plan, so no required check named `shots` can be left waiting. ## How to verify 1. Open a draft PR. `check` runs, `e2e` skips, no `shots` job, and Claude review runs. 2. Mark it ready without pushing. If `check` passed on that SHA after `main` last moved, `check` skips. `e2e` runs, since drafts never ran it. Claude review does not start. 3. Merge something into `main`, put the PR back to draft, and mark it ready again. Both `check` and `e2e` run, because `main` moved after their last pass. 4. Without a base move, a second ready skips `e2e` too, and the gate log links the run that passed.

author: codeyoma
body:
Closes #183. This is step ① of #178: the engine gets the **barrier** kind (`barrier`, answer version 1). Its two baselines predict and are scored live and appear on the leaderboard (`?kind=barrier`). The model `breiman` is #184 and the screen #185.

## What it does
- **Width w** (`features.py`):
  - The EWM standard deviation (span 100, as pandas `ewm(span=100).std()`) of one-minute close changes, in ticks of the reference price at t.
  - Only changes between bars exactly a minute apart count. The previous trading day's continuous-session bars come first, then today's from the open. The overnight jump and NXT pre-market bars are left out.
  - w = max(k, σ̂₁ × √4, rounded half up). With fewer than 20 bars or 2 changes, w = k.
  - The market view fixes w once per symbol and bar close, so the predictions, the answer and the features `barrier_width` and `barrier_sigma` share it. Turing excludes these features.
- **Storage:** w is kept in a new column `kind_predictions.width_ticks` and served as `width_ticks` on every kind prediction (null for range). It sits beside #200's `flat_ticks`, not inside `output`, so the output contract stays exactly the three probabilities and `no_previous`/`vi` rows still carry w.
- **Answer** (`barriers.py`, pure):
  - U and L are the reference mid ± w ticks.
  - By received time in [t, t+4m), the first best bid ≥ U or the first best ask ≤ L wins: `up_first` or `down_first`. Neither is `timeout`. The same received time is unscorable `ambiguous`.
  - The other unscorable and special rules follow #160. The path follows #178, with the round-trip cost added.
- **Output contract:** `{p_up_first, p_timeout, p_down_first}`, summing to 1.
- **Baselines:**
  - `barrier-climate`: symbol × 30-minute slot class ratios. It backs off to the symbol's day, then ⅓ each. It is refit nightly and installed by the 08:00 swap.
  - `barrier-persist`: the previous window's answer, or `no_previous` when that window has no class.
- **Stats:** 3-class stats with action classes up_first and down_first.
- **Barrier P&L** (research only):
  - An `up_first` call buys at t's ask and sells at U, at the bid when L hits, or at the last bid.
  - A `down_first` call is the mirror; a `timeout` call is no trade.
  - The round-trip cost is subtracted. It is reported for all calls, longs and shorts.
- **Bar rule:**
  - #160's close-position rule with the 1-tick buffer, around w, where the first minute that reached a barrier wins.
  - Both barriers in the same minute give no label (`same minute`), so the sample drops out of training.
  - Every bar rule now takes a `width` keyword, which the range ignores.
- **Backfill:** at startup, past barrier answers from 2026-10-12 are filled. They match a fresh replay, and the previous day's bars are read too.
- **Diagnose section 8:** the answer distribution, the w distribution and the share where w = k, the bar rule against the quote answer, the share of same-minute double touches, and perfect-foresight P&L.

## Checked
- `pytest`: 927 passed, 57 new in `test_barriers.py`. ruff, mypy and `check_forbidden.py` are clean.
- Rule tables worked by hand for the width, the answer, the bar rule and the P&L.
- Replay Harness: `width_ticks`, the answers and paths, one answer shared per bar close, restart and silence, and `barrier-persist` not predicting. The leaderboard serves `?kind=barrier`.
- The fill matches a replay and is idempotent.
- Direction and range results are identical with and without the barrier.

## Server
Nothing to do by hand at deploy. The bar rule's agreement with the quote answers and the same-minute share are provisional until `diagnose` section 8 runs on the server; that step is added to #203.

body:
## O que muda
**a) Workflows (6 arquivos)**
- `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04` em todos os jobs (o `ubuntu-latest` migra para o Ubuntu 26 em 19/10/2026).
- `actions/checkout@v4` → `@v5`, `actions/upload-artifact@v4` → `@v6`, `actions/create-github-app-token@v2` → `@v3`. São as **primeiras** versões de cada ação que declaram `runs.using: node24` (conferi o `action.yml` de cada tag e as notas de release). Não há mudança nas entradas que usamos; o `app-id` do `create-github-app-token` está deprecado em favor de `client-id`, mas continua funcionando (gera aviso). A troca exige mudar a variável do App Writer e fica para outro momento. Existem majors mais novos (`checkout` e `upload-artifact` v7); não adotei porque não avaliei as mudanças.
- Os logs já mostravam "forced to run on Node.js 24"; a mudança tira o aviso e a dependência dessa regra de compatibilidade. Runners hospedados já estão acima da versão mínima exigida (2.327.1).

**b) Documentação** (`BACKUP_REPOSITORY.md` I.15 e I.9; `docs/contexto/STATUS_ATUAL.md`)
- Decisão do HITL de tornar o repositório privado, com as consequências aceitas: proteção de branch indisponível no plano gratuito (o check "Registry traceability" vira só detectivo) e minutos de Actions entrando na cota.
- Artefatos de teste de restauração a apagar pelo HITL (`-restaurado-2` a `-restaurado-7`, Projects nº 15, 16 e 17); a evidência fica no OneDrive.
- A regra de log sem títulos e nomes continua como boa prática.
- Registro: SHAs dos 6 workflows atualizados.

## ⚠️ Pré-condição que a documentação agora registra (não foi pedida, mas bloqueia a decisão)
No plano **gratuito**, os **environments e seus segredos são ignorados em repositório privado** (fonte: documentação do GitHub, "if a repository is converted to private, any configured protection rules or environment secrets will be ignored"). **Todos os workflows usam `environment: onedrive-backup`**, que guarda `ONEDRIVE_REFRESH_TOKEN`, `SOURCE_READ_TOKEN`, `PROJECTS_READ_TOKEN`, `RESTORE_WRITE_TOKEN` e a chave do App Writer. Tornar o repositório privado agora interromperia backup e restauração. Resolver antes (decisão de projeto + PR próprio): segredos de repositório (o App Writer hoje regrava um segredo de **environment**), plano Pro, ou manter público. Este PR **não** altera onde os segredos ficam.

## Testes
`test_dispatch_check`, `test_restore_repo` (133), `test_bkp_issues`, `test_bkp_proj` e `validate_traceability --check` passam; os 6 YAML carregam. O run real de um backup curto depois do merge confirma as novas versões das actions (não rodei nenhum).

author: jarsarasty
body:
## Why

pymoca 0.11+ removed the built-in `Modelica` namespace and no longer carries
`import SI = Modelica.Units.SI` aliases across parent-class traversal, so the
channel-flow library stops resolving (`ClassNotFoundError: 'SI.X'`). This
blocks lifting rtc-tools' `pymoca==0.9.*` pin.

This PR makes the library resolve under pymoca 0.11+ while remaining
compatible with 0.9.3.

## What

- Remove 47 `import SI =` lines and expand 216 `SI.X` references to
  `Modelica.Units.SI.X` across the library and examples.
- Migrate 13 legacy `Modelica.SIunits.*` references to `Modelica.Units.SI.*`.
- Add a `tests/` suite and CI: jobs for pymoca 0.9.3 and 0.11.2 that flatten
  every library class and compile every example.
- Make matplotlib optional in the example scripts so a headless test run does
  not require it.

## Notes

- The expansion targets already resolve on pymoca 0.9.3, so the change is
  backwards-compatible across the pin.
- The 0.11.2 CI job pins `casadi<3.8` (pymoca maps `/` to the removed
  `MX.__div__` on casadi 3.8) and expects the goal-bounds xfails that an
  unrelated upstream pymoca defect still produces.

author: htsukamoto5
body:
Participants now learn the interface after role assignment and play two paired practice rounds before the 18-trial main game. The walkthrough starts with a blank preview and reveals the shapes, chat, timer, score and progress with role-specific explanations; its timer is stopped and its controls are disabled.

Practice uses two distinct targets excluded from the dyad’s main schedule, with the existing messaging gate, timing, feedback and fixed roles. Both partners continue through a bounded readiness barrier before main gameplay; score and progress reset there. Practice rows are retained with explicit phase/index fields and excluded from main-game counts. Round IDs remain unique across phases, and practice interruptions skip the main game. author: xarmian
body:
## What

`AdoptLegacyBuiltins` is a one-time startup pass. It matched each legacy convention or playbook against the library using the title, fields and content buffered by an unlocked scan. It then inserted origins in a later transaction without re-reading. If an item was renamed away from its library title, or deleted, between the scan and the insert, it was still adopted, and then offered a built-in's text it no longer names.

**The open question on the bug** was whether library update's seq guard already refuses the overwrite. For a content edit, yes: the adoption records an origin with no seed, so the state (`current` / `unknown_origin`) is computed from the item's text at read time. An update also needs the `expected_seq` of a preview that showed that text. Matching is by title (plus slug for playbooks; content only breaks ties between duplicate titles), so the race that does matter is a rename, a move, or a delete.

## Fix

Adoption now runs one transaction per workspace, following BUG-3666's wiki-link backfill:
- it takes the workspace seq lock first;
- it re-reads each candidate (`FOR UPDATE OF i` on Postgres) and matches on what it re-read;
- it skips items deleted, moved out of conventions/playbooks, or given an origin since the scan.

A crash between workspaces is safe, because adopted items drop out of a rerun's scan.

## Tests

`internal/store/bug3806_legacy_adoption_race_test.go` renames one convention and deletes another from an after-scan hook. An untouched playbook is the control.
- Before the fix, on SQLite: the renamed and deleted items were both adopted, and the control was adopted as it should be.
- After the fix: green on SQLite and test-pg (`TestAdoptLegacyBuiltins|TASK3462` over store and server, 23 PASS lines). The existing TASK3462 U4 adoption tests pass on both backends.

author: chinmaymk
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"chinmaymk"} -->
_Requested by **Chinmay** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_0176mKABrycX377npXK9kW2i?thread=cmsg_0176mKABrycX377npXK9kW2i6dT5bwW1pMaUrVKkqzEC73)_

## Problem

Statically known standard-library calls still went through runtime dispatch (`Invoke`, bound Functions, boxed arguments), 100 to 1000x slower than Go over 3M calls:
- `o.is_some()` built a bound Function and TypeScope per call: 995 ns.
- `abs_int(value: x)`, `sqrt(value: x)`: about 150 ns each (Function lookup, `[]Argument`, boxing of arguments and result, defer wrapper).
- `s.contains(value: "wor")`: 108 ns.

## Proposed change

- `is_some`, `is_none`, `unwrap_or` lower to plain runtime helpers; `@std/Optional` joins the receiver kinds that bind a member once per call site, so `map`, `and_then`, `ok_or` and friends skip the per-call bound Function.
- Pure scalar functions (`math` float functions, `abs_int`; String `trim`, `upper`, `lower`, `contains`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`) get typed Go implementations in `scalar_functions.go`. The library table wraps those same functions, and lowered code calls them directly with native Go scalars, so arguments and results are not boxed and the types flow into typed locals.
- Results over 3M calls: `is_some` 2984 to 34 ms, `abs_int` 449 to 26 ms, `sqrt` 503 to 13 ms, `String.contains` 410 to 63 ms.

## Alternatives considered

- Positional `Body` calls instead of `Invoke` for std functions and closures: built and measured; no gain beyond noise (the cost is boxing and the Function wrapper, not label matching), so dropped.
- Typed signatures for the whole library: much larger; this covers the pure scalar subset that appears in hot loops.
- Do nothing: these stay 50 to 1000x slower than Go.

## Testing

- Validation: `go test ./...` and `go run ./scripts/repo-check` pass. New e2e tests cover every Optional member, every typed math and String function (including through function values, `abs_int` overflow still faulting, `round` ties), and new lowering tests assert the plain runtime calls.
- Documentation: none; behavior is unchanged.
- Compatibility: none; generated Go changes only.

author: lalalune
body:
## Problem

The Android agent IPC (bionic/musl agent <-> app, private filesystem UDS) carried only `http_request` and `http_request_stream`. That meant the WS-only `agent_event` envelopes, including the ephemeral `voice-transcript` stream from #36214 (`speech-start | partial | final | error`), had no way to reach a port-free Android app.

## Change

**Agent: `events_subscribe` frame** (`plugins/plugin-native-inference/src/android/{private-ipc,event-subscription,private-dispatch}.ts`)

```
in:  {"id","method":"events_subscribe","payload":{"streams":["voice-transcript"],"headers":{"Authorization":"Bearer <ELIZA_API_TOKEN>"}}}
out: {"id","event":"subscribed","streams":[..]}        once, first
     {"id","event":"agent_event","data":<WS envelope>}  per matching event
     {"id","event":"keepalive"}                         every 15 s
     {"id","event":"error","error":".."}                terminal refusal, then close
```

- The stream filter is required, exact-match, 1-16 names. The per-boot bearer is required (same rule as the wake route).
- Live only, with no replay. The envelope has the WS shape. Ephemeral streams (from `EPHEMERAL_AGENT_EVENT_STREAMS`, now exported by `@elizaos/agent`) carry `ephemeral: true` and an `eph-<n>` id. Other streams get an `ipc-<n>` id. Neither id has a `bufferSeq`.
- Bounded: each frame is capped at 256 KiB. An oversized or unserializable event ends the feed with an explicit `error` frame (follow-up commit 09b69490c7, so the feed never has a silent gap). A reader with more than 1 MiB queued is disconnected rather than buffered. Payloads are never logged.
- Subscriptions get 2 dedicated slots, separate from the 4 request slots. They have no transport deadline and end when the peer closes, on overflow, or when the server stops.

**Android**
- `ElizaAgentService.subscribeLocalAgentEvents(String requestJson, Consumer<String> onEvent, LocalStreamHandle handle)` blocks and emits `subscribed`, then `event` (`dropped` is reserved and still tolerated), then exactly one `end` (`error` is absent only on cancel). It uses a 45 s rolling idle budget.
- Agent plugin (app Java and `plugin-native-agent` Kotlin): `subscribeEvents({streams, subscriptionId?})` returns `{subscriptionId}`, and events arrive as `agentEvent`. `unsubscribeEvents({subscriptionId})` ends a feed. Each plugin allows at most 2 feeds.
- R8 keep rules cover the reflected entry point and `LocalStreamHandle`.

**App TS client** (`@elizaos/capacitor-agent`): the `AgentEventEnvelope` / `AgentEventFeedEvent` types, plus `supportsAgentEvents(Agent)` and `subscribeAgentEvents(Agent, {streams, signal?}, {onEvent, onDropped?, onEnd?})`, which returns `{subscriptionId, ended, close()}`.

## Tests

- `bun test --conditions eliza-source __tests__/android-*` (plugin-native-inference): 16 pass. This includes a real-socket test of filtering, no replay, ephemeral semantics, auth refusal, invalid filters, slot isolation (2 feeds held open while 4 requests still succeed), listener release, frame cap, overflow disconnect and keepalive.
- `vitest run` (plugin-native-agent): 28 pass, 4 of them new for the client.
- Gradle: `:app:testDebugUnitTest --tests ai.elizaos.app.ElizaAgentEventSubscriptionTest` 3/3 pass. `:elizaos-capacitor-agent:compileDebugKotlin` and `testDebugUnitTest` are green.

Not covered: iOS has no counterpart here, and none of this has run on a device or emulator.

At `5c51cbacb277a0ffe8313b2aba774cd0caa11def`, the socket and sign-in integration tests passed 19 tests. The agent client and web tests passed 29 tests, including cancellation ordering and failed-cleanup reporting. The Android Gradle build passed the three `ElizaAgentEventSubscriptionTest` tests and Kotlin compilation. `ELIZA_ANDROID_SKIP_FORK_LLAMA_LIB=1` was used for the host tests because this checkout lacks the packaged inference library; no APK or device qualification is claimed. author: alexanderuv
body:
First part of Phase 1 (math and geometry) of the Jolt v5.6.0 parity roadmap. Parity means features, not code: Moonbounce supports what Jolt supports with its own design and API, as now documented in `docs/roadmap.md` and the README.

## What's in it

- **`Vec4` and `UVec4`**: 4-lane float and 32-bit integer math, comparison masks, select, shifts and swizzles. `Lane` handles swizzle indices.
- **Deterministic trigonometry**: vectorized sin/cos, tan, asin, acos, atan and atan2 using Moonbounce's own Remez-fitted minimax polynomials evaluated with FMAs. Every platform computes the same bits, so libm is no longer linked. A checksum test pins the bits. The worst-case error is lower than Jolt's on every function. Figures are the largest difference from the exact result over the test sweep, in billionths (an error of 69 means 0.000000069). Lower is better. A `Float` has about 60–120 billionths of resolution near 1, so the sin and cos errors are below one step of the format.

  | Function | Moonbounce max error | Jolt max error |
  |---|---|---|
  | sin / cos | 69 | 77 |
  | tan (relative to the result) | 159 | 770 |
  | asin | 129 | 161 |
  | acos | 226 | 319 |
  | atan | 133 | 136 |
  | atan2 | 260 | 272 |

- **The rest of `Vec3` and `Quat`**: normalized perpendicular, swing-twist, twist and rotation angle, slerp, Euler angles, from-to and random rotations, axis-angle and angular velocity. Also octahedral unit-vector encoding (max error 6.4e-5) and smallest-three quaternion encoding (max error 0.0042 rad).
- **Performance rules**:
  - Hot-path API (trigonometry, quaternion decomposition) is `@inline(always)`.
  - Vector constants (`Vec3.zero`, `Quat.identity`, …) are computed properties. Stored SIMD globals are reached through an addressor call that spills registers in client loops.
- **Tests**: 111 tests in 8 suites pass in debug and release.

## Benchmarks vs Jolt

Run with `JoltComparison/compare.py --rounds 5` on Apple silicon. Each figure is per 1,000 ops, and neither side allocates.

| Benchmark | Moonbounce ns | Jolt ns | Moonbounce is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Vec3.normalizedPerpendicular` | 1,166 | 1,473 | 26% faster |
| `Vec4.multiplyAdd` | 294 | 306 | even |
| `Vec4.reduceMin` | 151 | 145 | even (4%) |
| `UVec4.select` | 307 | 305 | even |
| `UVec4.countTrues` | 293 | 287 | even |
| `Vec4.sinCos` | 2,867 | 3,360 | 17% faster |
| `Vec4.atan2` | 2,406 | 3,362 | 40% faster |
| `Quat.swingTwist` | 1,518 | 2,118 | 40% faster |
| `Quat.slerp` | 15,524 | 21,960 | 41% faster |

All eight Phase 0 benchmarks remain even or faster.

### `Vec4.reduceMin`: fixed by using the NEON intrinsic

It measured 4–12% slower across runs, with 25% more instructions. The cause was in the shim, not the benchmark: the generic `__builtin_reduce_min` makes LLVM unroll the loop 2×, while Jolt's `vminvq_f32` unrolls 8×. On arm64 the shim now calls `vminnmvq_f32` directly. Results are bit-identical, and it now runs 3551 instructions per 1,000 ops against Jolt's 3652.

## Not yet in this PR

`Mat44`, double precision, packed float types, half floats, small/dynamic matrices, `AABox4`, ray tests, closest point, shapes, polygon clipping, Morton codes, convex support, GJK, EPA, and convex hull builders.

author: abysmalbiscuit
body:
## Agent summary

There is no second-model reviewer on PRs. This adds a `Grok review` workflow that runs the xAI Grok CLI headless on each non-draft PR from this repo and posts its findings as one review with inline comments and `suggestion` blocks. It requests changes on P0/P1 findings, comments otherwise, and dismisses its own earlier change requests on each run.

The review posts as the `grok-review-bot` GitHub App when the `GROK_REVIEW_APP_ID` variable and `GROK_REVIEW_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secret are set, and as `github-actions` until then.

It departs from xAI's sample workflow:

- **Grok can't write anywhere.** It runs with `--always-approve --tools read_file,list_dir,grep,glob --disable-web-search` (no shell; headless `dontAsk` cancels the turn on the first shell call), reads the diff from a pre-written `pr.diff`, has no GitHub token, and replies through `--json-schema`. A separate step posts the review with the write token. The sample gave `--always-approve` a write-capable `GH_TOKEN` while Grok reads PR-controlled text.
- **Grok loads AGENTS.md.** That needs `--trust` headless. `--trust` would also apply the permission rules and hooks in project `.grok/` and `.claude/` dirs, so those are removed first.
- **The prompt follows Codex's review rubric.** It flags only verified bugs the PR introduced, each with a priority, and ends with a verdict.
- **The CLI is pinned and on PATH.** It is pinned to 1.0.52, and `~/.grok/bin` goes on `GITHUB_PATH`, because the installer only edits shell rc files.
- **Fork PRs are skipped.** They get no `XAI_API_KEY`.

## Proof

Before: no Grok workflow existed.

1. ✅ `actionlint .github/workflows/grok-review.yml`
   - **After:** exits 0, no findings
2. ✅ the `Post review` step's jq turns a Grok reply into a review payload (run locally on sample findings)
   - **After:** P1 finding -> `REQUEST_CHANGES` with an inline comment holding a `suggestion` block; empty findings -> `COMMENT` "No issues found."
3. ✅ run 38635273391 on 55a721b9: Grok used only file tools for 16 turns ($0.10), returned schema-valid JSON with no findings, and `github-actions` posted "No issues found." on the PR
   - **Before:** run 38633712435 under `dontAsk` ended with `stopReason: cancelled` and an empty reply
4. ⚠️ **Not observed:** an inline comment with a suggestion block on a real finding; no run has produced a finding yet
5. ⚠️ **Not observed:** posting as `grok-review-bot`; the GitHub App does not exist yet

body:
## What

After a failed trip generation, "Try again" brought the form back on step 7 and toasted "Found Lisbon, Portugal" again.

The city check lives in `FormProvider` and outlasts the form. When the failure panel replaces the form, `FormStep2` unmounts. "Try again" mounts it again, and its toast effect ran on mount against the result that was still there.

## Fix

`FormStep2` keeps the last message it showed in a ref and toasts only when the message changes. Typing a city again still toasts, because the check clears its message while loading. This also stops a repeat toast when someone leaves `/form` partway through and comes back.

`docs/grounded-agent/PLAN.md` gets a "Follow-up fixes before branch 2" list with this fix and the next one (`axios-to-fetch`).

- `FormFailure.test.tsx`: a failed request, then Try again, must not call `toast.custom`. It failed before the fix and passes now.
- `tsc`, `npm test` (651), `npm run build` and `npm run test:e2e` (72) pass. The e2e walk still sees the toast on a fresh city check.
- Browser (production build, `E2E_FIXTURES=1`): I forced the server action to return a 500, clicked Try again, and landed on "Review and submit" with no toast. The only console errors came from the forced 500.

## Summary
Harden directory signature validation in the native desktop cleanup helper (`native/desktop-bridge/src/cleanup.rs`) to prevent accidental recursive deletion of unrelated user or build trees that happen to contain generic directories like `outputs` or `runtime`.

## Changes

  - Updated `has_signature` to require either a definitive application marker (`omnivoice.db` or `prefs.json`) or at least three confirming directory markers together (`voices`, `outputs`, `engines`, `runtime`).
  - Disallowed single generic subdirectories (e.g. `outputs` or `runtime` alone) from qualifying arbitrary paths as VoiceStudio cleanup targets.
  - Added unit test `generic_directories_alone_do_not_satisfy_signature` verifying that directories containing only generic folder names are rejected, while directories with application database files are correctly accepted.

author: daedalus
body:
Follow-up to #144, which merged before Sourcery's review arrived.

## Fixed

Each fix has a `test_regression_*` test that fails on master and passes here.

- **0xFF byte weight**: a byte at 0xFF in an 8-bit sum got no weight, because the signed check read 255 as -1. The weight is now `-delta * 255^-1 mod 2^bits` (255 is odd).
- **Additive fall-through**: an additive guess that failed verification skipped the byte map. It now falls through.
- **Scheduling**: additive fits run across all pairs before any byte-map search, so an early string compare can't spend the budget first.
- **Missing records**: a byte-map read with the record missing is re-run once before it counts as satisfied, because a short FIFO drain also drops records.

## Not changed

- **Solver never run**: `FuzzRound._search_affine` calls `search` and `mutate` drains the queue.
- **Positional args**: every `Fuzzer(...)` caller passes keywords.
- **Int-width string operands in the input**: these still go to Redqueen; retaining them would put every I2S int pair through the derived search.
- **Greedy additive split isn't exact**: this is exact for sums (`w = 1`); mixed weights stay a TODO.
- **Window-fit budget reserve**: not added.

Compiled gates are unchanged at 3000 execs: compcov G0/G2/G3/G5 (seeds 1-2), gf2 G0-G3 (seed 1).

author: edwinquick
body:
## Problem

On 0.1.5, with `claude-opus-5-5` (native 1M window, no `[1m]` suffix), the UserPromptSubmit hook reported **"degraded. Context 97% full"** at about 195k tokens. A few prompts later, `vitals-cli report` in the same session said **"healthy, 21% full (208k of 1000k)"**.

Cause: `detectContextWindow()` returned 1M only for `[1m]` (in the id, a settings file or `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`) or for an id already learned in `windows.json`. Otherwise it returned 200k. `computeVitals` corrected this only after the session went past 200k. So every reading between about 110k and 200k was scored against 200k, and above 90% the context signal gets weight 3. The hook and the CLI disagreed because the CLI ran after the session had crossed 200k.

## Fix

- **Native window from the model id** (`nativeContextWindow` in `state.mjs`). The table follows Anthropic's model overview, checked 2026-10-14 using the claude-api skill's model tables. Fable/Mythos 5.x, Opus/Sonnet/Haiku 5.x, Opus 4.6–4.8 and Sonnet 4.6 are 1M. **Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.5 and older stay 200k.** It handles dated, Bedrock (`us.anthropic.…-v1:0`) and Vertex (`@date`) forms. `[1m]`, learned windows and settings files still win.
- **Model id from the transcript.** `parseTranscript` now keeps `message.model`. The window resolves even when the hook payload has no model and on a bare CLI run.
- **An unknown window is reported as unknown.** `contextWindow`/`contextPct` are `null`. The report says "Context holds 195k tokens; the window size is unknown… (set SESSION_VITALS_CONTEXT_WINDOW)". Fill scores at most 1 (above 150k), so it can never push the tier to degraded by itself. Past 200k the session has proved 1M, as before.
- **One resolver for hook and CLI** (`contextWindowFor`). Both use the payload model, the transcript model, `SESSION_VITALS_MODEL` (CLI only), and any window the session has already proved. The window is resolved on every measurement, so the stored 200k guess in a 0.1.5 state file does not carry over. A stored value above 200k is still kept as proved.
- **README** has a new "Context window" section covering the detection order and `SESSION_VITALS_CONTEXT_WINDOW` as the escape hatch. `docs/rubric.md` is updated to match.
- Version is now **0.1.6**. The repo has no changelog file, so there is no changelog entry.

## Tests

30/30 pass (`node --test`). Against the 0.1.5 `scripts/`, the new tests fail.

- `claude-opus-5-5` at 195k: context weight < 3 and tier not degraded, both in unit scoring and end to end through the hook and CLI. This holds with the model in the payload and with it only in the transcript. The hook and CLI report the same 1M window.
- `claude-haiku-4-5` at 195k (a real 200k model): still "Context 98% full", degraded.
- Unknown id at 195k: no percentage, weight ≤ 1, not degraded.
- A table test of model ids, including 200k models and provider-prefixed forms.
- The issue #7 learning test now uses an unrecognised id, because `claude-opus-5-5` is no longer unknown.

I also ran a manual check on a live `claude-opus-5-5` session at 185k: it reports `contextWindow 1000000`, healthy. 0.1.5 would have reported 92% and degraded.

No new dependencies.

author: popdaph
body:
## Description

Follow up of #35217. First step to make the `files` tools the only way agents read and write documents (then `files.edit`, `files.create`, and removing `read_document` / `edit_document`).

While a document is open, the collab server holds its latest text and saves it to the file every few seconds, so the file lags. `files.cat` read the file, so an agent could read a stale version. Now, when the file is stored as Markdown and a live session holds it, `cat` reads the session's text instead, with the same line numbers and paging, and the editor shows the agent reading. Other files are read exactly as before.

Notes:
- If the collab server cannot answer, `cat` falls back to the file, as before this PR, and logs it (`info` for a refusal, `warn` otherwise).
- No `co_edition` check: as `collab-client-read` says, a session can outlive the flag. The cost is one internal request per `cat` of a Markdown file where a collab server runs: instant when nothing listens, up to 10 s if the collab server hangs.
- Until the next PR, `cat` and `files.edit` can see different text on an open document. They should ship close together.

## Tests

New `cat` tests: reads the session's text and shows the agent, pages through it, reads the file without a session or when the collab server fails, decides by stored content type, never asks about other files. Checked with Playwright in a local session: with the file and the session holding different titles, the agent's `cat` returned the session's.

## Risk

Low. Only changes `cat` on Markdown files a live session holds; any failure falls back to today's behavior.

## Deploy Plan

Standard deploy.

body:
## Owner ask
Talk to the supervisor: "walk me through this", "I don't like that, change it", "create a PR to fix this", "spin up an agent to fix yourself". Use GPT live voice (gpt-realtime-2.1) on the Mac, the phone and the G2 glasses.

## What this PR does (step 1 of 6: hub only)
- **Voice relay:** `WSS /nodes/voice` on the hub, authenticated separately for the owner bearer, the phone node token and the G2 token.
  - Push-to-talk by default; hands-free uses semantic VAD.
  - Paced uploads with backlog caps, one session per device, 120 s idle cap and 55 min hard cap.
  - G2 16 kHz audio is resampled to 24 kHz (the API rejects 16 kHz).
- **Realtime broker:** one OpenAI Realtime socket per session on `gpt-realtime-2.1`. The OpenAI key never leaves the hub.
  - Tool calls run on the hub's fleet ToolRegistry.
  - Transcripts go into the shared supervisor thread.
  - Barge-in cancels and truncates the reply.
- **Voice tools:** `fleet_walkthrough`, `voice_focus`, `feedback_record`, `fleet_diagnose` (current counts until self-diagnose lands), `self_fix_*` (store requests until the self-fix runner lands), plus the existing fleet tools with their existing gates.
- **Feedback store:** `src/fleet/feedback.js`.

Not in this PR: device clients for Mac, phone and G2; the self-fix runner; self-diagnose. Each comes in its own PR stacked on this one.

## Safety
- Owner confirmations come only from the owner's own input transcript. Model output, thread text and PR text never approve anything.
- Gated actions are read back with the hub's own description and code ("yes 42").
- Spend is reserved ahead per second of audio and per response. It counts toward both the voice daily cap (`OPENAGI_VOICE_DAILY_USD`, default $5) and the global daily budget, and is settled from reported usage.
- Provider errors are scrubbed before they reach clients.
- No merge, release, deploy or hub-restart tool exists.

## Live smoke (real API)
- Transcript in 0.45–0.7 s and first audio in about 0.5 s after commit.
- `fleet_status` tool round trip works.
- Cost is $0.017–0.021 per spoken turn and $0.005 as text.
- End to end through the hub, "tell amman to rebase" raised code 86, nothing was sent until "Yes, 86", then it sent once.

## Enable
`OPENAGI_VOICE=1` on the hub (off by default). `OPENAGI_VOICE_MODEL` defaults to `gpt-realtime-2.1`; `-mini` models are refused. `OPENAI_API_KEY` must be set on the hub.

## Reviews and tests
- Codex review (security and protocol): 6 findings, all fixed.
- Claude review (2 lenses plus adversarial verify): 10 confirmed findings, all fixed. They covered a per-frame fsync, leaked reservations, the global cap, audio arriving before start, barge timing and readback wording.
- Full suite: 2389 pass, 1 skipped. New voice relay, broker, feedback, owner-authority and budget tests.

> **High Risk**

> **Overview**
> Adds **hub-only voice** for the fleet supervisor: when `OPENAGI_VOICE=1`, authenticated devices connect on `WSS /nodes/voice` (Mac owner token, phone, G2). The hub holds one **gpt-realtime-2.1** session per device, resamples G2 16 kHz to 24 kHz, and runs fleet tools as the owner with transcripts mirrored into the shared supervisor thread.

author: chubes4
body:
## Problem
Activity and Missions went empty three times today because the local daemon was stopped (10:05, 15:33 and 16:08 local) and nothing restarted it. macOS has no supervisor. Desktop's locator only *read* `homeboy daemon status`, so it waited for a person to run `homeboy daemon ensure-running`.

## Root cause (investigated)
The Homeboy upgrade path was **not** the cause:
- The 15:28 upgrade to 0.426.0 converged on its own; a 0.426.0 daemon was serving by 15:37.
- Generation `termination.json` records show the 15:33 and 16:08 stops were `--force` lease stops, which only the CLI's `homeboy daemon stop --force --lease-id …` issues. Several other agent sessions were running Homeboy daemon operations and tests on this Mac at the time.
- The 10:05 stop was an ordinary `stop_requested` stop from an unidentified caller.

Whatever stops it, a pure client needs to recover on its next read.

## Change
- `HomeboyDaemonLocator` discovers the daemon with `homeboy daemon ensure-running`. That command returns the live daemon, or starts one if none is running. The locator reads `data.address`.
  - It costs the same as `daemon status` (~0.85 s measured, 3 runs each), and the result stays cached until a transport failure.
  - Core still owns lifecycle and safety: `ensure-running` refuses or plans recovery for busy or ambiguous daemons. Desktop only asks.
- The registry swaps `daemon status` for `daemon ensure-running`; Desktop no longer invokes `daemon status`.
- New contract test with a live-captured, scrubbed fixture. It decodes `data.address` and asserts the locator uses `ensure-running`.

## Verification
- `swift tests/ContractTests.swift tests`: all pass, including the new test.
- `xcodegen` + `xcodebuild` Debug: exit 0.
- `refresh-homeboy-command-manifest.sh --check` **already fails on `main`** because Homeboy removed `runs bench-compare` and `runs fuzz-compare` and added `workload *`. #102 refreshes that fixture, but it will also need the new `workload` commands. This PR doesn't touch the fixture. `daemon ensure-running` is already in it.
- Not done: stopping the shared daemon to demo recovery end to end, because other sessions are using it. Earlier today `homeboy daemon ensure-running` started a fresh daemon from a dead state (lease_missing) on this Mac, and Desktop now runs that same path.

Related: homeboy#15500 (one daemon authority), homeboy#15483 (Linux slow-drain upgrade case, a different failure).

---
AI disclosure: implemented and verified by Franklin (Pi agent, Anthropic Claude) for @chubes4. The agent traced the daemon stops through generation termination records and source, wrote the change and test, and ran the gates.

body:
Addresses the in-repo part of #301 ("Related, same class"). The cozempic `.mcp.json` fix is upstream/plugin-cache and not part of this repo.

## Problem
`tryStartDaemon` ran `uv run tldr daemon start` with cwd `$CLAUDE_OPC_DIR/packages/tldr-code`, without `UV_FROZEN`, and gated only on the directory existing. Two side effects:
- With a real tldr-code checkout, uv could re-resolve and rewrite that package's `uv.lock`.
- In the current opc checkout, `packages/tldr-code` is an **empty, untracked directory**, so `uv run` walked up to opc's own `pyproject.toml` and synced/re-locked opc. This is a likely source of the recurring dirty `uv.lock` in opc.

## Fix
A new pure helper, `localTldrStartSpec(tldrPath, projectDir, env)`, picks the local start command:
- No `pyproject.toml` → `null` (global `tldr` fallback). uv never walks up into opc.
- Executable `.venv/bin/tldr` (an editable install) → run it directly. No uv, no lock read or written.
- Otherwise, only when `uv.lock` exists → `uv run` with `UV_FROZEN=1`. Frozen mode exits when the lock is missing, and unfrozen mode would create one.
- Anything else → `null`.

## Review
- Codex adversarial round 1 (correctness): pyproject-only editable checkouts failed under frozen mode → fixed with the venv-direct path and the lock gate.
- Round 2 (design/failure surface): a non-executable venv launcher was treated as runnable → now requires `X_OK`. The suggested retry-uv-after-failed-direct-spawn was not added: the pre-existing code had no local retry, and the global fallback still applies.

## Tests
- `hooks/src/__tests__/daemon-client-local-start.test.ts`: 6 new tests, written test-first.
- Full hooks suite: 39 files, 622 passed, 13 skipped. `tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- Coverage %: not measured. `@vitest/coverage-v8` is not installed in `hooks/`.
- `/security` was not run. The change only builds an argv array for `spawnSync` (no shell), and every path comes from the existing `CLAUDE_OPC_DIR`/projectDir inputs.

`hooks/dist/` bundles that inline `daemon-client` were rebuilt with `npm run build`.

## What changed

The public pages now load Cormorant Garamond and Nunito Sans from this repository instead of fonts.googleapis.com.

The Google tag, `thanks.html` noindex, robots, the sitemap, the schema, the logo file, cache headers, and `api/app.py`.

author: github-agentic-autofix[bot]
body:
The `/fetch` endpoint accepted arbitrary user-supplied URLs, enabling server-side request forgery.

- **Destination control:** Map the `example` selector to a fixed URL; reject all other values with HTTP 400.

```text
/fetch?url=example  → http://example.com/
/fetch?url=http://127.0.0.1/  → 400
```

author: smarter-poker
body:
## What players saw

From 2026-10-13 13:15Z to 2026-10-14 23:03Z nobody could sit at any Midway Union cash table (67 open tables, every seat refused with `OPERATOR_FLOOR_PARKED`: 32,202 refused `atomic_table_buyin` calls in the three hours before the resume alone) and no tournament could be created for Club JAQK, Deep Stack Society, SHARK CLUB or Midway Union (2,316 refused inserts in the same three hours). Not one alert fired.

## Root cause

`fn_ca_launch_operator_command(... 'park' ...)` wrote the single row of `ca_operator_floor_hold` (operation `a970faa8`, "Owner Authorized Scoped Launch Accounting Reset") at 13:15:28Z, `close_cash` closed 74 cash tables under it, the reset it was taken for never ran (every `ca_launch_reset_*` table empty 34 hours later), and nobody issued the `resume`. The hold row had no timestamp, no deadline and no watch.

## Already done on production

Resumed at 2026-10-14 23:03:41Z as the hold's own actor through the engine's service authority (operation `523a2e84`): 74 resume receipts, hold removed; 271 seats on 69 Midway tables and 43 tournaments created in the next two minutes. Refusals stopped at 23:03:41Z.

## Hardening: migration `20261014231111`

- `ca_operator_floor_hold` carries `held_since` / `expires_at`; a BEFORE trigger stamps a 60-minute lease on every park or pause, so the pinned command functions are untouched.
- `fn_ca_operator_floor_hold_renew(actor, operation, reason)`: the owning operation extends its lease, `service_role` only, audited.
- `fn_ca_operator_floor_hold_watchdog()` on cron `ca-operator-floor-hold-watchdog-1m`: one critical `financial_alerts` row for a hold older than 10 minutes; release at expiry exactly as the owner's own resume would (scope row, resume command, receipts per closed table, recorded in `ca_operator_floor_hold_releases`); late receipts for closes the engine finishes after the release; resolution when nothing is refused.
- Qualification `scripts/ci/test_operator_floor_hold_watchdog.py` against the exact production floor owners (originals.json + the floor component of 20261012181905) on a local PostgreSQL: passed on the Mac, PostgreSQL 17.11, 2026-10-14 23:26Z. Not wired into `ci.yml` because that file is a hash-pinned input of the cash qualification manifests.
- Cron roster moved 132 → 133 with its law test; schema-manifest fragment promises the six functions and one table until the install is read back.

## Installation

The migration is applied through the Apply Merged Migration workflow after protected merge (the MCP route was refused for this session). Live proof in the file header: the cron row active and the lease trigger present.

## Named open item

Tournament `a38b88a9` (100 Chip Guarantee Freeroll, Oct 13 06:00, 58 players) remains dark: its eight retained original hands failed their successor handoff with `record "new" has no field "metadata"` (the scoped launch trigger defect repaired by 20261013133012) and spent their one-time claim. They are not among the 209 originals covered by 20261013163547 and need the same exact source-correction installation.

## Summary

Chunk 1 of the GUI Phase 7 implementation (dispatch plan §2), reviewed and shipped by the stage-3 agent. Lands the GUI foundation seams per the accepted design round:

- **Slint 1.18.1** (caret, Q12) in `[workspace.dependencies]` with **default features** (winit + femtovg + software + accessibility, Q10), `slint-build` codegen wiring, and the recorded CI consequence: GL/EGL/winit system libs on ubuntu jobs, no software-only profile (D2).
- **Theme/token module** `ui/theme.slint` (D9): `Theme` (palette, `base-scale` root multiplier, spacing scale, radii, window defaults), `Typography` (the closed §3.2 text-role table), `Semantic` (state colours) — the only place colours, font attributes, and base dimension arithmetic live.
- **Token lint gate** (§3.4/D12): `scripts/check_slint_tokens.py` — no literal colours, no font-attribute mentions, no literal spacing dimensions outside the theme module; proportional/token expressions exempt; **no suppression escape hatch**; wired into CI (+ self-test) and pre-commit.
- **Contrast check** (§9.1/D10): pure Rust test extracting the declared tokens from `theme.slint` (single rendering source), WCAG 2.x ratios, ≥ 4.5:1 body / ≥ 3:1 large/non-text, with completeness rules in both directions (unpaired token fails; pair naming an undeclared token fails; every `Typography` role mapped).
- **Window shell + mount API** (D5/D6): `mount`/`run`/`quit` in `taskboard-ui-slint`; the hand-over set (`ArcSwap<AppState>`, `EngineSignal`/`SystemEvent` receivers, command `mpsc`, typed `UiSettings`) stored as the seams chunks 2–3 snap into. Theme init is a window-construction step; `[ui] scale` pushes into `Theme.base-scale` (headless-proven on a dev-only null platform).
- **UI-command forwarder** (backlog [2026-10-09], D7): `spawn_ui_command_forwarder` adapting the UI mpsc onto a `CommandSink` (`EngineHandle` impl), hermetic fake-sink test (typed sequence, order-preserving, exits on close; no sleeps).
- **`[ui] scale` config** (Q22/D8): figment strict table, finite + 0.5–3.0 range, out-of-range is the typed `ConfigError::InvalidScale` (variant-matched, `kind() = "invalid-scale"`).
- **Bundled fonts** (Q18/D11): Inter static instances (400/600/700) + JetBrains Mono 400, SIL OFL 1.1, licence record with verified SHA-256s at `assets/fonts/LICENSES.md`; registered at startup through slint 1.18.1's documented `unstable-fontique-011` shared-collection API (the D11 recorded fallbacks `register_font_from_memory/path` do not exist at 1.18.1 — deviation verified against the 1.18.1 sources; the feature is additive over the default `shared-parley` chain, no new crates, Q10 untouched).
- **Desktop entry** (D4/D5): `mode = "desktop"` boots the GUI regardless of TTY (recorded behaviour change: bare+TTY desktop no longer opens the REPL); event loop on the main thread; ctrl_c/SIGTERM exit watcher; `SLINT_SCALE_FACTOR` read before any slint-side call and documented in README (D13); `set_const_scale_factor` unused.

## Review findings fixed on the branch (stage 3)

Folded into their topic commits (no fixup commits in history):
- Removed a vestigial `repl::entry_point` call + redundant kiosk bail in the bare-invocation daemon route (the daemon lifecycle's own mode gate already refuses kiosk).
- Deduplicated the credential-store selection into `secrets::resolve_credential_store` (one definition site for daemon + desktop lifecycles).
- Removed the self-admittedly unconstructible `UiMountError::FontRegistration` variant (speculative surface).
- Deleted the stale root `LICENSES.md` draft (empty hashes; the real record lives at `assets/fonts/LICENSES.md`).
- Fixed the lint gate's violation line numbers (offsets were taken from whitespace-collapsed text; now mapped back to source offsets) and wired its `--self-test` into CI.
- Forwarder doc now states the actual termination contract (lifecycle aborts it); dropped a needless `AppConfig` clone; typed errors flow through `?` instead of `Report::msg`; simplified the test platform's redundant `Once` and fixture-test comment.

Rebased onto current `main` (Cargo.lock = main's resolutions + the slint tree).

author: atqamz
body:
## Symptom

Since Qt 6.12 the overlay opens black: an opaque scrim and an empty bordered card with no text. At shell start-up the log shows seven warnings, one per menu colour binding:

```
PasswordstoreOverlay.qml[115:-1]: TypeError: Cannot read property 'background' of undefined
```

(same for lines 116 to 122).

## Cause

Qt 6.12 adds a built-in `QtQuick/Color` singleton. With an unversioned `import QtQuick`, a bare `Color` resolves to it instead of the shell's `qs.Commons` `Color`, in either import order. Every `Color.menu.*` read is then undefined and each `property color` keeps its black default. The shell fixed the same thing for itself in basecamp/omarchy#14553; third-party plugins are tracked in omacom/omarchy#14672, where the guidance is `import qs.Commons as Commons` and `Commons.Color`.

## Change

- `PasswordstoreOverlay.qml`: one added import and nine renames from `Color.` to `Commons.Color.` (seven menu tokens, two `Color.urgent`). `PasswordstoreWidget.qml` does not use `Color`.
- `manifest.json`: 0.2.1 to 0.2.2.
- Second commit, separate so it can be dropped: `test/lint` fails on a bare `Color.` reference. qmllint 6.12 reports nothing for it, so the existing suite passed on the broken code.

## Testing

- `test/lint`, `test/test-manifest`, `test/test-list` and `test/test-action` pass; `omarchy-plugin-validate .` passes.
- Ran the plugin in an isolated quickshell with a fake store. Before: black scrim, empty card, the seven warnings. After: translucent scrim, dark card, entries and footer drawn, no warnings.
- The lint guard fails on the old code and passes on this branch.
- Not run on a real Qt 6.11; with `import QtQuick 2.15` both `Color` and `Commons.Color` resolve to the shell singleton, so older shells are unaffected.

Once merged, a `[Verify]` issue against the marketplace entry can publish the new commit.

author: thomasfosterau
body:
## Summary

Closes #127. Implements the owner decision recorded on #127 (2026-10-14): each example exports its Effect program, and a unit test runs every one of them over a stubbed `FetchHttpClient.Fetch`. No new CI step: the suite runs under `vp run -r test:unit`, and the examples count toward coverage.

- **Examples export their programs** (`packages/payments-stripe/examples/`). `basic.ts` and `subscription.ts` export `program` and `layer`; `webhooks.ts` exports `makeWebhookHandler` and the demo `program` (with its test secret applied). Each keeps its top-level runner, now behind `if (import.meta.main)` (Node 22.18+, the version the examples README already requires), so importing an example has no side effects and `node examples/<file>.ts` behaves as before. The examples are otherwise unchanged and still read as documentation.
- **`tests/examples.test.ts`** imports every example and runs its program with the console captured and `fetch` stubbed (canned Stripe responses via `stubStripeTable`). The examples bring their own `FetchHttpClient.layer`, which reads `FetchHttpClient.Fetch` per request, so the test provides the stub as that reference. It checks:
  - `basic.ts`: the two requests (path + form params), the returned ids and the printed lines. A 401 is logged as `Authentication failed: …` and a 402 `card_declined` as `Provider error from stripe (card_declined): …`, and in both cases the failure stays in the channel.
  - `subscription.ts`: the four requests and their params, `Authorization` carrying the key read from `STRIPE_API_KEY` through `ConfigProvider`, the printed lines, and `PaymentConfigError` (with nothing sent) when the variable is unset.
  - `webhooks.ts`: every documented status (200, 200, 500, then 400 for each of the four refusals) and the handler's log lines, with a `fetch` that fails the test if called (it is offline). `makeWebhookHandler` fails with `ConfigError` when `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset.
  - **Enumeration:** `examples covered` lists `examples/*.ts` and requires a suite for each, so a new example without a test case fails. `importing <file> runs nothing` re-imports each example with `fetch`, `console.log` and `console.error` spied and requires that none of them is called.
- `tests/support.ts`: `stubFetch` / `stubStripe` also return the bare `fetch` stub, for a program that builds its own client.
- Coverage: `examples/**/*.ts` added to the coverage `include` in `vite.package.ts` (per package) and in the root `vite.config.ts` (the merged map `fallow audit` reads). The examples now appear in `coverage/coverage-final.json`. The uncovered parts are the `import.meta.main` runners and the `webhooks.ts` branches the demo never sends (the subscription and invoice handlers, an unreadable body, a signed non-envelope).
- `examples/README.md`: one paragraph on the export-and-test arrangement.

## Verification

Run on a fresh clone after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`:

1. `vp check`: **pass** (0 errors; the warnings are the repo's existing Effect-preset warnings).
2. `vp run check`: **pass** ("check: every type gate green").
3. `vp run -r test:unit`: **pass** (17 files, 758 tests; `tests/examples.test.ts` adds 11).
4. `vp run -r build`: **pass**.
5. `vp run docgen`: **pass** ("docgen: every example compiled and ran").
6. `vp run test:coverage`: **pass**. Then `fallow audit --format json --quiet --explain --gate-marker agent --base origin/trunk`: verdict **warn** (0 dead code, 0 complexity findings, 6 duplication groups). Four of the six are attributed as introduced. Three are existing `tests/support.ts` duplication with `payments-paypal/tests/support.ts`, attributed here because the lines around `stubFetch` / `stubStripe` changed. The fourth is the 7-line `import.meta.main` runner shared by `basic.ts` and `subscription.ts`, left in place on purpose so that each example reads standalone.

**Mutation checks** (each run on its own, then reverted):
- `webhooks.ts`: answering `SignatureVerificationError` with 401 instead of 400 fails "answers each signed or refused test delivery with its documented status, offline".
- `webhooks.ts`: replacing `if (import.meta.main)` with `if (true)` fails "importing webhooks.ts runs nothing".
- `basic.ts`: `amount: 2000` changed to `2500` fails "creates the customer, then a payment intent for it".
- adding `examples/extra.ts` with no suite fails "examples covered: every file in examples/ has a suite here".

`node packages/payments-stripe/examples/webhooks.ts` still prints the full demo when executed directly. Importing it prints nothing.

## Changeset

- [x] None needed. The change touches the unpublished `examples/` and `tests/` directories (the package's `files` is `dist`, `README.md` and `LICENSE`) and the workspace test config. Published behaviour does not change.

## Notes

- No exported signature, peer range or `dist/` output changes, and `sideEffects: false` is unaffected because `src/` is untouched.
- The examples use `import.meta.main`, which is typed by the pinned `@types/node` and available from Node 22.18. The examples README already names 22.18 as the minimum for running them.
- The package `README.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are deliberately left untouched (a concurrent #146 cleanup branch edits them).
