body:
## What changes

The broker site is now bilingual. Spanish stays at the original URLs; English lives under `/en`.

| Page | Spanish | English |
|---|---|---|
| Broker signup | `/` | `/en` |
| Client registration (broker's personal link) | `/registro?ref=<code>` | `/en/register?ref=<code>` |

- **ES | EN switch** in the header of every page. One click changes language and keeps the query string, so a client who switches language stays attributed to their broker. Switching is not logged as another click on the broker's link.
- **Broker link in the broker's language.** A broker who signs up on `/en` gets `/en/register?ref=<code>` on screen, in the WhatsApp share message, and in `referral_link` sent to GHL.
- **GHL webhooks now send `language`** (`"es"` or `"en"`) in both `BROKER_SIGNUP` and `BROKER_LEAD` payloads, so the workflow can send the welcome email in the right language.
- **English link previews:** the build emits `dist/en/index.html` with an English `<head>` (title, description, Open Graph), and `public/_redirects` serves it for `/en/*`. The build fails with a clear message if `index.html`'s meta text is edited without updating `EN_HEAD` in `vite.config.ts`.
- Page copy moved to `src/i18n/brokerCopy.tsx` and `src/i18n/clientCopy.tsx`, with Spanish and English side by side.

### Separate commit: Spanish copy fix
The Spanish pages still said the client form doesn't ask for email ("No pedimos tu correo", "Solo 3 datos"), but it has asked for it since the GHL webhook change. Counts, field lists and privacy promises now match the form (the full phone number is still never asked for). It's its own commit, so it can be reverted without touching the English version.

## Pending outside this repo
Until `BROKER_SIGNUP` in GHL branches on `language`, a broker who signs up in English gets their English link on screen but the **welcome email in Spanish**. Steps are in `docs/PLAN-GHL-BROKERS.md` (open technical item 4).

## Testing
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` pass.
- Browser test against the dev server with Supabase and both GHL webhooks intercepted (nothing reached the real CRM or database), 24 checks, stable across 6 runs:
  - both languages render, the switch works in both directions on both pages, `<html lang>` and title update;
  - English and Spanish broker signups produce `/en/register` and `/registro` links respectively, and the GHL payload carries the right `language`;
  - client registration through an English link stays attributed to the broker in Supabase and GHL;
  - duplicate-email and generic error messages appear in the page's language;
  - `/en/registro` (Spanish link with `/en` added by hand) opens the English client page;
  - no horizontal scroll at 320, 360 and 390 px widths.

author: peterhudson
body:
Regression could report PASS when a new recording was unreadable, required baseline evidence disappeared, or changed intervals matched a filename prefix. Add independent integrity checks and explicit JSON/text diagnostics while preserving valid additions, intentional --take/holdout exclusions, and existing numerical tolerances.

Baseline writes now reject missing or unreadable required evidence and refuse to replace an existing baseline that cannot be read. Successful changed labels can still be rebaselined after review. Label identity uses the existing rounded-second interval labels; subsecond differences, audio hashes, and complete settings provenance remain separate work. No numerical baselines or detector behavior changed.

Validation: 12 targeted regression unit tests and 3 executable tests passed, including exit codes, JSON diagnostics, subset selection, unreadable-baseline preservation, and new-baseline creation. Formatting and whitespace checks passed. Independent review identified the baseline-read issue, which was fixed and reviewed by the coordinator. [Full CI](https://github.com/peterhudson/timegrapher/actions/runs/38655291636) passed on `5c533a0`, including Linux, macOS, Windows, and corpus regression.

The stricter integrity rule requires coordinated baseline updates when required corpus take folders are removed or renamed, or baseline readings are removed. Intentional --take and holdout exclusions retain their documented behavior.

author: jartanftw
body:
## Summary

Every tool now applies the same scope rules, on every backend, as `docs/architecture.md`'s Scope rule says:
- `user_id` in a scope is refused (`invalid_scope`) instead of silently stripped.
- Empty, `*` and `null` values are refused (`validation_error`) on every operation, not only `delete_all_memories`.
- A value with whitespace at either end (after `agent_id` normalization) is refused, and so is a `run_id` with whitespace inside it, a NaN or infinite number, and a scope that isn't an object.
- An import entry whose scope breaks a rule is listed in the result's `errors`, and the rest import.
- mem0's adapter refuses a wildcard value instead of dropping it.
- Policy drops a search or list result that falls outside the requested scope, and logs a warning.

Gotchas:
- The result check compares the scope a backend returns. A new conformance test checks that search and list return it, and CI's conformance job runs it against real mem0.
- Existing tests that asserted the old behaviour now assert the new one: `user_id` stripped → refused; `run_id: "Run ABC"` → `"Run-ABC"`, keeping that test's point that non-`agent_id` values keep their case.
- `user_id` gets `invalid_scope`, the code for a key the scope doesn't accept, rather than `validation_error`.

## Related issues

Closes #124

## How to verify

- `pytest` (554 pass) and `pyright`.
- Each rule was confirmed by removing it and watching a test fail: the `user_id` refusal, the wildcard refusal, edge whitespace (on a backend with a third scope key), `run_id` inner whitespace, the non-finite and non-object refusals, the result check and its value matching, and mem0's refusal.

## Problem
`RandomGenerator.GetNumbersString(i)` built its draw range as `(int)Math.Pow(10, i-1)` to `(int)Math.Pow(10, i)`. For `i=10`, `10^10` exceeds `Int32.MaxValue`, so the cast silently saturates to `int.MaxValue` (2147483647) instead of throwing. The generator then only ever drew from `[1000000000, 2147483647)`, so every 10-digit result started with `"1"` or `"2"` — roughly an 8x reduction in the intended value space. This value seeds login challenge nonces (`GetNumbersString(10)` in `OpenIDC`'s `ApiController`), so the random string that would need to be guessed had far less entropy than its digit length suggested.

## Fix
Build the digit string directly (first digit `1`-`9`, remaining digits `0`-`9`) instead of computing a numeric range via `Math.Pow`, so there is no power-of-ten arithmetic left to overflow for any requested length.

## TDD
Added `GetNumbersStringOfTenDigitsCanProduceAFirstDigitAboveTwo` to `ServicesTests/RandomGeneratorTests.cs`: draws `GetNumbersString(10)` up to 2000 times and asserts at least one result's first digit is `3`-`9`.

- **RED** (before fix): failed — `expected a first digit of 3-9 to be producible for a 10-digit string, but it never appeared in 2000 draws` (impossible under the overflow, since the truncated range can never produce a first digit above `2`).
- **GREEN** (after fix): passes.

## Verification
Full solution build + full test suite (`passi.sln`, Release), same baseline run on `main`:

| project | baseline (main) | branch |
|---|---|---|
| ConfigurationManagerTests | 1 passed | 1 passed |
| GoogleTracerTests | 1 passed | 1 passed |
| ServicesTests | 23 passed | 24 passed (+1 new) |
| OpenIDCTests | 96 passed | 96 passed |
| WebAppTests | 70 passed | 70 passed |
| PassiWebApiTests | 46 passed | 46 passed |

Zero failures, zero skipped, on both.

## Risk
Low. Pure digit-generation change behind the existing `IRandomGenerator` interface; all existing length/thread-safety/boundary tests still pass unmodified.

## 概要
ゴリ押しで勝てて、防御を使う必要がほぼなかった戦闘を、「一手が重い」「敵を覚えて勝つ」ものにした（v0.83.0）。

### ルール
- **危険な合計値**: 敵ごとに決まった合計値（20以下）でだけ、一撃の重い技（HP 30 の 3〜5 割）が出る。それ以外の技は軽くした。場所は敵ごとに違う（骸骨兵 19〜20、大蝙蝠は 13 で止まって 13〜14 など）。敵の札は最後の1枚以外が見えているので、読んで防御できる。`FATAL_SKILLS`
- **BUST or DIE**: 敵の合計がちょうど 21 なら、敵の攻撃は 2 倍（`RuleSet.enemy21Multiplier`）。敵の手が 21 かバーストのときは、伏せ札がめくられるまで「BUST or DIE ── 敵の手は 21 か、バーストか」と予告する（読み上げにも出す。21 の確率は出さない）
- **21 は「必殺」**: どの敵も、21 の一撃（2 倍したあと）が、危険の一撃と同じか、それより重い（21 専用の技を追加）
- 敵の HP・止まる合計値・技の数値を調整

### 見た目
- 危険は静かに（赤い数字と、小さな赤い三角、「危険」の札）。21 の必殺は、下地を血の赤にして内側がゆっくり脈打つ（枠は普通。動きを減らす設定では止まる）
- 敵の技のレア度の色分けをやめ、役割の色に: 攻撃 = オレンジのアイコン、ブロック = 青、回復 = 緑、21 の必殺 = 赤

author: mcsantiago
body:
Stacked on #1: the base is `feature/inventory-import`, so this diff is only the "Did you mean" change. Merge #1 first; GitHub then retargets this to `main`.

## Why

Walkers can add an asset type on the spot. That is a deliberate usability trade-off: stopping a walk to ask the office for a catalogue entry costs more than an occasional extra type. The risk is taxonomy drift. "RTU", "Roof Top Unit" and "Rooftop HVAC Unit" become three rows in the office summary where there should be one.

## What changes

- **Shared matcher**: `packages/shared/src/similar.ts`, a pure function that compares a new name against the catalogue. It catches:
  - abbreviations: RTU, WAP, AED
  - spacing: "Roof Top Unit"
  - plurals: "Student Desks", "Bookshelves"
  - typos: "Projecter"
  - shared meaningful words: "HVAC"

  Generic words like "unit" and "system" don't count on their own.
- **Type picker**:
  - While typing, a "Did you mean" group lists look-alikes that the plain search did not already show.
  - On the new-type card, an "Is it one of these?" prompt offers **Use …** buttons.
  - Adding past the prompt takes **Add “RTU” anyway**.
  - A genuinely new name gets no prompt.

  It runs in the browser against the cached type list: no new endpoint, table or migration.
- **README**:
  - A design-decisions paragraph on the trade-off and the guard.
  - A new What's next item: an alias table, a `proposed` status for field-created types with office review, and merge.

## Known limit

Synonyms with no words in common ("Smart Board" for Interactive Display) are not caught. A test pins this down, and the README points to curated aliases as the fix.

## Testing

- 16 unit tests for the matcher (`apps/api/test/similar.test.ts`). The full API suite passes, 74 tests.
- Typecheck and web build are clean.
- A headless check at phone width (390px) on the Cedar Ridge sample covers:
  - RTU in the dropdown and on the card
  - **Use** picking Rooftop HVAC Unit
  - Projecter suggesting Projector
  - HVAC not duplicated under "Did you mean"
  - "Leaf Blower" getting no prompt

  No writes and no console errors.
- There is no CI on the repo yet, so these were run locally.

author: reubenbubu
body:
Closes #57 (adversarial GAP 45-7).

## What
- Optional base-policy section, validated and covered by the policy digest:
  ```toml
  [protected]
  immutable = ["db/migrations/V*__*.sql"]
  review = ["sdlc-policy.toml"]
  ```
- The runner computes `git diff --name-status -M -z base..candidate` before gates.
  - A Modified, Type-changed or Deleted `immutable` path, or one renamed away, fails as `protected-path` and no gates run. Added files are allowed.
  - A changed `review` path runs the gates and records `needs_review` with the paths.
- Glob semantics are documented in `runner.py`: `*` does not cross `/`; `**` does; `**/` means zero or more directories; patterns are anchored.
- The integrator refuses a `needs_review` candidate with `review-required`, even when it is approved. Changes to policy or framework paths therefore never land automatically. That is the deliberate reading of §3.1 item 7, "without policy review"; an owner path for them is not built.
- The supervisor treats `needs_review` as gates-passed: the task becomes `verified` and the status is `success`. Without that, the task would be sent back for rework as if it had failed.
- `examples/sandbox-app/sdlc-policy.toml` declares `review = ["sdlc-policy.toml"]`.

## Tests
- `test_31_7` loses its `expectedFailure`; its base fixture policy declares the migration as immutable, and the assertion is unchanged. Red: `'passed' != 'failed'`.
- 4 runner tests: immutable modified fails with no gates run, immutable added passes, a review path gives `needs_review`, rename-from of an immutable path fails.
- 1 integrator test: `needs_review` is refused.
- Full suite OK on 3.12 and 3.13 after rebase. Hermetic check is clean.

- `needs_review` end to end through serve and the integrator.

author: joyja
body:
Fixes #365

## hw TestBaseWrites
Root cause (test bug, product code is correct): the test waited for the refused write's error in `Sources[0].LastError`, but `LastError` is cleared by the next good poll. The refusal is latched in `LastWriteError` precisely for that reason. A poll landing between the write and the check erased the error (the CI failure shows it in `LastWriteError` only). Fix: check `LastWriteError`.

Flake rate, `-race -count=400 -cpu 1,2` with 2x-nproc CPU hogs running: before 15/800 failures, after 0/800.

## prom TestForeignCpuMemPollAndRate
Not reproducible locally (32-core box, real node_exporter, 0/60 failures before; CpuPct sat near 95-99 so the idle-runner case where the true value is 0 never arises). Reasoned from the CI job: on an idle 2-4 CPU runner the true CpuPct is about 0, so any noise goes negative. Remaining noise after #298: the counters are read by the exporter at an instant inside the request, not at our stamp (ms of jitter on a busy runner, large against a 300 ms window), plus node_exporter's 10 ms USER_HZ quantization, against a 1-point tolerance. Fix: 1 s window (about 3x less relative noise), tolerance 5 points (a wrong rate or time base is off by far more), and a 15 s wait for the first rate instead of the shared 3 s `waitFor`. No before/after rate to report for this one; it is a margin change, passing 5/5 plus under load.

Verification: `go vet ./...`, `go test ./hw ./prom/...`.

body:
## Deployment requirements

Normal Kanban rebuild/redeploy only. **No new environment variables, configuration, migrations, model settings, or server/device changes.** This PR has not been merged or deployed.

## Result

Completed-task diagnostics currently show neither session timestamps nor a way to distinguish current context estimates from cumulative provider usage. Add a compact Latest session section using fields already returned by the diagnostics API:

- Agent and recorded session state, with the API's live-session flag.
- Session start and last recorded output/hook activity in the browser's local timezone, including timezone abbreviation.
- Recorded start-to-last-activity span, frozen at recorded activity rather than growing while a completed task sits idle. Missing/invalid/reversed timestamps stay unknown; measured zero remains zero.
- Timing and context sections appear before Git/workspace details. Copy explains that session spans include waits and may reflect restored metadata; they exclude earlier sessions and do not measure total executing-agent runtime. Context estimates are explicitly distinguished from cumulative input/output/cache counters.

No extra network requests or transcript scans were added.

## Follow-up plan (not implemented here)

`docs/plans/diagnostics-task-quality-summary.md` is one bounded implementation task for the coding agent: an explicit on-demand recorded-summary query; a shared deterministic reducer for existing snapshots/schemaVersion 3 JSON; deduplicated cumulative input/output/cache usage; session interval coverage; per-tool counts; explicit failures and unchanged failed retries; compact evidence references. It distinguishes measured counters, heuristic validation/masking flags, unavailable telemetry, and exact active runtime that cannot be reconstructed historically.

Inspection of the supplied PRLINK-10 export confirmed metrics already exist on persisted assistant messages but are absent from this panel's runtime response. The follow-up must deduplicate inherited restart history before counting. No unredacted export or transcript is committed.

## How to test each feature

1. Open any completed task and expand Diagnostics. Check the Latest session agent/state, start, last activity, and recorded span. Check timestamps match the browser timezone and expose their full text on hover if truncated.
2. Leave the task idle and refresh Diagnostics. With unchanged summary timestamps, the recorded span must remain unchanged; it must not count time since completion. A restarted task must be described as the latest session, not an original task start or cumulative runtime.
3. Open a task without a session summary. Values show an em dash and the section explains that exported history may still exist. Missing/reversed/invalid timestamps must never yield negative spans or Invalid Date; the utility tests cover these cases.

author: surfcu
body:
### Problem

A DDCI adapter only learns about a newly assigned service from the PAT that `ddci_add_psi()` generates into the DDCI stream. Since d9df853 a newly registered channel's PMT goes out on the next tick, but the PAT and SDT are still sent only every 500 ms. So after a service joins or leaves, the DDCI side waits up to 500 ms for the new PAT before it sees the change and sends the CAPMT to the CAM.

Observed with tvheadend and a single DDCI CAM (adapter 8) when switching between services on the same transponder (with #1509, so no retune is involved):

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| +0 ms | `DDCI 8: PMT 19 add on slot 0` (adapter 2) |
| +105 ms | `PAT AD 8 new version` (adapter 8 sees the service) |
| +200 ms | CAPMT for the new service sent to the CAM |

Across 7 such switches the delay from the PMT starting on the source adapter to the CAPMT reaching the CAM was 173–662 ms, essentially the random phase of the 500 ms PAT timer plus the CI round trip.

### Change

- `ddci_device_t` gets a `psi_changed` flag, set only when the channel set really changes:
  - `ddci_process_pmt()`: when a PMT takes a new slot (`!already_registered`);
  - `ddci_del_pmt()`: when a PMT that held a slot is removed (`was_registered`).
- `ddci_add_psi()` consumes the flag once (`std::exchange`) and emits PAT and SDT on that write regardless of their timers; the regular 500 ms cadence continues afterwards. Per-channel PMT emission from d9df853 is unchanged.
- Re-sends of an already registered PMT (e.g. after `pmt_add_caid()`) do not force PSI, so slot accounting and the PAT/SDT version handling are unchanged.

### Tests (`tests/test_ddci.cpp`)

`test_channel_change_sends_pat_immediately`:
- no PAT while the timer is running;
- PAT on the first write after a join, and only once;
- no forced PAT on a re-send of a registered PMT;
- PAT on the first write after a leave.

The test fails without the change and passes with it.

### Tested with tvheadend

Same transponder service switches with a DDCI CAM, PMT started on the source adapter → CAPMT sent to the CAM:

| Build | PMT → CAPMT | Range |
|---|---|---|
| without this change (7 switches) | avg ≈ 410 ms | 173–662 ms |
| with this change (15 switches) | avg ≈ 109 ms | 43–277 ms |

The remaining time is mostly the round trip through the CI hardware (PSI written to the CAM and read back on the DDCI adapter).

author: qwerin
body:
CreatureMentalAttributeTest: Decompile CreateAttributeArray and DeleteAttributeArray

Depends on #500 and on the CreatureMentalBeliefs PR (#503); I'll rebase onto `main` once they are merged.

`AttributeTest::CreateAttributeArray` builds a table with one entry per `ATTRIBUTE_TYPE`. Each entry holds a prototype attribute and its debug name. The decision-tree code reads the table, and so does `Creature::ScriptLearnDistinctionAboutActivityObject` in CreatureScript. `DeleteAttributeArray` frees it.

| | 1.20 | 1.10 | 1.00 |
|---|---|---|---|
| unit functions matched (before → after) | 88 → 89 / 176 | 17 → 84 / 147 | 9 → 22 / 77 |
| `CreateAttributeArray` | 99.5 % | 99.5 % | 99.5 % |
| `DeleteAttributeArray` | 100 % | 100 % | 100 % |

The unit stays `NonMatching`: most of the ID3 code (`CalculateEntropy`, `CreateChildren`, …) is still to do.

### Source
- **`AttributeArrayEntry`** `{ Instance, Name[64] }` and its inline constructor. The entries are allocated with the global debug `new` (0x44 bytes) and `strcpy` the name; the Mac body is the same.
- **`AttributeTest::AttributeArray`** is a class static rather than a file static, because CreatureScript (`fn_004F6980`, Mac `ScriptLearnDistinctionAboutActivityObject`) indexes it directly. Neither the PC nor the Mac binary names the table or the entry type. I named them after `Create/DeleteAttributeArray`. The extra static member renumbers `_$S`/`_$E` in the units that include the header. All three hashes stay OK, `Audio.cpp` included.
- **Copied from the binary:** the last slot (`ATTRIBUTE_TYPE_ABODE_ON_FIRE`, name `"OnFire?"`) constructs an `AttributeCreatureDominantDesire`, as both PC (vtable 0x8cfb3c) and Mac do.
- **The `Attribute` classes declare no destructor.** Their scalar deleting destructors call `Base::~Base` without storing a vtable first. Only implicit destructors produce that; declaring `virtual ~X() {}` adds the store. The eight out-of-line definitions are removed. With `CreateAttributeArray` emitting the vtables in this unit, its eight `??_G` still match in all versions.

### Remaining difference in `CreateAttributeArray`
- **Inline budget:** the target calls `Attribute::Attribute()` out of line only for the last entry; our build already does it for the 22nd. The instructions are otherwise identical.
- **String relocations:** nine name strings are pooled with other units' literals at unnamed addresses (`0x9dd418` …).

### Config (all three versions)
- New symbols: `AttributeArray` (1.20 0xc83b18, 1.10 0xc72950, 1.00 0xba4e78) and `Attribute::Attribute()` (`fn_004CB6E0` in 1.20). 1.10/1.00 also get the `CreateAttributeArray` symbol.
- **Unit ranges:**
  - `.bss` starts right after the attribute `ValueName` buffers (1.20 0xc831b8, 1.10 0xc71ff0, 1.00 0xba4518). The array and the decision-tree statics in 0xc831b8–0xc84390 are only referenced from this unit, so `CreatureMental`'s `.bss` now ends there.
  - In 1.10/1.00, `.text` and `.CRT$XCU` start at the unit's `SecondsPerYear` initializer (0x4d2e40 / 0x4b77c0).
- **Virtual manglings** for the attribute and belief accessors that lie in this unit's 1.10 and 1.00 ranges (`TypeName`, `ValueRange`, `ValueName`, `GetType`, `IsDynamic`, `GetNum/NthAttribute*`, `CreatureBelief::GetType`). They were `QAEXXZ` placeholders. These renames bring 1.10 from 17 to 84 matched functions.
- 1.20: CreatureMentalBeliefs' third `.CRT$XCU` entry is renamed `_$S80` to follow the header's extra static member.

### Verification
- Clean builds of BW1W120, BW1W110 and BW1W100: ninja exit 0 and `build.sha1` OK in all three.
- `decomp-regress` against the CreatureMentalBeliefs head, all three versions: no lost matches. The flagged items:
  - The `.bss`/`.CRT$XCU` range moves above, and auto units that the unit now covers.
  - Symbol renames from 0 %.
  - The `_$S`/`_$E` renumbering in two NonMatching units in 1.20. Alignment `.CRT$XCU` drops 70 → 40 % and its `.bss` 98.7 → 98.1 %. I left Alignment's config names alone because #478 renames the same lines. CreatureMentalBeliefs `.CRT$XCU` drops 100 → 83 % (`_$E77/_$E78`). Renaming those would be reported as a lost match.
- `check-versions.py`: 0 failures. clang-format 22, `check_addr_comments` OK. `merge-tree` against #431/#478/#491/#462/#499 shows only the conflicts the base branch already has.

### Questions for @bwrsandman
- Neither the PC nor the Mac binary names the attribute table. Are `AttributeTest::AttributeArray` and `AttributeArrayEntry { Instance, Name }` acceptable names?
- Linking CreatureMentalBeliefs works in 1.20 and 1.10, with hashes OK (prepared on a separate branch). In 1.00 the original linker folded `FindBestObjectToActOn` of Small/Villager/Abode/Context/MobileObject into one copy. It kept that copy at Villager's position, but lld keeps the first copy (Small's). The resulting 0x10 shift is the only remaining difference. Would you take `MatchingFor("BW1W120", "BW1W110")` for that unit, as with VillagerPlaytime, or should it wait until the fold step can choose the kept copy?

author: rimioai
body:
## Context `rimz agents` is the reference design for the CLI scenes, and `rimz teams` now follows it. Before this change, some teams paths reported success when they did nothing, and the two lists used different rules for "needs you". **Breaking for scripts: exit codes change.** - A launch that starts no agent now exits 1. Before, it exited 0. This applies to a non-TTY launch on a closed worktree with work in progress, a non-TTY launch on a clean and landed worktree, and an interactive cancel. The refusal prints shell-quoted `team#lane` resume and fresh commands that carry the prompt. - A prompt given to a live cohort now goes to its leader. Before, the prompt was dropped with exit 0. If the leader is not live, the command exits 1, sends nothing, and prints a `rimz message` hint for each live member. - `rimz teams show team#nosuch` exits 1 and names the live lanes. - Argv-shape refusals exit 2: `rimz teams status` and `rimz teams forge stop`. A name that matches nothing exits 1. ## Design choices - **One needs-you rule.** The rule is `rimz::store::snapshot::needs_you`. It uses `SidebarRow::attention_status`, so the sidebar, `rimz agents list`, and `rimz teams list` use the same membership. The age is the open ask's `since`, else the row's last activity. - Visible change: `rimz agents list` now shows a parent whose provider-native child waits. - **Live-cohort prompt.** The prompt is sent through `message::dispatch` as a Boundary send with the `Done` gate, the same gate that resume and flip use. The receipt is the shared dispatch receipt. - The leader is found with `address::role_holders`, now `pub`. Flip delivery uses the same rule. - Resume's prompt path is unchanged. It runs before registration, when dispatch cannot resolve the leader. - **Owner not live.** This is a needs-you row, not a cohort state. JSON `state` values are unchanged, and JSON adds `stage.owner_live`. The row is skipped at `Done`. - **teams list and show.** - `teams list` uses the agents layout: a summary, a needs-you block with ages, attention-first ordering, and a `no live cohort:` line. - `teams show` lists every declared role, including absent ones. - **teams wait.** It writes diagnostics to stderr only: one line at start, one line when the stage, the owner, or the needs-you set changes, and one line on timeout. stdout and exit codes are unchanged. - **Help and addressing.** - Help is grouped as in agents, with the launch flags behind `launch --help`. `TEAM[#LANE]` is a described positional. - `flip` and `record` accept `[TEAM#LANE]`. They resolve to the live cohort, else to the team that holds the checkout. - `flip team#lane Done` on a stopped cohort ends the board's hold and prints `checkout released`. No worktree is removed. The hold guidance now names this command. - **Receipts and vocabulary.** `stop` and `restart` print `stopped|restarted team#lane (N members)`. "Instance" is removed from user-facing text, and JSON keys are unchanged. - **Contributor page.** `docs/contributing/cli-scenes.md` records the shared scene grammar. The root `AGENTS.md` links to it. ## Implementation Deviations from the plan, with the reasons: - **Roleless teams and inline specs** find the leader with `match_cohort`, because `role_holders` needs a role. - **The `TeamHold` lane match** also accepts worktree names and the root alias `#main`. A stopped cohort is then addressable the same way as a live one. - **The hint text changed.** Refusal hints are shell-quoted, so team addresses print as `'forge#topic'`. - **Missing-owner ages.** A missing-owner row with no recorded flip takes its age from the cohort's newest activity. - **Board bootstrap.** `record` without an address still bootstraps the board from the current directory. - **Report debt.** A `Done` flip after `stop` creates no new report debt, because the stop already settled the run. - **A third test changed.** `agent_launch::assert_from_pr_launch` asserted the old exit 0 and was updated. - **Review round 1** found one regression: `rimz teams forge.reviewer` lost its pointer to `rimz agents forge.reviewer`. It was fixed and is now under test. The seven review advisories were fixed in the same round. Verification: - The full gate (`cargo xtask gate --keep-going --check`) passed 10166 of 10167 tests on the final tree. The one failure, `message::mixed_submit_confirms_record_and_never_resends`, is in code that this branch does not touch. It passed alone and in a focused rerun of the integration `message::` suite. - The live tmux tests passed 3 of 3. - Focused reruns passed on the final tree: lint, docs-links, `cli::teams::`, reconcile, `team_stage`, and integration `teams_flip::`, `teams_wait::`, and `message::` (208 tests). ## Advisories - **No test pins these review fixes:** - park demotion in `teams wait` is computed only for a member without a row status. - `checkout released` prints only when a board-stage hold ended. - A focus failure after a sent prompt is a warning with exit 0. A test for each needs a fixture that the suite does not have. - The live-cohort prompt path has two tests: an integration test and a sandbox run. It was not run against a real provider cohort. - `flip Done` on a stopped cohort is a new path. `teams_flip::` and a sandbox run cover it. - In `teams wait`, `@owner not live` repeats on each later change line while the owner stays absent. - `address::team_cohorts` keeps its own `"external"` fallback lane. ## Context

The daemon migrated SQLite from a `MIGRATIONS` array in `store.ts`, versioned by position. Parallel PRs conflicted on the array, and a shipped migration could be edited silently. The user rejected an ORM for now (D63, D66, Q31) and approved hardening the runner. Bean: vantage-3o22. Blocked by: none. Merge this one **last**, after the PRs that add migrations (#52 is already in; it is converted here as `0005`).

## Higher Goal

Never lose or corrupt a user's evidence store on upgrade (D33), and let parallel work add migrations without conflicts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Each migration is its own file `packages/daemon/migrations/NNNN-slug.sql`, loaded in numeric order; the daemon package `files` ships them (`npm pack --dry-run` lists all six)
- [x] `schema_migrations` (number, name, sha256, applied_at) is created by migration 6 and backfilled; `schema_meta` still updated
- [x] Startup fails with a clear `MigrationError` on a checksum or name mismatch, a gap, a duplicate, a bad name, or a database newer than the code
- [x] `check_docs.py` fails on a gap, a duplicate, a bad name, and an edit, rename or removal of a migration on the base branch (demonstrated against a temporary base ref: 5 problems reported)
- [x] Tests: every legacy version 1 to 5 migrates with data intact, fresh start, second run no-op, later migration, rollback, checksum mismatch, duplicate, rename, newer database, handle closed on failure; daemon and `vantage start` on a fresh and an old database
- [x] data-schema spec documents how to add a migration and the rules; AGENTS.md and `update-spec` point to it; D91 proposed

## Out of Scope

An ORM or query builder. Automatic backup before migrating (specs promise it, code does not do it: bean vantage-xqdw). Down migrations. Any change to what a migration does.

## Summary of Changes

- `packages/daemon/migrations/0001..0005`: the old array, mechanically. Schema from old code and new files compared through `sqlite_master`: same 13 objects, plus `schema_migrations`.
- `packages/daemon/src/migrations.ts`: loader, validator, runner, `MigrationError`. Hashes ignore CRLF; `.gitattributes` already forces LF.
- Files are read from the package at start, not embedded. Why and the alternative: **D91, proposed** (no index row, no Decided by).
- `tools/migrations_check.py` wired into `check_docs.py`, with `tools/test_migrations_check.py`.
- Tests: `packages/daemon/test/migrations.test.ts`, three tests in `packages/cli/test/daemon.test.ts`; older upgrade tests now compare with the latest number instead of a literal.
- Docs: `docs/specs/data-schema.md` (Migrations), `docs/DECISIONS.md` (D91), `AGENTS.md`, `.agents/skills/update-spec`.

author: cocoacommander
body:
Adds one-command control of the local dev stack (Postgres, API, web dev server).

| Target | Does |
|---|---|
| `make start` | `docker compose up -d --build --wait`, waits for the API's `/health`, runs codegen, then starts Vite in the background (pid and log in `.dev/`, gitignored). Skips Vite if it's already running. Prints both URLs. |
| `make stop` | Stops Vite and `docker compose stop`. The database is kept. |
| `make restart` | `stop` then `start`, so backend and web changes are picked up. |
| `make reset` | Stops, `docker compose down -v` (wipes the DB volume so migrations re-run), starts, and loads the demo seed. |
| `make help` | Lists every target from its `##` comment. |

Vite is launched as `node node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js` rather than `npm run dev`, so the recorded pid is the server itself and `stop` doesn't leave an orphaned child. Codegen still runs first, as `predev` would.

README gains a "Running locally" section.

**Tested:** `help`, `start` (including a second `start` while running), `stop` (port 3000 freed, containers stopped), `restart`, and a request through the Vite proxy reaching the API. **Not run:** `reset`, because it would wipe the local dev database.

author: richardfogaca
body:
## Linked issue

Closes #3102

## Summary

- New opt-in Discord gateway setting `allow_all_public_channels` (**All public channels** in Settings → Gateway Channels). The bot also answers mentions in any public text or forum channel of the configured guild, and in public threads and forum posts under one, including channels created later. The channel list can be empty when this is on.
- New `denied_channel_ids` (**Excluded channel IDs**) skips channels such as staff or moderation rooms, along with their threads. It is only valid when the setting is on, and can't overlap the listed channels.
- `agor_gateway_discord_setup` accepts `allowAllPublicChannels` and `deniedChannelIds`. The Discord section of the message gateway guide documents the mode.

## Why / context

Every Discord channel had to be listed in `allowed_channel_ids`. In a community server, a new channel stayed silent until an admin added its ID, and a mention there was dropped without any reply or error. Slack treats an empty list as "all channels". Discord keeps that list required and adds an explicit opt-in instead, because a Discord bot usually sees every channel its role can access.

## Implementation notes

- **Listed channels behave as before.** They are still validated when the listener starts, and every other check is unchanged.
- **Unlisted channels are checked each time they are used:** inbound messages, replies, thread verification and the channel-history agent tools. The channel must be in the configured guild, be a text or forum channel, and be viewable by @everyone. Visibility counts the guild-level @everyone permissions as well as the channel's overrides, so a channel gated behind a role counts as private.
- **Unchanged rules:**
  - Author user and role allowlists.
  - Mention-only by default.
  - Proactive outbound targets, which must still be listed channels.
  - Per-forum `response_modes`: a forum must be listed to get a response mode.
- **Cache refresh in the listener:** cached channel records are dropped on `CHANNEL_*` and `THREAD_*` update or delete events. The cached guild record is dropped on `GUILD_UPDATE` and `GUILD_ROLE_*` events. Both caches are cleared on `READY`. `READY` also restarts the sequence guard, so a non-resumed reconnect no longer drops dispatches until the old sequence number is passed. That last fix also applies to existing setups.
- **Daemon inbound check:** external `/gateway` callers can only claim listed channels. Unlisted channels are admitted only from the daemon's own listener, after the connector has confirmed they are public.
- **Tenancy:** the new settings live in each tenant's own gateway channel row, and the caches belong to each connector instance. No state is shared across tenants.

## Validation / test plan

- [x] `packages/core`: `vitest run src/gateway src/types`, 717 passed. New coverage:
  - Validation of the new settings.
  - Inbound admission across public, private, role-gated, denied and other-guild channels, plus threads under them.
  - Replies, proactive refusal and history reads.
  - Cache refresh on channel, role and `READY` events.
  - The connection test's note that only listed channels are probed.
- [x] `apps/agor-daemon`: gateway, MCP tool, Discord delivery and gateway-token suites, 538 passed. New coverage: the inbound check with and without the setting, denied parents, and the external-caller restriction.
- [x] `apps/agor-ui`: `GatewayChannelsTable` suites, 53 passed. New coverage: the toggle and exclusions survive an edit, and a listed channel is required again once the toggle is off.
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` (core, daemon), Biome, Prettier (docs), multitenancy and realtime boundary checks.
- [x] Each new test fails when its fix is removed: @everyone visibility, the role-change refresh, the `READY` reset, the channel refresh and the external-caller restriction.
- [ ] Live Discord QA against a real guild: not done yet.

## Screenshots / demos

Not captured. The new controls are one switch plus an **Excluded channel IDs** tag field, which appears only while the switch is on. Both sit next to **Allowed public channel IDs**.

## Risks / rollout / rollback

- Off by default, so existing rows are unaffected apart from the reconnect sequence fix.
- When enabled, the bot answers in every public channel its role can see. Admins should keep the bot out of channels it must not read, or exclude them.
- Rollback: turn the setting off for the row, or revert the PR. Stored rows keep `allow_all_public_channels: false` and `denied_channel_ids: []`, which older code ignores.

## Out of scope / follow-ups

- Proactive sends to unlisted public channels.
- A "public" definition based on a member role rather than @everyone, for servers that gate all channels behind a verification role. Those servers should keep listing channels.

author: pcavadas
body:
## What & why

Before: every leveling and Doctor run played a noise-like stimulus whose spectrum is far brighter than a real pickup, so bright and dark chains were mis-levelled against each other. The Doctor measured its body window with the start pad inside it, counted band-edge bins twice, and folded stereo captures to mono before reading the tail, which hid a decorrelated reverb tail.

After: all eight bundled stimuli are pitched Karplus–Strong plucks (guitar and bass phrases, pick-position comb, soft pick) through a resonant low-pass pickup model per topology. The Doctor's body window starts at the signal and excludes the pad, bands are half-open, and stereo captures combine in the power domain, so dual-mono reads exactly as before and a decorrelated tail reads about 3 dB wetter.

The Doctor's constants (target curve, gates, stimulus reference, cut-through population and advisory) are re-derived from a factory sweep through the new humbucker. Each gate keeps the percentile the old gate held on the same presets through the old stimulus, so every rule's false-alarm rate on healthy presets carries over. Peak detection now reads the chain's transfer only where the stimulus has energy, so the gaps between the pitched stimulus's harmonics no longer show up as fake resonant or boxy peaks. A wire chain (an empty preset) draws no finding at any playback level.

How:
- `gen_samples` is rewritten around `pluck()` and a `LowPass` biquad. `topologies.rs` carries `freq`, `q`, `peak` and `pick_softness` per topology. A new test asserts every shipped WAV has a pickup-like spectrum.
- `leveller::analyze_capture` is now the one seam the app, the probe and the calibration sweep share. It takes a `DoctorSignal` (per-channel plus mix) and the stimulus body PSD from `stim_body_psd`.
- `probe --doctor-derive <factory_report.json> --baseline <old_report.json> [--slots <csv>]` derives the reference, target and contrasts from one sweep and rank-transfers every gate from the baseline sweep (`benchmark::derive_constants`, `benchmark::transfer_gate`). A max-plus-margin re-derive over the whole bank widened `lost` by 21 dB and silenced the defect presets.
- `Psd::observable_transfer_db` bridges the transfer over bins where the stimulus sits under its own one-octave median. On the raw factory captures it removed 5 of 6 healthy `resonant` fires and 2 of 5 `boxy` ones, and both injected defects kept their peak height within 1.2 dB.
- The Stage-tightened `muddy`/`boomy` gates are floored at 0 dB: the re-derived `muddy` gate is 0.8 dB, and Stage's −2 dB made a band sitting exactly on the target read as excess.
- `probe --doctor-replay <capture.wav,…> --stim <wav>` re-runs the analysis on raw captures offline.
- The old reference WAV is deleted; the HW-injection unit fixtures keep the gates they were measured against, and the oracle fixtures are built on the current target and gates.
- The doctor e2e no longer assumes the base sound of a checked preset is flagged: with real diagnoses it can sit in the collapsed "N sounds check out" group.
- The new stimulus has a 2.7 dB higher crest factor, so it clips about 2.7 dB sooner on a linear chain. The E2E Parallel fixture's scene ceilings move 3 dB down so the linear sim stays under full scale. On the unit, the factory re-sweep (255 presets) and the Dist and Klon scenes of two loud presets drew no clip refusal.

Closes #235
Closes #249
Closes #259
Closes #250
Closes #247

## How it was tested

- [x] `bun run lint` / `bunx tsc --noEmit` / `bun run test`
- [x] `cargo test --lib` / `cargo clippy --all-targets`
- [x] Offline e2e (`bun run e2e`), via `scripts/gates.sh`
- [x] Verified on a real Tone Master Pro (firmware: 1.8.58): factory re-sweep on the new stimulus, `--doctor-derive`, leave-one-out (in-sample any-rule rate 50.0% on both stimuli), and raw captures replayed offline with the final code: all 7 defect recipes diagnosed, none violating its must-not-fire list, and the empty slot reads no finding.

## Checklist

- [x] Conventional-commit title
- [x] Only touched-file formatting (no repo-wide `cargo fmt` / prettier reflow)
- [x] No lint escape hatches in `src/` (`any` / `@ts-ignore` / non-null `!` / `eslint-disable`)

author: benpaternostro
body:
## Summary

A merge to `main` now releases the plugin by itself. You no longer need to bump the version or run a workflow by hand.

**How it decides** (`.github/scripts/release-plan.sh`):

| The merge | Releases |
| --- | --- |
| Has the `no-release` label | Nothing |
| Sets a new version in `plugin.json` itself | That version, as it is |
| Changes `hooks/`, `types/` or `.claude-plugin/` | A patch, or a minor or major with the `minor` or `major` label |
| Changes only docs, tests or workflows | Nothing |

When it releases, **Release** runs CI. Then it commits the bump to `main` as `github-actions[bot]`, runs `claude plugin tag . --push`, and publishes the GitHub release. The notes are GitHub's generated list of merged PRs since the last tag, plus an Update section. Runs are queued one at a time, so two quick merges can't release the same version twice.

Other changes:
- The manual **Release PR** workflow is removed.
- The `minor`, `major` and `no-release` labels are created on the repo.
- The README release section is rewritten.

This PR only touches `.github/` and the README, so merging it releases nothing.

## Test plan

- [x] `release-plan.sh` run against recent merges on `main`:
  - #8 (workflows): skip

  - #6 (hooks): patch

Die Auswertung der verworfenen Fragen zeigt keine Gruppe „unbekannt/unbekannt“ mehr. Ursache: Der Kurs Industriemechaniker (SIN-621) hat keine eigene Map, seine Fragen bekommen jetzt das Modul der Metall-Map. Bleibt ein Rest, steht die Ursache dort („Kurs ohne Map“, „Einheit nicht in Map“, „Fragetyp fehlt“).

## Nach dem Merge
Die nächste Auswertung (Planer/Tages-Update) zeigt die Module. Ein Backfill ist nicht nötig: Die Zuordnung wird bei jeder Auswertung berechnet, nichts wird geschrieben oder gelöscht.

## Ausgelassen
Die Zahlen aus dem Issue (26/10/8/7) nicht gegen die Datenbank nachgemessen (kein Zugang); Ursache aus dem Code und der SIN-621-Migration abgeleitet, Annahmen in docs/decisions/SIN-665-verworfene-fragen-modul.md.

author: dominikzabcik
body:
A box can now keep the Actions cache on its own disk. With `cache = "20GB"` at the top of `config.toml` and `cache = true` in a class, that class's `actions/cache` steps, and every action built on `@actions/cache` such as `setup-node` with `cache: npm`, save to and restore from the box instead of GitHub. Workflows do not change. It is off by default and adds no Go or npm dependency.

## How it works

- **`internal/cache`** speaks the cache service v2 that `@actions/cache` uses: `CreateCacheEntry`, `FinalizeCacheEntryUpload` and `GetCacheEntryDownloadURL` as Twirp JSON, uploads shaped like Azure's Put Blob, Put Block and Put Block List, and plain `GET` downloads. Every other call under `ACTIONS_RESULTS_URL`, such as an artifact upload, goes on to `https://results-receiver.actions.githubusercontent.com` unchanged.
- **The agent** serves it on the `boxrunner0` gateway's port 5001, archives in `/var/lib/boxrunner/cache`, and gives classes with `cache = true` its URL in `BOXRUNNER_CACHE`. The firewall opens that port to the bridge as it does the mirror's (`firewall.Rules.Mirror` became `Open []netip.AddrPort`, with `firewall.Services` naming what is open). `install` and `doctor` check the same rules.
- **The job image** keeps each runner `node` under a second name, `node.real` (a hard link), and adds `node.boxrunner`. Only in a cache class does the entrypoint link `node` to the wrapper. Per action, the wrapper sets `ACTIONS_RESULTS_URL` to the cache when the cache answers within two seconds and names the same upstream the runner gave; otherwise node runs as before.
- **`doctor`** runs the wrapper in a job container and reports `actions cache`.

## Choices

| Fork | Picked | Why |
|---|---|---|
| How actions find the cache | A node wrapper, opt-in per class | The runner sets `ACTIONS_RESULTS_URL` after merging the job's env. falcondev's `Runner.Worker.dll` rename leaves `container:` jobs and Docker container actions with no results URL at all (`docker exec -e` passes only keys the runner set, `StepHost.cs`), which breaks their artifacts. `NODE_OPTIONS` is silently replaced by any workflow that sets it. The wrapper touches only host actions in cache classes and decides per action. |
| Server | Our own Go code | falcondev's server would see every job's runtime token and uses 10-digit upload ids. Ours is about 900 lines with tests, standard library only. |
| Repository identity | The runtime token's signature, checked against GitHub's JWKS | The token's `repository_id` and `ac` scopes give per-repository and per-ref isolation, including `cache-mode` and GitHub's read-only access for low-trust triggers. Mapping the client IP to a container could not tell refs apart, and a job with `CAP_NET_RAW` might spoof another container's address on the bridge (inferred, not tried). |
| Upload and download URLs | 256 random bits each; uploads expire after ten idle minutes, downloads after an hour | Unguessable, and nothing else to sign. |
| Disk | Entries and uploads in progress together stay within `cache`, and no write takes the cache's filesystem below `disk_floor`; to make room, the least recently restored entry of the repository that holds the most goes first; below the floor the cache empties itself and drops idle uploads | The cache must never hold jobs off the disk, and one repository must not push out the others. |
| Outage | Fall back per action | A failed cache call is a warning. Artifacts are the risk, see below. |

## Who can reach it, and what it trusts

Only the job bridge reaches the port; the firewall drops it from every other interface, the host's included. The server trusts GitHub's signature on a runtime token (one whose `scp` has `Actions.Results`) and the capability in a URL, nothing else. SECURITY.md lists the cache as defended and says what it trusts.

## Proof

- **Prototype** (`@actions/cache` 6.3.0 against the server): a 396-byte save as one PUT and a 200 MiB save through 64 MiB blocks and a block list restored byte for byte, one through a restore key. A pull request token restored `main`'s entry and saved into its own scope. Another repository missed.
- **End to end with real GitHub tokens**: all 9 jobs green (22.04, 24.04, 24.04-arm × runc, sysbox, docker) in [run 38654547907](https://github.com/dominikzabcik/boxrunner/actions/runs/38654547907) before the rebase onto main and in this PR's End to end runs on the rebased head. `scripts/e2e/run.sh` now turns the cache on, expects `ok actions cache`, then with the workflow's own `ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN` (handed over by a pinned `github-script` step): a job container saves through the wrapper, a second restores the same payload and uploads an artifact through the passthrough (finalized, artifact id 11936595380 in one job), the agent logs the save, and with the agent stopped an action sees GitHub's results URL and its restore misses cleanly.
- **Checks** on the head: `gofmt -l .` empty, `go vet`, `staticcheck@2026.2.2`, `go test -race ./...` pass (Go 1.26.9); Linux amd64 and arm64 builds; `shellcheck` on the entrypoint, wrapper and `run.sh`; `zizmor --offline` no findings (same 3 suppressed as main); `cd site && bun run check` passes.
- **CodeQL** flagged `go/log-injection` on a log line whose error could carry parts of a token. Key read failures are now logged by `Keys` with only its URL; the thread closed as outdated.
- **Each new test fails without its change.** I broke 31 behaviors one at a time with a script and ran the matching test: every one failed. Examples: dropping the repository check, the write bit, the read bit for write-only tokens, newest-first prefix matching, block-list order, the size check, LRU, the floor, expiry, signature, issuer and expiry checks, the JWKS refresh rule, the class check in `Spec`, the firewall's second port, the install plan's cache rules and doctor's verdict. Two tests passed at first and were strengthened. `go test -race -count=40` found one flaky assertion, now fixed.

## Security review

An independent review found the problems below. Each fix has a test that fails without it; the failure is quoted as the test printed it on the code before the fix (`f5b990c`, or with the fix removed for the deadline and join tests). The limits are stated in docs/config.md and SECURITY.md.

| Finding | Fix | Failed before |
|---|---|---|
| **High.** Uploads could fill the disk: any number of blocks of up to `cache` each, the floor checked only at reserve, open uploads uncounted, any number of reservations, and the block list copied the archive beside its blocks. The agent writes as root, so the job disk guard did not apply. | Every write takes its bytes from the cache's room as it goes, under the store's lock: entries plus uploads stay within `cache`, and no write takes free space below `disk_floor` (each write checks `Free`). A write that does not fit gets 400 and the bytes it wrote are released. The block list deletes each block once appended and counts the block being copied, so an upload never takes twice its size. At most 4,000 blocks per upload (125 GiB at `actions/cache`'s 32 MiB blocks, and it bounds the files one upload makes), 16 uploads in progress per repository and 64 in all. `Sweep` counts uploads and, below the floor, drops every upload between writes. | `TestBlocksCountTowardTheCache`: `three blocks of 400 bytes in a cache of 1000 = [201 201 201] with 1200 bytes on disk`. `TestOpenUploadsCountTowardTheCache`: `[201 201]`, `uploads take 1200 bytes`. `TestWritesStopAtTheDiskFloor`: `a block below the disk floor = 201`. `TestCommitDoesNotCopyTheBlocks`: `the upload takes 1300 bytes; want 600`. `TestJoiningCountsTowardTheCache`: `joining 300 bytes beside 1000 taken = 201`. `TestBlocksPerUpload`: `block 4001 = 201`. `TestUploadsInProgress`: a 17th and a 65th upload got `ok:true`. `TestSweepDropsUploads`: `below the floor, an open upload took a block (201) and 12 bytes stayed on disk`. |
| **Medium.** A finished entry could still change: `Finalize` renamed the arch

author: hjewkes
body:
## What

A motion is now defined once, as data, and evaluated at either medium (TD-909).

- `theme/tokens/semantic.ts` `motion` gains:
  - `tiers.video`: restates `motion.video` (`enter` 1000, `emphasis` 500, `hero` 1500, `count` 1500, `rise` 40 px, stagger 60 ms capped at 500 ms).
  - `tiers.app`: the UI scale (`enter` 250, `emphasis` 150, `hero` 400 = `duration.normal/fast/slow`; `count` 600; `rise` 8 px; stagger 40 ms capped at 300 ms).
  - `presets`: `riseIn`, `countUp` and `payoff`. Each has props with endpoints, a duration name or a spring, an ease, stagger, exit and `reduced` (`fade` | `jump`).
- `ui/motion/presets.ts` adds a pure `motionPreset(name, tier)`, exported as `MOTION.preset` from `/motion`. It returns `{ durationS, delayS(i, n), at(p, values?), reducedAt(p, values?), exitRatio, exitS, reduced }`.
  - A string endpoint names a tier value (`rise`) or a caller value (`from`, `to`).
  - `fade` keeps opacity only. A spring preset fades on `out` so opacity never overshoots.
  - `jump` gives the end state.
- `ui/motion/curves.ts` now holds the ease map and the spring presets, moved out of `tokens.ts`. `tokens.ts` and `presets.ts` both read them, so neither imports the other.
- ChapterCard takes its rise (the app tier's 8 px) and its exit ratio (0.85) from `riseIn`. It keeps its own cubic/quad curves, because `riseIn`'s `out` bezier would move its mid-entrance frames.

## Byte-identical renders

- **ChapterCard frames:** a scratch test compared `chapterCardFrame` from `main` with this branch at 10,201 progress values (−0.01…1.01) using `toStrictEqual`. All were identical, and `CHAPTER_CARD_EXIT` matched. Five of those frames are now pinned in `ChapterCard.test.tsx`.
- **ChapterCard stills:** `chapter-card/td-909/{before,after}-p{0.05,0.1,0.5,0.95}.png`.
  - Both sets come from one isolated Storybook. For `before`, the server ran `main`'s `chapter-card-motion.ts`.
  - Each pair is byte-identical (same sha256).
  - Provenance: that server served `motion/presets.ts`, which exists only on this branch.
- **ChapterCard stories:** the story file is untouched.
- **ChipBand:** not on `main` yet (#868 is open). `riseIn` at the video tier is pinned to golden frames from #868's `chipEntry` at six (index, count, t) points, bit for bit. When ChipBand lands, `chipEntry` can call `MOTION.preset('riseIn', 'video')` without changing a frame.

## Tests (each names the mutation it catches)

`presets.test.ts` has 17 tests. `ChapterCard.test.tsx` adds 5. I ran these mutations, restoring after each, and every one failed tests:

| Mutation | Failing tests |
|---|---|
| App tier `rise` reads the video rise (40 px) | 7 (the px assertion and the ChapterCard frames) |
| `riseIn` on `enter` instead of `emphasis` | 6 |
| Lerp written as `from + (to - from) * e` | 3 |
| `fade` keeps `translateY` | 2 |
| Stagger without the `staggerMax` cap | 2 |
| `payoff` loses `allowOvershoot` | 1 |
| `fade` on the spring's own curve | 1 |
| `jump` animates instead of jumping | 1 |
| Unbound endpoint becomes NaN | 1 |

## Gates

- `pnpm verify:unit`: pass. That covers format, lint, type-check, build, api:check, docs:check, examples type-check, unit tests (551 files, 10,677 tests) and arch:check.
- `pnpm test:axe`: pass (1,095 passed, 1 skipped).
- `pnpm --filter @titan-design/react-ui size`: pass after the budget change below.
- API reports updated. The new types are `MotionPreset`, `MotionPresetFrame`, `MotionPresetName`, `MotionPresetValues`, `MotionReduced`, `MotionReducedFrame` and `MotionTierName`, plus `MOTION.preset` and the `motion.tiers`/`motion.presets` token shape.

## Size budget raised

The preset data ships in the theme entries:

| Entry | Measured | Old limit | New limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `theme` | 19.17 kB | 19 kB | 21 kB |
| `theme/tokens` | 11.25 kB | 11 kB | 12 kB |

Each new limit is the measured size plus 5%, rounded up to the next whole kB. `motion` measures 14.93 kB (limit 24 kB) and `index` 142.15 kB (limit 150 kB).

## Notes for review

- `riseIn` runs on `emphasis`, not `enter`. ChipBand's entry runs 0.5 s, and its frames must not move. At the app tier that makes `riseIn` 150 ms.
- ChapterCard is a video chapter card, but its 8 px travel equals the app tier. Two changes are possible: the video tier's 40 px, and `riseIn`'s `out` curve in place of its cubic one. Both are visible, so they are left for an A/B round.

body:
## Summary

- **Antigravity removed.** Its consumer terms don't allow use through a third-party app, so PPI no longer offers it.

author: juliarvalenti
body:
H6. Coder's suggestion: count instructions, not wall-clock time.

**Counting (`wow.lua`)**
- Every call into the addon is counted in Lua VM instructions, with a debug count hook. That covers event handlers, `C_Timer` callbacks, slash commands and clicks. It's deterministic, so no CI flakes.
- The fake's own API functions are paused out, since the real client's are C.
- JIT is off while counting (LuaJIT's compiled code skips hooks).
- `client.frame(fn)` counts a burst as one frame.
- Under `--coverage` (its hook is already set) nothing is counted.

**Budgets (`run.lua`):** any scenario fails if a handler is over `HANDLER_BUDGET` = 150,000 (about 1.5 ms in plain Lua 5.1) or a frame over `FRAME_BUDGET` = 400,000 (about 4 ms of a 16 ms frame). Lua 5.1 counts run about 1.6× LuaJIT's, and the budgets fit both.

**New `bursts` scenario.** What the client delivers in one frame:
- a 500-row AH page with a list docked;
- 300 item loads;
- 20 quest log updates with a plan loaded;
- a 50-letter mailbox;
- full bags changing.

**Report:** the run ends with the 8 costliest handlers and the costliest frame, on the CI summary page too. The addon job gets a second harness run without `--coverage`, so budgets are enforced on Linux as well as in the Windows/macOS `cargo test`.

**What it found:** a 50-letter mailbox made `MAIL_INBOX_UPDATE` cost **182,160** instructions (Lua 5.1), because it probed all 16 attachment slots of every letter. `scanMail` now stops once it has found the letter's item count (gaps from taken attachments are still handled): 69,840. **Addon 0.9.4**, fixtures regenerated.

Mutation-checked: without the mail fix, `bursts` fails ("MAIL_INBOX_UPDATE took 182160 instructions (budget 150000)").

author: jox36
body:
Corrección del botón Atrás y del OK bloqueado en el reproductor en vivo (interfaz TV).

## Novedades
- El botón Atrás ya funciona dentro de la lista de canales y de los demás paneles del reproductor
- Un solo Atrás por paso: panel → opciones → ocultar → volver a la guía
- El botón OK ya no se queda sin responder

## Causa
- En Android TV, Compose convierte Atrás en "salir del grupo de foco" antes de que llegue a la app. El panel bloqueaba toda salida que no fuera hacia abajo, así que Atrás no hacía nada. En la barra de opciones, el primer Atrás solo movía el foco al reproductor, por eso hacía falta un segundo.
- El OK bloqueado: a veces el foco quedaba en un panel que desaparecía (por ejemplo, al elegir un canal) y ninguna pantalla recibía las teclas.

## Cambios (`LiveFullscreen`)
- Atrás se intercepta en `onPreviewKeyEvent` del reproductor, antes que el sistema de foco. Se atiende al soltar la tecla y se consume completa. `BackHandler` queda como respaldo.
- El `exit` del panel solo bloquea izquierda, derecha y arriba. Abajo vuelve a su opción y el resto sigue el comportamiento normal.
- Los cambios de foco se hacen en el cuadro siguiente (`focusRootTick` / `focusOptTick`).
- Red de seguridad: si nada tiene el foco, vuelve al reproductor en ~0,1 s.

Compila en el CI. Falta probarlo en el TV Box.

author: sykomiked
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"sykomiked"} -->
_Requested by **Michael-LaurenceZEDECZEDEI** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01SiwTxCAS9qQaLbWY3tFVth?thread=cmsg_01SiwTxCAS9qQaLbWY3tFVthJHwknMdeyzw5vJqjgvG1jK)_

Before: only the matrix products ran on the GPU (#85). Norms, RoPE, attention and SiLU stayed on the CPU, so a token made about 197 CPU↔GPU round trips (~110 µs each on an M3 Max). That made all-GPU generation slower than the CPU (32 vs 57 tok/s), so generation stayed on the CPU. Nothing measured how much verified work a token buys.

After: every step of every layer has an integer-exact GPU kernel, and a whole forward pass is one op list (957 launches for Qwen2.5-1.5B) committed once. The CPU hands the data over once and reads the logits back once. `zt_bench --gpu-resident` turns it on.

The docs now state the GPU-first rule in the owner's own words (`docs/GPU_STRATEGY.md`, rule R16). They also give a bare-metal estimate from memory bandwidth, mapped onto the owner's freight-packet design.

A new swarm module, `swarm_yield`, measures **token yield**: verified work per token (counting retries and revisions) and per second. Each epoch is charted as a candle, like a trading day. An off-by-default link can share an existing pool, such as the node bounties, by verified work (`docs/TOKEN_YIELD.md`).

The logits stay bit-for-bit the CPU's. Each kernel is a port of `zt_model.c`'s integer steps, written once in `zt_metal_math.h` and compiled both as Metal and as C.

**How**
- `zt_metal_math.h` adds the layer kernels: RMS norm, the activation quantiser, bias, RoPE, KV store, six attention steps, residual and SiLU. They share one signature, and saturation counting is atomic on the GPU.
- `zt_gpu.h/.c` builds the op list for a pass, plus a C backend (`zg_sim`) that runs the same list on any host.
- `zt_kern_t.fwd_full` is a new hook that `forward()` tries first. It is declined for a Q8 cache, LoRA, a tap, a distributed model or `zt_q8_t` rows; those passes take the per-product path or the CPU.
- `zt_metal.m` generates a wrapper per kernel and encodes the list into one serial compute encoder. The KV cache is shared in place, so the state must be mapped page-aligned.
- `zt_bench` gets `--gpu-resident` (Metal) and `--gpu-sim` (C backend, any host).
- `kernel/src/swarm/swarm_yield.{h,c}` (rules Y1-Y8), in both kernel images:
  - Only work that passes the quality gate (Q1, r·l ≥ 1.8) counts, and every token counts.
  - Arithmetic is exact in 128/192 bits without `__int128`.
  - Y7 is the candle chart: open, high, low, close and token volume per epoch; the last 144 epochs are kept.
  - Y8 gives pool weights by verified work, fed to `pay_commons_split`'s capped split. It never mints and never sets a voucher's rate. It is off by default, which gives an even split.

**Verified**
- M3 Max: `make -C kernel test-metal` passes 30/30, including the resident passes. All four bench modes give the same `zt.logits_fnv`.

  | Mode | Prompt (tok/s) | Generation (tok/s) |
  |---|---|---|
  | CPU | 126 | 60 |
  | `--gpu` | 242 | 61 |
  | `--gpu-decode` | 235 | 31 |
  | `--gpu-resident` | 289 | 38 |

  The resident pass reads a prompt fastest (2.3× the CPU), but generation is still slower than the CPU: 957 launches a token, and the norm and softmax kernels are naive. Next steps are in `docs/GPU_STRATEGY.md` §4.
- Linux:
  - The new `test_zt_gpu` (18/18, plain and ASan/UBSan) checks each kernel against the function it ports.
  - The fixture models run whole passes and match the C reference.
  - Real Qwen2.5-1.5B through `--gpu-sim` gives an identical `zt.logits_fnv`.
  - The existing tensor tests, `test_zt_dist`, the freestanding builds and `test_hosted.sh` all pass.
- `test-yield` (in verify-all, ASan/UBSan) passes:
  - It covers known answers, 200,000 random cases against the host's 128-bit arithmetic, and 2,000 random candles.
  - It also runs the pool link end to end against `pay_commons_split`.
  - `swarm_yield` is a CI mutation target: 266 of 273 mutants are killed, and the 7 survivors are equivalent.
  - It compiles freestanding for x86_64, aarch64 and i386.

body:
## Summary

Two hidden-tab fixes for the Metric adapter.

**Deferred keyword keyup (4656f97)**
- The first hidden-tab dry-run after #249 read every filter back, then failed the submit preconditions because the Analytics button stayed disabled.
- Cause: the in-page comma sent `keyup` in the same task as the `input` event. Metric read the keyword input before the tokenizer re-rendered it and saw the stale `keyword,` text.
- Fix: `commitMetricKeywordComma` now sends keydown/keypress/beforeinput/input only. `releaseMetricKeywordComma` sends `keyup` in a separate call after a 0.3 s wait, like a real key release.
- A no-submit diagnostic dry-run with this order returned `DRY_RUN_OK` with Analytics enabled and the submit hit on the target.

**Landing report spinner and hidden-tab select close (ed48d02)**
- A later hidden-tab capture failed the submit preconditions before any lookup was spent: Analytics disabled and a select popup visible.
- Causes, from the saved debug DOM: Metric's landing report was still loading (Analytics disabled with an inline loading icon, no `ant-btn-loading` class), and the platform dropdown stayed open because a hidden document ignores CDP Escape.
- `waitForMetricSubmitIdle` polls the Analytics button (1 s, at most 120 polls while the icon shows; 5 when disabled without it) before the form is edited and in the submit preflight. The preflight `loading` check also reads the inline icon, and dry-run reports `preflight.submitIdle`.
- In a hidden document, popup closes and the preflight send an in-page Escape to each open select input in the search builder, press outside on the body and blur the builder input.

Adapter manifest repinned as `p6-209-metric-adapter-v7`. The runbook digest and hidden-tab section are updated, and handoff Rounds 15 and 16 are added.

Refs #790, #733, #791. Adds repair data and one test. Nothing is applied to production.

## Root cause of #790

The issue's premise is off. `1f2684ec` is not merged under `22284a03`. Its `duplicate_of` is the two-character string `22`, which matches no row, and `22284a03` has been merged under `d0cf78b7` since 08-28. The two twins of the Trump story, `a8d8ded2` (marketbrief) and `45b51149` (huggingnews), carry the same `22`. They are one correct story and all three are hidden. (Read-only production D1, 2026-10-14.)

- When: 2026-09-29 22:49 UTC, one run (`fetched_at` 1790720994 on all three).
- Which pass: the LLM cluster pass. Until `049e36df` (2026-10-03), `normalizeClusters` kept any string in `existing`, and the merge plan wrote it as `duplicate_of`. `llm_calls` begins 10-07, so the model and run id for that run are not recorded.
- Would current master allow it: no. `normalizeClusters` drops an id that was not in the request, and nothing wrote a dangling id after 09-29. Replayed on the two titles with current code: `isTitleNearDuplicate` is false, the titles share no `evidenceTokens` token, and `backsExisting` is false, so the title pass and the #745 gate would also refuse the Meta/Anthropic canonical.
- Larger finding: 639 rows (09-16 to 09-29) are merged into ids that do not exist, mostly placeholders the model copied (`abc123`, `ghi789`, ...). The unmerge tool cannot restore them (it needs a 64-hex canonical). Filed as #791.

This PR adds a test that pins the `normalizeClusters` guard (it fails when the `validExisting` check is removed) and the fixture below.

## Sweep

2,824 rows have `status = 'merged'`, fetched since 2026-09-16 (30 days), and a canonical that exists. 147 of them share no `evidenceTokens` token with the canonical's title. I read each pair and labelled it:

| label | pairs |
|---|---|
| wrong merge, new (in `unmerge-790`) | 113 over 51 canonicals |
| wrong merge, already in `unmerge-728` or `unmerge-749` | 12 |
| same topic, different event (not listed, as in #749) | 13 (12 plus `9b848647`<=`7dfb6f4d`, already known) |
| same story, correct merge | 9 |

Cross-language and official-rewrite pairs are the correct ones (SynthID Bio, the OpenAI math proofs, `'AI' is Not a Tool`). A different story with only a topic in common counts as wrong when the headlines are unrelated, and as "same topic" when they are different events in one running story (the Slovenia domain wave after the Trump order, two separate rogue-agent reports).

Most wrong pairs are the shape #733 found: huggingnews and marketbrief twins attached to an unrelated canonical (for example 9 unrelated stories under `6c37fbb2` "Mistral Large 4", 14 under `e972903b` "How to Write with an LLM"). Merge times run from 09-18 to 10-14 (UTC). I did not re-measure which of them current master would still make.

`distinct: true` on every listed pair, since each is a different story. Two pairs (`d86f0911`, `f0acbb7e`) are skipped by the plan as `demoted-canonical`; the tool cannot restore them.

`cd apps/web && pnpm agent unmerge scripts/fixtures/unmerge-790/pairs.json`, no `--apply`, no admin token needed. The dry-run branch in `scripts/aidr-agent.ts` reads through `wranglerSelect`, which refuses anything but one SELECT, and it never calls the admin endpoint. 5 read-only queries.

author: mr-aliesmaeili
body:
## Selected task and why it is next

F-12's core bootstrap/forced-change flow and its credential-transition correction are already merged (#149, #152) — no hardcoded initial password, explicit validated bootstrap configuration, `must_change_password`, the 403 gate and the frontend `/change-password` flow are all present in the tree at `main` `56072fefc565c305d0eb3701922d30f5bb44c26e` (only the un-owned policies OQ-14/OQ-19 remain). L-05 and L-06 are merged as well, and the device/quota, revocation, replacement, receipts, audit-retention and owner-side issuance areas are gated by OPEN product decisions (OQ-74, OQ-76–OQ-79, OQ-81–OQ-85). Rather than invent a new milestone (there is no L-07 scope), this PR fixes a **reproduced defect in already-decided behaviour** in the licensing import conflict authority.

## Defect / missing behaviour

`evaluateImportConflicts` had no branch for "the document names an explicit supersession target **and** the candidate window also overlaps a *different* retained version that still governs". It kept the named target as the retirement and silently ignored the other overlap, so the import was applied even though that version was never retired.

Reproduced on the baseline (domain-level scratch spec, then shipped as regressions): `{ conflict: null }` for a candidate over a retained governing version `V1` (2026-01-01→2027-01-01) and a retained future-dated renewal `V2` (2027-01-01→2028-01-01), where the candidate (2027-06-01→2028-06-01) names `V1`. Applied, the retained set contains `V2` (never stamped) and the candidate, so `resolveEffectiveVersion` reports **`ambiguous` with 2 covering versions** from 2027-06-01 — the defensive read design §3.2 rule 7 exists to make unreachable — and the `license.version.superseded` audit row explains a retirement that did not create the overlap. A second variant is covered too: the candidate overlapping the named version *and* another one ("a candidate that would overlap more than one still-governing version is refused rather than guessed", OQ-80 §8.1).

Authority contradicted: ADR-0046 **Decision 4** (effective windows pairwise disjoint after every import), design §3.3 (a supersession is declared for exactly one version; overlap allowed only in so far as it is replaced), **OQ-86 Option C** (every retained version's effective window counts), OQ-80 §8.1, and the domain's own type documentation ("`explicit` … exactly that version may be overlapped"). No product decision is required or taken by this change.

## Root cause and implementation detail

`backend/src/modules/licensing/domain/license-version.ts`, `evaluateImportConflicts`, explicit arm after `others.length > 1` and before the Option B hand-over:

```ts
if (target !== null && overlap !== null) {
  return conflictOnly({ reason: 'overlapping-range', overlapping: 1 });
}
```

* The refusal is the rule-4 arm that already existed for retired historical windows, extended to the one still-governing overlap a named retirement does not cover. Nothing is written, the operation id stays unused, and the operator can re-issue a document that names the version it actually overlaps.
* Both the read-side pass (`LicenseImportService`) and the authoritative in-transaction re-evaluation (`LicensesRepository.importVersion`, under the installation lock) call this pure function, so the refusal and the nothing-written guarantee hold on both paths.
* Unchanged: a supersession that names the overlapped version still applies (with the displacement stamp at the successor's own `validFrom`); a supersession of a non-overlapping scheduled/expired version with no other overlap still applies (the documented "correction" case); the OQ-80 Option B hand-over, the legacy `VLIC1` rules, the §8.6 reduction flow, transfer/recovery/resolution and every existing refusal reason are untouched.

## DB / API / frontend impact

**None.** No schema, migration, permission, endpoint, DTO, OpenAPI document, generated client or frontend change: the refusal reuses the existing `overlapping-range` 409 contract and its existing operator messages (the frontend maps the machine reason; its Persian conflict copy already covers this class).

## Tests added / defects corrected

* **Domain** (`backend/src/modules/licensing/domain/license-version.spec.ts`): the defect, its variant, the accepted controls, the non-overlapping correction, the unchanged legacy `VLIC1` hand-over, the ambiguity counterexample, and a bounded reachability enumeration that applies every committed candidate state (mirroring the transaction's guarded stamp) and asserts at most one eligible covering version at every probe instant.
* **Hermetic HTTP** (`backend/test/license-import.e2e-spec.ts`, production pipeline, in-memory repositories): 409 `Conflict` with the stable reason and no state change — no version, no stamp, no supersession event, `license.import.rejected`/`overlapping-range` as the last audit row, the state endpoint still deterministic — plus the accepted control naming the overlapped version.
* The tests fail before the change: reverting only `license-version.ts` yields **3 failed | 67 passed** domain tests and **1 failed | 19 passed** hermetic e2e tests on the unchanged additions.

## Fast local checks actually executed

* `npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund` (dependency installation only).
* `npm run typecheck` — clean.
* `npx vitest run --config ./vitest.config.ts src/modules/licensing/domain/license-version.spec.ts` — **70/70 passed** (≈0.35 s).
* `npx vitest run --config ./vitest.config.e2e.ts test/license-import.e2e-spec.ts` — **20/20 passed** (≈8 s; hermetic, in-memory repositories, no database).
* `npx prettier --check` on the changed files and `npx oxlint` on them — clean; `python3 scripts/check-docs-links.py` — 0 broken links.

No full suite, no live-PostgreSQL suite, no migration rehearsal and no Docker/Compose environment was executed locally; those run only in GitHub Actions.

## Heavy checks verified through GitHub Actions

Run URL(s) and the exact verified SHA are posted as a PR comment on the final head; this description is updated only if the head changes. Everything below is CI-only: the full unit suite, the fresh-database migration deploy and rehearsals, the full e2e including the live-PostgreSQL licensing suites (the same in-transaction evaluation refuses there too), and the generated-client drift check.

## Docs / decision records updated

* `docs/licensing/version-model-and-file-exchange.md` — §3.3 rule statement ("exactly the one named version may be overlapped"), the import-pipeline conflict row, and the stale pre-decision "Known behaviour under OQ-86" paragraph, which still described the retired-version exclusion that OQ-86 Option C removed.
* `docs/adr/0046-signed-license-documents-and-version-lifecycle.md` — dated addendum (Decision 4 unchanged; the authority now enforces it without exception).
* `docs/tasks/licensing-explicit-supersession-overlap-correction.md` — repository-first selection, acceptance checklist, evidence matrix and limitations.
* `STATE.md` §42 — baseline SHA, defect, fix, evidence and status.
* **No OQ row changed**: OQ-86 is already decided; this change implements it. No new L-07 scope was created.

## Remaining blockers, limitations, unresolved decisions

* OQ-14/OQ-19 (lockout/admin credential lifecycle) and OQ-74, OQ-76–OQ-79, OQ-81–OQ-85 (device licensing/quota, revocation, replacement, receipts, audit exposure/retention, clock rollback, owner-side system) remain OPEN; no policy is invented here.
* Design §11's migrated L-02 backfill can still present two covering versions at a *historical* instant (the replaced-by pointer was never persisted). That is recorded behaviour, not writable by the current pipeline, and is untouched.
* CI on this private GitHub Free repository is advisory; the manual merge protocol applies.

## Merge status

**This PR has not been merged**, no auto-merge is enabled, and nothing was pushed to `main`. Product Owner accep

https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid-1/#transferred-size-suggestion

The automatic minimum size of a replaced grid item uses its transferred size

any definite minimum and maximum sizes, and convert them through with
the aspect ratio.

2.) If the spanned tracks in the opposite axis all have fixed max track
sizing functions then the opposite axis input to the transferred size
suggestion should be further clamped by the stretch fit into the space
that comes from the sum of max track sizing functions.

body:
This will use `DbTable` to define the columns returned for `Sku` hardware descriptions and `NvlinkNmxcEndpoint` connection records, continuing the model adoption in #7377.

The queries already name their columns explicitly, so adding a database column doesn't change what they return. However, those lists repeat fields already defined by the Rust models, leaving multiple places to update when a model changes.

The seven queries now use `db_table_columns()` to generate those explicit lists from the models. SKU matching and decoding stay the same, as do endpoint lookup, creation, update, and listing behavior.

### Key Deliverables

- Define the selected columns alongside `Sku` and `NvlinkNmxcEndpoint` through the existing `DbTable` derive.
- Reuse those definitions in two SKU queries and five NMX-C endpoint queries.
- Keep explicit SQL column lists without maintaining a separate copy in each query.
